codex.chapter.aero_basics.intro.0: Aeronautics and Simulated turn glued blocks into physical constructs with mass, inertia and air resistance. Flight needs controllable lift, propulsion, stability and a way to land; one miraculous material replaces none of the other parts.
codex.chapter.aero_basics.intro.1: Start with a small craft right at the ground. Learn assembly, test every change without valuable cargo, and keep a way back to the pad before flying far.
codex.chapter.aero_basics.subtitle: Real physics, airships and levitite
codex.chapter.aero_basics.title: Create Aeronautics: Flight
codex.chapter.ca_electric.intro.0: Create Addition links rotation to FE electricity. A generator consumes mechanical power, a motor gives it back, wires and accumulators carry and store the charge. There is no perpetual motion between the two kinds of energy.
codex.chapter.ca_electric.intro.1: Build a short line with one consumer and read the real numbers. Then add storage, liquid fuel and interfaces for moving machines.
codex.chapter.ca_electric.subtitle: Turning rotation into energy and back
codex.chapter.ca_electric.title: Create Addition: Electricity
codex.chapter.cbc_advanced.intro.0: The next guns ask for new alloys, layered barrels and an understanding of breeches. A stronger barrel widens your options but cancels no limits: ammunition, length, joints and the way the breech closes still decide whether the gun fires or bursts. Keep a log of loads you have proven.
codex.chapter.cbc_advanced.intro.1: Make and inspect the parts first, then exercise the empty gun. Test fuzes, the autocannon and mortar shells one at a time, on a range that is already prepared.
codex.chapter.cbc_advanced.subtitle: Steel, autocannons and special shells
codex.chapter.cbc_advanced.title: Big Cannons: Heavy Ordnance
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.intro.0: Big Cannons teaches you to build large guns the real way: melt the metal, cast a blank, bore the barrel. The foundry needs heat, water and Create rotation, and firing needs a separate range where a shot flies into empty land rather than your warehouse.
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.intro.1: Finished parts, an assembled gun and a properly loaded gun are three different states. Match connections and charge to the material’s strength: too much bursts the barrel, too little leaves the shot stuck in a long bore.
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.subtitle: Metals, molds and the first gun
codex.chapter.cbc_foundry.title: Big Cannons: Foundry
codex.chapter.create_andesite.intro.0: Andesite machines turn rotation into useful operations: pressing metal, milling grain, cutting wood and processing items with air. Complete each operation with a small batch before connecting machines with belts.
codex.chapter.create_andesite.intro.1: Plan the input and output alongside the machine itself. A full chest, a reversed funnel or an insufficient processing section can halt production despite a working drive. The bread and sheet lines in this chapter teach you to check the material’s entire route.
codex.chapter.create_andesite.subtitle: First machines: press, millstone, saw, fan
codex.chapter.create_andesite.title: Andesite Age
codex.chapter.create_basics.intro.0: A small workspace beside water and a chest for parts is enough for a first workshop. In Create, machines receive rotation through shafts: a source provides stress capacity, and working machines consume more of it the faster they turn. The first quests assemble a source, a transmission and instruments before a whole factory hangs on the shaft.
codex.chapter.create_basics.intro.1: The wrench is for installation, the goggles for diagnosis, and Ponder shows how blocks go together. The book sees prepared parts; watch the assembled machine work in the world with your own eyes. Item objectives remember the largest amount of one kind seen at once: different items can be shown in turn, and a recorded machine never has to come down for a new quest.
codex.chapter.create_basics.subtitle: Andesite alloy, shafts and sources of power
codex.chapter.create_basics.title: First Rotation
codex.chapter.create_brass.intro.0: Brass unlocks precise item feeding, mechanical arms and sequenced assembly. The first batch comes from copper and zinc in a heated basin; afterward you can progressively automate the workshop itself.
codex.chapter.create_brass.intro.1: Begin by separating raw materials, intermediate items and finished products into clear routes. Filters and ingredient reserves matter more than high speed: unfinished mechanisms must return to the correct operation, while completed products go to storage.
codex.chapter.create_brass.subtitle: Brass, crushing wheels and smart automation
codex.chapter.create_brass.title: Brass Age
A contraption is a group of blocks that moves as one structure after assembly. Glue and chassis determine membership, a bearing or another drive provides motion, and tools and storage perform work. Begin with a small platform carrying nothing valuable.

Before startup, inspect the movement area, container attachments and a way to stop the drive from outside. Owning components confirms preparation; correct assembly and a safe route require an in-world trial.
codex.chapter.create_contraptions.title: Contraptions
codex.chapter.create_copper.intro.0: The copper branch links water supply, steam and compressed-air gear. A boiler needs space, heat and water all at once; a diving set needs a backtank charged in advance. Parts in a chest do not create those conditions.
codex.chapter.create_copper.intro.1: Test the installation somewhere calm, and only then expand it or go underwater. Lava has its own rules for the whole armour set, and they are covered separately.
codex.chapter.create_copper.subtitle: Steam, pressure and diving
codex.chapter.create_copper.title: Copper Age
codex.chapter.create_fluids.intro.0: Fluids in Create move through pipes when a pump pushes them. The source, the pumping direction, a buffer tank and the consumer are four things worth thinking through separately. Start with water: it is a safe way to test connections and valves.
codex.chapter.create_fluids.intro.1: The same arrangement will later serve a mixer, a spout and a steam boiler. Keep different fluids in different main lines, and test dangerous spills well away from wooden buildings.
codex.chapter.create_fluids.subtitle: Pipes, pumps, valves and industrial pouring
codex.chapter.create_fluids.title: Fluids
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.intro.0: Once there are several machines, convenient transmissions and predictable stops start to matter. This chapter teaches you to turn axes, disconnect branches, set speed and tie machinery to redstone. A small test rig beside an already working source is the best place for it.
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.intro.1: Signal and rotation play different roles: the signal gives the command, the source provides the motion. Sensors and displays will show the result, provided they are connected to the very line you are watching.
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.subtitle: Gearboxes, clutches, speed and its price
codex.chapter.create_kinetics.title: Controlling Rotation
codex.chapter.create_packages.intro.0: Package logistics separates requesting from transportation. The stock network reports available items, a packager creates a box, and belts, chains or trains carry it to a receiver. Wireless stock communication does not teleport contents.
codex.chapter.create_packages.intro.1: Send one inexpensive package between two points first and verify its address, reception and unpacking. Then connect a stock ticker and automatic requests: complex orders are easier to diagnose on an already working route.
codex.chapter.create_packages.subtitle: Create 6 logistics: boxes, stock and orders
codex.chapter.create_packages.title: Packages and Factory
codex.chapter.create_tools.intro.0: Create tools help build, carry supplies and reproduce tested structures. Learn extended reach and schematic saving before using the schematicannon for automatic construction. Copying requires understanding the selected boundaries and material list beforehand.
codex.chapter.create_tools.intro.1: Some features are intended only for Creative mode. The guide identifies these separately so you do not search for nonexistent Survival recipes or mistake a reading objective for receiving an item.
codex.chapter.create_tools.subtitle: Create tools and building from blueprints
codex.chapter.create_tools.title: Gear and Schematics
codex.chapter.create_trains.intro.0: A train connects distant workshops and stores without a continuous belt line. Begin with sturdy sheets, railway casings, track and an assembly station. Schedules, freight interfaces and shared traffic control come afterward.
codex.chapter.create_trains.intro.1: Start with a short line and one light train. An onboard boiler is not required for a Create train to move; correct assembly, controls and a reachable route matter more. Check loading and return travel separately from locomotive decoration.
codex.chapter.create_trains.subtitle: Tracks, stations, schedules and Steam 'n' Rails
codex.chapter.create_trains.title: Trains
codex.chapter.create_world.intro.0: Create add-ons place structures and decorative components in the world that are worth examining during ordinary travel. Inspect found structures from outside first: appearance does not guarantee working automation, a safe entrance or particular loot.
codex.chapter.create_world.intro.1: Record interesting coordinates and observe actual design choices such as shaft routes, tank placement and maintenance access. These observations can inform your base whether you leave the discovered building intact or later rebuild it.
codex.chapter.create_world.subtitle: Structures, decor and small add-ons
codex.chapter.create_world.title: Create in the World
codex.chapter.dim_aether.intro.0: Aether consists of sky islands where local tools and fall protection matter. Secure a platform around the portal, learn Skyroot, Holystone, and Ambrosium, then progress to Zanite and Gravitite.
codex.chapter.dim_aether.intro.1: The three dungeon types have different combat rules. Attack the Slider with a pickaxe, present medals to the Valkyrie Queen, and freeze the Sun Spirit with a reflected Ice Crystal. Rewards come from different dungeon chests, so a card title does not necessarily locate every requested item.
codex.chapter.dim_aether.subtitle: The sky dimension: dungeons, gravitite and valkyries
codex.chapter.dim_aether.title: Aether
codex.chapter.dim_end.intro.0: An End expedition starts with locating a stronghold and develops into a reliable outer-island route. Prepare extra Eyes of Ender, and leave a respawn point and spare equipment in the Overworld before jumping in.
codex.chapter.dim_end.intro.1: Collect Dragon’s Breath during combat, find Elytra on End Ships, and obtain shells from Shulkers. These are distinct expedition results. Eden frames belong to Eternal Tales and need a crafted crystal; defeating the dragon does not automatically open them.
codex.chapter.dim_end.subtitle: The dragon, ender pearls and the way beyond
codex.chapter.dim_end.title: The End
codex.chapter.dim_nether.intro.0: The Nether supplies Blaze Rods, quartz, nether wart, and Ancient Debris. Secure your return first: a protected portal, recorded coordinates, and spare ignition matter more than an inventory full of ore.
codex.chapter.dim_nether.intro.1: Fortresses, bastions, and Eternal Tales structures are distinct destinations. Netherite is unnecessary for starting wart farming or brewing protection; some cards can be pursued in parallel. The side branches turn an initial dangerous visit into a sustained supply route.
codex.chapter.dim_nether.subtitle: What the pack's mods take from the Nether
codex.chapter.dim_nether.title: The Nether
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.intro.0: The Twilight Forest opens with a small water portal, but the road beyond is gated by the mod’s advancements. After the Naga and the Lich the path splits three ways: swamp, dark forest and snow. All three must be finished before the Highlands open.
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.intro.1: A trophy, a special drop and the action that lifts a regional curse are three different things, and mixing them up is costly. The Fire Swamp admits only those who have eaten Minoshroom’s meal; a trophy on the pedestal opens the stronghold. The Magic Map shows where to go next instead of forcing a way through an active curse.
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.subtitle: A strict boss chain from the Naga to the Yeti
codex.chapter.dim_twilight.title: Twilight Forest
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.intro.0: The final trials bring together three independent paths: Eternal Darkness battles, Arkemer technology and milestones from several major mods. This is a late chapter whose requirements build on the detailed guides in earlier maps.
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.intro.1: Finishing Apotheosis completes this final chain but does not automatically mark other chapters or side projects. The book's overall counter still shows how many quests remain for full completion.
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.subtitle: The book's last quests
codex.chapter.end_apotheosis.title: Apotheosis
codex.chapter.end_marathon.intro.0: The marathon tests reliable production with a large order. Begin with a small batch, find the slowest stage and ensure the line can stop when its output fills. Only then increase the order.
codex.chapter.end_marathon.intro.1: All the main quests of this chapter take the items handed in. Before the reward, gather the whole batch in your ordinary inventory: what sits in the network or a backpack is invisible to the book. Steel is accepted as blocks so that such a volume fits on a player at all.
codex.chapter.end_marathon.subtitle: Numbers you can't catch without an autocraft chain
codex.chapter.end_marathon.title: Marathon
codex.chapter.end_monuments.intro.0: Monuments begin with a production reserve: girders, tracks, casings and rare building materials. The main cards accept the specified batch in exchange for a reward; they do not recognize the shape of a finished tower, fortress or town.
codex.chapter.end_monuments.intro.1: Turn-in resources disappear when you claim the reward. Keep this batch separate from the building stock. Side quests put the resulting production to use in the world and use manual confirmation against a specific result.
codex.chapter.end_monuments.subtitle: Builds that justify the whole factory
codex.chapter.end_monuments.title: Monuments
codex.chapter.et_amber.intro.0: Amber requires Sorcery level thirteen and materials from several systems: fishing, sorcery and metallurgy. Prepare them in advance so your first journey can focus on exploration rather than missing ingredients.
codex.chapter.et_amber.intro.1: The story leads from Nightingale to the maze and then Xaxxas’s castle. Location hints use your first portal in this world as their reference, so preserve its coordinates.
codex.chapter.et_amber.subtitle: A bright dimension with a dark secret
codex.chapter.et_amber.title: Kingdom of Amber
codex.chapter.et_archaeology.intro.0: Archaeology turns suspicious blocks into materials, pottery sherds and blueprints. Use a brush, preserve rare originals and only then decide what to recycle for experience.
codex.chapter.et_archaeology.intro.1: The Jewelry Table uses a separate chain of rough gems, sandpaper and magnifiers. Its output quality is linked to Archery, so developing both branches in parallel is useful.
codex.chapter.et_archaeology.subtitle: Brushes, blueprints, vases and totems
codex.chapter.et_archaeology.title: Archaeology
codex.chapter.et_comets.intro.0: Comets is an early extraterrestrial stage with islands, local metals and the Terrible Tree. Its crystal requires Sorcery level two; building blocks for bridges and a tested return method are particularly valuable on your first visit.
codex.chapter.et_comets.intro.1: Save Aerolite, Skylite and summoning materials. Defeating the Tree is checked when summoning Rock-Blaze, so simply buying Hell Fire cannot replace that milestone.
codex.chapter.et_comets.subtitle: First dimension: floating islands and the Terrible Tree
codex.chapter.et_comets.title: Comets
codex.chapter.et_darkness.intro.0: Eternal Darkness strengthens the world and enables Humanity and Fear. A Totem of Eternal Darkness activates it, and a Totem of Eternity reverses it; prepare both before experimenting.
codex.chapter.et_darkness.intro.1: Super Duper Darkness is a separate mode in which any damage kills immediately. It is not automatically required for every special victory: check each advancement’s exact conditions.
codex.chapter.et_darkness.subtitle: Hard mode and humanity
codex.chapter.et_darkness.title: Eternal Darkness
codex.chapter.et_eden.intro.0: Sunstones connect the Nyetet victory with Eden. Preserve individual stones: the crystal uses two alongside a Silver Block, Dragon’s Breath and Monster Blindness, requiring Sorcery level six.
codex.chapter.et_eden.intro.1: Eden’s story begins by speaking with D’Kudja and freeing the Altar of the Sun. Some collection cards in this chapter concern much later opponents.
codex.chapter.et_eden.subtitle: The sunny world of the Sunfurry
codex.chapter.et_eden.title: Gardens of Eden
codex.chapter.et_farming.intro.0: Plants and fish supply food, crafting and dimension crystals. First obtain one confirmed harvest or catch, then expand production and add machine support.
codex.chapter.et_farming.intro.1: A pot needs water and fertiliser; a net needs the right surroundings and bait. The book will tick the harvest and the catch, but keeping an eye on water and bait is up to you.
codex.chapter.et_farming.subtitle: Pots, machines, nets and bug nets
codex.chapter.et_farming.title: Garden, Fishing and Catching
codex.chapter.et_gear.intro.0: This chapter collects equipment from different stages rather than asking you to craft everything on day one. Choose the nearest useful branch based on resources already unlocked, leaving late collections for their corresponding dimensions.
codex.chapter.et_gear.intro.1: Armor often requires wearing the full set; weapons and accessories are generally checked on acquisition. Preserve an item’s progress before an upgrade recipe consumes it.
codex.chapter.et_gear.subtitle: Armors, weapons and artifacts
codex.chapter.et_gear.title: Eternal Tales Gear
codex.chapter.et_intro.intro.0: Everything starts with the Journal and Eternal Town: here you take story assignments, read up on skills and meet Miguel. The Journal keeps the characters’ assignments, and this map ties them to crafts and travels.
codex.chapter.et_intro.intro.1: Defeating a boss, finishing a dialogue and obtaining an item are separate conditions. Read each card’s objectives: the conversation after your return can matter as much as the battle.
codex.chapter.et_intro.subtitle: Journal, Eternal Town and notice boards
codex.chapter.et_intro.title: Eternal Tales
codex.chapter.et_karvat.intro.0: Karvat is accessible at Sorcery level eight and follows the restoration of Gulibeg’s power. Speak to him first: the power pieces he provides become summoning items for four lesser gods.
codex.chapter.et_karvat.intro.1: After the four temples, combine their powers for Enicrih and return to the quest giver. Khogachi and the Arkemer opponents in side cards belong to other routes, not this ritual.
codex.chapter.et_karvat.subtitle: Divine forest and deities
codex.chapter.et_karvat.title: Lands of Karvat
codex.chapter.et_nether_end.intro.0: The Nether supplies early travel materials and its own Clocktower storyline. The End contains an Ancient Enderman, the restoration of a chorus plant and objectives beyond defeating the dragon.
codex.chapter.et_nether_end.intro.1: Plan trips from a checklist: keys, Nether Fish and Fire Moss serve different recipes, while Ancient Chorus helps a traveler after dimension changes.
codex.chapter.et_nether_end.subtitle: The Piglin Clocktower and the Ancient Chorus
codex.chapter.et_nether_end.title: Nether and End
codex.chapter.et_overworld.intro.0: The Overworld introduces ores, events and the first major opponents. A Cobalt Pickaxe matters for Vivid, while the Interdimensional Creator connects this preparation with later travel.
codex.chapter.et_overworld.intro.1: Some collection cards include late objectives from other dimensions. Their map placement does not promise that every listed boss lives near your first base.
codex.chapter.et_overworld.subtitle: Ores, lunar events and first bosses
codex.chapter.et_overworld.title: The Overworld
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.intro.0: The road to Purgatorium begins in Comets and the Nether. Defeat the Terrible Tree first, then summon Rock-Blaze with Hell Fire and obtain Hellrock by interacting with the living boss.
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.intro.1: The crystal needs a block made from nine Hellrock and Sorcery level four. Within Purgatorium, assemble the Fallen Rune, find the correct altar and prepare for Nyetet.
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.subtitle: Darkness, the Rock Blaze and the Fallen Rune
codex.chapter.et_purgatorium.title: Purgatorium
codex.chapter.et_rayana.intro.0: Rayana opens with a Sorcery level eight crystal and leads into the Bloody Cult story. Speak with the Daredians first, then prepare a Bloody Eye and search for the Aede temple.
codex.chapter.et_rayana.intro.1: The Infected Kraken listed here belongs to another side route: summon it during rain on an Overworld Mucunfectio Beach.
codex.chapter.et_rayana.subtitle: Tropics, vampirism and Pterion
codex.chapter.et_rayana.title: Rayana
codex.chapter.et_skills.intro.0: Eternal Tales skills improve through their corresponding activities: mining, fighting, growing, trading and others. They are separate from vanilla experience and affect the mod’s own items and recipes.
codex.chapter.et_skills.intro.1: Some cards here check skill development; others check related equipment. Read the actual objectives: making a chest or armor does not prove that a skill has reached a high level.
codex.chapter.et_skills.subtitle: Nine skills and level points
codex.chapter.et_skills.title: Skills
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.intro.0: Sorcery connects rune mining, essence storage and equipment improvement. Begin with one clear cycle: mine runes, process them in the cauldron and obtain an essence container.
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.intro.1: Runic Matrix is an armor enchantment. Blueprints, the printer and altars are separate systems; their shared magical theme does not make them interchangeable.
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.subtitle: Runes, essences, matrix and astral enchanting
codex.chapter.et_sorcery.title: Sorcery
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.intro.0: Ultimate World continues after the main victory. Its crystal combines four earlier crystals with The Ultimate Bricks; Arkemer crafting separately depends on the Aetherium Forge and Aftermath storyline.
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.intro.1: This chapter collects long-term goals. Open material sources and the forge first, then make equipment for a purpose; some late items consume tools you have already crafted.
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.subtitle: Arkemers, aetherium and the real endgame
codex.chapter.et_ultimate.title: Ultimate World
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.intro.0: Unahzaal’s dimension requires Sorcery level sixteen and crystals from several previously opened worlds. Preparing the Damaged Astral consumes a weapon collection, so separate your fighting gear from recipe ingredients beforehand.
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.intro.1: The main Unahzaal victory opens later events and the Arkemer line. Gifts, special Darkness conditions and Tetragrammaton are distinct objectives rather than one shared completion mark.
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.subtitle: The multiverse and the end of the road
codex.chapter.et_unahzaal.title: Unahzaal
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.intro.0: Volcanech requires Sorcery level ten and materials from earlier worlds. Fire Resistance, repaired armor and attention to enemies with floating weapons and sulfur clouds are useful here.
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.intro.1: For the golem, prepare a Flame Sphere and Pyro Volcanite in advance, and a Spawner Cracker for the scout’s assignment. Arahulum from the side line is summoned in the End.
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.subtitle: Volcanoes, aggression and betrayal
codex.chapter.et_volcanech.title: Volcanech
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.intro.0: A kitchen turns stray finds into supplies you can carry far from home. Farmer’s Delight adds a knife and cutting board, a cooking pot for complex dishes, new crops and large feasts for the table. Cook the first portion slowly enough to understand each step, and only then widen the menu.
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.intro.1: Keep work surfaces, heat and storage close together while leaving a clear walkway. Recipes are half the job: seeds go back to the beds, ingredients get replenished, and finished food goes into a separate travel reserve.
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.intro.2: The side quests tie the garden, the prep work and the daily running of the kitchen together. Item objectives look at what is in your inventory; manual ones wait for you to confirm that the kitchen really works.
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.subtitle: Farmer's Delight: knives, board, pot and skillet
codex.chapter.fd_kitchen.title: Kitchen
codex.chapter.final_bridges.intro.0: This map connects paths you already know: rotation with electricity, processing with storage, transport with supplies. Start with a small pair of devices and one trial order to see where items or energy travel.
codex.chapter.final_bridges.intro.1: The main cards gather the equipment and the first results. Whether the combined installation actually works is shown by the practical branches with manual confirmation. Test compatibility on specific inputs and outputs, not by a familiar mod name.
codex.chapter.final_bridges.subtitle: How three tech lines join into one
codex.chapter.final_bridges.title: Bridges Between Mods
codex.chapter.final_goals.intro.0: Ten summits gather late results from the pack's major paths. They are milestones for finishing chosen routes, not a claim that one rare item automatically proves a complete factory or fully explored world.
codex.chapter.final_goals.intro.1: Each node lists exact requirements: items, personal advancements or a manual check. The final card combines all ten summits; side projects and unfinished chapters still count toward the book's overall progress.
codex.chapter.final_goals.subtitle: How the pack ends
codex.chapter.final_goals.title: Final Goals
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.intro.0: Apotheosis connects affix loot, gems, and personal World Tiers. Compare found equipment with your current set before salvaging unwanted pieces into upgrade materials. Affix rarity and ordinary enchantments are separate properties.
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.intro.1: Apothic Enchanting uses Eterna, Quanta, and Arcana, while the active World Tier also limits available Eterna. Unlocking a tier does not activate it: use the tier selection screen before configuring a stronger enchanting table.
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.subtitle: Affixes, gems and gear that never repeats
codex.chapter.hunt_apotheosis.title: Apotheosis
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.intro.0: Hunting here includes observation, taming, trials, and mutant battles. Read the creature’s Animal Dictionary entry before travelling: food, habitat, and useful interactions often matter more than weapon strength.
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.intro.1: Mowzie’s Mobs encounters depend on enemy behaviour. Some rewards come from trade or a challenge, and attacking too early can remove the peaceful option at that settlement.
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.subtitle: Alex's Mobs, Mowzie's Mobs and Mutant Monsters
codex.chapter.hunt_beasts.title: Beasts and Mutants
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.intro.0: Cataclysm leads through eight major bosses and additional encounters in their structures. Use the special locating eyes, each associated with a structure and dimension. Discovering an arena is not the same as being ready to fight.
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.intro.1: Some enemies awaken through consumed offerings. Prepare the offering, armour, healing, and return route before starting. The final advancement requires personal victories against specific bosses; obtaining another player’s weapons is insufficient.
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.subtitle: Eight dungeons, eight bosses and weapons found nowhere else
codex.chapter.hunt_cataclysm.title: Cataclysm
codex.chapter.ie_chemistry.intro.0: The IE chemical workshop turns crops into oil, ethanol, fuel and plastic. Begin with a steady supply of plants, separate power and labelled fluid lines: similar tanks do not make fluids interchangeable.
codex.chapter.ie_chemistry.intro.1: In this version the refinery needs a catalyst for biodiesel: saltpeter dust. Acetaldehyde takes a silver plate. Catalysts are not consumed, but without the right item the reaction never starts; check the specific recipe page.
codex.chapter.ie_chemistry.subtitle: Plant oil, ethanol, biodiesel and polymers
codex.chapter.ie_chemistry.title: Chemistry and Fuel
codex.chapter.ie_gear.intro.0: Engineer's gear runs on replaceable parts, liquid fuel, ammunition or stored energy. Before an outing, inspect not just the tool but the drill head, the saw blade, the magazine's contents and the battery's charge.
codex.chapter.ie_gear.intro.1: The workbench and the maintenance kit swap supported components. Prepare a safe testing ground for weapons and turrets, and clear boarding and landing points for travelling along wires. A crafted device is not ready for work by itself.
codex.chapter.ie_gear.subtitle: Weapons, tools and armor
codex.chapter.ie_gear.title: Engineer's Gear
codex.chapter.ie_machines.intro.0: IE's big machines are stacked from ordinary materials right in the world and then formed with the engineer's hammer. The ports for energy, items, fluids and redstone sit in fixed places: a connector on a random wall will not start the installation.
codex.chapter.ie_machines.intro.1: This chapter checks the building parts and the operation of the assembled mechanisms, not the finished multiblock item that survival cannot provide. Give every machine its first run on a small batch and leave a free output for by-products.
codex.chapter.ie_machines.subtitle: Crusher, press, arc furnace and excavator
codex.chapter.ie_machines.title: Multiblock Machines
codex.chapter.ie_power.intro.0: The Immersive Engineering grid carries energy through wires strung between connectors. A connector ties the grid to a machine, a relay joins wire segments and a transformer converts one voltage to another. Each of the three blocks has its own job.
codex.chapter.ie_power.intro.1: Rotational generation relies on IE's own water wheels and windmills paired with the kinetic dynamo; a shaft from another mod will not turn that dynamo. For safety, give the wires routes of their own and watch the load in IF/FE per tick.
codex.chapter.ie_power.subtitle: Wires, voltages, generators and transformers
codex.chapter.ie_power.title: Power Grid
codex.chapter.ie_start.intro.0: Immersive Engineering rests on materials, wires and machines assembled in the world from many blocks. The Engineer's Manual shows the layers of each structure and where to strike with the hammer; its diagrams match the installed version and are more reliable than old pictures from the internet.
codex.chapter.ie_start.intro.1: The first steps are coke, creosote, treated wood and steel. The early blast furnace is tended by hand, so leave room for fuel and slag. Electricity will be needed by the next workshop; the first metallurgy manages without FE.
codex.chapter.ie_start.subtitle: Where Immersive Engineering begins
codex.chapter.ie_start.title: Hammer and Coke
codex.chapter.life_furniture.intro.0: A comfortable base remains practical: resting, storing supplies and finding work areas should all be easy. Furniture mods provide different forms and materials, while decorative blocks give a workshop a coherent character.
codex.chapter.life_furniture.intro.1: Test unfamiliar pieces in a small area. Inspect neighbouring connections, opening doors and clear passages. Check power and operating requirements separately for functional furniture.
codex.chapter.life_furniture.intro.2: This chapter does not prescribe one correct style. Its quests teach the tools and help create spaces you enjoy using every day.
codex.chapter.life_furniture.subtitle: Handcrafted, Refurbished Furniture and architectural decor
codex.chapter.life_furniture.title: Furniture and Comfort
codex.chapter.life_world.intro.0: Beyond the workshop walls lies a world worth exploring with a plan rather than at random. A new biome brings materials, a discovered structure becomes a landmark, and a well-thought-out route brings you home with the loot.
codex.chapter.life_world.intro.1: This chapter introduces maps, search compasses and waystones. Learn navigation first, then prepare a short expedition. Distant terrain rendering helps you choose a direction, but it does not make faraway land safe or interactive.
codex.chapter.life_world.intro.2: Optional branches offer field assignments: scout a route, survey a biome and establish a staging post. Manual ticks record checks you have actually performed, rather than merely asking you to read a page.
codex.chapter.life_world.subtitle: Terralith, compasses and distant rendering
codex.chapter.life_world.title: The Pack's World
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.intro.0: Mystical Agriculture grows resources through seeds and essences. Begin with Inferium and Prosperity Shards, then prepare an altar for resource crops. Harvested essence usually needs a separate recipe to become iron or another useful material.
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.intro.1: Yields grow with better soil and accelerators, and harvesting can be left to machines that need looking after. The final quests ask you to gather and process a fresh harvest all over again — old stock in a chest will not help here. The highest tiers demand a large farm and rare resources from dangerous expeditions.
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.subtitle: Six essence tiers and a field instead of a mine
codex.chapter.magic_agriculture.title: Mystical Agriculture
codex.chapter.magic_ars.intro.0: Ars Nouveau separates personal spell mana from Source used by devices. Your book stores composed spells, while Source Jars supply the workshop and helpers. Sourceberries support a beginner but do not merge these two reserves.
codex.chapter.magic_ars.intro.1: First come the imbuement chamber and the novice’s book; then glyph inscription, Source transfer and the enchanting apparatus. Portals and rituals are started in different ways. The supply check at the end of the chapter asks you to watch Source being spent and recovered beside a working consumer.
codex.chapter.magic_ars.subtitle: Source, glyphs and spells you write yourself
codex.chapter.magic_ars.title: Ars Nouveau
codex.chapter.magic_botania.intro.0: Petals make your first flowers, the Pure Daisy supplies construction materials, and the Endoflame turns fuel into mana. Build this chain near your base with room to expand.
codex.chapter.magic_botania.intro.1: Separate generation, transport, and storage: a generating flower binds to a spreader, which fires into a pool. The pool produces nothing by itself. The final quests check that reserves recover after actual consumption.
codex.chapter.magic_botania.subtitle: Botania: where flower magic begins
codex.chapter.magic_botania.title: Petals and Mana
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.intro.0: Alfheim unlocks item trading, improved materials, and Corporea. This is a trading portal, and players cannot walk into the elven world. Activation and trading require mana reserves in two pools.
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.intro.1: Gaia trials need a prepared arena and a consumed summoning item. Establish supplies and equipment before challenging the ordinary Guardian. Relics and rank SS are long-term goals after reliable production.
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.subtitle: Elves, relics and the end of the flower road
codex.chapter.magic_botania_end.title: Alfheim and the Gaia Guardian
The Runic Altar connects basic mana materials with functional flowers, accessories, and Terrasteel. Prepare a dedicated supply line and spare Livingrock: completed rune recipes require a manual finishing step.

Terrasteel costs half a normal pool per ingot. Expand production before an expensive attempt, rather than after losing an unfinished batch. This equipment supports safer exploration and prepares you for elven trading.
codex.chapter.magic_botania_runes.subtit: The second circle: altar, runes, harder flowers
codex.chapter.magic_botania_runes.title: Runes and Terrasteel
codex.chapter.magic_irons.intro.0: Iron’s Spells uses found and crafted scrolls, inscribed into a book for repeated casting. Begin with an accessible Copper Spell Book and Inscription Table. The Ruined Book in the first card belongs to a later Ancient City expedition and is unnecessary for your first spell.
codex.chapter.magic_irons.intro.1: The Inscription Table, Scroll Forge, and Arcane Anvil perform different operations. Magical clothing expands your capabilities, while rare runes and orbs improve specialisation. The Dead King’s staff requires a separate serious battle in the catacombs.
codex.chapter.magic_irons.subtitle: Eight schools of magic and the battle mage's road
codex.chapter.magic_irons.title: Iron's Spellbooks
codex.chapter.mc_build.intro.0: Structurize selects, measures and saves blueprints; Domum Ornamentum turns chosen materials into decorative shapes. These tools help prepare projects but do not cancel the cost of construction or the citizens' labour.
codex.chapter.mc_build.intro.1: Try a small detail on free ground first. Block shape, fill material and orientation are three separate parameters: what looks right from afar may not suit the builder.
codex.chapter.mc_build.subtitle: Structurize, Domum Ornamentum and Multi-Piston
codex.chapter.mc_build.title: Construction and Styles
codex.chapter.mc_found.intro.0: A colony grows through citizens, construction orders and material deliveries. A hut block only marks the spot: the building itself is raised by an assigned builder after an order in the build window. Start with level ground, a food reserve and housing.
codex.chapter.mc_found.intro.1: The Codex remembers item objectives one after another: a hut once shown can be placed at once, and there is no need to dismantle a finished house to show it again. Judge the citizens' work by their requests and by what appears in the world, not by a line in a list.
codex.chapter.mc_found.subtitle: Town hall, builder and first citizens
codex.chapter.mc_found.title: Founding a Colony
codex.chapter.mc_military.intro.0: A colony's defence begins not with a sword but with roads, light and supplied guards. A tower without a fighter protects no one, and barracks will not replace weapons, food and training.
codex.chapter.mc_military.intro.1: Plan the defence before the raid and leave citizens a path to their homes and to help. A rare trophy is a possible outcome of a fight, not a reward owed for every repelled attack.
codex.chapter.mc_military.subtitle: Guards, barracks and repelling raids
codex.chapter.mc_military.title: Defense
codex.chapter.mc_production.intro.0: Production professions live on three things: resources, tools and the colony's requests. A felled log will not turn into a plank by itself, and a warehouse will not teach the blacksmith an unfamiliar recipe. Keep in mind who gathers, who crafts and who carries, and you will see where everything stalled.
codex.chapter.mc_production.intro.1: Let the first be a short chain for one building material. Once the first delivery has arrived, add professions and research. A few empty buildings add duties but do not yet make an economy.
codex.chapter.mc_production.subtitle: From forest and mine to smithy and glassblower
codex.chapter.mc_production.title: Colony Production
codex.chapter.mc_research.intro.0: Citizens' schooling and university science are different things. The library raises adults, the school prepares children, the university opens technologies to the settlement. Each needs an assigned citizen, a suitable building and a chosen activity.
codex.chapter.mc_research.intro.1: Read a research's conditions before paying: the university level, earlier discoveries and required buildings decide whether the button opens. The quest log adds the citizens' stories to science but does not replace the research tree.
codex.chapter.mc_research.subtitle: University, school, library and research
codex.chapter.mc_research.title: Science and Growth
codex.chapter.mek_gear.intro.0: Mekanism gear needs more than crafting: it runs on energy, chemical fuel or installed modules. Try every new tool on safe ground before an expedition; an empty charge or the wrong mode is easily mistaken for a fault.
codex.chapter.mek_gear.intro.1: The MekaSuit and Meka-Tool are tailored to the task at the modification station. Modules work only with compatible items, and flight and radiation shielding call for their own test even when every part is already in your inventory.
codex.chapter.mek_gear.subtitle: Power armor, modules and the Meka-Tool
codex.chapter.mek_gear.title: MekaSuit
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.intro.0: The nuclear branch begins with chemical fuel and cooling prepared in advance. Before the first fissile fuel goes in, steam removal, waste intake, temperature readings and a tested emergency stop must all be working. Reactor casings in a chest answer for none of those conditions.
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.intro.1: Radioactive chemicals cannot be handled like a tank of water. Keep the site away from your living quarters, wear the full protective kit and never dismantle filled pipes. The fusion branch has a fuel chain and a launch procedure of its own.
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.subtitle: Uranium, fission reactor, waste and radiation
codex.chapter.mek_nuclear.title: Nuclear Power
codex.chapter.mek_ore.intro.0: Ore processing raises your metal yield, but you pay for it in energy, machines and chemicals. The ×2–×5 labels apply to ore blocks; raw iron follows its own ratios. Choose the chain that fits the way you mine, and test it on a small batch you can count by hand.
codex.chapter.mek_ore.intro.1: Each new stage is added in front of the machines you already know. Keep the simple line running while you set up oxygen, brine and acids: chemistry needs room for by-products and pipes of its own.
codex.chapter.mek_ore.subtitle: From doubling to fivefold yield
codex.chapter.mek_ore.title: Ore Processing
codex.chapter.mek_power.intro.0: A dependable power system has three parts: a source, transmission and storage. Start with a generator for a few machines and measure the load under real work. An empty battery does not always mean a weak generator; sometimes the energy simply is not leaving through the right side.
codex.chapter.mek_power.intro.1: Steam power demands attention to water and steam removal. Assembled casings only prove you have materials; output and stability come from the whole installation, its settings and the world you play in.
codex.chapter.mek_power.subtitle: From heat generator to steam turbine
codex.chapter.mek_power.title: Power Generation
codex.chapter.mek_qio.intro.0: Quantum devices do away with long transport lines, yet they still depend on frequency, access rights and chunk loading. Test a pair side by side first: a configuration mistake shows itself before you build the remote site.
codex.chapter.mek_qio.intro.1: QIO stores items on drives and opens access to them through a chosen frequency. Teleporters move the player; quantum entangloporters carry supported resources. These are separate subsystems, each with rules of its own.
codex.chapter.mek_qio.subtitle: Quantum storage and instant travel
codex.chapter.mek_qio.title: QIO and Teleportation
codex.chapter.mek_start.intro.0: Mekanism begins with electricity and a handful of materials you will make again and again: osmium, steel, circuits and alloys. Build a small workshop first, one where you can see what goes into every machine and what comes out. A clear layout is easy to scale up into a factory; hunting for a mistake among a hundred pipes is not.
codex.chapter.mek_start.intro.1: Energy, items, fluids and chemicals travel through different networks. This chapter teaches you to tell them apart and to configure machine sides. A casing or a cable in your inventory only proves you have parts; whether the line works is a separate experiment.
codex.chapter.mek_start.subtitle: Metallurgic infuser, steel and steel casing
codex.chapter.mek_start.title: Osmium and First Machines
codex.chapter.missiles.intro.0: The missile add-on builds a guided physical craft from an engine, fins, a computer and a launch mount. The parts must belong to one construct and be linked together; a single block’s recipe does not describe a finished missile.
codex.chapter.missiles.intro.1: Check the bindings and the hold first, without a warhead. Test thrust and the fuze on a separate range, once Aeronautics physics assembly is familiar.
codex.chapter.missiles.subtitle: CBC Aeronautics Missiles: guided rocket weapons
codex.chapter.missiles.title: Missiles
codex.chapter.more_et_side.intro.0: The Eternal Tales side goals are collections, transformations, events and odd trials. An advancement’s name does not always describe the check: sometimes an item is needed, sometimes a worn set, sometimes waiting for an event to end.
codex.chapter.more_et_side.intro.1: Read the action at each goal and prepare a safe place for in-game effects. Collections are easiest kept as a list, and explosions or dangerous food are tried well away from the colony and valuable luggage.
codex.chapter.more_et_side.subtitle: What in Eternal Tales doesn't lead to Unahzaal but is worth the time
codex.chapter.more_et_side.title: Side Paths
codex.chapter.more_explore.intro.0: The atlas leads to specific biomes, not to landscapes that merely look alike. Most of the chapter is Terralith in the Overworld; the last three destinations belong to Eternal Tales. Nature’s Compass searches for the chosen biome in the current dimension.
codex.chapter.more_explore.intro.1: Write down coordinates of a safe approach and check the place name on screen or in F3. Flying high over a pretty spot and visiting the biome are not the same: the borders count where your character stands.
codex.chapter.more_explore.subtitle: Biomes of Terralith and other worlds
codex.chapter.more_explore.title: Atlas
codex.chapter.more_home.intro.0: Home is a working workshop, a convenient kitchen and a place to rest. Take furniture from mods that are actually installed and keep the paths to chests and machines open, so beauty does not get in the way of play.
codex.chapter.more_home.intro.1: The Furnicraft archive in the mods folder does not mean a loaded pack. These quests rely on Handcrafted, Refurbished Furniture, Domum Ornamentum and other items of the pack; nothing extra needs enabling.
codex.chapter.more_home.subtitle: Comfort as a discipline of its own
codex.chapter.more_home.title: Home
codex.chapter.more_kitchen.intro.0: Here are real dishes of several cuisines, not a list of edible names. Farmer’s Delight cooks in a pot over a fire, on the crafting table and on the cutting board; MineColonies specialities are cooked by colony citizens.
codex.chapter.more_kitchen.intro.1: Turn-in goals take the food as a contribution. Keep a separate stock for the book and feed yourself and the colony from another: a dish on the table or a portion already eaten is not in your inventory.
codex.chapter.more_kitchen.subtitle: Farmer's Delight, the MineColonies kitchen and Eternal Tales food
codex.chapter.more_kitchen.title: Cookbook
codex.chapter.more_munitions.intro.0: The arsenal accepts batches of Create Big Cannons ammunition. Most goals are turn-ins: the stock disappears, so supply your own battery separately.
codex.chapter.more_munitions.intro.1: Shells are not tested in a residential quarter. A training shot needs a prepared range, a suitable gun, the right propellant and an understanding of what the shell will do; a calibre that looks right guarantees no compatibility.
codex.chapter.more_munitions.subtitle: Munitions, fuzes and battery supply
codex.chapter.more_munitions.title: Arsenal
codex.chapter.more_qol2.intro.0: The pack’s conveniences help you find places, build, store loot and understand items. Each device has its own job: the structure compass finds no biomes, and the trash can destroys cargo rather than extending storage.
codex.chapter.more_qol2.intro.1: Try a new tool on a small, clear example. Check energy, materials, filters and undo before working on an expensive build: a menu entry proves no safe setup.
codex.chapter.more_qol2.subtitle: Gadgets, hammers, bins and everything else that saves hours
codex.chapter.more_qol2.title: New Conveniences
codex.chapter.more_rails.intro.0: The depot serves real Create trains and the Steam ’n’ Rails extensions. A decorative boiler gives the locomotive its look, while an assembled train with bogeys, controls and a route does the pulling.
codex.chapter.more_rails.intro.1: Test coupling, signals and supply on a short stretch before letting the train onto the main line. Turned-in fittings vanish; keep equipment for the working railway separate.
codex.chapter.more_rails.subtitle: Steam 'n' Rails in all its glory
codex.chapter.more_rails.title: Depot
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.intro.0: Beneath a hundred mods lives the same game: enchanting, trading, the beacon and elytra are still here and still decide a lot. This chapter secures them once the first resources are in.
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.intro.1: Counted goals ask for the stated stock of one item at once, while different items are remembered one after another. Before an expensive recipe, tell the item itself from its working setup and from the consumables it is useless without.
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.subtitle: Vanilla progression the pack won't let you forget
codex.chapter.more_vanilla.title: Old Roads
codex.chapter.offroad.intro.0: Offroad adds wheels and boring rigs for ground-based physical machines. Hubs hold the tyres, rotation drives them, and redstone signals steer and brake. The body is assembled with Simulated.
codex.chapter.offroad.intro.1: Run a small vehicle on flat ground before attacking slopes and tunnels. A boring rig needs more than cutting wheels: room for the spoil and a convenient way to unload.
codex.chapter.offroad.subtitle: Wheels, suspension and all-terrain
codex.chapter.offroad.title: Create Offroad: Ground Vehicles
codex.chapter.radar.intro.0: A radar network is four jobs: detect, relay, choose a target, aim the weapon. Begin with a monitor and an empty mount, make sure you understand the marks and bearings, and only then connect fire.
codex.chapter.radar.intro.1: Identification lives in codes and filters. A transponder or a warning receiver by itself does not make your craft invisible to someone else’s battery.
codex.chapter.radar.subtitle: Detection, air defense and automatic aiming
codex.chapter.radar.title: Create Radar: Targeting
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.intro.0: Autocrafting executes recorded patterns. The network assembles an ordinary recipe itself, but external processing it only starts: it hands out the raw material and waits for the finished item to come back. Until the expected result arrives, the order hangs. Start with one simple recipe and one furnace.
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.intro.1: Keep three separate things in mind: the crafting pattern, the processing pattern and the physical route items take between machines. The monitor shows what the network is waiting for, and a small trial batch tells you exactly which link stopped.
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.subtitle: Patterns, autocrafters and production chains
codex.chapter.rs_autocraft.title: Refined Storage: Autocrafting
codex.chapter.rs_network.intro.0: Refined Storage turns a dozen scattered chests into a single searchable list. The controller gives the network power, disks and connected containers give it space, and the grid is the window through which you insert and take things out. Build the first network on cheap items and leave your usual storeroom untouched for now.
codex.chapter.rs_network.intro.1: Devices on the floor are not yet a network. Before moving valuable stock, make sure there is power and connection, that items survive a restart and that there is room to spare. In the installed second version of Refined Storage, some old rules from other guides no longer apply.
codex.chapter.rs_network.subtitle: Controller, cables, disks and grids
codex.chapter.rs_network.title: Refined Storage: Network
codex.chapter.space_glacio.intro.0: Glacio is in the Proxima Centauri system and requires the fourth rocket tier. Its atmosphere contains oxygen, unlike the Moon and Mars. Cold, terrain and distance from home still require a prepared expedition.
codex.chapter.space_glacio.intro.1: The final map node consumes equipment as a colony contribution. Do not submit the base’s last working devices: separate the donated batch from equipment supporting actual survival and return.
codex.chapter.space_glacio.subtitle: Glacio — the end of the road and the start of a colony
codex.chapter.space_glacio.title: Proxima Centauri
codex.chapter.space_ground.intro.0: The first Ad Astra flight begins with metallurgy, fuel and breathing reserves. Establish electricity, a compressor, steel production and an oxygen loader before crafting the rocket. A rocket carries a prepared expedition rather than replacing preparation.
codex.chapter.space_ground.intro.1: Returning requires a launch pad and separate fuel. Many equipment advancements trigger on obtaining items; launch readiness is checked manually after filling the suit and packing the return kit.
codex.chapter.space_ground.subtitle: Steel, oxygen, fuel and the first rocket
codex.chapter.space_ground.title: Launch Table
codex.chapter.space_hot.intro.0: Venus and Mercury require protection against high temperature and missing oxygen. Wear a complete suitable suit and prepare the return before departure; a tier-three rocket provides transport, not surface protection.
codex.chapter.space_hot.intro.1: Calorite opens this branch’s final transport and flight equipment. Mine it through short prepared outings while preserving breathing reserves and a safe landing site rather than moving the entire base into unfamiliar conditions in one trip.
codex.chapter.space_hot.subtitle: Venus, Mercury and calorite
codex.chapter.space_hot.title: The Hot Planets
codex.chapter.space_mars.intro.0: Mars opens ostrum and more convenient expedition supplies. Arrive with oxygen and a return kit already prepared; new ore supports progression but should not be required to get home.
codex.chapter.space_mars.intro.1: Cryo fuel reduces carried fuel volume, while the energizer services electric equipment. Hot planets require a complete netherite spacesuit and tier-three rocket, so reserve part of the Martian yield for both.
codex.chapter.space_mars.subtitle: Ostrum, cryo fuel and a real colony
codex.chapter.space_mars.title: Mars
codex.chapter.space_moon.intro.0: On the Moon, first secure the return kit and search for desh. Stay near the lander until rocket, pad and fuel are recovered. Lower gravity helps movement but does not replace oxygen reserves.
codex.chapter.space_moon.intro.1: A permanent outpost needs electricity and a sealed room. The oxygen distributor, ventilation and solid cable passages work together; a crafted distributor does not make an open lunar site safe.
codex.chapter.space_moon.subtitle: First step, desh and life under a dome
codex.chapter.space_moon.title: The Moon
codex.chapter.start_first_day.intro.0: Your first day establishes a reliable place to live. Gather wood, make tools and light, then choose a site you can easily return to. A large factory can wait until you have food, shelter and an orderly place for supplies.
codex.chapter.start_first_day.intro.1: This chapter introduces the pack’s carrying tools, backpack, tooltips and map. Learn them with inexpensive items and inspect the result immediately. These conveniences change familiar controls without removing the dangers of night or distant journeys.
codex.chapter.start_first_day.intro.2: Optional quests help prepare a workshop, organise reserves and choose a direction. Item goals use your inventory; confirm manual objectives after carrying out the described check.
codex.chapter.start_first_day.subtitle: Where the pack begins and what not to rush into
codex.chapter.start_first_day.title: First Day
codex.chapter.start_qol.intro.0: The pack’s conveniences save time once you understand their rules. Recipe search helps plan production, sorting clears storage and tooltips explain an unfamiliar block before you dismantle it.
codex.chapter.start_qol.intro.1: Master JEI and your own controls first. Try the other tools as the need arises: the building gadget once builds start repeating, the chunk loader once equipment has to run far from you. You will not need them on the first evening.
codex.chapter.start_qol.intro.2: Reference pages are marked manually. Read their limits and run the suggested small check; that is more useful than immediately enabling every available feature.
codex.chapter.start_qol.subtitle: Mods that add nothing to progression but change everything
codex.chapter.start_qol.title: Pack Conveniences
codex.chapter.storage_local.intro.0: Local storage is needed before the digital network and stays convenient after it. A backpack carries tools on an expedition, a Mekanism bin holds a mountain of one resource, and the Create vault takes the flow from a production line. Choose by the task, not by the name.
codex.chapter.storage_local.intro.1: Test automatic modules on cheap items. Be especially careful with deletion: whatever vanished through the void module will not come back, even if you disable the filter afterwards.
codex.chapter.storage_local.subtitle: Backpacks, chests and everything that needs no network
codex.chapter.storage_local.title: Local Storage
codex.chapter.story_colony.intro.0: A colony grows from its first workplaces to supply, schooling, industry and a garrison. A hut block is only an application: the builder raises the building from requested materials, and the work is done by an assigned, well-fed citizen.
codex.chapter.story_colony.intro.1: The book remembers blocks it has seen, so once registered they can be placed. Watch the citizens’ requests and the real delivery routes: a dozen stockpiled huts will not turn into a town on their own.
codex.chapter.story_colony.subtitle: The colony from four citizens to a technopolis
codex.chapter.story_colony.title: A City That Grows Itself
codex.chapter.story_current.intro.0: The electrical line ties fuel, steel, generators and consumers from different mods into a single grid. Start with one clear source and one load, then grow: a bigger generator will not save you from mismatched connectors and a blocked output.
codex.chapter.story_current.intro.1: Quest titles describe parts, not power; whether a plant really works is visible only in the world. Emergency shutdown, cooling and waste deserve special attention — without them, nuclear energy is best left alone.
codex.chapter.story_current.subtitle: Three factories — one power grid
codex.chapter.story_current.title: Current
codex.chapter.story_expedition.intro.0: The expedition line links several independent adventures into one route across worlds. The book’s cards lead from stage to stage, but portals, story conditions, protected areas and personal advancements stay in the hands of each mod.
codex.chapter.story_expedition.intro.1: Before every crossing, prepare the way back and a place for trophies. Where an advancement is granted for an item, take it into your own inventory first; where an event is required, a single visit to the dimension is not enough.
codex.chapter.story_expedition.subtitle: Through every world, in the order they open
codex.chapter.story_expedition.title: Expedition
codex.chapter.story_forge.intro.0: The engineer’s road strings familiar Create machines into one freight route: a source of rotation, ore processing, a steam boiler and a train running between the base and the mine. Build in small sections that work on their own, and join them only once each has been tested.
codex.chapter.story_forge.intro.1: Wind and water are equal entrances to this line, and so are the millstone and the crushing wheels. Ordinary items are remembered the moment they first appear in your inventory, so they can go straight into service; batches for turn-in must be in your bag in full at the moment of turn-in and vanish with the reward.
codex.chapter.story_forge.subtitle: From the first alloy to a train that hauls ore by itself
codex.chapter.story_forge.title: The Engineer's Road
codex.chapter.story_sky.intro.0: The air project brings together a physics construct, observation, weapons and supply. Test lift and control on a small moored platform first, then add equipment and repeat the trial at the new mass.
codex.chapter.story_sky.intro.1: A radar contact is not permission to fire, and a crate of parts is not a ship. Set up identification and a safe sector before loading ammunition, and after every change make a test flight without a shot.
codex.chapter.story_sky.subtitle: Air fleet, artillery and radar — one defense
codex.chapter.story_sky.title: Sky and Powder
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.intro.0: Industrial Foregoing automates resource gathering and farm upkeep with machines that have an adjustable working area. Before every start, display that area and check where the face points: standing next to a field does not yet mean the machine is set up correctly.
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.intro.1: Plastic opens the first casings; later tiers require the dissolution chamber and special fluids. By-products of farming and meat processes need outputs of their own, or a perfectly good machine will stop with a full internal tank.
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.subtitle: Latex, lasers and farms that run themselves
codex.chapter.tech2_foregoing.title: Industrial Foregoing
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.intro.0: Mekanism Tools adds ordinary tools and armour from other materials. They wear like any gear and need no charging, unlike the atomic disassembler. Choose the material by the resources at hand and by the task.
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.intro.1: The paxel combines several tools, shields give separate protection, refined materials require Mekanism machines. This chapter's advancements mostly respond to obtaining items; no dangerous fight is required.
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.subtitle: Six materials that beat netherite
codex.chapter.tech2_mektools.title: Mekanism Tools
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.intro.0: Create: New Age links mechanical rotation, electricity and heat. The coil turns rotation into energy, the motor does the reverse, and the heat engine draws rotation from heat. Each conversion has its own cost and its own limits.
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.intro.1: Start with a small generator and a familiar load. The reactor branch needs a complete shell and constant heat removal; it works differently from Mekanism, and another mod's cooling scheme cannot be carried over just because the word "reactor" matches.
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.subtitle: Electricity, heat and a nuclear reactor for Create
codex.chapter.tech2_newage.title: Create: New Age
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.intro.0: Immersive Petroleum adds underground fluid reservoirs and a drilling system of its own. Seismic surveying reveals deposits, the derrick opens the well, and the pumpjack works a finished wellhead once the reservoir pressure has dropped. A pump over a random chunk yields no oil.
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.intro.1: Distillation yields several fluids plus bitumen, and each needs its own receiver. In the installed version the tower's direct diesel product contains sulfur; clean fuel comes from further processing, so watch the exact fluid names.
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.subtitle: Oil, wells and what's distilled from them
codex.chapter.tech2_petroleum.title: Immersive Petroleum
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.intro.0: PneumaticCraft runs on compressed air rather than an electrical grid. The compressor fills the system's volume, machines consume the air, and pressure equalises between connected blocks. An open pipe end is a leak; exceeding the allowed pressure is an explosion.
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.intro.1: Make the first line short, with a manometer and a controlled cut-off. Heat serves separate chemical processes and is no substitute for pressure; plastic, circuit boards and drones will gradually add new ways of producing things.
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.subtitle: Pressure, plastic and drones you program yourself
codex.chapter.tech2_pneumatic.title: PneumaticCraft
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.intro.0: Powah offers FE sources, batteries and wireless transfer with successive material tiers. Start with one generator and a clear load; a high-tier cable creates no energy, and a big cell only stores what has already been produced.
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.intro.1: Special material processing happens in the energizing orb through separate rods. The reactor is assembled from a large set of same-tier blocks and fed uraninite; one reactor block is no power station yet.
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.subtitle: Energy without complications: generators, cells, reactor
codex.chapter.tech2_powah.title: Powah
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.intro.0: Here the book reads player advancements rather than removing loot. Conditions vary: some record combat, others trophy acquisition, while the garrison trial counts colony soldiers.
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.intro.1: Follow each objective’s action description. Claiming a reward does not replace local progression, preparation for a dangerous dimension or checking your own advancement in multiplayer.
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.subtitle: Boss victories the book can notice
codex.chapter.trials_bosses.title: Trials: Trophies
codex.chapter.trials_early.intro.0: Early deliveries teach you to separate operating reserves from goods for exchange. Every consumable objective requires its entire listed batch in your inventory now; turning it in removes the items. A nearby chest does not count.
codex.chapter.trials_early.intro.1: Secure tools, food and planting stock first, then prepare a surplus. Rewards pay for the delivery, not a particular production method: inspect their contents and leave inventory space.
codex.chapter.trials_early.subtitle: Turn in resources — get what speeds the start
codex.chapter.trials_early.title: Trials: First Days
codex.chapter.trials_late.intro.0: Late deliveries use products from long production chains. Fund them from a stable surplus: reactor operation, storage construction and transport maintenance take priority over an immediate reward.
codex.chapter.trials_late.intro.1: The book removes all marked resources. The archive trial accepts storage components that cannot contain your belongings; active network disks are excluded from the delivery.
codex.chapter.trials_late.subtitle: Turning in rare materials at the pack's peak
codex.chapter.trials_late.title: Trials: High Technology
codex.chapter.trials_mid.intro.0: Industrial trials ask whether you can spare finished goods without stopping your own factory. Exact mod items matter here, beyond similar names or recipe compatibility.
codex.chapter.trials_mid.intro.1: Several consumable objectives are handed in together, so prepare every kind and quantity in advance. Finished parts in a chest say nothing yet about how the line runs; the side quests invite you to test supply, output and recovery after a stop separately.
codex.chapter.trials_mid.subtitle: Machine output in exchange for machines
codex.chapter.trials_mid.title: Trials: Factory Hum
codex.hint.none: Not found in this pack’s recipes or loot tables — check JEI
codex.msg.not_enough: Codex: not enough items to turn in
codex.quest.aero_basics.airship.text.0: The Steam Vent feeds steam into the balloon and lifts the craft; it is no relief valve. Like a steam engine it needs heat, water and boiler volume. Take the item from the goal and a small airship with an airtight envelope.
codex.quest.aero_basics.airship.text.1: In a steam layout the vent sits by the boiler and fills the balloon above it. Set maximum feed and the signal. The first craft can be lifted with the burner you already know, with the steam system added later as a second way up.
codex.quest.aero_basics.airship.text.2: Check the balance and your ability to shed lift at low altitude. Cutting thrust does not kill inertia at once. Before flying, prepare a return pad, accessible controls and a stock of consumables.
codex.quest.aero_basics.airship.title: First Airship
codex.quest.aero_basics.assembler.text.0: The physics assembler creates a construct that lives by the rules of mass and motion while staying built from your blocks. Take it and a few cheap blocks on flat ground; no engine or balloon yet, so assembly stays separate from flight.
codex.quest.aero_basics.assembler.text.1: Mark the group with super glue or honey glue, then hold interact and pull the assembler’s lever as Ponder shows. Check the bounds: blocks along diagonal edges may join too. The ground, a neighbouring warehouse and the pad’s support must stay out.
codex.quest.aero_basics.assembler.text.2: Inspect the makeup and stability of the resulting hull. Any suitable assembler can disassemble it, so you need not carry the original block inside every machine. Detached parts become independent objects, so make sure the hull is connected before building on. This skill serves the airship, the wheeled vehicle and the rocket rig.
codex.quest.aero_basics.assembler.title: Physics Assembler
codex.quest.aero_basics.burner_aero.text: The adjustable burner fills the balloon with hot air. It is a separate aviation block with its own settings, not a blaze burner under a basin. You need the burner and a proven airtight envelope above a light construct.

Place the source so the balloon sits above it. Set maximum feed on the panel and regulate the output share with redstone signal strength. Start low and watch the balloon fill; there will be no instant lift-off.

Lift is limited by the envelope’s volume and weakens with altitude. If the craft will not climb, check mass, airtightness and settings rather than cranking the signal. Test dropping lift near the ground before the first flight; combine several sources only once you understand one.
codex.quest.aero_basics.docking.text.0: Docking couplers connect in pairs and hold two sides rigidly while leaving them separate constructs. One coupler makes no dock. Prepare the counterpart, and for a rope link, compatible connectors or a winch with the right coupling.
codex.quest.aero_basics.docking.text.1: Extend the units and align them carefully. Once aligned closely enough they lock; a comparator reads the progress. Moving items or fluid needs feed and extraction on both sides, not just the lock.
codex.quest.aero_basics.docking.text.2: They part when one coupler retracts. Before that, make sure the craft can hold position on its own. Ropes attach a different way, and two winches do not pair with each other. Test mooring without cargo or sharp thrust, then add supply and a pad around a connection that actually works.
codex.quest.aero_basics.docking.title: Docking and Mooring
codex.quest.aero_basics.engine.text.0: The portable engine provides on-board rotation by burning fuel. The engine assembly part is made by running an iron sheet through cutting and pressing eight times in a row, and the result is probabilistic. Prepare a stock of blanks and an outlet for by-products.
codex.quest.aero_basics.engine.text.1: Build the black engine by its recipe and run it on the ground with one machine. Load suitable fuel, choose the rotation direction and check the output. Blaze cake enables a boosted mode but is not needed for the first check.
codex.quest.aero_basics.engine.text.2: On the craft, make sure the source, the drive and the fuel stock belong to one construct. An on-board engine cancels neither consumption nor stress. Test stop and restart before take-off: run out of fuel far from the pad and the very props you steer with will stop.
codex.quest.aero_basics.engine.title: Portable Engine
codex.quest.aero_basics.envelope.text.0: The envelope encloses the volume that lifts the craft when filled with hot air or steam. Sixteen white blocks are a starting stock, not a ready balloon for any cargo. Make a light gondola and lay out a closed envelope above it.
codex.quest.aero_basics.envelope.text.1: The walls must be airtight, with as much empty space inside as possible. The source fills the balloon from the top down; a hole or an improper shaft passage lets the air out. Shafts are enclosed in envelope blocks the intended way.
codex.quest.aero_basics.envelope.text.2: Solid blocks inside steal volume: a sphere stuffed with wood is not an empty one. Check airtightness before adding heat and cargo. Dye changes colour, not size. Once assembled, the envelope with a burner or steam becomes the lift system.
codex.quest.aero_basics.envelope.title: Airship Envelope
codex.quest.aero_basics.flight_service_b: A compass helps with orientation, but the ordinary one points at the world spawn, not your airfield. Take the item from the goal and note the pad’s coordinates separately; a suitable binding works for the right destination if you already have one.
Set a visible landmark by the landing zone and choose a short route from which the pad is still in sight. Check the compass bearing on the ground so you do not discover its real meaning in the air.

The “batch” in the title refers to the navigation item, not to airship production. Before the flight, check remaining fuel, lift control and the way back. The next quest is take-off, a turn, a landing and a check of behaviour with cargo.
codex.quest.aero_basics.flight_service_r: Manually take off, turn, return to the original pad, and check loaded behavior and thrust shutdown

The final test is a full short control cycle. Choose a quiet pad, remove valuable cargo and prepare a small known load for the second part of the check. Before starting, inspect the fastenings and the fuel stock.

Take off, turn and return to the starting pad. Check behaviour with cargo and the thrust shutdown before any long flight. Remember inertia: cancelling the movement command does not stop the hull at once.

Tick the goal after the test in the world. If the cargo causes a roll or eats altitude, fix placement and lift and repeat the short trial. Until a successful return, do not increase distance and mass together; plan long routes with resources to spare for the way back.
codex.quest.aero_basics.flight_service_s: A test pad is needed before the first flight with valuable cargo. The two leads in the goal are a preparatory stock; an ordinary lead will not tether a physical ship. Mooring uses compatible ropes or docking couplers.

Pick a clear spot by the base, mark the starting position and clear a wide landing zone. Check the light hull, access to controls and the ability to shed lift. Keep a spare path to the pad in case the craft sets down nearby.

Switch the systems on one at a time: lift, horizontal thrust, then course correction. Make sure take-off clears trees and wires. Cargo goes on after the controls are proven, not as ballast for an unstable construct nobody understands yet.
codex.quest.aero_basics.goggles_aero.tex: Aviator goggles show flight data that is hard to read off the horizon by eye. Make them and wear them in a supported slot. Try them first on a familiar craft by the pad, not on a long flight.

Look at the readings while parked and during slight movement. Compare altitude and position changes with landmarks in the world. Which data appears depends on the construct and the installed version’s interface.

The goggles are no autopilot and no protection from falling; they only help you see. If an expected reading is missing, check your equipment and the state of the assembly. Learn where the information sits before the first flight with cargo, and keep the return point’s coordinates: instruments choose no landing pad.
codex.quest.aero_basics.guide_loaded_doc: Manually complete a short freight flight, dock, and transfer the full batch into stationary storage without disassembly or hand-carrying

An air-freight journey ends with reliable docking and unloading, not merely flying over the base. Prepare a small known load, a tested dock and free stationary storage. Distribute mass evenly while retaining control access.

Make a short flight, return and align connectors gently. Wait for locking, then transfer cargo through configured insertion and extraction on both sides. Check the final chest quantity and connection stability during unloading.

Tick the goal after a full cycle without dismantling the ship or carrying cargo by hand. A craft relieved of its mass answers the old lift differently, so check the mode before undocking. This trial ties aviation to real supply and shows where fuel reserves and a convenient working passage are needed.
Return to the Dock with Cargo
codex.quest.aero_basics.guide_sensor_sig: Manually verify altitude and both tilt-axis signal directions on a ground rig before connecting thrust

A sensor can amplify an error if its signal controls an actuator in the wrong sense. Prepare altitude and gimbal sensors, lamps or visible indicators, and a small ground-based physical construct. Keep thrust disabled.

Change height or tilt slightly and compare output with the desired correction. Check altitude limits and inversion, and each gimbal axis. Record which signal should reduce lift or restore orientation.

Tick the goal once both reactions are clear and the command’s sign matches the actuator. Only then connect limited correction near the ground. If oscillations grow, switch the automation off and go back to checking the sign, not to raising the gain. A correct sensor in a wrong circuit makes no autopilot.
codex.quest.aero_basics.gyro.text.0: The gyroscopic bearing keeps the prop pointing the right way and suits stable layouts. It will not hold a heavy ship still with one item. Take the bearing, the gyroscopic mechanism and a small proven construct.
codex.quest.aero_basics.gyro.text.1: Replace or supplement the ordinary prop unit as Ponder shows. The bearing tries to keep the prop vertical, yet block orientation and mass distribution still matter. A redstone signal resets the tilt, so do not wire it until you know why.
codex.quest.aero_basics.gyro.text.2: First watch the slight roll without cargo, then add equal load on both sides. If it sways, check placement and thrust rather than expecting full stabilisation. The effect changes with altitude. Keep manual correction and a safe descent before trusting stability on a long flight.
codex.quest.aero_basics.gyro.title: Gyroscopes
codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.text.0: Levitite keeps a construct aloft but does not lift it by itself. The blend is cooked in a heated basin from four End stone powder, two zinc nuggets and 500 mB of water, yielding 500 mB. You need a bucket of blend and a place to crystallise.
codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.text.1: Pour the blend into a mould and start crystallisation with heat as Ponder shows. The reaction spreads through the connected volume and breaks some mould blocks. Once started, the liquid cannot be recovered.
