codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.text.2: Get eight blocks and test them on a small construct. It rises only with extra force, and at low speed levitite noticeably resists movement. Expect no “negative mass”; cargo balance and thrust decide the behaviour. Keep the blend away from stray heat.
codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.title: Levitite
The navigation table emits a redstone signal towards a target set by a navigation item. It is no flight schedule and drives no props. Make the table and test it on a stationary pad.

Insert a suitable navigation item and compare outputs on different faces. The signal is weaker on a face that looks past the target; different items set different destinations. Check the chosen place against coordinates before wiring steering.

Automatic flight still needs signal processing, thrust, stability, altitude limits and a way to stop. Start with lamps showing the bearing, then a short controlled turn. Do not send the first craft off unattended: reliable navigation is built on top of proven manual flight and return.
codex.quest.aero_basics.navigation.title: Navigation Table
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.0: A propeller makes thrust when it spins and moves the construct. The ready wooden propeller and the bearing for a built-up prop are two different drives. Make both and watch their scenes; they are installed differently.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.1: For a built-up prop, a construct of at least two sail blocks is assembled in front of the bearing. Feed rotation and see which way the thrust points; reverse it by reversing rotation or with the wrench setting.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.2: Check the engine mount and the prop’s clearance before moving the hull. Thrust changes with altitude and while moving through air, so a ground test promises no equal speed in the sky. Start with a short run and stop near the pad; adjust lift and horizontal travel separately.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.title: Propellers
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.0: Sensors emit signals for your logic, but an autopilot does not assemble itself from them. The altitude sensor responds to height, the gimbal sensor to orientation, the laser sensor to a visible beam. Take the three devices and start with a ground rig and lamps.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.1: On the altitude sensor set the lower and upper bounds and check which way the signal changes. On the gimbal sensor set the angle and test each axis. The laser sensor needs its own beam source: blocks block it and a filter limits the colour.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.2: Compare the outputs with the real position before wiring a burner or steering. Reversed feedback amplifies a roll instead of damping it. Keep manual control and make the first corrections near the ground; once checked, the sensors help hold altitude and approach a dock.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.title: Sensors
codex.quest.ca_electric.accumulator.text: The modular accumulator stores FE between the alternator and its consumers. Recipe: brass casing, capacitors, a copper rod and electrum wire. Take one module and split input and output across different connections so you can see both sides.

Connect the alternator to the input and watch the charge rise. Once some is stored, stop the alternator and start the motor: the reserve should shrink while keeping it running. Modules combine only in the allowed shape, so check expansion against Ponder.

An accumulator smooths interruptions but covers no constant generation deficit. If the charge ends each cycle lower than before, cut consumption or add a source. Do not confuse the module with the obsolete standalone accumulator; real readings show whether charging and discharge work.
The alternator turns Create rotation into FE electricity. Take the alternator and a source with spare power: in this version it needs at least 32 RPM, so a slow waterwheel will need a step-up gear.

Bring in the shaft, check the speed and connect an electrical receiver. Watch output and stress: the faster the alternator spins, the more mechanical power it asks for. Start with one load or a small accumulator.

No power? Check RPM, the direction of the electrical connection and a free receiver. Do not loop the alternator into a motor hoping for a perpetual power station: conversion adds nothing. A stable source will feed the future storage grid and every electrical machine.
codex.quest.ca_electric.alternator.title: Alternator
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.task.3: Manually: the burner with a straw accepts bioethanol and heats the basin
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.0: The straw turns an ordinary blaze burner into a liquid fuel receiver. It is rolled from paper or bamboo. You need a blaze burner, the straw and a bucket of bioethanol; there is no separate “liquid burner” item in the recipes.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.1: Apply the straw to the placed burner and feed bioethanol from a bucket or pipes. The fuel itself is mixed from sugar, ash flour and two biomass, 125 mB per cycle, so a bucket takes several cycles.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.2: The basin above the burner should heat and the liquid should really be accepted. Tick the manual goal once the strawed burner drinks bioethanol and heats the basin. If nothing happens, check the straw, the fuel and the feed in turn.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.title: Liquid Blaze Burner
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.0: Connectors carry FE between wires and compatible blocks. Take four regular connectors, suitable spools and a redstone relay. Build a short line from the alternator to a motor or accumulator, not the whole base at once.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.1: Attach the connectors to the devices and set the modes with a wrench: at the source the connector pulls energy, at the consumer it pushes. Join them with compatible wire. Large connectors and high-current spools have limits of their own.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.2: The relay passes current only with a redstone signal, so an empty receiver is often explained by it. Test the line with the lever on and off. If there is generation but the consumer idles, inspect each end’s mode and the relay: a wire on screen shows no current direction.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.title: Connectors and Cables
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.0: The digital adapter connects ComputerCraft to supported Create devices. On its own it is no display and shows no numbers after placement. Take the adapter and pick a measurable block, a speedometer or a stressometer.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.1: Make sure a compatible computer exists and attach the adapter as a peripheral per the integration’s documentation. Certain instruments, bearings, the piston, pulleys and the speed controller are supported; a neighbouring chest does not join that list by itself.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.2: Read one value and compare it with the goggles tooltip before commanding a moving machine. If you have no computer line yet, set the adapter aside and use the standard Create display.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.title: Digital Adapter
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.0: Electrum goes into electrical parts and heavier wiring. In the Create Addition recipe, a gold and a silver ingot are mixed in a heated basin and give two alloy ingots. Gold and zinc will not substitute.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.1: Take silver from the pack’s metallurgy, gold and a mixer with a burner. Test one pair of ingots, then make eight electrum. If the recipe does not show, confirm in JEI that your silver ingots belong to the required tag.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.2: Part of the alloy is later rolled and pressed for components, so set some aside. The electrum spool serves connections of its own type, not “just faster copper”. The add-on’s amulet charges items; it is not the experience store the old description made it.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.title: Electrum
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_conversion: Manually compare two modes by RPM, generation, demand and charge change, then select a sustainable mode

Two steady operating modes make conversion between Create and FE easier to understand. Prepare an alternator at sufficient speed, a small accumulator and a motor driving one consumer. Keep stress and electrical readings accessible.

Record alternator input RPM and generation, then motor demand at a modest speed. Change only one setting and compare after the system settles. Watch whether stored energy rises or gradually disappears.

Tick the goal after comparing the two modes and choosing the one the source sustains without sagging. If consumption exceeds generation, the accumulator only postpones the stop. Do not feed the motor back into the alternator hoping for a gain. This trial suggests the gearing for a remote machine and keeps you from buying extra infrastructure instead of fixing the balance.
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_reserve.ta: Manually verify a machine runs from storage during generator shutdown and charge rises again after generation resumes
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_reserve.te: An accumulator is useful when its reserve actually covers an ordinary source interruption. Prepare a working alternator on a shaft, a partly charged accumulator module and one controlled consumer. Do not test on an important factory’s only supply.

Stop the alternator’s shaft for a brief known interval and observe falling charge while the machine continues operating. Restore generation and check that the reserve recovers. If charge does not rise, inspect connection directions and generation balance.

Tick the goal after both observations and note the length of the tested pause: the word “accumulator” does not mean a whole night’s reserve. Added consumers? Reassess, the old capacity may no longer suffice. For a moving machine, count the time between dockings and the energy needed to get back separately.
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_reserve.ti: A Reserve for a Brief Outage
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.0: The electric motor turns FE back into rotation and suits places where a long shaft is awkward. You need the motor and a grid with enough output or charge in an accumulator.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.1: Connect power and set the speed on the rear panel. Start at low RPM, run the shaft to one machine and watch consumption. Higher speed means higher draw, so raise it only after steady operation.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.2: An ordinary Create train needs no motor; it runs by its own rules. This quest checks rotation from electricity. If the machine stands still, check FE stock, wiring, the chosen speed and the output network’s stress in turn; a drained accumulator is not fixed with a new cogwheel.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.title: Electric Motor
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.0: The portable energy interface transfers FE between a contraption’s accumulators and the stationary grid; a direct wire to a moving accumulator is no substitute. The goal asks for one interface, but they work in pairs, one on the machine and one at the base.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.1: Place the working faces opposite each other with a gap of one or two blocks and bring the contraption to the link point. The connector modes on the stationary side set the energy direction. Docking represents all accumulators connected on the moving construct.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.2: Transfer a little energy, disconnect and make sure the machine moves on. A redstone signal on the stationary interface forbids docking, so mind the neighbouring wiring. It is handy for on-board consumers; an ordinary Create train needs no accumulator.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.title: Portable Energy Interface
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.0: The rolling mill rolls metal into rods and wire, and the result depends on the input shape: ingots usually become rods, sheets become wire. The old advice to “roll a rod once more” replaces no specific metal’s recipe.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.1: Take the mill, rotation and a few copper ingots and sheets. Drop the blank on top, wait for the cycle to finish and take the result. One metal is enough for the first try; check the product in JEI.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.2: If the mill stops, check the drive, the recipe and the free outlet. A belt and two funnels automate it, but see the manual cycle first. Rods and wire feed electrical parts and spools, so keep them apart from look-alike blanks.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.title: Rolling Mill
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.0: The Tesla coil charges compatible energy items beneath it. It also has a dangerous mode that hurts nearby creatures, switched on by a redstone signal. You need the coil, FE and a spot away from the workshop entrance.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.1: Connect power and put a drained item under the working part as Ponder shows. First make sure its charge rises without any signal for the dangerous mode. Keep the outlet and the pickup spot clear.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.2: The coil does not smelt sand into glass unless such a recipe exists; its proven job here is charging. If you plan the creature-damage mode, fence the area and keep a neighbouring lever from switching it on by accident. A tool’s compatibility shows in its energy before and after the trial.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.title: Tesla Coil
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.0: Copper wire goes into spools and electrical parts, and a filled spool lays a line between connectors. Roll eight wire from copper sheets and make a copper spool. Keep the empty spool base after laying.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.1: Place two compatible connectors and use the filled spool on the first, then the second. The copper variant is meant for its own low-current network; a pricier spool does not make a random pair of connectors compatible.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.2: Inspect the line and check the transfer once a source appears. If the link is not created, check the connector type and the allowed distance. Eight wire in your inventory are recipe material, not eight laid lines. Remove a wire with the empty spool, not by dismantling machines.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.title: Wire and Spools
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.0: The armour inspection tool shows how a block behaves in the Big Cannons damage system. With it you choose protection by numbers rather than by the look of the material. Take the tool and several different building samples to the range.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.1: Inspect each block and compare the figures. They promise no resistance to any charge: the outcome also depends on the shot, its speed and the shape of the obstacle. Build a small test sample instead of testing the wall of your working base.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.2: The gas mask protects against gas effects and replaces neither armour, cover nor distance from a blast. Wear it in a supported slot and read its tooltip before a dangerous trial. Both items help you prepare; judge the final protection against the ammunition you actually chose.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.title: Armor and Protection
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.0: An autocannon cartridge combines projectile, casing and propellant into one item. Make the armour-piercing and flak variants by their recipes plus the tracer attachment. A bare projectile blank is not yet a loaded cartridge.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.1: Follow the path in JEI from casing to finished round and add parts where the recipe asks. Load a small identical batch into the container. Tracers show the trajectory; their placement and intervals are set apart from the main cartridges.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.2: Test the types one at a time, not mixed in the first belt: flak and penetration do different jobs, and the same hit gives a different result. After a short burst, check consumption and the casing outlet.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.title: Autocannon Rounds
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autocannon.text: An autocannon fires ready cartridges and works unlike a big gun with separate charges. Make a steel barrel, a finished breech and an ammo container; check the remaining breech and connection parts against the recipes of your type.
Assemble compatible sections on a suitable base. Put a few cartridges in the container and leave room for casings. Aim the empty rig, then give a short fire command.

The signal strength on the mount’s firing side sets the rate of fire, so do not start at maximum. The recoil spring adds barrel travel and is part of the autocannon’s setup. Limit the sector and watch the remaining ammunition so a short trial does not become an unplanned burst.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.0: A breech allows loading from the rear and must close fully before firing. Make a steel sliding breech and its quick-firing variant, which you get by applying the quick-firing mechanism to a finished sliding breech.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.1: The sliding breech opens by rotation, and ammunition goes in through the freed bore. The quick-firing one is worked from the side: shell first, then propellant, then close. The sequence differs from ramming from the muzzle.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.2: Withdraw the loader from the opening before firing. A sliding breech changes the gun’s allowed strength, so a charge chosen for another closure may no longer fit. Set up an automatic arm for the quick-firing variant only after hand experience, with a place for spent casings and a check that the breech is closed.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.title: Breeches
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.0: Bronze sections behave differently from cast iron. In this pack, bronze is mixed from copper, zinc and ash flour under ordinary heat; the tin variant depends on which materials you have. Copper and zinc without the additive make brass, so the composition matters.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.1: Smelt the bronze, melt it under the casting lid and cast the sections. Bore the set blanks with water and rotation as in the training foundry. The result is three finished bronze barrels.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.2: Do not bolt them onto a cast iron chamber and call the gun bronze: the weakest link and the breech still decide everything. Before the first shot of the new build, match length and charge again. Any gain in range or reliability shows only on the assembled gun.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.title: Bronze
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.0: The mortar drop shell is meant for a special gun that fires when the round is dropped into the bore. The item alone does not turn any vertical barrel into a mortar. Make the shell and study the allowed construction in its documentation and Ponder.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.1: Set up and inspect the empty gun on a separate site. Find out how the mortar mode is loaded and where the trajectory will go. Do not lean over the bore while feeding the round.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.2: A lobbed shot flies beyond the visible backdrop, so survey the landing area and limit yourself to one shot. This explosive round is neither the mortar stone nor grapeshot. Check the rig’s compatibility before loading and enter the result in the range log.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.title: Mortar
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.nethersteel.tex: Nethersteel is an expensive gun metal with its own chain. The mixing recipe takes a netherite scrap and four steel ingots or eight cast iron, needs superheating and yields eight ingots. A coal burner is not enough here.
Strong heat, smelting the alloy, then casting, machining and finishing the parts by their recipes. The goal needs three finished barrels and a screw breech, not a single metal blank.

A screw breech is first unlocked by rotation, then withdrawn by a mechanism for loading, and returned and locked before firing. Expensive metal promises no safe shot: an obstruction in the bore, a crooked assembly and a wrong load stay dangerous. Exercise the empty breech, then fire a proven combination.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.0: High-explosive and armour-piercing shells detonate, and the nature of the blast is set by a compatible fuze. Do not confuse the AP Shell with the non-exploding AP Shot. Make both shells plus an impact and a timed fuze, and keep them apart until configured.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.1: Open the recipes and tooltips of the specific ammunition, then fit the fuze to its intended face. Set the timed fuze’s delay before loading; test the impact fuze on a separate target. Without a chosen detonation mechanism a shell need not behave like a high-explosive round.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.2: Run the first trial far from buildings, with empty space behind and around the target. Do not try a new charge and a new fuze at the same time. Write down the configuration and the result so a repeat load does not depend on memory.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.title: Shells
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.0: Steel guns are built from plain and built-up sections. Get steel from your own metallurgy line and look up the recipes of the castings you need. The goal asks for three plain barrels and one reinforced built-up section, so a stock of ingots will not close it.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.1: Plain blanks go through casting and boring. A built-up section is assembled from layers with the cannon builder and finished by a fan blowing through lava; the transformation happens only with the right stack of layers and takes time.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.2: A pile of nested sleeves is not yet a built-up block: check the item name and inspect the joints. A reinforced barrel does not protect a weak chamber or breech. After moving it, keep access to the bore and test the allowed charge on a separate target.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.title: Steel
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.0: A big cannon is assembled from compatible sections of one material and type. The quest asks for three cast iron barrels, a chamber and a closed end. The end closes the breech, not the muzzle: the shot must keep a clear path out.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.1: Lay the parts along one axis and check which way each faces. The chamber takes the charge; the barrels give the shot its road. Three sections in stock do not oblige you to put all three on your first test gun.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.2: Match length and minimum shot velocity to the material’s strength. With cast iron, a long bore may demand a charge above the limit, so make the first gun short. Joints and a mount come before firing; a sound bore and a safe load are checked on the assembled gun.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.title: First Barrel
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.0: A mould model sets the cross-section of the future part. Cut the small model from a suitable log with a mechanical saw and pick that result in the recipe, or you will get plain planks. You need the model, casting sand and some molten cast iron.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.1: Apply the model on the site to get a mould layer; check the orientation against Ponder. Join layers if the mould is tall, then fill it with melt through a fluid feed. Setting begins once the mould is full enough and takes time.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.2: A comparator tells filling from readiness: a set mould outputs 15. Remove the shell with the intended interaction and you will find a blank whose bore is not yet cut. Do not hit it with an ordinary pickaxe before checking the mining rules: some cast parts crumble into scrap.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.title: Barrel Mold
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.0: A shot cannot pass through a cast blank until it is bored. You need a drilling machine, two extension rods, a steady water supply and a rotating rig that holds the blank. The boring head is part of the machine itself; there is no separate item to hunt for.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.1: Align the machine with the blank fixed on its rotating base as shown in Ponder. Feed water and start a slow advance. The drill must spin no slower than the blank, and a faster mode asks for more water.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.2: If the machine stops, read the reason in its tooltip: dry drilling and lack of speed are cured differently. Collect the scrap separately and remove the finished cast iron barrel only with a suitable tool. One good part matters more than a queue of unproven castings.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.title: Boring
Manually move a finished cast section intact to a new location and check its orientation

A finished cast section can be lost through incorrect harvesting. Many such blocks return scrap to an ordinary pickaxe; a suitable Silk Touch pickaxe or contraption movement preserves them according to mod rules. Choose one small already bored training component.

Read the cannon-moving Ponder scene and prepare its destination before removal. With a tool, verify the required enchantment; with machinery, confirm that the section belongs to the assembly and has a clear route.

The tick goes on when the same section stands in its new place rather than a freshly made substitute; inspect its orientation and future joints. Learn this before expensive steel castings: the foundry and the range usually stand apart, and an intact move is part of production, not luck.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.guide_cast_signa: A cannon cast can report filling and completion through redstone. Prepare a comparator and a small cast with a known metal requirement. Position observation so you do not approach molten metal for every inspection.

Connect the comparator and compare empty, partly filled and completed states. Values zero through fourteen indicate filling; fifteen means completion after solidification. Full volume and a finished component are therefore not the same moment.

Run a clear indicator to the walkway and do not strip the shell before readiness. The comparator is the whole item goal here; the point of the quest is the three states you observed. Later this scheme helps automate mould removal, once you know how to extract a part without turning it into scrap.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.guide_load_limit: Manually record material, breech, projectile travel length and a load meeting minimum velocity without exceeding strength

A safe load is chosen from both maximum strength and minimum velocity for bore length. Cast iron makes this particularly apparent: an overly long first gun may lack a convenient permissible load. Prepare goggles and an empty short cannon on the range.

Read material, breech and propellant properties. Record projectile travel length and compare required initial speed with allowed stress. Include the projectile’s starting section when mod rules count it as part of the traveled bore.

Tick the goal after choosing a consistent combination, not after a lucky shot. If the smallest sufficient charge already exceeds the strength, shorten the barrel or change the design; “it might hold” does not work here. The record becomes a template for new materials and keeps the number of charges prepared apart from the number allowed in one shot.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.0: The mechanical loader pushes ammunition along the axis like a special piston. The ram rod and worm from the goals are hand tools for ramming and extraction, not mandatory heads for the block itself. An automated rig also needs extension rods and a fitted head.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.1: Line up the loader, the ammunition and the bore on one axis. The ramming head loads; the extracting head pulls out anything stuck. In the usual scheme the cannon is returned from assembled state to blocks before loading.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.2: Run an empty stroke and make sure the mechanism withdraws fully from the bore before assembly and fire. Auto-loading does not turn a cannon into a machine gun without staged control. Keep the hand tool for maintenance: after a misfire, never ram a new shot on top of the one still inside.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.title: Autoloading
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.0: The casting lid turns a Create basin into a smelter. Prepare cast iron first: an iron ingot and coal compacted by a press in a heated basin yield a cast iron ingot. That is a separate step before melting, not a random mix under the lid.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.1: Place the lid on a basin with suitable heat and load the cast iron. One ingot gives 90 mB of melt while a bucket holds 1000, so you will need more than a dozen ingots. Pipe the liquid into a separate tank.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.2: If the process stalls, check the heat and the free liquid outlet. Keep different melts in different tanks and fence off the casting area. The lid and a bucket of melt in your inventory complete this quest; the next one pours the metal into a real mould.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.title: Melting Metal
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.0: The Cannon Mount assembles and aims a gun; the wheeled Cannon Carriage hauls it and is controlled by hand. They are different bases. Make both, but run your first trial on one stationary mount with no ammunition.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.1: Position the gun relative to the mount as Ponder shows. A signal on the hammer side assembles the cannon; kinetic inputs change the angles. Keep the fire-command side away from the assembly lever so a stray pulse cannot land there.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.2: Aim the empty barrel and disassemble again: the gun should return to its start position. Learn the wheeled carriage separately; it is not automated like the mount. Leave room around it and stay out of the path of a long barrel swinging back. Move on to loading only with a proven base.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.title: Mount and Carriage
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.0: A powder charge accelerates the shot and loads the barrel at the same time. Show the book four packed powder first, then turn them into four charges: both goals pass in sequence, no spare stock needed. Packing is a press over a basin with three suitable powder; a finished charge combines packed powder with an empty casing.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.1: Keep ammunition away from the test mount’s levers. Before loading, compare the charge’s load with the strength of the chamber and breech, and the shot’s velocity with the bore length. The figures show in tooltips through engineer’s goggles.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.2: Too much charge bursts the gun; too little leaves the shot in the barrel, so “always one bag” is no rule to live by. For the first shot pick a short gun and an allowed charge together, and never change material, length and ammunition at once, or you will not know what went wrong.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.title: Powder Charge
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.range_service_ba: The paper in this goal stands for a test log and proves no shot. Take a sheet and decide where you will write: a book, a sign or your own notes. What matters is the record kept, not paper in a pocket.

Before the first shot, note the gun’s material, the shot’s travel length, the ammunition type and the charge. Mark the aiming point and the mount’s position. After the trial, add the result and any faults found.

Change only one thing between two control shots. If the shot did not leave, unload and inspect the gun first: a log entry pulls no stuck projectile out. You will confirm the repeatable cycle by hand in the next quest, after a safe inspection.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.range_service_ru: Manually fire a control shot, repeat loading, record the charge and verify the mechanism returns to its starting position
Acceptance is a repeatable cycle, not one lucky hit. Take a proven range, the record of your chosen charge and two identical loads compatible with your gun. Observers stand off the line of fire.

Fire a control shot and repeat the loading. Record the charge and make sure the mechanism returned to its start position. Between shots, check that the bore is clear and the loader fully withdrawn; if you suspect a jam, extract the remains first.

Tick the goal after the check in the world. If the second cycle differs from the first, go through the breech, the assembly and the feed in order. A faulty load is not cured with a stronger charge: that breaks the rig and everything around it.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.range_service_se: A separate range protects the working base. The target block from the goal is a visible bearing mark, not armour that stops any shot. Choose a remote site and look at what lies beyond the impact point.
Place the target against a safe backdrop, mark the operator’s spot and close the line of fire to villagers, animals and players. Verify the charge, shot, breech and loading sequence of your own gun.

Test assembly and aiming without ammunition first. Assembly and fire commands must be kept apart, and the barrel must hit nobody on disassembly. The target in your inventory completes the goal; whether the range is ready is decided by inspection. The next goal starts a log so a repeat shot has something to compare with.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.0: Moulding sand holds the melt until it sets. One batch in this pack is two ordinary sand, dirt and a clay ball. Gather clay by the water in advance and prepare materials for sixteen batches.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.1: Mix it at a crafting table and keep casting sand apart from building sand, next to your mould models and a clear spot where mould layers can be stacked.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.2: Dirt is mandatory in the recipe; sand and clay alone will not do. Consumption depends on the height and cross-section of the mould, so sixteen batches will not cover every gun. Make one practice layer, watch how the mould fills, and only then build a tall casting column.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.title: Casting Sand
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.0: Solid shot and grapeshot give different shots: the ball pierces its target, grapeshot fans out right past the muzzle. Make both projectiles, but start the range test with one.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.1: For muzzle loading, the charge sits at the closed breech, the shot in front of it towards the muzzle, rammed home properly. Look down the bore before assembling: nothing extra should be inside. On the mount, the fire command goes to its own side after assembly and aiming.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.2: Do not light a random section on advice meant for another mechanism. Make sure length, shot and charge agree, then fire once. Repeatability and the return of the loading mechanism are checked further along the branch.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.title: First Shot
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.0: In survival, cannon blocks placed one by one do not always fuse on their own. The welder joins adjacent compatible sections, with limits on materials and gun types. Take the tool and an already aligned pair of cast iron parts.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.1: Apply the welder to two neighbouring sections in turn. They must sit on one axis with compatible faces, the same material and the same type. Check every joint; an autocannon will not weld to a big barrel.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.2: Some parts cannot be welded, or the joint comes out weaker; then a solid part made and moved as one piece is the better choice. Before mounting, walk the assembled section once more and clear stray blocks out of the bore.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.title: Welding Sections
codex.quest.create_andesite.bakery_batch: Now produce sixteen bread through the prepared operations. Begin with a small wheat supply and an empty output chest so the trial results do not mix with previously cooked food. Check that the millstone receives rotation.

Mill the grain, wash its flour into dough, then bake the dough in a separate hot processing area. Watch the first item at each transition. If an intermediate item does not change, inspect the airflow medium and allow enough processing time.

Collect sixteen bread into your normal inventory for credit; they do not need to be surrendered or consumed. Inventory tracking cannot distinguish production methods, so completion alone does not prove automation. Keep the bread for travel and use the remaining wheat to test interruptions and a full output chest.
codex.quest.create_andesite.bakery_run.t: Manually verify separate flour, dough and bread routes; a full output chest must not eject bread or return it to hot airflow

The bread-line trial shows how the line behaves in ordinary work and during a blockage. Prepare a little wheat, clear access to the depots and temporarily disconnect other consumers if they get in the way of watching. The manual tick appears after the trial bread.

Feed the wheat and make sure flour, dough and bread do not mix on the return path. Then fill the output chest and see where the finished bread goes: it must not fly outside or return into the hot airflow. Free some space and check that unloading resumes.

Tick only after these observations in the world — the book cannot see the blockage or the item route. If bread goes missing, fix the output or limit the feed first; a faster fan will not cure an overflowing warehouse.
codex.quest.create_andesite.bakery_setup: A bread line makes good use of wheat by connecting milling, washing and baking. Prepare the millstone, fan and two depots listed in the objectives. These begin a test rig, but continuous operation also needs power, water, a heated processing area and transfers between stages.

First mill wheat. Put the first depot in airflow passing through water to turn flour into dough. Reserve the second for baking dough with a valid recipe, such as smoking airflow through a campfire; craft another fan for independent air streams.

Do not combine the wet and hot stages in one undivided area. Label the inputs and leave room to remove intermediate items manually. This quest checks equipment ownership; the next batch demonstrates a product, and a separate trial checks the entire line’s reliability.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.0: A mechanical belt transports items and also transmits rotation between its ends. Belt connectors are crafted from dried kelp, so harvest and dry kelp beforehand. Both objectives check the same item; they represent a stock of placement connectors, not individual belt segments.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.1: Place two compatible parallel shafts and use the connector on one, then the other. Begin with a short horizontal belt. Supply rotation and drop one inexpensive item onto it to see the travel direction.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.2: Connect the beginning to an input and the end to an output chest through funnels. Without extraction, items accumulate and stop the flow. Keep the belt’s working section clear above a press; internal belt segment items are not needed for construction.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.title: Mechanical Belts
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.0: A blaze burner gives the basin controlled heat. Craft an empty burner first and show it to the book, then go after a blaze in the Nether. Take armour, food and fire protection: to catch a blaze you have to get close to it.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.1: Click the empty burner on a living blaze and it fills. Place it directly under the basin and give it ordinary fuel, coal for example. Brass needs exactly that: a heated basin with a mixer above it.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.2: A captured blaze does not yet mean the right temperature for every recipe. Blaze cakes give special superheating, but the first brass does not need them. Check the flame colour and the recipe before loading expensive materials; add automatic fuel feeding after a steady manual cycle.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.title: Blaze Burner
Andesite casing is the basis of the early machines. Stock up on logs, an axe and andesite alloy; eight casings take eight wooden blanks. Do not turn all your timber into planks: this needs stripped wood.

Place a log, strip the bark with the axe and apply andesite alloy to the stripped block. The finished casing can be picked up and used in recipes. Repeat eight times, keeping a little alloy for the machines themselves.

If nothing happened, check that the log is really stripped and that you are holding alloy. The press does not make casings from planks. A deployer can repeat this operation later, but for the first press and millstone it is quicker to make casings by hand beside the crafting table.
codex.quest.create_andesite.casing.title: Andesite Casing
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.0: Chutes move items between levels without long sloping belts. Prepare four and begin with a vertical run between an upper chest and a lower receiver. Keep access to both ends so you can inspect their contents.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.1: An ordinary chute transfers items downward. Upward movement uses airflow from an encased fan above or below; the chute itself does not take rotational input like a pump. If a fan blocks one end, arrange insertion or extraction from the side.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.2: A smart chute adds filtering, extracted stack size and redstone shutoff, but does not replace the fan. Test upward movement with one item and read the direction using goggles. This vertical route suits millstones, overhead storage and factory floors with little room for belts.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.title: Chutes
codex.quest.create_andesite.crafter_basi: Create’s mechanical crafters assemble a recipe from cells laid out in the world. They already need brass, so this branch brings you back to the andesite workshop after heated metalwork. Five cells make a small training rig, not every large recipe pattern.

Place the cells in one plane, supply rotation and point their arrows toward a shared output with the wrench. Lay out the materials of a simple recipe and leave a free receiver for the result. A large pattern needs more cells.

If the assembly does not start, check the occupied cells, the arrow directions and the drive. Precision mechanisms are not assembled here; they need deployers and sequenced processing. The main job of these cells is still ahead: the oversized crushing wheel recipe, which does not fit on a normal crafting table.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.0: A depot holds one stack of items at a convenient processing point. A press or deployer can work above it, while treated fan airflow can reach it from the side. Craft a depot and four andesite funnels, then place input and output chests nearby.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.1: First place material on the depot manually and confirm that the chosen machine processes it. Add funnels one at a time, checking direction: one supplies items and the other extracts them. The wrench helps change supported connection orientations.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.2: An andesite funnel lacks the full filtering features of a brass funnel. Extraction that happens too early may remove raw material before processing, so initially collect output manually. When finished sheets must be distinguished from ingots, use an appropriate belt arrangement or wait for brass filters.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.title: Depot and Funnels
codex.quest.create_andesite.ejector.text: A weighted ejector sends items through the air between points where a belt would be awkward. Crafting it requires a precision mechanism. Prepare a clear launching area and a generous receiving zone without lava, drops or exposed walkways.

Configure its target before placement, following the item’s hints and Ponder scene, then provide rotation to charge it. Begin with one inexpensive item and watch the entire trajectory. Make sure no wall or low ceiling obstructs the route.

The ejector can launch entities too, so stay off its platform while commissioning it. Prepare a separate safe landing if transporting players. After testing, arrange a receiving chest and suitable collection: an item landing on the ground has not yet reached secure storage.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.0: A fan creates airflow, while a medium in that airflow determines item processing. Water enables washing, lava enables blasting, ordinary fire or a campfire enables smoking, and soul fire enables special haunting recipes. For your first trial, wash flour because its result is easy to recognize.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.1: Place water between the fan and a depot holding flour, supply rotation and check airflow direction. Water must intersect the airflow, and the item must remain in the treated portion long enough. Ordinary ice does not provide universal freezing.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.2: Build a separate enclosed area with nonflammable walls for hot processing. Unsuitable items can be lost in dangerous media. Before connecting storage, test one JEI recipe and confirm that finished products leave instead of remaining in the shared airflow.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.title: Encased Fan
codex.quest.create_andesite.guide_washin: Washing is good for more than flour: gravel has a recipe with useful random results. Prepare gravel, a fan with water and a separate depot. Do not connect this rig to the bakery output, so metal does not mix with food.

Put gravel into the airflow that has passed through water and wait for it to change. Collect the iron nuggets apart from the rest. The output is random: nine gravel do not promise nine nuggets, and the exact chances are shown in the installed recipe.

Gather nine nuggets and take them into your normal inventory — they are not handed in and remain for alloy or assembly. Watch at least one batch of gravel go through the wash with your own eyes before extending the line.
Manually separate nuggets and byproducts, fill an output, and verify item retention and recovery after freeing space

After washing, a mixed output makes feeding the assembly machines awkward: they need specific parts, not everything on the depot. Prepare brass funnels, a filter and separate receivers. Take a little gravel and clear room for by-products in advance.

Give one output to iron nuggets and the other to everything else. Wash the batch and look into both containers. Then fill the nugget receiver for a while: the line should hold the items, not spill them into the water or onto the floor.

Confirm by hand only after correct sorting and the full-output test. Stopping is fine as long as the material is safe; once room is freed, the flow should resume. Now nuggets can go to alloy or sequenced assembly, and stray by-products take their own controlled path.
codex.quest.create_andesite.millstone.te: A millstone processes grain and other materials that have milling recipes. Craft the machine, collect wheat from a farm and leave room above it for feeding. Supply rotation through an appropriate gear connection; Ponder provides a useful placement reference.

Insert wheat, wait for milling to finish and extract the flour. This objective needs eight portions. Start small: the machine is easier to inspect before adjacent funnels immediately remove its output.

Do not insert arbitrary ore expecting guaranteed doubling. The specific JEI recipe determines output and byproducts. Flour opens the bread line, since washing can turn it into dough. Later you can connect the millstone’s input and output to storage; keeping access clear makes blockages easier to find.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.0: A mixer combines ingredients in a basin to make alloys, food mixtures and other products. Prepare the machine and basin, leaving space below the basin for a future burner. Position the mixer above it as shown in Ponder and connect its cogwheel to a transmission.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.1: For the first trial, use the unheated andesite alloy recipe: add andesite and a suitable nugget to the basin. The mixer needs sufficient speed; if its head will not descend, check rotation speed, ingredients and available capacity.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.2: Heated recipes need a separate heat source under the basin. Remove finished contents manually or through a configured output; a nearby depot alone does not guarantee extraction. After a successful test, prepare a brass line with separate arrangements for metal ingredients and burner fuel.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.title: Mechanical Mixer
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.0: A mechanical press turns ingots into sheets for fans, pipes and other components. Prepare a press, depot, eight iron ingots and a working transmission. Mount the press above the depot as shown in its Ponder scene, so the working head can reach the item.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.1: Connect rotation to the press’s side shaft and place ingots on the depot. Wait for the stroke, then collect the iron sheets. Process one ingot first to check height and power before feeding the rest.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.2: A rotating shaft does not prove that the press is positioned correctly. If processing does not occur, check the depot spacing, available capacity and input recipe. Eight sheets let you craft further equipment; continuous belt feeding is easier to build after a successful manual trial.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.title: Mechanical Press
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.0: A mechanical saw performs two distinct jobs: processing items on its work surface and cutting blocks in front of its blade. Craft one and begin with timber processing on a stable platform. Supply rotation and face the blade upward for cutting recipes.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.1: Place a suitable input on the work surface or feed it by belt. Some materials have several possible results; set the saw’s output filter to avoid receiving unwanted slabs or stairs. Compare the first recipe with JEI.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.2: Tree cutting uses a different orientation, and a saw on a moving contraption works when it encounters a tree. Keep these modes separate and stay clear of the blade. A stationary saw saves timber and alloy when producing parts; build a logging contraption after learning about moving structures.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.title: Mechanical Saw
codex.quest.create_andesite.sheets_line_: Prepare thirty-two iron ingots and an empty receiver for this trial batch. Before feeding, confirm that the press and belt rotate and that the output funnel leads to the correct chest. A small verified batch is more useful than an arbitrary warehouse full of inputs.

Load the ingots into the input chest and wait for processing. Watch items pause beneath the head and finished sheets move onward. If the line stops, check the output first: a full receiver can look like a broken press.

Take thirty-two iron sheets into your normal inventory. The objective checks possession without consuming metal, leaving the sheets available for pipes and later equipment. Items do not record how they were made; observe operation without manual feeding, then perform the separate restart trial.
Manually stop and restart rotation after a trial batch; processing must resume without manually repositioning items

Stopping the drive should not force you to rearrange materials on the production line. Prepare a few ingots and room in the output chest. A clutch or a safely disconnectable shaft section accessible from a walkway is useful for this trial.

Run a trial batch, then interrupt rotational power. After switching it back on, the line must resume processing without manually repositioning items. Watch the press, the section beneath it and the extraction point, rather than just belt movement.

If an ingot remains after restarting, check whether the press drive was disconnected separately from the belt and whether output is blocked. Confirm manually after a successful in-world trial. The Codex does not automatically record machine interruptions; the checkbox is your confirmation of the described result.

A sheet line removes the need to place every ingot under the press by hand. Gather a press, two belt connectors and two funnels, then prepare input and output chests. Leave enough space between them for the press head and transmission maintenance.

Join shafts with a belt and mount the press above its working section. Aim one funnel to feed ingots and the other to extract into the output chest. Place an ingot manually first and confirm that it passes under the press before unloading.

If an unprocessed ingot leaves, check press height and output-funnel position. The route must not bypass the machine on a neighboring belt. Owning the components completes preparation; a trial batch and a stop-and-restart test will establish how the automatic line behaves.
Andesite alloy goes into shafts, cogwheels and the first machines. Mine ordinary andesite and iron underground; smelt the ore and break some ingots into nuggets. Zinc nuggets work too, but there is no need to hunt for zinc just to start a workshop.

On the crafting table, place two andesite and two nuggets diagonally in a 2×2 square to get one alloy. Prepare sixteen and keep a little stone in reserve. Polished andesite does not work in this recipe.

A mixer will later make alloy more cheaply; for now the crafting table is enough to get rotation going. Do not spend the whole batch on one kind of part, or the next machine will send you back down the mine.
codex.quest.create_basics.andesite.title: Andesite Alloy
A large water wheel expands an early workshop without using fuel. It needs more clearance around its axis, so mark out the channel and maintenance area first. Install it near the existing transmission and leave a way to disconnect the new branch temporarily.

Supply flowing water and check rotation before joining the main network. A large wheel has its own speed; sources working together must deliver compatible rotation. Adding more water cannot correct an incompatible connection.

Measure the resulting capacity with a stressometer before attaching more machines. The large wheel adds capacity, while gearing determines the required working shaft speed. Keeping the old wheel as a separate source for an auxiliary line is useful when a shared connection becomes cramped.
codex.quest.create_basics.bigwheel.title: Large Water Wheel
Cogwheels join axes and pick a speed for the machine. Four small and two large ones are enough to compare a direct transmission with speeding up and slowing down. Check the materials in JEI and leave room in front of the machine for rearranging.

Meshing cogwheels turn in opposite directions. Driving a small wheel from a large one doubles the speed; driving a large one from a small one halves it. Not every neighbouring position counts as meshing, so use the Ponder scene as a model for axis placement.

Speeding up a consumer raises the load, not the source’s capacity. If everything stops after you change the gearing, go back to the lower speed and compare the instruments. A familiar pair of cogwheels will serve the mixer, the press and any machine with an awkward input.
codex.quest.create_basics.cogwheel.title: Cogwheels
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.0: Engineer’s goggles reveal extra information about the machine you are looking at. Craft and equip them in a suitable equipment slot; use the helmet slot for a reliable initial check. Carrying them in a bag is not enough.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.1: Look at a source, an operating consumer and a fluid tank. The information depends on the block: some show stress and speed, others contents or boiler status. Read the units so that capacity is not mistaken for rotational speed.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.2: If an expected line is missing, check your equipment and aim at the actual relevant block. Goggles help locate bottlenecks without extra instruments, but do not replace observing items leaving the machine. Remember that replacing combat headgear matters during dangerous expeditions; workshop diagnosis is best done somewhere safe.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.title: Engineer's Goggles
A dedicated production branch can be switched off while the source and auxiliary devices keep turning. Prepare a clutch and a lever and find a stretch of transmission before the press or millstone. Choose a spot you can reach without stepping among moving parts.

Insert the clutch into a gap in the shaft and power it with the lever. Make sure the source keeps working while the chosen consumer stops. Remove the signal — rotation should come back in its old direction.

Do not put the switch after a branch you also meant to service: that part would stay powered. Label the lever and keep it in sight. This setup serves the next experiment, where you will hunt the cause of a stop with the instruments.
codex.quest.create_basics.guide_stress_r: Manually identify the stop using instruments and restore rotation by disconnecting load, reducing speed or correcting direction

A stalled network does not always ask for another generator. Prepare instruments, a switch for a separate branch and a consumer with adjustable gearing. Use a cheap training rig without cutting water to a working boiler.

Compare speed and stress with the machine connected and disconnected. If the rig is overloaded, shed the extra load with the clutch or slow the consumer down. For conflicting directions, fix the transmission rather than adding capacity. There is no need to overload a big factory on purpose — a safe case on a separate network is enough.

Once you can explain the stop and restore rotation with one chosen fix, confirm the goal by hand. Then bring back the working setting and check that the machine produces again. That is how goggle and instrument readings turn into a clear repair sequence.
codex.quest.create_basics.handcrank.text: A hand crank tests a small machine while there is no permanent source yet. Craft it and put it on a free end of a shaft. A short transmission and one consumer are enough for the experiment; a crank cannot carry a whole factory.

Hold the interaction on the crank and the network turns. Sneaking reverses the direction, which is handy for nudging a piston or seeing which way a belt will run. Manual work burns hunger, so keep food nearby.

If the crank does not move the machine, check the connection and the load. A moving platform must not be your only way out during the test. Once everything checks out, replace the crank with a water wheel and keep it for commissioning lone machines away from the workshop.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.task.0: Open the cogwheel Ponder scene by holding W over the item
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.0: Ponder demonstrates a mechanism in a small interactive scene, showing placement, connections and startup order. Start with a cogwheel, because meshing gears are easier to understand in motion than in a static crafting recipe. Open your inventory or JEI and hover over the item.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.1: Hold W unless its binding has changed. Watch the cogwheel scene, move between steps and rotate the camera to see the axes. If no key hint appears, check the Ponder control binding and whether the selected item has scenes.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.2: After watching, reproduce one gear pair beside the workshop. Ponder explains block behavior, while JEI shows recipes in this installed pack. Use both: an illustrated setup does not mean its materials are already in your inventory.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.title: Ponder Scenes
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.0: Sails finish and extend a windmill that already works. A white sail and an empty frame both count as sail blocks: cloth changes the look, not the number of capacity units per block. Craft eight white sails from the JEI recipe.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.1: Stop the bearing and wait until the structure turns back into ordinary blocks. Add sails to the connected wings, check the symmetry for the sake of a comfortable walkway and assemble the windmill again. Symmetry pleases the eye, but the source only cares how many sail blocks it counts.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.2: Compare the speed before and after the expansion. The bearing counts only the assembled structure, so sails in a nearby chest add nothing. If there is no gain, check whether the new blocks joined the assembly and whether the windmill has hit its ceiling.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.title: Sails
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.0: A shaft carries rotation along its axis and connects a source to a machine. Craft eight shafts from andesite alloy using the JEI recipe; a crafting table is enough for now. A mechanical saw will later produce six shafts from one alloy.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.1: Place several shafts end to end. Their axis must continue the source output and the machine input: touching side surfaces does not create a connection. Use cogwheels or a gearbox to turn the transmission around a corner.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.2: Check movement at both ends before building a long main line. Shafts neither increase speed nor add capacity. If the network stops after a machine is connected, look for excessive stress or conflicting directions instead of trying to fix it with more shafts.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.title: Shaft
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.0: A speedometer measures its shaft speed, while a stressometer shows how much network capacity is being used. Craft both instruments and connect them to the same network as the working machine. An instrument on an isolated shaft says nothing about the neighboring line.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.1: Read them without a consumer, then connect a press or millstone. Read speed and stress again after changing the gearing. This reveals why faster processing can stop the entire workshop: the consumer needs more available capacity.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.2: During an overload, temporarily disconnect the new machine to restore rotation. Then reduce its speed or add a source. Avoid joining opposing outputs at random: conflicting directions are different from insufficient capacity. Leave instruments visible from a walkway so the next fault can be diagnosed without removing the floor.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.title: Stressometer and Speedometer
codex.quest.create_basics.waterwheel.tex: A water wheel turns without fuel. Prepare the wheel, a bucket of water and non-flammable blocks for a short channel. The flow has to touch the paddles: a wheel beside still water simply stands there.

First make sure the wheel itself turns, then run a shaft to the workspace. Wall the channel in — spilled water washes away redstone dust and carries items off the floor. Ponder shows the arrangement of flow and shaft clearly.

Connect one machine and compare its behaviour with the empty network. If capacity is short, add compatible sources or slow the consumers down. A wheel serves the first press and millstone well; just make sure it is really turning rather than sitting in your inventory.
A windmill generates rotation from an assembled moving structure with sails. Place a windmill bearing with its output toward the planned transmission, then build a connected frame in front of its working face. At least eight suitable sail blocks are needed to start; this quest asks for sixteen frames.

Sail frames count too. Attach the wings to the block in front of the bearing, using sail connections and glue where other frame blocks need joining. Leave clearance around the structure and interact with the bearing to assemble it.

If it will not start, check the sail count and their connection to the bearing. Once assembled, connect a shaft at the back. Stop and disassemble the windmill before extending its wings; a large moving structure is awkward to repair.
codex.quest.create_basics.windmill.title: Windmill
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.0: The wrench places Create parts precisely and rebuilds the workshop without needless losses. Craft it from the JEI recipe and keep it on the hotbar next to the shafts. A pickaxe breaks blocks, but it cannot turn a part.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.1: Click an installed part with the wrench and it rotates or switches variant. Sneak-clicking removes supported blocks. Practise on a single shaft: different faces of a block respond differently.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.2: Before taking a working line apart, stop the rotation and pick up items from exposed sections. The contents and state of neighbouring machines do not always survive dismantling. The wrench is a real help with funnels, transmission axes and train assembly: one placement mistake is fixed with one turn, not a new block.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.title: Wrench
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.0: A mechanical arm transfers items between preselected points. It is not required for the first precision mechanism; instead, a mechanism is part of its own recipe. Prepare the arm after sequenced assembly is running and leave clear space beside several depots.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.1: Before placing the arm, use it to select supported inputs and outputs. Repeated interaction changes a point’s role; check the selection colors, then place the arm and supply rotation. Use an intermediate depot or funnel for an unsupported inventory.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.2: Try transferring one stack, then fill one output. The distribution mode determines whether the arm skips a blocked destination or waits. It has no universal filter of its own; brass funnels can provide restrictions. An arm is useful for supplying burners and several nearby operations.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.title: Mechanical Arm
codex.quest.create_brass.assembly_line_b: Produce eight precision mechanisms using the prepared loop. Refill all three component supplies beforehand and empty the outputs. Random outcomes mean more golden workpieces are needed than completed products, so do not budget inputs solely around eight.

Feed sheets gradually and watch unfinished mechanisms return. Each passes through five trios of operations; completed mechanisms and byproducts must leave the line. If one hand stops, check its material before increasing the speed of the entire installation.

Collect eight mechanisms into your normal inventory for credit. You keep the items; the Codex checks possession rather than production history. Reserve some output for spare arms and speed control. After this batch, test a temporary nugget shortage so routine supply exhaustion does not require rebuilding the queue manually.
codex.quest.create_brass.assembly_line_r: Manually remove and restore iron nuggets; the queue must resume and completed mechanisms must not enter a sixth lap

Sequenced assembly has to survive a shortage of one consumable without losing workpieces. Leave a few unfinished mechanisms on the line and make sure the output chests have room. What matters here is the order of recovery, not record speed.

Remove the iron nuggets for a while, then put them back. Check that the queue of workpieces moves on and that a finished mechanism does not go around a sixth time. Follow at least one workpiece through the last stage and the output, including any by-product.

After a successful test, tick the goal by hand. If the queue stands still, look at the arm’s filter and the return paths. Do not push workpieces past the stalled operation: once feeding is repaired, they should continue their own sequence without losing a stage.
codex.quest.create_brass.assembly_line_s: A return loop removes manual repetition of fifteen operations per workpiece. Prepare the three deployers, brass funnels and belts listed, plus separate component stocks. The loop entrance must accept golden sheets and returning unfinished mechanisms.

Arrange operations in this order: small cogwheel, large cogwheel, iron nugget. Give each hand a filter and its own feed. After the third stage, extract completed products and return only the unfinished mechanism to the first stage.

Provide a separate byproduct outlet: byproducts appear when the recipe finishes and must not block the return route. Run one workpiece first and follow every lap. Item objectives confirm equipment, not filters or routing; the batch and supply-interruption trial will demonstrate those.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.0: Brass is needed for filtering funnels, deployers and more advanced automation. Prepare copper and zinc ingots, a mixer with a basin, and a fueled blaze burner. Zinc is mined as an ore resource and smelted, so reserve storage for it beforehand.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.1: Put one copper and one zinc ingot into the heated basin: the recipe produces two brass ingots. Ordinary heat is enough; blaze cakes are unnecessary. Check mixer rotation and wait for its head to descend.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.2: Repeat enough times to obtain sixteen ingots, replenishing burner fuel as needed. If mixing stops, inspect heat, speed and basin contents. Divide the first brass between casings and feeding equipment; spending it all on decoration would delay the next branch, which needs several different mechanisms.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.title: Brass
codex.quest.create_brass.brass_casing.te: Brass casing connects your new metalworking capability with precision machinery. Prepare eight stripped logs and brass ingots. Making casings beside the crafting table is convenient when deployer and funnel components are already stored there.

Place a log, strip its bark and apply a brass ingot to the stripped surface. Collect the casing and repeat until you have eight. The method resembles andesite casing production, but uses a different covering material.

Do not substitute copper for brass or press planks: that produces another result or fails the recipe. Keep part of the stock for later equipment. The casing itself neither filters items nor receives commands; those features belong to machines crafted from it. You can now move on to deployers for the first sequenced assembly operations.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass_funnel.te: Brass funnels choose which item to pass and how many, and tunnels spread the flow across belts. Prepare four funnels, two tunnels and an ordinary filter. For the test, mix two easily distinguished materials in a small chest.

Assign one funnel a specific item and point it at a separate receiver. Then give the filter a list of items and check its mode — allow or deny. On the tunnel, separately choose how it distributes between the outputs.

An ordinary filter is not an attribute filter: rules based on item properties live in another item. Test sorting with a small mixed batch and watch the funnel directions especially. These devices hold the assembly loop together: only unfinished workpieces go back around, while finished mechanisms and stray by-products leave the cycle.
Chromatic compound is listed among Create’s items, but the recipes in this pack offer no confirmed survival way to obtain it. Old advice about light, shadow and special casings belongs to a branch that does not exist here. Instead of the unobtainable material, this quest teaches practical sorting by properties.

Craft an attribute filter and open its settings with a sample item. Choose an available property from the list and put the filter into a brass funnel on a separate chest. A cheap mix of things is fine for the test.

The rule should pass the expected items and hold back the rest. Take the conditions from the installed version’s interface, not from guesses based on names. Such a filter brings order to a mixed store of tools or food without any hunt for rare materials.
codex.quest.create_brass.chromatic.title: Sorting by Attributes
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.0: Crushing wheels process anything with a crushing recipe, including some ores and obsidian. Their oversized recipe is assembled by Create’s mechanical crafters: prepare as many cells as the JEI pattern demands. A working pair needs two wheels.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.1: Set the wheels at the correct spacing and drive them toward each other so items are pulled into the gap. Arrange collection below and controlled feeding above. Make the first test with one cheap material that has a known recipe.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.2: Fence off the dangerous gap: the wheels maim creatures. Cut the drive before maintenance and never pick items out of a running crusher. Output and by-products depend on the recipe, so do not expect every ore to double the same way. Washing after crushing can be a useful separate stage.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.title: Crushing Wheels
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.0: A deployer repeats individual player actions: using an item, placing a block or attacking in its selected mode. Prepare two devices and an accessible rotational drive for the first assembly operation. Leave space in front as shown in Ponder: it acts at the position two blocks ahead.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.1: Give the hand its required item and test on a simple target. The wrench switches use and attack modes, while the filter restricts its held contents. For belt processing, face the deployer down toward the intermediate item.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.2: If the hand moves without a result, check mode, held item and target position. Redstone stops new actions after the current cycle finishes. Sequenced assembly consumes components, so provide separate feeds for small cogwheels, large cogwheels and nuggets instead of one unfiltered mixed input.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.title: Deployer
A precision mechanism is born from a golden sheet by sequenced assembly, not on a crafting table. Prepare golden sheets, small and large cogwheels and iron nuggets. The first time, move the workpiece between deployers by hand or swap the item in a single hand.

Apply a small cogwheel, then a large one, then an iron nugget. In the installed recipe this trio repeats five times. Watch the state of the unfinished mechanism so you do not start an operation out of turn.

The result is random: four sheets do not promise four mechanisms. Keep spare parts and collect by-products separately. Four finished mechanisms in your inventory unlock the mechanical arm and the speed controller. A full return loop is easier to build once the order is clear on a single workpiece.
codex.quest.create_brass.precision.title: Precision Mechanism
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.0: An item vault combines several blocks into a large machine-accessible inventory. Prepare four blocks and insertion and extraction equipment: its contents cannot be opened manually like a normal chest. Build an output before loading valuable materials.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.1: Construct a valid elongated shape and attach a funnel to a wall. Its square cross-section can be up to three blocks wide, and length is limited by that width. Verify formation, then insert a small stack of stone.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.2: Arrange extraction into an accessible chest and confirm that all test items return. The vault does not sort its contents; connected logistics need filters. This buffer suits the gap between crushing and further processing, or a freight contraption. Leave readable external indication so a large closed inventory does not conceal an overflow.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.title: Item Vault
A mechanical bearing rotates an attached structure using an external drive. Unlike a windmill bearing, it consumes rotation rather than creating a source from sails. Prepare a bearing and a small glued crossbar for testing.

Place the structure in front of its working face and supply rotation from behind. Inspect clearance for a full turn, including corners and projecting tools. Begin at low speed to see which blocks joined the assembly.

If some remain behind, stop and check their connection to the block in front of the bearing. Account for stop and disassembly settings when returning it to blocks. This drive suits a circular farm or rotating bridge; use a windmill bearing and suitable sails when the purpose is power generation.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.cart.tex: A cart assembler turns a structure above rails into a moving contraption. This is separate from Create’s large train system. Prepare an assembler, minecart, ordinary rails and a small glued platform with an empty chest.

Place the assembler on a rail section and position the platform in its assembly area. Bring in the minecart and control assembly as shown in Ponder, first testing a short straight route. A coupling connects suitable minecarts; it does not convert Create railway bogeys into ordinary carts.

Stop at a disassembly point after traveling and inspect the cargo and platform membership. Keep the first route away from dangerous bends and drops. Cart contraptions support early mining and transport, but their mounting, control and rails differ from a later station-built locomotive.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.clockwor: A clockwork bearing builds hands that follow world time. It is a special clock mechanism, not an ordinary bearing with a single speed. Prepare it and short, clearly distinguishable hands made of cheap blocks.

Assemble the hands and links as the Ponder scene shows: the hour and minute parts have their own attachments. Supply rotation and check the dial orientation. Leave air between the hands and the wall so the clock reads from outside. The hands must not be glued to each other — the minute part attaches in front of the hour part as a separate structure.

Watch the positions at different times of the game day. If both parts move the same way, check how they are attached, not just their length. A clock belongs on a square or at a station; leave production control to signals and sensors — a visible hand is not a timer by itself.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.controls: Contraption controls expose the available functions of an already assembled machine. A seat keeps a passenger on a moving structure, but by itself it does not turn the structure into a steerable train. Prepare the controls block and the green seat from the objectives.

Glue both blocks to a test platform and assemble it with your usual drive. Check the seating and the panel. What you can do depends on the structure: a lift picks floors, other assemblies have their own toggles.

This block is not the train controls. Before boarding, keep an external way to stop and make sure you can dismount calmly once stopped. A slow short ride is enough for the first try. Tested seat and panel move on to a working drill or a passenger cabin; just remember that a seat is not a brake.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.elevator: An elevator pulley carries a cabin between marked floors. Prepare the pulley itself and ordinary redstone contacts: on assembly, stationary contacts become elevator contacts. A cabin and two landings need three contacts, which is why the objective counts the base parts.

Build a glued cabin, put a contact on it and a stationary one opposite. Mark the second floor with a contact in the same vertical column. Supply rotation and assemble the lift by clicking the pulley. Name the floors and set up pulse calls.
