Run the empty cabin to both floors first. Fence the shaft, keep an emergency exit and check that the doors do not open onto a drop when the cabin is away. Floors are chosen through the contraption controls inside; whether the stops are right is proven only by a ride.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.gantry.t: A gantry carriage travels along a special gantry shaft and carries an attached structure. The single carriage requested is not a complete system: you also need gantry shafts, power and glue. Begin with a short horizontal guide above a clear area.

Build a continuous guide, mount the carriage in the correct orientation and attach a small platform. Supply rotation to the shaft and test travel in both directions. Review Ponder’s movement and rotational-transfer modes before connecting working tools.

Do not leave a guide end over a drop, and define the useful travel range beforehand. If the structure will not move, check shaft type and carriage connection; ordinary shafts cannot replace gantry shafts. After a short trial, the system can carry a drill or freight attachment along a fixed line.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.glue.tex: Super glue connects blocks that must move together. Chassis helps assemble larger structures with configurable attachment ranges. Prepare glue, four linear chassis and a few inexpensive blocks for a first platform.

Select the future assembly area with glue according to the item hints. Keep the floor, warehouse wall and rotational source outside the selection. Configure chassis attachment direction and range, and prepare the required faces as shown in Ponder.

Inspect the highlighted attached blocks before starting. A touching chest or tool does not always join automatically. Move the structure a short distance and confirm that everything intended travels with it. Once connections are understood, you can build piston gates, rotating farms or lifting platforms without accidentally attaching half the workshop.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.guide_ha: Open the mechanical harvester Ponder scene and review its contraption operation

A circular harvester is a useful contraption without a large drilling rig. Prepare a mechanical bearing, a few frame blocks, a harvester, a chest and glue. Choose a small plot of mature wheat with a walkway around it.

Open the harvester’s Ponder scene and work out which way its working edge faces on a moving structure. Build a short bearing arm so the harvester passes over the crops and the chest is glued to the same assembly. Make the first turn a slow one.

Make sure the arm does not grab a fence or the neighbouring base, and that mature crops are really taken. The viewing goal counts your acquaintance with the scene; the farm’s operation you check separately. Before a big expansion, find out how the chosen crop survives harvesting and whether the layout needs replanting.
Manually verify crops enter onboard storage and transfer through docked interfaces to a stationary chest without disassembly

Crops in a moving chest have not yet reached the bakery store. Prepare a pair of portable storage interfaces, a funnel or another means of extraction, and an empty stationary chest. Run the test on the small harvester you already proved.

Attach one interface to the contraption and place the other opposite the point it passes, at a valid distance. Connect extraction on the stationary side. Harvest a little, wait for docking and watch the items arrive in the final chest.

The goal is done once crops complete the whole route without dismantling the machine or carrying them out of onboard storage. If docking happens but items stay put, check the extraction direction and the free space. That turns a separate farm into a raw-material source for the bread line, and the bearing no longer has to stop after every harvest.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.piston.t: A mechanical piston moves a structure in a straight line, and extension poles set the travel. Prepare the piston and four poles. For the first try, a short horizontal area and a small glued panel are enough — no need for a whole wall.

Install the poles along the piston axis and feed rotation from the side. Reversing the drive reverses the travel. If the panel should come back with the head, add a sticky attachment and test it before the first full extension.

Watch the ends of travel and the clearance for the whole structure, protruding parts included: an ordinary piston does not pick up a free-standing block by itself. Stop the drive before fixing connections. Sliding gates and bridges come next, and a sequenced gearshift can take over the precise movement program later.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.pulley.t: A rope pulley raises and lowers an attached structure. It suits a small freight platform or vertical drill, but does not choose floors like a dedicated elevator mechanism. Craft the pulley and prepare a solid support over a shallow testing area.

Supply rotation, lower the rope to the platform and check its glued attachments. Reversing rotation changes travel direction. Begin without a passenger or cargo, watching the lower limit and the return upward.

Stay out from beneath the moving platform and leave a ladder out of the shaft. If only part of the structure moves, stop and fix its connections. Add containers and tools after testing. For a passenger elevator with floor calls, use the next branch with landing contacts and cabin controls.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.tools_co: Tools give a moving structure a job: a drill breaks blocks ahead, a harvester takes mature crops, a plough works the soil, and a roller changes the surface in its chosen mode. Prepare the four tools from the objectives and a small test area.

Attach the tools with their working side toward the intended path, and the container to the same assembly. Take one tool and a few dirt blocks. For placement work, the material must sit in an accessible contraption inventory.

Not all of these blocks work only in motion: some also have a stationary powered use, so test the mode you actually mean to use. Fence the drill’s path and never point it at the base. Before building a big farm or a road machine, make sure the results and dropped items are really collected.
A copper backtank stores compressed air for a diving helmet and certain tools. Craft it, then reserve an accessible rotating transmission section in the workshop. A freshly crafted item should not be assumed charged.

Place the backtank as a block and connect rotation. Wait for it to fill while watching its air reserve, then remove and equip it in the chest slot. Higher speed helps charging, but the source and connection must work correctly.

Check the charge again before traveling. Compatible equipment consumes air, which does not automatically refill merely because you stand on land wearing the tank. It occupies an armor slot, so account for enemy protection. Bring a helmet for the first dive and choose somewhere with an easy route to the surface.
codex.quest.create_copper.backtank.title: Copper Backtank
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.0: A steam boiler turns heat and water into capacity for engines. Prepare the eight tanks and two engines from the objective, plus a pump, pipes and a heat source. A set of parts in the inventory is not a boiler yet.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.1: Build a valid reservoir, put heat underneath and mount engines on the walls. Supply continuous water, then create the engine outputs by applying shafts to them. Keep the pump on an independent drive for the first start, or a stopped boiler will lose its own water.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.2: Check three limits through the goggles: size, water and heat. Raising one is pointless while another holds everything back. Add load gradually and do not expect the full output of two engines from any eight-tank shape. Reliable generation starts with steady supplies and burners you can reach.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.title: Steam Boiler
Copper casing is used in Create fluid machinery and other devices. Prepare four logs, an axe and four copper ingots. Smelt the copper first; copper sheets are not needed for this operation.

Place a log and strip its bark with the axe. Apply a copper ingot to the stripped wood, then collect the resulting casing. Repeat for the full stock. This is an item application to a world block, not plank pressing.

If no casing appears, check the stripped log and held material. Do not confuse casing with a fluid tank: it stores no water itself. The four casings support later equipment; divide remaining copper between pipes and sheets so water-service development does not stall.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.0: A copper diving helmet uses backtank air for underwater breathing, while diving boots help movement along the bottom. Craft both and fully charge the backtank before leaving. A helmet without an air supply does not grant unlimited diving time.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.1: Equip the set and test it beside a gently sloping shore. Enter the water, inspect remaining air time and try walking in the boots. Find an easy exit beforehand: heavy boots behave differently from ordinary swimming.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.2: During an expedition, reserve air for the return journey and watch for enemies. This equipment is for water and does not protect against lava. It helps explore submerged places, lay underwater pipes and operate a hose, but easy surface access remains part of preparation even with a full backtank.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.title: Diving Gear
codex.quest.create_copper.guide_boiler_r: Manually stop and restore heating; with independent water supply, the boiler must power a machine again without carrying buckets

A proven restart is worth more than a handsome boiler that only works until its first stop. Pick a time without urgent production, prepare fuel and leave the independent water supply on. Do not change the reservoir shape during the test.

Cut the fuel and wait for the heat to drop while watching the boiler limit through the goggles. Then restore the burners and check that capacity comes back. Reconnect the disconnected consumers one at a time, to tell a heat shortage from a network overload.

The tick goes in once the boiler powers the chosen machine again without buckets and without spinning the pump line up manually. If the restart fails, note which parameter is the limit and fix that one. Keep a small fuel reserve nearby for maintenance instead of sending the whole warehouse into burners that never go out.
codex.quest.create_copper.guide_boiler_s: A boiler needs water before its engines can power anything. If the only pump turns from that same boiler, the two lock up on each other after a stop. Prepare a water wheel and a separate pump for a reliable start.

Build a small water drive and connect it only to the supply pump. Run a pipe to the boiler, check the direction and whether the goggles show enough water. Set the pump speed with gearing rather than rebuilding the whole engine room without need.

Stop the production branch and make sure the pump keeps turning. The components count here; the real restart is tested in the next experiment. Constant water does not replace burner fuel: each boiler limit is serviced separately.
codex.quest.create_copper.netherite_divi: Netherite gear works in extreme heat, but only a complete matching set protects from lava. The helmet and backtank in the objective are not the whole kit: you also need netherite leggings and netherite footwear. And the air supply must be charged.

Upgrade the copper items with the smithing recipes in JEI, then check all four armour slots. For the first test, prepare a separate safe way out of the lava and a spare fire resistance potion. Do not start by jumping into a deep lake.

The helmet spends air to protect you from fire and lava: watch the reserve and turn back early. Two parts in the inventory complete the item objectives but do not make the player invulnerable — only a fully worn set protects. A tested kit is useful around lava sources, where copper diving gear is helpless.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.0: A steam whistle gives an audible signal and lends character to an engine room or a train. It adds no capacity to the boiler. Craft a whistle and find an accessible fluid-tank wall with enough heat.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.1: Mount it on the tank and trigger it to hear the sound. Another whistle item extends the installed one and lowers its pitch, and the wrench switches octaves. Engineer’s goggles show the current note.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.2: If there is no sound, check the mounting and the heat before rewiring anything. Start with a single short signal, especially near a shared base, and tie it to a clear event such as equipment becoming ready. Several horns in a row stop meaning anything; for heat and water levels a visible display serves better.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.title: Steam Whistle
codex.quest.create_fluids.chocolate.text: Liquid foods need ingredients, containers and a free receiver at the same time. Prepare sugar, cocoa and milk for chocolate. In a heated basin, a mixer combines sugar, cocoa beans and 250 mB of milk into 250 mB of chocolate; a bucket takes several such batches.
Honey can be drained from bottles: each provides 250 mB of fluid and returns a glass bottle. Harvest from bees with safe hive access and account for their reaction to collection.

Keep chocolate and honey in separate tanks, then fill one bucket of each for the objective. If the drain stops, inspect empty-bottle storage and fluid output. Owning two buckets confirms the products; a continuous food line additionally needs container return and reliable ingredient supplies.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.0: A hose pulley draws fluid from a body of liquid or floods a space with it. Assemble the pulley, a pump and pipes, then choose a small safe pond for the first try. You need a stable platform above it: once drained, the familiar water surface disappears.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.1: Supply rotation, lower the hose end into the liquid and connect the pulley to the pump line. The pump direction chooses draining or filling, while the pulley drive moves the hose itself — two different operations that are easy to confuse.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.2: The pond should drop and the receiving tank should fill. Very large sources may count as bottomless, but the threshold and allowed fluids depend on world settings; read the pulley’s status. Do not count on infinite lava without checking, and fence the area before draining a dangerous lake.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.title: Hose Pulley
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.0: Fluid pipes join the source, the pump and the consumer. Craft eight pipes — copper, by the JEI recipe — and choose a short route between two accessible points. Pipes carry fluid, but they do not pump it themselves.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.1: Place the connections one at a time and inspect junctions: a neighbouring tank can quietly join the network. The wrench switches supported pipe variants, and a viewing section shows what is happening inside without dismantling the line.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.2: Fill the first route with water after installing the pump. If the fluid does not move, trace the path from inlet to outlet and check which side the pipe meets the machine on. Smart pipes and valves handle filtering and shut-off — there is no need to replace every ordinary section with them. A short, clear main line is easier both to maintain and to extend.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.title: Fluid Pipes
codex.quest.create_fluids.portable_fluid: Portable interfaces connect the storage of a moving contraption to a stationary network. The fluid one works with tanks, the item one with inventories. The quest asks for one of each, but a real docking of either kind needs a pair: one on the machine, one at the base.
Place the interfaces facing each other at a valid distance and bring the contraption to the docking point. Connect a pump to the stationary fluid interface, and feeding or extraction to the item one.

Test the docking with a small batch while watching both inventories. Blocks standing nearby without the right orientation transfer nothing. Give the contraption enough time to stop, especially a train. This is how a drill rig or a freight train unloads without being dismantled after every trip.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.0: A mechanical pump makes fluid move through pipes in one direction. Prepare a pump, a few pipes, a water source and an empty tank. For the first try, place the pump close to both ends: a fault is harder to find on a long main line.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.1: Connect the source to the inlet side and the tank to the outlet, then feed rotation into the pump’s cogwheel. Check the direction arrow. Change it by rotating the pump or reversing the drive; a redstone signal does not control the pump.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.2: Watch the level in the receiver. If it does not rise, check the source, the rotation and the direction, then the pipe joints. Higher speed pumps more, but it does not fix a wrong route. For future water supply, give the pump a steady drive independent of machines that are often switched off.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.title: Mechanical Pump
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.0: A spout fills items with fluid, and an item drain pulls it out of suitable containers. Prepare both devices, pipes and a small water tank. The spout needs fluid from above and an item under its nozzle; it takes no rotation.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.1: For a simple test, fill an empty container by the JEI recipe while it sits on a depot or belt. Then put the full container on the drain and route the fluid into a receiver. Follow where the emptied container goes.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.2: A stuck container usually means the fluid has nowhere to go or the item output is blocked. Do not connect honey, lava and water to one setup at once. After a successful trial, this pair of devices will serve drinks, chocolate and sequenced assembly, where the exact fluid and the processing order matter.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.title: Spout and Drain
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.0: A fluid tank holds a reserve between the source and the consumer. The four blocks in the objective make a small reservoir on which you can watch adjacent parts merge into one. Choose a level spot with access to a wall for the pipe and to a window for watching.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.1: Place the tanks in a compatible shape and connect a pump with water. Not every arbitrary shape becomes one reservoir: when expanding, keep a valid footprint and check the merge through goggles or the window.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.2: Watch it fill and make sure the water is not escaping into an accidental side branch. One reservoir is not for a mix of water, honey and lava: separate tanks are easier to label and service. Later they smooth out supply gaps, and in a specially heated setup they become part of a steam boiler.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.title: Fluid Tank
codex.quest.create_fluids.water_service_: The next water-service component is a fluid valve. Despite this quest’s batch wording, its objective checks the valve rather than a volume of water. Craft one and prepare a pipe section between the buffer and a chosen consumer.

Install the valve and arrange rotation to change its position. In this version it is a mechanical valve; an ordinary redstone signal does not replace its drive. Use a hand crank or a transmission with a gearshift for convenient operation.

Fill the buffer before testing and choose a receiver with a visible level. Opening must permit flow and closing must isolate that branch. The valve neither creates pressure nor forces fluid against the pump. After obtaining the item, proceed to the separate installed-system trial and keep the control accessible.
Manually open and close the valve, check levels and pump direction, and confirm water delivery resumes when rotation restarts
Now test the water supply as one system. Prepare a partly filled tank and a consumer that can actually take water: when both reservoirs are full, the valve position is hard to notice.

Open and close the valve while watching the tank level and the consumer. Make sure the pump direction matches the flow and that water returns once rotation restarts. Check as well that an accidental side branch does not bypass the closed valve.

Tick only after the test in the world. If the flow does not come back, start with the pump drive, then check the valve position and the space in the receiver. A sound layout lets you service a consumer and get back to work without moving pipes or carrying buckets.

A shared water supply saves carrying buckets to every consumer. Prepare a pump, eight pipes, four tanks and a reachable water source. Put the buffer near the workshop, leaving room around it for inspection and future branches.

Connect the source, the pump and the reservoir with a short route. Check the pump direction before starting and set aside an accessible section for a valve: it comes in the next quest, and it is easier to plan its place now.

Make sure water reaches the tank independently of the production mixer or press — a separate drive simplifies maintenance and, later, the boiler supply. The book only sees the set of parts, so after assembly watch the level itself: if it is not rising, there is no water supply yet.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.chaindrive.t: Encased chain drives compactly connect several parallel shafts. Prepare four drives and mark out a row of machines requiring matching rotation. This is useful where several exposed cogwheels would occupy the entire walkway.

Place the drives beside one another in compatible orientations and connect one to the source. Run shafts to the consumers, first checking them without load. Correct a component with the wrench if neighboring drives have not formed a shared chain.

An ordinary chain drive relays rotation, while the adjustable version separately changes its speed ratio according to a signal. Do not assume every drive has that feature. Check total stress after attaching machines: a compact transmission does not reduce actual load. Leave room for a clutch to service one group of consumers.
A clutch stops one branch without shutting down the whole workshop. A gearshift keeps transmitting but reverses its output on a redstone signal. Prepare both blocks, a lever and a small load whose direction is easy to see.

Insert the clutch into a gap in the shaft: without a signal it transmits rotation, with a signal it disconnects. Test the gearshift on a separate section — the lever should reverse a belt or a piston’s travel.

Stopping and reversing are different things. A held signal keeps the chosen state, and a short pulse does not turn the gearshift into a movement program; automatic return needs your own logic or a sequenced gearshift. Put the manual switch by the walkway so the machine can be serviced without entering the moving area.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.clutch.title: Clutch and Gearshift
codex.quest.create_kinetics.display.text: A display link carries information from a supported source onto a readable surface. Prepare one link block and two nixie tubes. For the first rig, choose a simple value — a sensor reading or a speed available in the source’s settings.

Select the target display with the link item, then install the link on the source following the hints. Open the settings and choose what to show. Tubes have little room; a long message looks better on a large board.

Change the monitored value and make sure the picture updates. If there is no text, check the chosen target, the source and the output format rather than feeding rotation into the link. Put the display beside the walkway and label it: a number without units is easily taken for item stock when it is really speed.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.flywheel.tex: A steam engine extracts rotation from an operating boiler. In this Create version, a flywheel is a decorative rotating component: an engine does not require it, and it does not store spare energy. This quest asks for both items, but their purposes differ.

Mount the engine on a fluid tank belonging to an active boiler. Use a shaft on the engine to create its kinetic output, then connect a consumer. Before connecting, inspect boiler heat, water supply and size with engineer’s goggles.

You can place the flywheel on an operating transmission for decoration. Adding it will not fix a stopped engine: first investigate boiler limits and output connection. This check distinguishes actual generation from decorative components in the future engine room.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.gearbox.text: A gearbox changes the route of rotation when a straight shaft meets a wall or a machine stands to the side. Craft one gearbox and prepare a few shafts. A horizontal turn between the source and an already tested consumer is enough for the first try.

Feed a shaft into one side of the box and take the output from another suitable side. Change the orientation with the wrench; the vertical variant carries rotation between floors. Check the output direction before attaching a belt or a pump.

A gearbox adds no capacity and does not replace a speed-up gear. If nearby machines turn the wrong way, trace the path through the box. Do not merge two outputs back into one network without checking: an innocent fork easily becomes a conflicting loop.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.0: Redstone links carry a redstone signal between parts of the workshop. Two blocks need the same pair of items in their frequency slots, including their order. Prepare a transmitter, receiver and linked controller as listed.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.1: Place one link beside a lever and another beside a test lamp, then select receiver mode according to its block hint. Choose an uncommon item pair to avoid operating another machine on the same frequency. Configure a controller button with that pair afterward.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.2: Test pressing and releasing the button from the operator’s actual location. Wireless control does not imply unlimited range or operation of every unloaded machine. If the lamp does not respond, check modes, frequencies and distance. Connect the clutch or drive after testing, while retaining a local maintenance switch.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.title: Wireless Link
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.0: Redstone gives a machine short commands and remembers a state. The pulse repeater controls the timing of a signal, the powered latch keeps a switched state, and the analog lever sets its strength. Craft the three listed items and an ordinary lamp for the rig.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.1: Test each element on its own before wiring up a moving structure. Compare a brief button press with a lever’s steady signal. On the latch, check set and reset against the connection sides shown in Ponder.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.2: Do not feed an unfamiliar combination straight into a lift or a drill. Let the lamp first show exactly the behaviour the clutch or gearshift expects. Then move the circuit to the machine, keeping a manual switch within reach. A small, well-understood circuit saves you a long dust trail and accidental restarts.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.title: Redstone Logic
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.0: A rotation speed controller sets the speed without a long staircase of cogwheels. Crafting it takes a precision mechanism. Also prepare a large cogwheel and an instrument, so you can see that the setting really took effect.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.1: Mount the large cogwheel above the controller as Ponder shows and feed rotation into its axis. Set the output speed on the side panel. The sign of the value flips the direction; start with a modest figure that is easy to watch.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.2: Check the speedometer on the output and the total stress after connecting a machine. The controller does not create capacity from nothing: a consumer that is too fast will overload the source. Zero in the setting stops the output, so on a sudden stop look at the panel as well. The block is especially handy for a lone mixer or a line that is often reconfigured.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.title: Rotation Speed Controller
codex.quest.create_kinetics.sequenced.te: A sequenced gearshift runs a preset rotation program. It suits a door, a bridge or a platform that must travel exactly as far as intended. Prepare a precision mechanism for crafting, and a drive plus a clear safe run for testing.

Open the settings and write a short program: move, pause, move back. Pick step sizes for the operation and the connected mechanism — angular rotation and linear travel are not the same thing. Start the program with a control signal.

Make the first move short and watch where the structure stops. The gearshift does not know where your walkway or valuable storage is, so inspect obstacles beforehand. Once the program works, add a manual way to stop the drive. This block adds no capacity to the network.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.stockpile.te: A stockpile sensor helps start production when supplies are low and stop it when storage fills. A content observer serves another purpose: detecting matching items on a supported section. Prepare both blocks and a small chest containing one material.
Attach the stockpile sensor to storage and set lower and upper thresholds. Add and remove items gradually while watching a lamp. Different thresholds prevent rapid switching around one value.

For the observer, choose the required item or filter and pass it through the monitored line. A signal is not automatic proof of finished production: the observer may be seeing raw input. After testing, connect the sensor to feeding controls or a clutch, and verify that high stock stops production while low stock restarts it.
codex.quest.create_packages.cardboard.te: Cardboard is needed for package machinery and other newer Create items. It comes from pulp, not from pressed paper. Prepare a mixer with a basin, water, a press and plant material: bamboo, sugar cane or permitted saplings.

Mix four units of listed material with 250 mB of water. Run the resulting pulp through the press — out comes cardboard. The cycle repeats for eight sheets, so arrange a separate route from the basin to the press.

If mixing does not start, check in JEI whether the plant qualifies and whether water is arriving. Do not send the wet blank straight into the packager recipe: it needs pressing first. Cardboard is convenient to make in batches next to the bread workshop, where the basin, water and depot processing are already familiar.
codex.quest.create_packages.chain_convey: A chain conveyor joins package-delivery nodes and transmits rotation between them. Prepare four nodes and ordinary chains for connections. Place the first two within clear view, leaving an unobstructed route and access to shafts above or below.

With chains held, select two conveyors to connect them, then supply rotation to the network. Connection length is limited: long routes use several spans rather than one endless chain. Attach frogports to suitable nodes.

Send one addressed box and follow it to the receiver. Reachable addresses matter at junctions, and a full port can delay delivery. Players can also travel on chains with a wrench, but check height and a safe exit first. Observing from the ground is sufficient for the freight trial.
codex.quest.create_packages.factory_gaug: A factory gauge watches stock and can order replenishment. The two devices in the objective are enough to link a simple product with its ingredient. Take one real recipe from a working workshop: the gauge builds no machines and processes no materials itself.

Bind the gauges to the network, assign the monitored items and connect the dependencies in the interface. Set how much product to make per batch and where to send the ingredients. Finished goods must return to linked storage, or the network will never see the top-up.

Set a small target stock and take a few items out of it. Follow the order, the production and the return of the result. If the stock is forever short, look for a wrong address or an output outside the network. A gauge on a packager can run local storage: what it sees depends on where it stands.
codex.quest.create_packages.frogport.tex: A frogport sends and receives packages through a chain network. A first route needs two ports, two addresses and connected chain conveyors. Prepare both devices for now; they cannot move contents through empty space without transport.

Select a chain conveyor with the port item before placing the frogport nearby, then assign its address in the interface. A suitable inventory or packager can stand underneath. Repeat at the receiving end with a different address.

A package addressed elsewhere is sent onto the chain, while one matching the destination port is removed there. If a box spins in place, check for a reachable address and connected network. Begin with one shipment and a free receiver; accidental duplicate addresses make diagnosis harder.
codex.quest.create_packages.guide_addres: Manually verify the order reaches its specified address, unpacks and contains the ordered quantity

Before the factory starts ordering resources on its own, check one address from the ticker to the final chest. Put a little cheap stock in linked storage and clear the receiving packager. Write down how many items you expect.

Place one order with the exact frogport address. Follow the box as it is created, travels the chain, is received and unpacked. Compare the quantity at the recipient with the order, without mixing the trial with older contents.

Once the address and the contents match completely, confirm the goal by hand. If the box is stuck, find where it is first; ordering again only lengthens the queue. Check the address spelling, the chain connections and the free space. This test becomes the model check for every new recipient in the future factory.
codex.quest.create_packages.guide_repack: An order supplied by several stores may arrive as separate boxes, and that is awkward for machines that need the complete set of ingredients in a predictable order. A re-packager gathers the parts of one logistics order before passing it on.

Prepare a re-packager and a buffer inventory for incoming packages. Route the fragments there, attach the device and power it with redstone. It waits for all the parts and emits one combined package, so leave a clear output toward the next recipient.

Test a small order with ingredients from two linked sources. Do not substitute a missing fragment with a random box of similar contents: the device knows which order a part belongs to. Re-packaging helps in front of automatic crafters and is unnecessary for every simple single order.
codex.quest.create_packages.packager.tex: A packager takes items from an attached inventory and creates a package. When receiving a box, it can unpack contents back into storage. Prepare the device and a separate chest with a small inexpensive batch.

Attach the packager facing the chest and apply redstone for a simple shipment. A sign on the packager can supply an address; inspect the resulting package label before introducing it to transport. The box itself moves like an item.

Leave enough room in the destination inventory: a packager will not accept a box it cannot fully unpack. Test the first shipment on a familiar rig before enabling stock orders. An address does not automatically create a route; the next branch builds physical delivery between sender and receiver.
codex.quest.create_packages.postbox.text: A postbox transports packages using trains that stop at its linked station. It does not teleport a box to any other postbox. Prepare the red postbox and an existing route between two stops; a complete trial also needs a receiving postbox at the other end.

Select the station with the postbox item before placing it nearby, then assign an address. Packages addressed elsewhere wait for collection by a train, while those matching the receiving postbox are unloaded at its stop.

Send one inexpensive box and wait for the relevant service. Confirm that the train actually visits both stations and that the address matches exactly. Mail logistics can serve distant areas, but timing and capacity still depend on transport and free postbox space.
codex.quest.create_packages.requester.te: A redstone requester orders a configured set of items when signaled. It suits an installation that periodically needs the same ingredients. Prepare it after a successful manual ticker order, so delivery faults are not confused with control faults.

Bind the requester to the stock network and configure the order contents and destination address. For the first trial, select a small amount of inexpensive material and send one button pulse. Follow the complete route through unpacking.

Do not immediately connect a fast pulse generator: repeated commands can fill transport with unwanted boxes. Test sustained signals and missing stock before choosing a clear trigger from your machine. A requester does not automatically measure every production need; factory gauges provide the next approach to maintaining a target stock.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.0: A shop presents trading through the package network and is useful at a shared base. The red table cloth and desk bell requested are only part of the setup; working trade needs configured goods, exchange conditions and warehouse delivery. Start with an inexpensive test item.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.1: Connect stocked inventory to a packager and stock link, then bind a ticker in the shop. Place a mob or blaze burner in front as keeper. Interact with the keeper while holding the cloth to create an offer; after placing the cloth, set its price in the side slot. Put the bell somewhere accessible.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.2: Test a small purchase, including payment removal and package arrival. Avoid listing rare resources until conditions and destination are checked. Owning a bell does not create a store. After testing, the shop can provide standard consumable kits while you work elsewhere on the base.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.title: Shop
codex.quest.create_packages.stock_link.t: A stock link makes a packager’s inventory available to a shared ordering network. It transmits information and requests, not the items themselves. Prepare a link and a tested packager attached to a chest from which a small batch can be safely shipped.

A newly placed link creates a network. To add another component to the same network, bind it by interacting with an existing link first, following the item hints. The link must serve the intended packager, or the ticker will show the wrong stock.

Verify chest visibility through a connected ticker once available. Stock-network communication spans distances freely, but every box still needs a delivery route. Redstone can change priority or suppress stock broadcasting; if goods disappear from the list, inspect that connection too.
A stock ticker shows the stock of linked storage and places orders. Prepare a ticker and a shopping list, then bind the device to the right storage network. Before the first order, check the packager, the recipient’s address and the box’s physical route. Seat a creature or place a blaze burner in front of the ticker — it acts as the stock keeper.

Click the stock keeper, open the goods list, choose a little of a familiar material and set the delivery address. Watch the source store form a package and follow it to the receiving port. The shopping list is useful for recurring sets of parts.

If an order does not arrive, take it step by step: is the stock visible, was a box created, did it find its address, could it be unpacked. Do not fire off new big orders until the first one is found. A ticker simplifies supply, but it does not replace a clear store output and a roomy receiver.
codex.quest.create_packages.ticker.title: Stock Ticker
A crafting blueprint keeps a chosen recipe on the workshop wall, within reach. It helps make recurring parts from your inventory, but it remains a reminder, not a machine fed from the warehouse. Prepare a blueprint and the ingredients of one frequent recipe.

Hang the blueprint on an accessible surface and set the recipe in its interface. A simple part such as shafts makes a good first example; click the configured entry and check that the materials left your inventory.

If the item does not craft, compare your inventory with the recipe and check for free space. A blueprint does not bypass sequenced assembly, heating or the oversized mechanical-crafter recipes. Gather the truly frequent recipes on the wall and label them: a few clear entries speed up repairs better than a huge panel of unused ones.
codex.quest.create_tools.blueprint.title: Crafting Blueprint
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.0: A schematicannon constructs a placed schematic using supplied materials. It needs the cannon, a prepared schematic, gunpowder and accessible chests of blocks. Choose a clear site and inspect the entire preview first.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.1: Load the schematic into the cannon, review the material list and fill nearby supply inventories. Check existing-block replacement settings, which determine what happens to an already built area. Start construction only afterward.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.2: If work stops, read the missing material or reason in its interface instead of blindly adding gunpowder. The cannon neither creates rare components nor proves that a copied machine works. After completion, inspect transmissions, filters and container contents, then run a small batch just as you did with the original installation.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.title: Schematicannon
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.0: The extendo grip extends the reach of the item in your main hand. Craft it by the recipe, put it in the offhand and keep building blocks in the main hand. Make the first test at a wall on level, safe ground.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.1: Place and remove a block at a distance you could not reach before. Watch the grip’s durability. A charged backtank you are wearing may spend air instead of durability, so check its reserve before a long build.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.2: Two grips do not double every distance — trust the item’s own tooltip. Extra reach does not save you from falling and does not make the ground under you any safer. The tool shines when mounting ceiling transmissions and tall walls: you can work from a platform without scaffolding every block.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.title: Extendo Grip
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.0: The potato cannon fires suitable plant items. Craft it and bring ordinary potatoes, keeping your food reserve separate. Not every edible item makes a projectile, and each projectile flies differently.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.1: Choose a safe target away from animals, villagers and other players. Load a compatible crop as the tooltip says and fire a few single shots. Watch the ammunition and the weapon’s durability.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.2: A charged backtank can give the tool air, but it will not produce endless projectiles. Do not turn your only travel food into ammunition. The cannon suits ranged defence and experiments with different crops; test new projectiles at a separate range, not beside a wooden workshop.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.title: Potato Cannon
A schematic saves a chosen structure so it can be placed and built again. Prepare a schematic and quill and a schematic table. Start with a small proven installation with no valuable stock inside, so the boundaries are easy to check.

Mark two opposite corners of the area with the quill and save the schematic under a clear name. At the schematic table, load the file into a schematic item. Then place the preview on a free spot and check height, orientation and size.

A schematic does not replace building materials and does not carry container contents. Make sure the factory floor or a neighbour’s house does not sneak into it: extra layers complicate the build. A small press rig makes a good first copy, easy to compare with the original before meeting the schematicannon.
codex.quest.create_tools.schematic.title: Schematics
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.0: The wand of symmetry mirrors block placement around a configured plane. It suits facades, towers and matching building wings. Prepare the wand and a stock of inexpensive blocks; additional Survival copies require building materials.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.1: Use the wand on a surface to place its mirror, and open settings by sneak-using it. Keep the item on the hotbar. Place one block and check where its reflection appears before building an entire wall.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.2: If the copy enters another structure or goes underground, stop and adjust the plane. Remove the active mirror through its intended action afterward so unrelated building is not accidentally duplicated. Symmetry helps geometry but does not verify machine orientation: a mirrored transmission may need separate rotational adjustments.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.title: Wand of Symmetry
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.0: A toolbox carries several supply types and helps refill linked inventory slots nearby. This objective requires the brown variant, so check its color when crafting. Begin with shafts, cogwheels and building blocks.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.1: Place the toolbox beside the work area, divide items among compartments and link the required inventory slots through its intended controls. Start with one slot and confirm that it receives the chosen material.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.2: Refilling depends on toolbox availability rather than working from anywhere in the world. Before moving it, inspect contents and linked-slot behavior so your familiar tool arrangement is not disrupted. Avoid keeping your only expedition food there without checking access. A toolbox particularly suits long track or transmission projects that repeatedly need several component types.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.title: Toolbox
codex.quest.create_tools.worldshaper.tas: Read: the worldshaper is a Creative-mode tool and is not required in Survival
codex.quest.create_tools.worldshaper.tex: The handheld worldshaper is a Creative-mode tool for changing terrain with large brushes. It has no ordinary Survival acquisition recipe, so this is an informational quest with a manual “Read” confirmation. You do not need to search for it as the next mandatory item.

If working separately in a Creative test world, the tool samples material from a targeted block and applies a configured brush. Begin in a small area away from builds: a large terrain edit can affect more space than the aiming point suggests.

In your main Survival world, prepare factory sites with ordinary tools or contraptions already learned. Confirm reading once you understand the distinction. This quest requires neither command-giving the item, changing game mode nor demonstrating actual worldshaper use.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.0: A display board shows passengers station information without opening an interface. The four blocks in the objective make a small panel, but it does not know the schedule by itself — a display link to a supported railway source is needed.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.1: Place the board in a readable shape by the platform and connect the source through a display link. In the settings, choose station or train information and see whether the text fits. Widen the panel if necessary without blocking the walkway.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.2: Wait for a real arrival and compare what is shown with what happens. If the board is blank, check the source and the link target, not the number of blocks. Label the station name separately: a clear sign helps even when data is temporarily missing. This matters most once the base has several routes and shared platforms.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.title: Board
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.task.1: Manually: two bogeys stand on straight track within the station assembly area
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.0: A bogey is the carriage’s support on Create track; it is created in station assembly mode. Prepare two railway casings and enter that mode. No separate bogey item is needed.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.1: Apply a casing to straight track inside the marked station area, then place the second bogey on the same straight. Leave room between them for the intended carriage and inspect both positions before gluing on the body. If needed, the bogey variant changes with a click on the track.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.2: The book sees the casings in your inventory; confirm the placement by hand once two bogeys really stand on straight track inside the assembly area — two casings in a chest do not count. The next step adds the carriage and controls, after which the station assembles the train.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.title: Bogeys
This objective checks a freight schedule even though the quest title mentions a trial batch. Prepare one schedule item and two configured stations. Avoid loading a full wagon while stop conditions remain untested.

Add loading and unloading in journey order. Begin with understandable waits, then tune conditions to actual interface operation: the train must allow cargo transfer and be able to depart afterward. Check for a suitable conductor and controls facing both required directions.

Hold the completed schedule in your normal inventory for item credit, then give it to the operator. Inventory tracking does not validate the station list or prove transportation. Reserve a small clearly identified batch for the next trial, easily distinguished from previous stock in destination storage.
codex.quest.create_trains.freight_run.ta: Manually ship a small batch and wait for the return; check unloading, departure and an empty loading store
codex.quest.create_trains.freight_run.te: A freight route check is a completed transport cycle, not just having a train. Prepare a small known batch, a free output chest and a way to watch both stations. Before departure, make sure the operator already has the schedule.

Send the train with that batch and wait for it to return. Check the unloading, the departure condition and what happens when the loading store is empty. Cargo must not be lost through a bad docking, and the train must not wait forever for an amount the store will never provide.

Tick after these checks in the world. If the train did not come back, first open the schedule status: waiting for cargo, an unreachable route and an occupied signal are cured differently, and a faster locomotive removes none of them.
A freight route connects a material source to destination storage. Prepare the two stations and two portable storage interfaces listed, then choose a small train with attached storage. Serving several stops may require additional interfaces beyond the checked set.

Give stations clear names and align stationary interfaces with the onboard one at the stopping position. Connect loading at the source and extraction into a chest at the destination. Check each docking connection separately while the train is stationary.

Approximate placement along the platform is not enough: working faces must oppose one another at a valid distance. Allow transfer time and access to storage after disassembly. Items confirm equipment; schedule configuration and a real journey in the next quests will check whether cargo arrives.
codex.quest.create_trains.guide_passing_: Manually verify two opposing trains pass in sequence, never enter an occupied single-track section together, and continue their routes
Two opposing trains on one line need somewhere to pass. A signal cannot create that space itself. Prepare additional passing-loop track, signals and two small trains already tested individually.

Build a parallel section long enough for waiting and connect both ends. Divide occupancy with signals, checking displayed block boundaries and a free exit beyond junctions. Arrange directions so trains can wait without blocking each other’s exit.

Test an opposing journey slowly and confirm manually when both trains pass through in sequence without meeting on an occupied single-track section. If they wait for each other indefinitely, pause schedules and correct the signaling. Add freight after a successful trial while preserving enough waiting length for the complete train.
A Passing Loop for Two Trains
codex.quest.create_trains.guide_reverse_: A short railway branch often ends in dead ends from which the train must leave backwards. Prepare two controls blocks and check the length of the straights at both stations. The second controls settle the direction; they do not replace a reachable track or a correct schedule.

Disassemble the train at a station and install controls for both directions. Make sure they joined the connected structure, then assemble the train. Set up the conductor and the route so the required direction is available at every departure.

Drive to the second station by hand and come back first, then test the schedule. If the train will not leave, look at direction availability and the waiting conditions. Such a branch is a help at a mine, where there is no room for a big turning loop.
A Route Without a Turning Loop
codex.quest.create_trains.railway_casing: Railway casing is needed for stations and other train parts, and during assembly it turns into a bogey right on the track. Make four casings from sturdy sheets by the JEI recipe. Keep some material for the controls and the next station.

Craft the casings in the workshop first and take them into your normal inventory. Before the bogeys, pick a level stretch of future track: the station’s assembly area must fit the whole train, not just the cab.

Do not search the chests for a separate bogey item: in Create it appears when casing is applied to track in assembly mode. Nor does a casing become a finished locomotive. Four are enough to start a railway, and later machines have their own recipes and materials.
A schedule defines stations and waiting conditions for an automatic train. Prepare a schedule and a route between two stops that you have already tested manually. Execution needs a suitable conductor at the controls; a schedule in your pocket does not start the train.

Open the schedule, add stations in visiting order and choose understandable departure conditions. A short timed wait suits the first trip; later use loading, unloading or signal conditions. Give the schedule to the conductor through its supported interaction.

Watch a full circuit and confirm the train can depart in the required direction. If a station is unreachable, check connected track, control orientation and its name. Avoid waiting for an impossible cargo quantity: the train will obediently wait forever even when scheduling works correctly.
codex.quest.create_trains.schedule.title: Schedule
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.0: Railway signals divide a network into sections and control automatic train traffic. A track observer detects passing trains and serves a different purpose. Prepare two signals and an observer, then choose a simple, clearly visible section.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.1: Select track with the signal item and place the device nearby. Check its direction and the displayed section boundaries; study normal versus chained modes in Ponder before handling junctions and passing loops. Connect the observer to a separate lamp to test a passing event.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.2: Test one train before adding a second. Signals do not create a passing loop on single track or fix a route where two trains cannot physically pass. Avoid full-speed opposing trials. If a train remains stopped, inspect section occupancy and a free exit instead of removing every signal.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.title: Signals
A Steam ’n’ Rails conductor is a separate creature that you create and seat beside the train controls. For the blue cap, prepare blue wool, a saw, a deployer, a precision mechanism and string. The objective wants the blue variant specifically.

Cut the wool blank, then apply the mechanism and string according to the cap recipe. Click the finished cap on an andesite casing — a conductor appears. Also prepare the whistle and learn its actions in a safe area.

Seat the conductor at the controls of an assembled train and hand over a schedule. Test a short trip and the return. If the train will not leave, check the controls, station reachability and schedule conditions one by one before creating a second conductor.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_coupler.te: A Steam ’n’ Rails track coupler joins and separates suitable trains without fully disassembling them into blocks. The buffer in the second objective is end decoration and does not replace configured coupling machinery. Begin on a separate level track without regular traffic.

Select track with the coupler item and place it nearby. Use the wrench to choose coupling, decoupling or both, and scroll to set the distance between working pads. A station helps align the relevant train parts precisely.

Apply a signal only after correct alignment and stopping the test train. Check that the intended cars separated and that the remaining section has the required controls. Do not assume decorative buffers prevent every crash. This device suits a shunting yard after ordinary freight routing is reliable.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_handcar.te: A handcar is for short trips along the track and route inspection. Craft it by the Steam ’n’ Rails recipe and choose a clear straight away from automatic trains. The first try is easier before general traffic opens.
Put the handcar on compatible track and drive it following the game’s hints. Cover a short stretch, test stopping and coming back. Leave a spot nearby where you can calmly get off.

A small handcar is not invisible to other trains — never pull out in front of a freight train. Clear the route for a while before an inspection, or take a separate branch. A handcar helps spot awkward platforms, gaps and sharp kinks in the track, but a freight schedule is still tested with the train that will actually run it.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_style.text: Locomotive styling helps tell trains apart and makes the cab more welcoming for passengers. The coal smokestack in the objective is a Steam ’n’ Rails decorative part; the train can run without it, and it is no substitute for controls. Turn to the stack once the main route is proven.

Disassemble the train at a station and mount the stack where you want it on the body. Check that it joined the connected structure, does not block the driver’s view and leaves access to the controls. Then assemble the train again.

Look the train over on a straight and on a curve while keeping access to the freight interfaces. Do not widen the body hard up against the platforms: a new projection makes boarding awkward. Add decoration gradually, once the real station clearances and maintenance spots are known.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.0: A station sets a stopping point and opens the train assembly interface. Prepare two stations for the first route and a straight stretch of track long enough for the planned train. Give them distinct names right away — by the warehouses they serve, for example.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.1: Select a track section with the station item, then place the station beside it. Check the approach direction and open assembly mode at the first stop. The game shows the area where bogeys can be placed and the carriage built.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.2: Do not build the whole train until the area is chosen correctly: an accidental curve or a short straight makes assembly harder. Set up the second station as the destination and make sure a connected track runs between them. Test the route by hand with one train, and add the schedule after the train has visited both stops.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.title: Station
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.0: Sturdy sheets are used in railway equipment and come from sequenced processing of obsidian dust. First crush obsidian using its recipe, then prepare a lava-fed spout, a press and a safe workpiece route. Each sheet needs 500 mB of lava.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.1: Pass the dust through lava filling, then perform two pressing operations in order. Use two presses or send the workpiece through one press again; the important point is completing the second stroke.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.2: Separate finished sheets from unprocessed obsidian intermediates and collect eight. If processing stops, check spout lava and the item’s current stage. Keep lava in a closed pipe route and service it from a safe platform. This stock opens railway casings and the first trackside devices.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.title: Sturdy Sheet
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.0: Create tracks serve large trains and differ from ordinary minecart rails. Prepare thirty-two pieces, building blocks and a level area near the base. Make an assembly straight first, then a short route toward a second station.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.1: Place endpoints and connect them using the shape preview. Curves and slopes have geometric limits, so leave enough distance for gradual bends. Inspect the preview before confirming construction.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.2: Track placement does not promise finished supports, a safe bridge or sufficient materials. Build a foundation where players will walk and fence dangerous edges. If a connection fails, simplify the bend and check endpoint orientation. A straight test line lets you learn train operation before investing in an expensive mountain route.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.title: Tracks
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.0: A first train needs bogeys, a body joined to them and train controls. An ordinary Create train does not need an onboard boiler or electric motor to move. Prepare the controls and a small platform glued to the bogeys in the station area.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.1: Install the controls facing the direction of travel and assemble the train through the station interface. Then click the controls and set off carefully along the straight. To leave stations in the opposite direction too, add a second set of controls facing backward or build a turnaround.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.2: Fuel in assembled chests or barrels adds speed, but stopping and returning matter more at first. A decorative firebox does not count as an engine. The item objective only confirms the controls; make the first real trip by hand, before the conductor and the automatic schedule.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.title: First Train
codex.quest.create_world.arise.task.0: Manually find and inspect a Create structure in the world
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.0: Structures Arise scatters buildings with Create parts across the world: fluid tanks, windmills, houses and a lost railway station. They are finds for a traveller, not a promise of a working factory in every biome. Take food, light and something to note coordinates with.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.1: Explore new land by ordinary travel and look a discovered building over from outside. Enter carefully: the layout, enemies and loot differ every time. Trace at least one visible mechanism or railway detail before taking everything apart.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.2: Once a Create building is really found, tick the goal by hand. Save the spot for a second visit and note what you would like to repeat at the base. A chest does not promise schematics, and a standing mechanism may be waiting for its drive to be restored.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.title: Create: Structures Arise
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.0: Copper shingles and metal girders help finish a workshop and tell its zones apart. Make one of each item from the objectives — copper and the other materials by the JEI recipes. Start with a small sample wall or canopy.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.1: Place girders so they do not block access to shafts and valves. Judge the shingles in daylight; copper oxidises over time and changes its look, and suitable treatment locks in the state you chose.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.2: A decorative block does not become part of a contraption by itself: moving elements still need connecting. Do not hide temperamental parts behind pretty cladding, and keep walkways, inspection windows and flow labels. Once the palette is chosen, finish the factory so that its look helps maintenance instead of forcing you to strip the roof for one filter.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.title: Decorative Blocks
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.task.0: Manually find and inspect a rural Create structure
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.0: Rustic Structures adds rural buildings with Create elements: a barn, a smithy, a well and a windmill. Prepare for ordinary exploration rather than a search for one mandatory structure at guaranteed coordinates.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.1: Take food, a boat if it helps, and materials for a safe night. On finding a rural building, look at its surroundings, entrances and machine details. Do not assume all the decoration is powered or that a village must be living next door.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.2: The tick goes in after a real find. Save the coordinates and pick a useful idea for your own farm — a good approach to the barn or a spot for a windmill. A crafted casing is no substitute for the expedition: what counts here is your own inspection.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.title: Create: Rustic Structures
codex.quest.create_world.stickywheels.te: Sticky Wheels adds a sticky tire for Offroad wheeled vehicles. The installed recipe uses an ordinary Offroad tire with four honey bottles around it. Prepare those materials; the underlying wheel and vehicle belong to a separate transport system rather than Create train bogeys.
Craft the sticky tire and check its role on a small wheeled build using the relevant add-on’s hints. Choose a level clear area and a modest slope for testing, with enough stopping space.

Do not interpret “sticky” as guaranteed travel up any vertical wall or safe braking on every surface. Behavior depends on the complete vehicle and wheel contact conditions. The item objective confirms tire crafting; test the capabilities of your actual vehicle gradually before attempting a dangerous slope.
Aether accessories go into their own slots and each works differently. A Golden Ring is crafted from four Gold Ingots. An Ice Pendant turns up in dungeon loot, while a Golden Feather comes from silver rewards — the crafting table covers only one of the three.

Let each item register, then equip and test it separately. The pendant freezes water and lava beneath you, and the feather slows falling. Test the feather from a low height over safe ground before trusting it near a cliff, checking the functional slot.

A similar ring or another pendant behaves differently — do not assume effects by looks. Collect the three items gradually; what is ticked stays ticked. They add to protection and mobility, but keep building fences at the portal and bridges: an accessory will not find the way home for you.
codex.quest.dim_aether.accessories.title: Accessories
codex.quest.dim_aether.aether_portal.tas: Enter Aether through a water-activated Glowstone portal
codex.quest.dim_aether.aether_portal.tex: Build the Aether portal from Glowstone in a Nether-portal shape with a two-by-three interior. Activate it with a water bucket instead of flint and steel. Bring building blocks, food, and return supplies; supplement ordinary torches with local lighting later.

After crossing, fence the platform and record the portal position. Islands are separated by void and some creatures push players, so avoid unguarded edges. Prepare a parachute or another controlled-fall method before travelling far.

Falling out of Aether transfers you to the Overworld and may cause a dangerous landing, so it is no safe portal substitute. The objective records visiting the dimension. Test the return route, then collect nearby wood and establish a small supply cache.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.0: The Aether Altar enchants specific items and repairs suitable armour. Craft it by surrounding Zanite with Holystone and place it near Ambrosium storage. Put the input in its working slot and Ambrosium Shards in the fuel slot.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.1: The Freezer is a separate device powered by Icestone. Craft it from Holystone, Icestone, and Skyroot Planks. Test a simple freezing recipe rather than automatically feeding it the altar’s Ambrosium.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.2: The quest records both devices, but their roles and fuels differ. Enchant berries or Holystone for a first altar test before processing rare Gravitite. Separate raw materials from results to avoid confusing ordinary blocks with enchanted ones.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.title: Altar
codex.quest.dim_aether.bronze_dungeon.te: Recognise a Bronze Dungeon by its Carved Stone and the stone Slider’s chamber. Bring a durable pickaxe, armour, and healing; an ordinary sword cannot replace a mining tool against this boss. Beware of chest mimics in the corridors.

Start with a suitable pickaxe strike. The Slider charges along straight lines, so move sideways out of its path and strike between charges. Collect the Bronze Key after victory, let it register, and open the matching treasure.

The second objective’s Victory Medal comes separately from defeating a lesser Valkyrie in a Silver Dungeon. Bronze treasure does not substitute for it. Keep the first medal for the next trial; the Queen requires ten, linking preparation for two different dungeon types.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gold_dungeon.text: A Gold Dungeon houses the Sun Spirit in a Hellfire Stone chamber. Prepare healing, fire protection, and a reliable weapon. Interact through his warnings to issue the challenge; do not begin that conversation during an unprepared inspection.

Reflect one of his Ice Crystals back by striking it. A hit freezes the boss for roughly nine seconds, creating an opening for normal attacks. Avoid fire projectiles and spawned minions; ordinary snowballs do not replace this mechanic.

After the victory pick up the Gold Key and open the treasury. The Hammer of Kingbdogz from the extra objective lies among the bronze rewards, not with the Sun Spirit. Finish any missing bronze expedition separately and do not spend key loot until the book has ticked it.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.0: Gravitite is rare pink ore inside Aether islands. Mine it with Zanite or another suitable pick, checking overhead space first: an uncovered ore block can float upward. Prepare Ambrosium for processing before investing in distant mining.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.1: Put the ore into the Altar to obtain Enchanted Gravitite. Accumulate eight blocks in inventory, let them register, then use those same eight for the chestplate. Saved item detection means a duplicate batch is unnecessary.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.2: The high-jump ability belongs to a complete Gravitite armour set; a chestplate alone does not demonstrate it. Equip the piece and finish the set gradually. Test behaviour over a safe platform before relying on the armour to cross an island gap.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.title: Gravitite
codex.quest.dim_aether.guide_altar_heali: Enchant Holystone in the Aether Altar to obtain a Healing Stone. Prepare Holystone and Ambrosium Shards, place them in the appropriate slots, and wait for processing. This is a useful first operation before spending rare Gravitite.

Collect the stone and save it for dungeon recovery. It grants regeneration when consumed, so use it during a safe opening instead of expecting an instant rescue from the next heavy hit. Carry food separately because healing does not replace hunger restoration.

Refuel the altar after testing and prepare a small travel reserve. The item objective records one completed stone, while repeating the operation confirms production. This recipe links common local material with combat preparation and reduces dependence on random healing loot.
codex.quest.dim_aether.guide_first_parac: Cold Aerclouds around Aether islands provide material for a basic parachute. Collect them from a stable platform without removing your final foothold. Craft a Cold Parachute and keep it accessible before bridge building.
Test it during a short fall over a broad safe area. Confirm descent slows and learn its activation. The Cold Parachute is single-use, so craft another after the test for actual travel.

Owning the item records preparation, not timely deployment. Add bridge railings and do not expect a parachute to return you to an island after every knockback. Later silver rewards offer other slow-fall options; this consumable covers the dangerous early stage.
codex.quest.dim_aether.guide_medal_purse: Victory Medals come from duels with lesser Valkyries in Silver Dungeons. Collect ten together before challenging the Queen. Prepare armour and healing, inspect the space between pillars, and fight manageable individual duels.

Collect each medal and check weapon durability afterwards. A lance from bronze treasure helps with reach but does not replace collecting medals. Preserve a route to somewhere safe for recovery between fights.

Wait for the ten medals to be ticked and take that same stack to the Queen. The book remembers the quantity it has seen; a second stack for the count is unnecessary. With the batch ready, the terms of the challenge are clear, and you will not knock on the boss’s door without proof of your victories.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.text.0: The first tree of the Aether is the Skyroot. Its wood gives planks, sticks and a Skyroot Pickaxe, which already mines Holystone and Ambrosium Ore. Skyroot tools can double suitable natural drops, so the wooden pick will not be thrown away after you upgrade.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.text.1: Craft a Holystone Pickaxe from Holystone and keep looking for Ambrosium. Stone tools sometimes throw in extra shards just for working. Gather sixteen shards in one stack and show the book both picks; a registered tool can then be used without keeping a spare.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.text.2: Ambrosium is the local fuel, and an eaten shard restores a little health. Do not eat the whole reserve before you have made torches and started the altar. These two picks open Zanite mining and the first lit tunnels inside the island, well away from the edges.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.title: First Tools
codex.quest.dim_aether.lore.text.0: The Book of Lore describes Aether items and blocks. Craft it from a normal book and a suitable local material. It is especially helpful after early dungeons introduce unfamiliar accessories, tools, and unusual abilities.
codex.quest.dim_aether.lore.text.1: Open the book and place the item you want to inspect in its study slot. Begin with the Altar, Incubator, and a found accessory to compare fuel, purpose, and usage conditions without spending rare loot on random experiments.
codex.quest.dim_aether.lore.text.2: Obtaining the book completes the item objective, but read at least one useful entry before continuing. Its descriptions distinguish full armour sets from individual pieces and bronze rewards from silver ones. Keep it near portal storage for consultation after every expedition.
codex.quest.dim_aether.lore.title: Book of Lore
codex.quest.dim_aether.moa.text.0: A Blue Moa hatches from a blue egg laid by wild adult birds. Look for eggs on island surfaces without chasing birds toward dangerous edges. Prepare an Incubator, Ambrosium Torches as fuel, and Aechor Petals.
codex.quest.dim_aether.moa.text.1: Place the egg in the Incubator and wait for hatching. Feed the chick petals when it is ready to eat until it matures. Aechor Plants shoot poison, so collect petals with protection and healing, retaining four together for detection.
codex.quest.dim_aether.moa.text.2: Saddle the grown tame Moa and test on a broad island. Blue Moas have three midair jumps, white four, and black eight; these are limited sequences rather than endless flight. Assess distance and landing space and keep spare jumps for course corrections.
codex.quest.dim_aether.moa.title: Moa
codex.quest.dim_aether.silver_dungeon.te: A Silver Dungeon is an Angelic Stone Valkyrie temple. Defeat lesser Valkyries and collect ten medals to challenge the Queen. Prepare armour, healing, and a weapon with comfortable reach; the medal detected in the previous quest can join this reserve.

Speak with the Queen and present the required medals to start the duel. Maintain distance, track her movement, and avoid the next attack position. Collect the Silver Key after victory and use it on the reward chest.

The Valkyrie Helmet appears in silver rewards, while the Valkyrie Lance comes from bronze treasure. Neither is guaranteed in every chest; search another dungeon of the relevant type for missing items. Owning the lance neither summons the Queen nor replaces ten medals.
codex.quest.dim_aether.zanite.text.0: Zanite is Aether’s purple mineral for the next tool tier. Find its ore inside islands and mine it with a Holystone Pickaxe. Approach low veins carefully; the final stone block may conceal open void.
codex.quest.dim_aether.zanite.text.1: Collect eight gemstones together, let them register, and craft the Zanite Pickaxe. It becomes faster as it wears down, but that does not provide unlimited durability. Plan replacement before it breaks in a distant tunnel.
codex.quest.dim_aether.zanite.text.2: Repairing the pick reduces its speed bonus because that bonus depends on wear. Test mining safely. Zanite also supplies the altar and armour, so plan several short expeditions instead of spending your final gemstone on an arbitrary accessory.
codex.quest.dim_aether.zanite.title: Zanite
codex.quest.dim_end.dragon.task.0: Enter the End through the stronghold portal
codex.quest.dim_end.dragon.text.0: Before entering the End, bring ranged weapons, blocks, food, fall protection, and empty bottles. Set a respawn point near the stronghold in the Overworld. On arrival, assess the route from the obsidian platform and avoid looking at Endermen.
codex.quest.dim_end.dragon.text.1: Destroy tower crystals while keeping away from their explosions, then attack the dragon during suitable perching opportunities. When a purple breath cloud appears on the ground, use an empty bottle near its edge and retreat immediately.
