codex.quest.et_eden.aragotium.text.0: An Aragotium Ingot is a progression material, including one of the five Volcanech crystal components. While exploring Eden, preserve relevant raw materials and inspect the ingot’s acquisition method specifically, rather than recipes for similarly named armor.
codex.quest.et_eden.aragotium.text.1: Smelt Raw Aragotium in a furnace or blast furnace; alternatively, combine nine Aragotium Nuggets into an ingot. Take the output into your personal inventory before consolidating the entire batch into blocks.
codex.quest.et_eden.aragotium.text.2: Reserve at least one for the future crystal. Spend the rest on equipment after comparing recipes, preventing an early upgrade from forcing you to repeat the whole route for a mandatory next-world ingredient.
codex.quest.et_eden.aragotium.title: Aragotium
codex.quest.et_eden.crystal_eden.text.0: The Eden crystal is assembled at Sorcery level six. The creator’s five positions contain a Silver Block, Sunstone, Dragon’s Breath, another Sunstone and Monster Blindness. Two identical stones really are required in separate positions.
codex.quest.et_eden.crystal_eden.text.1: Collect Dragon’s Breath in the End using empty bottles at the dragon’s cloud, and save Sunstones from Nyetet. Do not replace the Silver Block with an ingot; inspect your Sorcery level on the board before assembly.
codex.quest.et_eden.crystal_eden.text.2: Take the crystal into your inventory for detection. It helps establish your own portal and later becomes an Unahzaal crystal ingredient, so preserve spare materials and the recipe information after construction.
codex.quest.et_eden.crystal_eden.title: Eden Crystal
codex.quest.et_eden.enter_eden.text.0: The first crossing into Eden begins with a finished Gardens of Eden Crystal: Sunstones go into its recipe but will not open the portal on their own. Find an Eden-brick frame in a structure on the outer End islands or build your own. Touch the crystal to the inside of a sound frame — that is where the opening appears.
codex.quest.et_eden.enter_eden.text.1: Prepare a Return Ticket and travelling supplies before activation. After entering, inspect the arrival point, mark the portal, and find a safe route to a Sunfurry settlement. The bright world still has dangerous island edges and hostile creatures; travel light on the first visit.
codex.quest.et_eden.enter_eden.text.2: The card checks the entry advancement and presence in Gardens of Eden. Then meet local traders and D’Kudja while maintaining a route home independent of story progress.
codex.quest.et_eden.enter_eden.title: Gates of Eden
codex.quest.et_eden.jaghax.task.0: Kill Jaghax, Chaotic Elemental; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_eden.jaghax.text.0: Jaghax is summoned with Jaghax’s Lamp specifically in Eden. Miguel describes the lamp as combining a Djinn Lamp, Fire Fuel and Soulbones; Sunfurry Messiahs can sell the latter. Prepare the components before selecting an arena.
codex.quest.et_eden.jaghax.text.1: Use the completed lamp in a spacious Gardens of Eden location after arranging healing and an escape route. It is linked to a creature in this dimension, so trying it at an Overworld home does not meet the summoning condition.
codex.quest.et_eden.jaghax.text.2: Defeat the opponent that comes out and check the kill advancement. A lamp made, or even used, is not enough for it. After the fight keep the drops and put your gear in order before going further into Eden.
codex.quest.et_eden.jaghax.title: Jaghax
codex.quest.et_eden.scorched.task.0: Find Scorched Lands Of Eden Biome
codex.quest.et_eden.scorched.text.0: Scorched Lands reveal another side of Eden and provide an exploration goal beyond settlements. Prepare food, blocks and a Return Ticket, then search for the Scorched Lands of Eden biome. Keep the portal route marked, especially across broken islands.
codex.quest.et_eden.scorched.text.1: Enter the right biome and wait for the advancement. One charred block or a patch of odd soil is not yet that biome; if in doubt, check its name on the map or the debug screen.
codex.quest.et_eden.scorched.text.2: Record the location and inspect accessible materials without needing a full clear. This reconnaissance point supports repeat expeditions, while the card itself is completed by visiting, not building or killing.
codex.quest.et_eden.scorched.title: Scorched Lands
codex.quest.et_eden.sunfurry.task.0: Make any of Sunfurry armor set
codex.quest.et_eden.sunfurry.task.1: Free the Altar of the Sun from the Eternal Dawn
codex.quest.et_eden.sunfurry.text.0: D’Kudja, the Sunfurry Grand Messiah, asks you to free the Altar of the Sun from Eternal Dawn. Find him in Eden and accept before fighting. Prepare weapons, healing and room around the altar, then defeat the creature occupying it.
codex.quest.et_eden.sunfurry.text.1: After victory, wait for D’Kudja and finish his conversation, which leads to the Drink of the Sun reward. Keep a bottle in your inventory for the item objective instead of drinking the last one before detection.
codex.quest.et_eden.sunfurry.text.2: Sunfurry armor qualifying for Eden Warrior is also required. Handing in the assignment alone therefore does not finish the whole card: check armor, story advancement and drink separately. Local traders can also help supply future summons.
codex.quest.et_eden.sunfurry.title: Sunfurry
codex.quest.et_eden.sunstone.text.0: Collect Sunstones after defeating Nyetet and save four individual pieces for this card. The internal item name contains nugget, but its displayed name is Sunstone; nine can also be combined into a building block.
codex.quest.et_eden.sunstone.text.1: Do not consolidate your whole reserve immediately. The Eden crystal needs two individual stones, and the block form cannot replace them in the recipe. Wait for item detection first, then divide your finds between travel and crafting.
codex.quest.et_eden.sunstone.text.2: If you reached this card through the End storyline without the stones, return to Purgatorium and prepare for Nyetet. Its proximity to Ancient Chorus links routes; it does not imply that ordinary chorus produces Sunstones.
codex.quest.et_eden.sunstone.title: Sunstone
codex.quest.et_farming.bugs.text.0: A Bug Net turns encountered insects into useful bait. Carry it while exploring vegetation and interact with suitable insects instead of attacking them with a normal weapon. Read the captured specimen’s tooltip.
codex.quest.et_farming.bugs.text.1: Different species have different Fishing Luck. Separate ordinary bait for test catches from rare bait worth saving for valuable fish. Luck improves probability; it does not guarantee a particular fish on the first attempt.
codex.quest.et_farming.bugs.text.2: This card only checks possession of the Bug Net. After obtaining it, catch at least one insect and use it in a prepared Fishing Net, making the tool part of a working supply chain rather than merely a collected item.
codex.quest.et_farming.bugs.title: Bug Net
codex.quest.et_farming.fishing_nets.text: A Fishing Net catches fish on bait without your rod. The ordinary net needs water on all four sides of the block and two levels below it. A shallow decorative pool looks suitable but does not meet that condition.

Catch an insect with a Bug Net, apply it to the Fishing Net and wait for a catch. Select bait by Fishing Luck when seeking a rare ingredient. The Nether Fishing Net is a separate device for its own environment; an ordinary catch does not replace obtaining it.
This card requests advancements for both nets. Establish regular fishing early: Nether Fish, for example, will be needed for the Rayana crystal.
codex.quest.et_farming.guide_bait_log.ta: Catch two insect species, compare their Fishing Luck and complete one fishing attempt with each
codex.quest.et_farming.guide_bait_log.te: Catch two different insect species and compare Fishing Luck in their tooltips. Note which is more common and which has better luck before spending them on the net. This supports choosing bait for future rare fish.

Check the water around the net and complete one catch with each bait type. Record results without assuming that a single lucky attempt proves a guaranteed rare catch. The statistic changes probability rather than promising a specific item.
Two catches done, the baits compared — you can tick it. Ordinary insects will do for everyday supply; save the rare ones for particular crystal ingredients.
codex.quest.et_farming.guide_first_harve: Grow and harvest a plant in a pot while keeping water and fertilizer above five

Choose one accessible plant supported by the pot and note its initial state. Add water and fertilizer until both values exceed five, then let it grow. Avoid changing several conditions simultaneously, which makes a stoppage difficult to diagnose.
Watch the reserves and wait for a finished harvest. If growth stops, inspect supplies, pot type and soil before relocating the whole setup.
Tick it only after you have gathered the produce. A pot with a pretty planting is not a harvest; this experiment becomes the baseline for checking the Irrigating and Fertilising Machines.
codex.quest.et_farming.guide_serviced_ha: Obtain another harvest with machine servicing and no manual water or fertilizer refills into the pot
Use the same pot and plant that already produced a manual harvest. Add service from Irrigating and Fertilizing Machines, fill their reserves and make sure the pot lies inside their operating area.
Do not refill the pot by hand during the next cycle. Watch its reserves and machine consumption so you can distinguish actual servicing from growth using old leftover water.

A second harvest with replenishment working — and the goal is met. If the machines are empty or too far away, fix one cause and repeat the cycle. What matters to the book is the servicing, not two expensive blocks beside the bed.
codex.quest.et_farming.machines.text.0: Irrigating and Fertilizing Machines help service pots when manual refilling starts interrupting other work. First achieve normal growth in a single pot: a machine cannot fix an unsuitable plant or an overlooked planting condition.
codex.quest.et_farming.machines.text.1: Obtain both devices, position them according to the operating area shown in their interface and fill them with the required supplies. Watch whether water and fertilizer reserves change in the selected pot; an installed machine may still be empty.
codex.quest.et_farming.machines.text.2: These advancements check obtaining the machines, not automatic harvesting. For your own verification, leave a plant for a full growth cycle and confirm that servicing continued without manual refilling.
codex.quest.et_farming.machines.title: Machines
codex.quest.et_farming.pets.text.0: This peaceful branch contains two distinct actions: pet a Raccoon and tame every Gultrav type required by the advancement. Start with the Raccoon: interact and confirm that petting occurred instead of accidentally striking it.
codex.quest.et_farming.pets.text.1: Gultrav types require separate searching and taming. Track credited varieties in the advancement display; several identical pets do not replace a missing type. Provide safe accommodation for earlier pets before searching for another.
codex.quest.et_farming.pets.text.2: This is a gradual exploration goal, not necessarily one short outing. Check the two advancements separately: success with the Raccoon says nothing about whether every required Gultrav variety has been tamed.
codex.quest.et_farming.pets.title: Pets
codex.quest.et_farming.pot.text.0: Three pot types support different plant groups: ordinary, Nether and extraterrestrial. Start with a normal Gardener’s Pot and an accessible plant, then make the others as their materials become available. One pot type does not satisfy all three objectives.
codex.quest.et_farming.pot.text.1: Plant the specimen and add water and fertilizer. Both reserves must exceed five for growth to begin. Soil occupies a separate slot and speeds cultivation; check the chosen plant’s requirements before selecting it.
codex.quest.et_farming.pot.text.2: The objectives are three pot acquisition advancements, but wait for a real harvest to establish reliable supply. Reserve some produce for replanting and check resource consumption before your next expedition.
codex.quest.et_farming.pot.title: Gardener's Pot
codex.quest.et_gear.accessories.task.1: Get Thinking Stone by defeating Unahzaal with -100000 Humanity
codex.quest.et_gear.accessories.text.0: Celestial Sphere, Thinking Stone and an immunity accessory belong to different stages. Thinking Stone is particularly late: its advancement description links it to defeating Unahzaal at −100000 Humanity. Do not search for it as an ordinary early mineral.
codex.quest.et_gear.accessories.text.1: Choose an accessible immunity accessory for an effect your next expedition actually needs and check equipment conditions. Some protection depends on a set or a particular way of wearing it; an amulet in a backpack does not always mean active immunity.
codex.quest.et_gear.accessories.text.2: Obtain the three marks gradually. Preserve Thinking Stone for Gauntlet of the Destinies if you plan to craft it; this collection checks acquiring items, not making your character completely invulnerable.
codex.quest.et_gear.accessories.title: Accessories
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_early.text.0: The early collection includes Charged Copper, Forest Ranger and Treasure Hunter Armor. Start with an accessible complete set after comparing materials and bonuses, rather than making one random piece from every series. Charged Copper requires all four pieces.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_early.text.1: Wear the Forest Ranger and Treasure Hunter sets to trigger their advancements. Mixed equipment may protect you without satisfying a particular series check.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_early.text.2: Inspect tooltips after each mark and decide which set should remain your working equipment. The collection does not require wearing every option permanently; switch complete sets carefully and preserve a spare before the next expedition.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_early.title: Early Armors
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_late.text.0: The late card requires Truadamantite and Ergosphere Forged Armor. Wear the complete Truadamantite set; the Ergosphere objective checks obtaining all four pieces. A collection of attractive helmets or an arbitrary mixed set does not replace these conditions.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_late.text.1: Truadamantite uses a composite recipe of metals, Brimstone Fungi and Phantom Membranes. The Ergosphere set belongs to late Arkemer technology, so return for it after opening the Aetherium Forge and material sources.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_late.text.2: Study Ergosphere configuration through its controls or a Smartphone before use. Life Support and black-hole protection are described separately; acquisition does not verify that every protective ability is enabled and used correctly.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_late.title: Late Armors
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_mid.text.0: The middle collection — Dark Mage, Warlock, Whaler and Runic Armor. Each set suits its own occupation: the Runic one is especially good for gathering runes, and do not expect identical bonuses from the rest, however similar the names.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_mid.text.1: Assemble one full set, wear it and wait for its advancement before moving to another. Store every piece near your changing area so forgotten boots do not hold the check open.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_mid.text.2: Four marks establish familiarity with distinct equipment options. Choose an appropriate effect for an expedition and check durability; the newest set is not necessarily best for every situation.
codex.quest.et_gear.armors_mid.title: Mid Armors
codex.quest.et_gear.fun.task.0: Make Smartphone to configure some Arkemer technologies
codex.quest.et_gear.fun.task.1: Get All Of The Lava Lamps
codex.quest.et_gear.fun.text.0: Smartphone, lamps and Energy Drink form a calmer collection, but the Smartphone has a practical use: it configures Arkemer and Ergosphere Armor, Gauntlet of the Destinies and certain late items. Obtain it before changing complex equipment settings.
codex.quest.et_gear.fun.text.1: Collect every lamp variant required by the advancement, not only the ordinary Lava Lamp. Check the missing variants list: it includes water, snow, blood, acid, Liquid Aetherium and other contents.
codex.quest.et_gear.fun.text.2: The Energy Drink has to be drunk — merely holding it is not enough. Check the three groups of goals separately; the lamp collection can grow at leisure while the Smartphone is already configuring your working gear.
codex.quest.et_gear.fun.title: Curiosities
codex.quest.et_gear.guide_spare_chest.ta: Leave spare weapons, armor, food and route supplies at respawn; verify access without the main Portable Chest
codex.quest.et_gear.guide_spare_chest.te: Portable storage should not be the only place containing every useful possession. Prepare spare weapons, armor, food and route materials near your respawn point. An ordinary home chest is suitable.

Check access to this reserve while setting your main Portable Chest aside. If the ticket, tools and only food are all inside it, the backup route is not ready. Divide supplies by purpose without duplicating every rare artifact.

Access checked — tick it. There is no need to die on purpose: it is enough to be sure you can get back on your feet without the contents of your main backpack and without a risky trip for a first pickaxe.
codex.quest.et_gear.ranged.text.0: The Collector hands over Atimite’s Crossbow in exchange for its broken artifact and three Ancient Coins. Do not throw the damaged find away — the restoration starts with it. Read the terms of the trade before paying.
codex.quest.et_gear.ranged.text.1: Rocket’s Gun is crafted from late materials including Mystic Essence, Danger, Fobastone, a Crystal of Eternity, Quantum Distabilizer, Fotium and a Nether Star Plate. This is a separate recipe rather than another crossbow trade.
codex.quest.et_gear.ranged.text.2: Obtain both weapons for their advancements. Then test ammunition and controls in a safe area; preserve Rocket’s Gun if you intend to make the Arkemer Aleph Railgun.
codex.quest.et_gear.ranged.title: Ranged
codex.quest.et_gear.storage_et.text.0: Portable Chests expand expedition capacity without constant warehouse visits. The ordinary version uses a Chest, two Chains and four Leather. The large version needs two Chests, an Iron Block, two Double Chains and four Leather.
codex.quest.et_gear.storage_et.text.1: Obtain both variants in turn and open them somewhere safe. Insert a few inexpensive items, close and reopen the container to understand handling before transporting unique trophies.
codex.quest.et_gear.storage_et.text.2: The advancements check chest possession, not the safety of your entire haul. Separate supplies from discoveries and keep personal inventory slots free for bosses whose banners must be picked up.
codex.quest.et_gear.storage_et.title: Portable Chests
codex.quest.et_gear.weapons.text.0: Ammit Staff, Khonshu Staff, Bloody Anchor and Hoz de Muerte use distinct blueprint recipes. Obtain their blueprints through archaeology first and preserve originals. Sharing the weapon category does not mean all four assemblies have the same base.
codex.quest.et_gear.weapons.text.1: The staffs use a Lunar Battle Torch and Truadamantite; the anchor uses an Echo Anchor and Crystals of Eternity; the scythe uses Volcanech materials, a Flame Sphere and Uranium. Prepare radiation protection for Uranium handling; the earlier unprotected experiment is not repeated here.
codex.quest.et_gear.weapons.text.2: Take each finished weapon into your inventory and check all four advancements. Read its skill, essence and usage requirements before combat.
codex.quest.et_gear.weapons.title: Weapons
codex.quest.et_intro.bard.task.0: Give a coin to the Bard
codex.quest.et_intro.bard.text.0: The Bard offers a peaceful break between assignments. Bring a coin, find the Bard among the residents and give it through interaction. Watch the character’s response and advancement notification: dropping a coin on the ground is not payment.
codex.quest.et_intro.bard.text.1: The second goal is a separate musical item, the Guitar. Find its recipe or a trader’s offer and keep the Guitar in your inventory until the book ticks it. The Guitar and the coin for the Bard are two different stories: one does not close the other.
codex.quest.et_intro.bard.text.2: This is optional. It introduces the idea that peaceful interactions also have advancements, and that coins have uses beyond buying combat equipment.
codex.quest.et_intro.bard.title: Bard
codex.quest.et_intro.coins.text.0: Ancient Coins and Gold Coins are the money of Eternal Tales. You pick them up in structures and after fights, and it pays to compare traders’ offers before buying: they are different coins, with no common currency between them.
codex.quest.et_intro.coins.text.1: Obtain both kinds and wait for their two advancements. Store reserves separately from ordinary gold; an ingot, nugget and Gold Coin are different items. Keeping some currency for story purchases is useful.
codex.quest.et_intro.coins.text.2: In particular, avoid spending your last Gold Coin before Purgatorium: its wanderer sells a part of the Fallen Rune. This reserve can save you a return trip in the middle of preparations for Nyetet.
codex.quest.et_intro.coins.title: Coins
codex.quest.et_intro.guide_return_report: Open the Journal after handing in Aeter’s assignment and verify its completed entry

After Aeter’s first assignment, open the Journal and locate its completed entry. Compare it with your actions: accepting the request, placing the Jukebox and returning for the conversation. These are three parts of one story, not interchangeable ways to earn a reward.
Look at the active assignments: is there an unfinished stage left? If so, go back to the character and finish the dialogue — a second Jukebox made at random will not help.

Confirm manually after checking the completed entry. This habit helps in every dimension: inspecting the Journal after reporting back is easier than remembering a forgotten conversation many hours later.
codex.quest.et_intro.journal.text.0: The Journal collects Eternal Tales character assignments and reminds you where to deliver your finds. Craft a Notice Board from any plank and paper, then combine it with a normal book. Make another board to place in your base: the first is consumed by the Journal recipe.
codex.quest.et_intro.journal.text.1: Open the Journal, then find a character with an assignment and agree to help. Aeter in Eternal Town is a convenient starting point. Crafting the book alone does not mean you have accepted a quest.
codex.quest.et_intro.journal.text.2: This card requires both the Journal in your inventory and the first accepted assignment advancement. Check the active entry after your conversation; it will help you resume the story after a long expedition.
codex.quest.et_intro.journal.title: Journal
codex.quest.et_intro.miguel.task.0: Summon Miguel by right-clicking an Eternal Banner with a chicken egg
codex.quest.et_intro.miguel.text.0: Miguel explains bosses, shows related items and directs your first major expedition. This objective specifically requires summoning him. Find an Eternal Banner and right-click it with an ordinary chicken egg, as stated by the advancement.
codex.quest.et_intro.miguel.text.1: Summon the storyteller somewhere safe where you can find him again. After he appears, open his dialogue, read the first assignment and remember the route to your home or town. Meeting an existing Miguel does not replace the required action.
codex.quest.et_intro.miguel.text.2: Before visiting Vivid, ask about the maze and Cobalt Pickaxe. The items section becomes useful later when an unfamiliar trophy turns out to be part of another boss’s summoning method.
codex.quest.et_intro.miguel.title: Miguel the Storyteller
codex.quest.et_intro.notice.text.0: The Notice Board combines the mod’s reference manual, skill information and several interface settings. Paper and any plank are enough to craft it. Place it somewhere you regularly return to and open the skills section.
codex.quest.et_intro.notice.text.1: Development points belong to Eternal Tales’ own system, so vanilla experience levels above the hotbar cannot replace them. Earn a skill point through gameplay, then choose and increase a skill on the board.
codex.quest.et_intro.notice.text.2: This card checks both possession of the board and a completed upgrade. Reading the manual does not satisfy the second objective. Pay particular attention to Sorcery: its levels will be needed when crafting dimension crystals.
codex.quest.et_intro.notice.title: Notice Board
codex.quest.et_intro.quests_all.text.0: This card concludes Eternal Tales’ story assignments and remains open for most of your journey. Check the Journal after each world: an unfinished conversation with the quest giver can hold back an advancement even after the required enemy is defeated.
codex.quest.et_intro.quests_all.text.1: Complete the Overworld, Nether, End and subsequent dimension storylines, then return to the later Aftermath story. Do not expect to finish this goal before the individual lines; its position near Miguel introduces a long-term objective rather than an imminent ending.
codex.quest.et_intro.quests_all.text.2: Once all assignments are handed in, check the overall advancement itself. Collected trophies or a list of defeated bosses do not replace completed character quests.
codex.quest.et_intro.quests_all.title: All Quests
codex.quest.et_intro.starter.text.0: The Starter Kit is an item containing a selection of supplies, not a mandatory progression stage. If you received one at the start or among your rewards, keep it in your inventory long enough for the book to detect it. This card does not itself provide a kit.
codex.quest.et_intro.starter.text.1: Open it somewhere peaceful with free inventory slots. Sort the contents by purpose: consumables are useful on the road, while spare equipment belongs near your respawn point.
codex.quest.et_intro.starter.text.2: Lacking a kit does not prevent you from meeting Miguel or developing skills. This optional stop encourages checking reward contents before an expedition and avoiding lost supplies in an overcrowded inventory.
codex.quest.et_intro.starter.title: Starter Kit
codex.quest.et_intro.town.task.0: Complete Aeter’s assignment: craft and place a Jukebox, then finish the conversation
codex.quest.et_intro.town.text.0: Eternal Town serves as a regular meeting place with characters, not merely a landmark. Find it while exploring the Overworld, record its coordinates and speak to Aeter. Her Musicians Town assignment asks you to craft and place a Jukebox.
codex.quest.et_intro.town.text.1: The Jukebox takes eight planks and a diamond. Accept Aeter’s request first, then build it and come back to finish the conversation. A Note Block will not do here: she wants a Jukebox and nothing else.
codex.quest.et_intro.town.text.2: This card checks the completed story assignment, so simply visiting town does not count. Afterwards, meet the other residents: Miguel’s storyline begins here, and the town provides a useful destination for future returns.
codex.quest.et_intro.town.title: Eternal Town
codex.quest.et_karvat.crystal_kar.text.0: The Karvat crystal requires Sorcery level eight, like Rayana. Its creator ingredients are Darkplasm, Soulbone, a Comet Crystal, Spore Edennus and a Crimson Eel. Comet Crystal here is a separate material, not the Comets dimension crystal.
codex.quest.et_karvat.crystal_kar.text.1: Collect ingredients from routes already open and prepare the fish and plant in advance. If the recipe fails, compare full item names first: the shared word crystal can conceal the wrong component.
codex.quest.et_karvat.crystal_kar.text.2: Collect the output and keep it in your inventory for detection. Next, prepare a Karvat portal and supplies for the temples; owning the crystal does not complete a dimension visit or Gulibeg’s assignment.
codex.quest.et_karvat.crystal_kar.title: Karvat Crystal
codex.quest.et_karvat.enter_kar.text.0: A Karvat portal, a Return Ticket and supplies for several temples — that is what you need before crossing. Once there, write down the coordinates and look around before going far from the arrival point. A temporary camp is handier than moving the whole base.
codex.quest.et_karvat.enter_kar.text.1: Find Gulibeg and speak to him: his assignment supplies the basis for later summons. Do not replace this conversation with random gems from other worlds, because the quest giver’s power is part of the required recipes.
codex.quest.et_karvat.enter_kar.text.2: The card credits the entry advancement and presence in Lands of Karvat. Then prepare temples and gems; victories over the gods are checked separately by the next card.
codex.quest.et_karvat.enter_kar.title: Ancient Dimension
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.task.0: Free Karvat from Enicrih!; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.task.1: Kill Haciru; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.task.2: Kill Hirots; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.task.3: Kill Ikkorh; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.task.4: Kill Arla; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.text.0: Accept Gulibeg’s assignment and preserve the power pieces he gives you. Combine them with Topaz, Turquoise, Garnet and Corundum to make distinct summoning items for the four lesser gods. Match each item to its temple before use.
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.text.1: Find the temples of Arla, Haciru, Hirots and Ikkorh, prepare their surroundings and complete four battles. Do not spend their power trophies on unrelated crafting: they are needed together for the next step. Check the relevant advancement after each fight.
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.text.2: Combine the acquired powers and summon Enicrih in his temple. The objective list’s order does not mean he is summoned first. After the fifth victory, return to Gulibeg to finish the separate story assignment.
codex.quest.et_karvat.gods.title: Gods of Karvat
codex.quest.et_karvat.guide_temple_map.t: Accept Gulibeg’s assignment, record four temple coordinates and match each with its required power piece

Separate reconnaissance from spending summoning items. After speaking to Gulibeg, locate the four lesser-god temples, record their coordinates and match their names to the prepared powers. Know the route between them and your return point before activation.
Look over each arena, noting dangerous creatures and narrow exits. Do not pour every rare component into one unlabelled field chest: a reserve sorted by temple guards against a mixed-up summon.
Confirm after recording four sites and checking the corresponding items. No kills are required here; the result is a prepared route that makes the main god sequence orderly and understandable.
Free Lands of Karvat from Enicrih
Talk with Guligeg and get piece of his power
Divine Power concludes by returning to Gulibeg after defeating the four lesser gods and Enicrih. Save the quest giver’s coordinates from the beginning and track the active Journal entry. A collection of boss victories alone does not hand in the assignment.

After the final battle, collect the required trophies and return for the conversation. Finish the dialogue, then check the Karvat quest advancement and acquisition of a Piece of Gulibeg’s Powers. Do not discard it immediately after the notification.
Completion confirms both the story and its associated reward. Sort leftover temple materials before moving toward Volcanech: some will support later recipes and side branches.
codex.quest.et_karvat.karvat_quest.title: Divine Power
codex.quest.et_karvat.khogachi.task.0: Kill Khogachi; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_karvat.khogachi.text.0: Khogachi is a large relative of Khoirin and a separate miniboss. Miguel associates its legends with Amber’s Yasiden Forests; do not treat it as a required Karvat temple god. Return to this side hunt after opening the appropriate route.
codex.quest.et_karvat.khogachi.text.1: On reconnaissance watch the big bird’s name; bring ranged weapons and healing, and pick ground where a hit will not throw you into the abyss. Ordinary Khoirin do not count for the advancement — do not chase them instead of Khogachi.
codex.quest.et_karvat.khogachi.text.2: Defeat Khogachi specifically and save its feathers and other trophies. The card checks a miniboss kill rather than visiting a forest; its mark distinguishes a completed hunt from merely encountering the creature.
codex.quest.et_karvat.khogachi.title: Khogachi
codex.quest.et_karvat.quetzal.text.0: In the installed version, Quetzalcoatl and Chac-Mool belong to the late Arkemer storyline. This card collects two victories rather than requiring an unknown temple in Karvat. Continue Aftermath through the choice of allegiance and the automaton encounters.
codex.quest.et_karvat.quetzal.text.1: Once a story encounter begins, follow the dialogue and prepare for opponents appearing in its arena. Leave retreat space from Chac-Mool’s close attacks in particular, and arrange repairs and healing before the next scene.
codex.quest.et_karvat.quetzal.text.2: Check both marks by boss name. Ordinary creatures with similar appearances do not replace these story encounters, and the card’s placement in Karvat does not change the actual route into their battles.
codex.quest.et_karvat.quetzal.title: Quetzalcoatl
codex.quest.et_nether_end.end_quest.task: Bring Vital Soup for Ancient Enderman
codex.quest.et_nether_end.end_quest.text: The Ancient Enderman in the End asks for Vital Soup to restore the Ancient Chorus he guards. Find him, accept his request and record the meeting place. Speaking first and delivering afterwards is more reliable than bringing arbitrary food without an active assignment.
Prepare Vital Soup specifically and give it to the quest giver. Finish the dialogue, then obtain an Ancient Chorus Fruit. An ordinary Chorus Fruit does not satisfy this storyline’s item objective.

Check the End quest advancement and the required fruit in your inventory. Ancient Chorus helps travelers against Portal Sickness, so preserve its source rather than treating the first fruit as disposable story clutter.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.endacea.text.0: Endacea offers another way of moving around the End. Look for the Eternal Tales creature specifically, prepare a safe place for interaction and read any available interaction hint. Even a peaceful transport experiment can cause a fall near an island’s edge.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.endacea.text.1: Mount the Endacea and confirm that you are actually riding it. Approaching, feeding or simply interacting does not necessarily satisfy the advancement. Check the controls and dismount onto solid ground.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.endacea.text.2: This card requires riding, not killing or obtaining an item. Once you understand the controls, decide whether Endacea suits your route; a Return Ticket remains useful as an independent way home.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.endacea.title: Endacea
codex.quest.et_nether_end.guide_warlock_: Prepare a vertical stack, bottom to top: Polished Blackstone, Polished Blackstone Bricks, Gilded Blackstone, with a clear arena

The column for the Piglin Warlock is built in a proven order: Polished Blackstone at the bottom, Polished Blackstone Bricks above it, Gilded Blackstone on top. Similar black blocks are not interchangeable — the summon checks this exact stack.
Later, use Nether Chronicles on the upper gilded block. For now, building the pedestal and clearing its surroundings is enough; do not begin the fight without healing and repaired armor.

Confirm the manual objective after checking the three-block order and free space. Item objectives ensure materials, not correct construction. This example helps diagnose failed summoning without randomly rebuilding neighboring walls.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.nether_res.tex: This expedition basket combines Bonespur, Nether Fish and a Nether Fire Moss Block. Check full item names: decorative moss, an individual plant and the required block are not always interchangeable. Prepare a Nether Fishing Net and suitable bait for the fish.

Collect materials in a safe order and mark gathering sites for repeat visits. One of each satisfies the current objective, but a small reserve saves another trip when you start assembling several crystals.
Fire Moss is needed for Purgatorium, while Nether Fish is needed for Rayana. Completion confirms the stored items and Bonespur advancement, not the operation of a fishing setup.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.nether_tower.t: Open the Clocktower with four keys and obtain the Hellish Clock

The Piglin Clocktower is secured by four locks. Find it in the Nether and obtain keys from Hell Overseers in the Blazing Wastes. Mark the tower and your route before hunting so you do not lose your way with the collected keys.
Although the item objective displays one Hellish Key, the story’s tower opening requires four. Gather the complete set, open the locks in sequence, then explore the tower and finish its assignment.

Avoid spending every key before the item objective registers. This card requires both a key and the Nether storyline advancement; discovering the building alone does not finish the hidden crown’s story.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.tsar.task.0: Kill Tsar Of Piglins; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_nether_end.tsar.task.1: Kill Piglin Warlock; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_nether_end.tsar.text.0: For Piglin Warlock, build a vertical stack from bottom to top: Polished Blackstone, Polished Blackstone Bricks and Gilded Blackstone. Use Nether Chronicles on the top block; the book is consumed. Prepare armor, Fire Resistance, healing and an open arena before activation.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.tsar.text.1: The Tsar of Piglins is summoned with the Staff of the Circle of Flames on a Hyacinthum Netherite Block — a different item and a different build, so beating the Warlock does not close the second goal. Check the materials and look over the arena before the second fight.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.tsar.text.2: Collect trophies and check each advancement after victory. In Eternal Darkness, the Tsar summon also involves an enhanced Warlock; deliberately choose the mode when preparing your first normal attempt.
codex.quest.et_nether_end.tsar.title: Tsar of Piglins
Kill Ravrite Queen; collect the boss banner in your inventory
Kill Dreadful Sapling; collect the boss banner in your inventory
Kill Grotesterk, The Stormtiger; collect the boss banner in your inventory
This collection combines bosses from different stages, and their names do not imply a shared summoning method. The Ravrite Queen is associated with Amber’s Ravrites. Grotesterk is also summoned in Amber using a Storm Rune dropped by Amber warriors in the maze, castle and Xaxxas’s summoned forces.
The Dreadful Sapling is grown separately: its seeds drop from the Halloween Spirit, then go into a Gardener’s Pot supplied with water and fertiliser. Keep that bed well away from peaceful crops.
The book needs three victories, and you will return to this card from other chapters. Before heading for Vivid, do not look for these creatures next to your first base — they do not live there.
codex.quest.et_overworld.bosses_ow.title: Overworld Bosses
codex.quest.et_overworld.interdim.text.0: The Interdimensional Creator combines five components into crystals and checks your personal Sorcery level. Obtain the device and place it at your base. A Return Ticket makes a useful first product: it requires Sorcery level one and helps you return from expeditions.
codex.quest.et_overworld.interdim.text.1: The ticket uses a Cobalt Nugget, Bricks, a Book and Quill, a Hay Bale and a Basalt Ingot. Arrange them according to the creator’s recipe and collect the output. Do not confuse the Bricks block with an individual brick item.
codex.quest.et_overworld.interdim.text.2: Try the ticket after a short trip and see where it brings you back. The book needs the device, the ticket and the advancement for using it: a ticket lying in a chest will not test the way home.
codex.quest.et_overworld.interdim.title: Interdimensional Creator
codex.quest.et_overworld.moons.task.0: Make The Blood Moon Rise By Using Bloody Totem
codex.quest.et_overworld.moons.task.2: Make The Blue Moon Rise By Using Blue Totem
codex.quest.et_overworld.moons.text.0: Lunar events change the composition and danger of nighttime enemies. Before summoning one, prepare a lit shelter, food, healing and an escape route; an unfinished village is an awkward testing ground. Use the appropriate summoning item for the chosen event.
codex.quest.et_overworld.moons.text.1: This card lists Blood, Blue and Clown Moons, plus a separate Blood Moon survival objective. Calling an event and surviving its night are different conditions; the first notification does not complete every goal.
codex.quest.et_overworld.moons.text.2: Check the current moon on the board and inspect advancements afterwards. Pause between events to repair equipment and sort drops: different nights provide different materials for later recipes.
codex.quest.et_overworld.moons.title: Lunar Events
codex.quest.et_overworld.ores.task.3: Get Uranium without Radiation protection from Elementary Gem
codex.quest.et_overworld.ores.text.0: Cobalt and Ruby expand your tool selection, and a Cobalt Pickaxe is needed to awaken Vivid. Explore ores, check their mining requirements and craft both listed pickaxes. Avoid exhausting the necessary tool immediately before visiting the maze.
codex.quest.et_overworld.ores.text.1: The fourth objective is intentionally hazardous: obtain Uranium without the Elementary Gem’s radiation protection. That is an advancement condition, not the recommended way to routinely handle Uranium. Prepare healing, free storage and a way to remove the material from your inventory promptly.
codex.quest.et_overworld.ores.text.2: Restore protection after the brief check. The card does not require prolonged exposure; completion uses separate advancements for Cobalt, the tools and this experiment.
codex.quest.et_overworld.ores.title: New Ores
codex.quest.et_overworld.seasonal.task.0: Kill Ekatebrina; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_overworld.seasonal.task.1: Kill Halloween Spirit; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_overworld.seasonal.text.0: Halloween Spirit is called with its special item at night. Miguel explains that the summoner is made from spirits’ Ectoplasm and additional materials; his summoning description does not require the calendar month of October. Prepare a nighttime arena and healing before activation.
codex.quest.et_overworld.seasonal.text.1: Ekatebrina has several tiers, but this card requires the first victory named by its advancement. The later Ice Dragon and Everfrost Serpent belong to separate fights and do not replace this objective. Choose the summoner for the correct version.
codex.quest.et_overworld.seasonal.text.2: Check both victories separately. Keep the Halloween Spirit’s drops: its Dreadful Seeds grow a Dreadful Sapling in a pot, and with it the neighbouring boss collection continues.
codex.quest.et_overworld.seasonal.title: Seasonal Bosses
codex.quest.et_overworld.vivid.task.0: Kill Vivid, God of Life; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_overworld.vivid.text.0: Vivid lives in his own Overworld maze; Miguel describes a large fortress in forests or plains. Awakening him requires a Cobalt Pickaxe because cobalt breaks down the mask restraining him. Bring a serviceable pickaxe, armor, healing and building blocks for safe progress.
codex.quest.et_overworld.vivid.text.1: Clear passages and remember the exit first, then interact with the statue using the required tool. The maze contains many enemies, so beginning the boss encounter with crowded corridors is dangerous.
codex.quest.et_overworld.vivid.text.2: After victory, collect Vivid’s Oathsword and check both objectives. Killing the boss and obtaining the sword are tracked separately. Return to Miguel and proceed to preparing the Interdimensional Creator.
codex.quest.et_overworld.vivid.title: Vivid
The Purgatorium crystal requires Sorcery level four and five components: a Nether Fire Moss Block, Skylite Ingot, Lapsidian Ingot, Aerolite Ingot and Hellrock Block. The last is crafted from nine individual Hellrock obtained from the living Rock-Blaze.
Lapsidian can be prepared before entry: two Lapis Blocks and two Obsidian produce dust that smelts into an ingot. Arrange the ingredients in the Interdimensional Creator and collect the crystal.

The portal is built from the matching bricks; bring a stock of light and a Return Ticket. The book looks at the crystal itself, the entry advancement and your presence in Purgatorium. Once across, set up a safe corner and only then look for the rune parts.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.guide_hellroc: One Hellrock introduces the exchange, but the Purgatorium crystal needs a full block of nine. While Rock-Blaze is alive, hold Asteroid Stone in your main hand and repeat right-click interactions, collecting the dropped result.

Each interaction consumes one Asteroid Stone. Watch your health and preserve a safe retreat rather than risking everything for the final piece. Avoid finishing the boss before obtaining the batch if the exchange can be completed safely.
Wait for nine-stone detection before combining them into a block on the crafting table. This prevents the common recipe mistake of putting an individual stone into the creator instead of a block.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.guide_rune_pa: Collect the three Fallen Rune parts without immediately combining them. The first comes from Rock-Blaze, the second is crafted from Phantom Souls, Agates and Blood Stones, and the third is bought from Benny Lafitte for a Gold Coin.

Lay them together and compare names. Missing the second means gathering materials and crafting; missing the third means finding the trader and payment. Repeating Rock-Blaze for every missing component is ineffective.
Combine the parts after all three item marks register, then prepare Nyetet’s altar. This stop distinguishes loot, crafting and trading within a single summoning item.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.hellrock.text: Hellrock is not made on an altar: right-click the living Rock-Blaze with Asteroid Stone. First defeat the Terrible Tree in Comets and bring a reserve of Asteroid Stone. Then find a Nether Hellish Dungeon containing a Hellish Altar.

Craft Hell Fire from Fireoil, two Fire Charges, Comets Glowlichen, Skylite, an Ashy Scarab and Aerolite. Apply it to the altar after preparing the arena; the fire is consumed, and your personal victory over the Tree is mandatory.

While the boss is alive, hold Asteroid Stone in your main hand and interact: one stone is consumed and Hellrock drops nearby. Obtain nine for the Purgatorium crystal’s block even though this objective requests one. Only then finish the fight.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.lapsidian.tex: Lapsidian serves both gear and travel, and the first ingot can be made without having been to Purgatorium. Two Lapis Blocks and two Obsidian give Lapsidian Dust; smelt it. That way one component of the entry crystal is ready in advance.
The second objective is Soulbone. Save qualifying drops and inspect traders’ offers; Miguel states that Sunfurry Messiahs in Eden sell these bones. Do not confuse them with ordinary skeleton bones.
Both items are needed for this card. Reserve Soulbones for Rayana and Karvat crystals and Lapsidian for later tools; the objectives share a card, but their acquisition methods differ.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.nyetet.task.0: Kill Nyetet, the Fallen Guardian; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.nyetet.text.0: Summon Nyetet by using a completed Fallen Rune on a Purgatory Altar. Find this altar in Purgatorium and check its full block name: Rock-Blaze’s Hellish Altar serves another summon. Clear nearby enemies and mark an exit before activation.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.nyetet.text.1: Apply the rune to the altar; it is consumed, and the boss appears above the area nearby. Keep healing accessible, maintain retreat space and avoid spending a spare summon while the first fight is still active.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.nyetet.text.2: Wait for the advancement after victory and collect the Sunstones. They support access to Eden and its crystal. Secure the drops before continuing Purgatorium exploration or its story assignment.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.nyetet.title: Nyetet, the Fallen Titan
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.quest_purg.ta: Help Heveline to heal her brother
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.quest_purg.te: Heveline and her sick brother live in a ruined Purgatorium house. Speak to her and accept the request for five Leviathan Blossoms. Mark the house first: finding it again from memory after searching dark terrain is inconvenient.

Collect five Leviathan Blossoms and return them to the quest giver. Check the flower’s name rather than relying only on appearance. Avoid using finds in other recipes before reserving the complete delivery.

Hand over the flowers and finish the conversation to receive the Purgatorium quest advancement. Carrying the plants alone is insufficient. Afterwards, keep a separate crafting reserve and prepare for the next dimension.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.rock_blaze.ta: Defeat Rock-Blaze; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.rock_blaze.te: Rock-Blaze is summoned in a Nether Hellish Dungeon by applying Hell Fire to a Hellish Altar. The summoner must already have the Terrible Tree advancement. If the altar refuses, check that personal victory: somebody else’s trophy or purchased fire does not replace it.

Clear the approaches and prepare armor, Fire Resistance, healing and an exit before summoning. While the boss remains alive, obtain the Hellrock you need by right-clicking it with Asteroid Stone in your main hand. A dead boss cannot perform this exchange.
Keep room to move, watch your health and avoid trapping yourself beside lava. After victory, collect the first Fallen Rune part and check the kill advancement.
Next, combine nine Hellrock into a block, craft the Purgatorium crystal at Sorcery level four and continue assembling the rune for Nyetet.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.rune.text.0: The Fallen Rune consists of three distinct parts. The first is a guaranteed Rock-Blaze drop. Craft the second from three Phantom Souls, four Agates and two Blood Stones; it is a recipe, not a random drop of the finished part.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.rune.text.1: Purgatorium’s wanderer Benny Lafitte sells the third for a Gold Coin. Find him, complete the trade and save his coordinates for future summons. Ordinary gold ingots do not replace the currency.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.rune.text.2: Combine the three parts in a shapeless crafting recipe and keep the completed rune in your inventory for detection. Do not use it before finding the Purgatory Altar and a safe fighting area: the next step consumes the rune and begins the Nyetet encounter.
codex.quest.et_purgatorium.rune.title: Fallen Rune
codex.quest.et_rayana.crystal_ray.text.0: The Rayana crystal requires Sorcery level eight. Prepare Darkplasm, Soulbone, Destroyer’s Eye, Sunhog Leather and Nether Fish. Check the fish reserve beforehand: establish a net before assembly instead of searching for a fishing site after filling the other slots.
codex.quest.et_rayana.crystal_ray.text.1: Destroyer’s Eye has its own advancement in this card. Pick it up into your personal inventory before using it in the recipe, then arrange the five components in the Interdimensional Creator.
codex.quest.et_rayana.crystal_ray.text.2: Collect the finished crystal and check both marks. It opens the jungle route but does not prove that you have visited Rayana: the portal and first crossing belong to the next objective.
codex.quest.et_rayana.crystal_ray.title: Rayana Crystal
codex.quest.et_rayana.enter_ray.text.0: For your first Rayana expedition, bring a Return Ticket, lighting and consumables for extended exploration. Prepare a portal using Rayana bricks and activate it with the matching crystal. Leave rare materials unnecessary for reconnaissance at home.
codex.quest.et_rayana.enter_ray.text.1: Mark the portal on arrival, survey the jungle and seek a Daredian settlement to begin the assignment. Avoid using discovered summoning items among homes: first identify the altar’s purpose and the future battle site.
codex.quest.et_rayana.enter_ray.text.2: Completion requires the entry advancement and presence in the dimension. Finish reconnaissance with a clear route between the portal and quest characters; it will help when returning after defeating Pterion.
codex.quest.et_rayana.enter_ray.title: Jungles of Rayana
codex.quest.et_rayana.kraken.task.0: Kill Infected Kraken; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_rayana.kraken.text.0: Summon the Infected Kraken in the Overworld on a Mucunfectio Beach during rain. Look for an infected beach with blue sand, not Rayana’s jungle. Find the correct biome first and mark a safe approach to the water.
codex.quest.et_rayana.kraken.text.1: Kraken Bait is crafted from Prismarine Shards, Infected Shrimp, Bone Shards, Infected Meat and a Sea Prism. Prepare it alongside ranged weapons and healing, wait for rain and use it on the suitable beach.
codex.quest.et_rayana.kraken.text.2: After victory, check the kill advancement and the separate Mucunfectio discovery objective. Ordinary fishing bait does not replace Kraken Bait; dry weather or the wrong biome explains a failed summon.
codex.quest.et_rayana.kraken.title: Infected Kraken
codex.quest.et_rayana.pterion.task.0: Kill Pterion; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_rayana.pterion.task.1: Free Rayana from Pterion and his Vampirism
codex.quest.et_rayana.pterion.text.0: First accept the Daredians’ assignment to free them from Pterion. Summoning requires a Bloody Eye; locate the Aede temple in Rayana by cobblestone pillars projecting from the ground. Find its Bloody Altar and mark the exit route.
codex.quest.et_rayana.pterion.text.1: Clear the surroundings and prepare ranged weapons, ammunition and healing before applying the Eye: the enemy is a giant bat. Use the Eye on the correct altar and fight where you can see the boss and move freely.
codex.quest.et_rayana.pterion.text.2: Check the kill advancement after victory, then return to the Daredians and report success. This card also requires completing the Rayana assignment, so moving immediately to another dimension leaves it unfinished.
codex.quest.et_rayana.pterion.title: Pterion
codex.quest.et_rayana.vampirism.text.0: The Bloody Eye summons Pterion; becoming a vampire is not required for this item objective. Prepare four Vampyre Jewels, two Topaz, two Turquoise and a Fermented Tarantula Eye. Hunt vampires for the jewels while keeping healing available.
codex.quest.et_rayana.vampirism.text.1: The Fermented Tarantula Eye occupies the center, Vampyre Jewels form a cross around it, and Topaz and Turquoise alternate in the corners. Craft the Bloody Eye and wait for book detection first.
codex.quest.et_rayana.vampirism.text.2: Save it until you locate the Bloody Altar in an Aede temple and accept the Daredians’ request. Crafting enables a fight rather than proving victory; prepare a safe arena and return route separately.
codex.quest.et_rayana.vampirism.title: Vampirism
codex.quest.et_rayana.volkihar.text.0: Volkihar is a craftable item, not an advancement for meeting another vampire. Its recipe combines a Blood Bender, four portions of Vampyre Blood, two Neuro Elements and two Sanguinite Alloy Ingots. Prepare the base item separately from consumable materials.
codex.quest.et_rayana.volkihar.text.1: Place Blood Bender in the center, blood in a cross around it, and Neuro Elements and ingots in the corners. Check the precise blood and alloy types: similar vampire trophies are not interchangeable.
codex.quest.et_rayana.volkihar.text.2: Obtain the completed Volkihar in your inventory and wait for the advancement. Read its tooltip and choose a safe target before use; the card checks acquiring the item rather than mastering every ability.
codex.quest.et_rayana.volkihar.title: Volkihar
Excavate Suspicious Block by Venetium or Truadamantite Brush

Archaeology improves by carefully excavating suspicious blocks with a Venetium or Truadamantite Brush. Take one of these brushes on an expedition and search for suitable archaeological blocks instead of breaking them with a pickaxe alongside their surroundings.

Clear space around the find and continue brushing until its item is extracted. Touching the block or merely owning the tool does not complete the advancement; finish an excavation with a qualifying brush.

Blueprints can appear among your discoveries. Save useful ones for crafting, and later recycle spare copies in a Shredder for skill progress. One expedition can then support both your collection and further development.
codex.quest.et_skills.archery.text.0: Archery develops through ranged and throwing weapons. Begin with a weapon whose ammunition you can replenish, and practise against ordinary enemies while keeping your distance. This skill also contributes to gem processing at the Jewelry Table.
codex.quest.et_skills.archery.text.1: The card’s objective is to obtain qualifying archery armor. Before crafting, check the set’s purpose and the advancement’s accepted items: arbitrary armor worn while carrying a bow does not become archery armor.
codex.quest.et_skills.archery.text.2: Wait for the advancement after obtaining it and compare the equipment tooltips. Continue developing the skill for gem quality and Archer Gloves, as well as the damage of your first bow.
codex.quest.et_skills.archery.title: Archery
codex.quest.et_skills.digging.text.0: Digging develops through mining ores; higher levels improve the chance of an extra piece of raw material. Start in a safe mine with a suitable pickaxe, lighting and food. Surrounding stone provides access to veins, but every cobblestone block should not be treated as a skill exercise.
codex.quest.et_skills.digging.text.1: Mine ore and compare the board’s value until you obtain the first Digging level. Then obtain a Digging Chest: this is a separate item objective, not an ordinary chest holding mining supplies.
codex.quest.et_skills.digging.text.2: Both marks are required. After the first level, gradually move to more valuable veins; bonus drops help supply later crafting without building another production system.
codex.quest.et_skills.digging.title: Digging
codex.quest.et_skills.fear.text.0: Fear works only while Eternal Darkness is enabled. Its protective effects appear at three health points or fewer: Speed, Strength and Night Vision depend on skill level. This is emergency help in a dangerous state, not a reason to keep your health low continuously.
codex.quest.et_skills.fear.text.1: The skill grows through kills made under the Fear effect. Study it later when you can heal and retreat safely; intentionally taking damage before a powerful boss is a poor training method.
codex.quest.et_skills.fear.text.2: This card checks only activation of Eternal Darkness with its totem, not a Fear level. Prepare a Totem of Eternity to reverse the mode before enabling it, and read the dedicated difficulty chapter.
codex.quest.et_skills.fear.title: Fear
codex.quest.et_skills.fishing.text.0: Fishing and insect catching are related but separate skills. Catch insects with a Bug Net, then use them as bait in a Fishing Net. Better bait Fishing Luck raises the chance of rare fish, so saving a rare insect for a desired catch is sensible.
codex.quest.et_skills.fishing.text.1: Place the ordinary net in water, with water on all four sides and on two levels beneath it. Apply your caught bait and wait for a result without draining the area.
codex.quest.et_skills.fishing.text.2: This card checks the Fishing Net, Bug Net and Fishing Chest. It does not check the catch itself; complete a trial catch to make sure future ingredients can be obtained reliably.
codex.quest.et_skills.fishing.title: Fishing and Catching
codex.quest.et_skills.growing.text.0: Growing is tied to mod plants cultivated in a Gardener’s Pot. Make an ordinary pot, place a suitable plant on top, and add water and fertilizer. The manual says growth begins when both reserves exceed five; this refers to resources in the pot, not a requirement for Growing level five.
codex.quest.et_skills.growing.text.1: Soil can occupy a separate slot to speed growth. Monitor supplies and wait for a harvest before concluding that the setup works. A planted specimen without water does not provide sustainable production.
codex.quest.et_skills.growing.text.2: The card requires the pot advancement and a separate Growing Chest. The skill and working planter will support crops from later dimensions.
codex.quest.et_skills.growing.title: Growing
codex.quest.et_skills.level.task.0: Gain any Eternal Tales Skill Boost effect
codex.quest.et_skills.level.text.0: Eternal Tales development distinguishes activity experience, skill level and points distributed through the Notice Board. Open it to inspect your starting values, then mine some ore or practise another activity to see which value changes.
codex.quest.et_skills.level.text.1: This card, though, asks for something else — a boost effect for any skill. Find an item whose tooltip says Skill Boost outright and use it as intended. An ordinary Bottle o’ Enchanting gives vanilla experience and does not count here.
codex.quest.et_skills.level.text.2: Check your active effects and the advancement. A boost is useful before the corresponding work; receiving the effect does not permanently increase every skill.
codex.quest.et_skills.level.title: Player Level
codex.quest.et_skills.slaying.text.0: Slaying grows with every creature you defeat. According to the reference, points depend on the enemy’s maximum health divided by twenty, so ten zombies and ten sturdy beasts give a different gain.
codex.quest.et_skills.slaying.text.1: Record your level on the board and fight enemies your equipment can reliably handle. Arrange lighting, retreat space and healing first; a dangerous boss is unnecessary for an introductory exercise. Check the value again after several fights.
codex.quest.et_skills.slaying.text.2: This objective is manual: confirm it only after your Slaying skill actually increases. The skill will later be needed for emblems, making it useful to develop alongside story expeditions.
codex.quest.et_skills.slaying.title: Slaying
codex.quest.et_skills.sorcery_skill.text: Sorcery is needed for more than weapons: its levels unlock dimension crystal crafting. Mining Rune Stones found across the mod’s worlds is an early source of development. Bring a pickaxe and collect a dropped rune.
Later, using sorcery items and weapons also develops the skill. Do not confuse essence reserves with skill level: a full container does not unlock a recipe if your personal skill is too low.

This card requires obtaining a rune and a Sorcery Chest. Afterwards, move on to the Extraction Cauldron and watch your level on the board: Comets requires level two, while Purgatorium requires level four.
codex.quest.et_skills.speech.task.0: Complete a trade with an Eternal Tales trader
codex.quest.et_skills.speech.text.0: Speech develops through trades with Eternal Tales traders and grants discounts on some offers. Find one of these traders and inspect the stock before spending currency. A trade with a normal vanilla villager does not replace the required interaction.
codex.quest.et_skills.speech.text.1: Pick a useful purchase you can afford, prepare the required currency and complete the exchange. Make sure the money is gone and the goods are in your inventory: an open trade window is not yet a deal.
codex.quest.et_skills.speech.text.2: Confirm this card manually after trading with a mod character. To observe skill development, compare values before and after several trades: one purchase need not grant an entire level.
codex.quest.et_skills.speech.title: Speech
codex.quest.et_sorcery.altars.text.0: Eternal Tales altars have different purposes and interaction conditions. This card specifically requests an Arei Altar; a Rock-Blaze or Purgatorium altar is not a substitute, even if it resembles the same kind of stone structure.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.altars.text.1: Get the Arei Altar block and keep it in your inventory until the book ticks it. Before setting it up for real, find out what activates it and clear the space: a ticked block is not yet a fight begun.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.altars.text.2: Store summoning items beside a label naming their intended altar. This helps prevent confusing a device with its consumable or wasting a rare item at the wrong site while preparing future expeditions.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.altars.title: Altars
codex.quest.et_sorcery.astral.text.0: The Astral Enchanter improves gear in its own way. The block takes bone blocks, runes, chiseled stone bricks and Geobstractsite. Set it up at your base and start not with your only weapon but with something spare.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.astral.text.1: Open the interface, choose a compatible upgrade and prepare the materials it lists. Check the result before confirming: the station’s name does not mean that every item accepts every enchantment.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.astral.text.2: The goal is to enchant an item at this very station. Take the result, check how its tooltip changed and that the advancement has appeared. The block in your inventory or an enchanted book brought along will not stand in for that.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.astral.title: Astral Enchanter
codex.quest.et_sorcery.books.text.0: Spell books provide specific magical effects and differ in how they are used. Choose your first book for a clear purpose, such as an exploration aid, and read its tooltip carefully: not every book works indefinitely or without consumables.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.books.text.1: Obtain an Eternal Tales sorcery book specifically. An ordinary enchanted book belongs to a different system. Before use, check essence requirements, possible item consumption and the intended target, then test it somewhere safe.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.books.text.2: This objective only requires the advancement for obtaining a qualifying book; successful use is not checked separately. Understanding one effect makes it easier to judge expensive spells and avoid wasting supplies.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.books.title: Spell Books
codex.quest.et_sorcery.cauldron.text.0: The Extraction Cauldron turns runes into essence reserves. Craft it from an ordinary cauldron, iron plates and glass panes. Place the device, open its interface and add runes while monitoring the corresponding essence.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.cauldron.text.1: Once reserves exceed twenty, the reference describes transferring essence into Soul Sand Bottles. Prepare containers in advance: an installed station does not itself provide a finished essence gem.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.cauldron.text.2: For the second objective, craft an actual gem: four Ayeris Bottles and an Essence Shard, for example, combine into an Ayeris Gem. Obtain it in your inventory and check the advancement. A filled bottle and a gem are different outputs in this processing sequence.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.cauldron.title: Extraction Cauldron
codex.quest.et_sorcery.matrix.text.0: Runic Matrix is an armor enchantment that improves rune collection and Sorcery development. There is no separate machine with this name to build. Find an available way to obtain the enchantment and check for it in the item tooltip.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.matrix.text.1: The second objective concerns Runic Armor. Prepare the set’s materials and obtain the pieces named by the advancement. A full-set effect cannot be tested using only a helmet stored in a chest: wear the required equipment for practical work.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.matrix.text.2: After both objectives register, return to a familiar Rune Stone deposit. These improvements support regular sorcery supplies, so assess them over several mined stones rather than a single random drop.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.matrix.title: Runic Matrix
codex.quest.et_sorcery.rituals.task.1: Duplicate a blueprint on the printer
codex.quest.et_sorcery.rituals.text.0: Despite the title Rituals, this card checks a blueprint and its duplication. Start with archaeology: finish excavations using a suitable brush and save any blueprint found, especially when you cannot yet craft its item.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.rituals.text.1: The blueprint printer will ask for copying materials — they are listed in its window. Put in the original, print and take the copy. Do not feed your only valuable blueprint to the Shredder: there it turns into experience and vanishes.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.rituals.text.2: The book needs two events: any blueprint obtained and a copy made on the printer. Boss summons and altars have nothing to do with it. Copies build a crafting reserve and protect rare finds.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.rituals.title: Rituals
codex.quest.et_sorcery.runes.text.0: Runes come from Rune Stones, with varieties tied to their place of origin. Start with accessible Overworld stones, use a pickaxe and collect the drops. Exotic runes will later require trips to other dimensions.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.runes.text.1: A Rune Bag helps prevent different rune types from filling your inventory. Obtain it and organize your reserves, but make sure you have actually picked up a rune for the first advancement. A similarly colored decorative block is not a Rune Stone.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.runes.text.2: Rune Prospector on the pickaxe and Runic Matrix on armor help with larger batches. Your stock will feed the Extraction Cauldron while also supporting Sorcery development.
codex.quest.et_sorcery.runes.title: Runes
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aetherium.text.0: Aetherium is an Arkemer crafting material. One confirmed acquisition route converts Ageagoria Anthem into one Aetherium; preserve late-story materials and inspect their uses before spending a unique find.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aetherium.text.1: A separate advancement requires all four Aetherium-Imbued Arkemer Armor pieces. Assemble the helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots, obtaining each in your inventory. One chestplate does not count as a full set.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aetherium.text.2: Wear the set for practical use and study its configuration; some settings are controlled through a Smartphone. The objectives check the material and armor collection rather than activation of every ability. Prepared equipment makes the other Arkemer devices safer to explore.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aetherium.title: Aetherium
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aftermath.task.0: Complete the Aftermath storyline and uncover Arkemer history
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aftermath.text.0: After defeating Unahzaal, explore the Overworld: Miguel points to new traces of his dimension. Aftermath leads through ship wreckage, meetings with A’Hisi, further fragments and an allegiance choice in the Arkemer story. Follow the active Journal entry and record each discovery’s coordinates.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aftermath.text.1: Finish your chosen route; the Aetherium Forge is associated with its reward and is needed by many items in this chapter. Do not wait to complete every technology card before beginning the story itself.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aftermath.text.2: The Flecheresha Stone trial is separate and brings back strengthened opponents. Prepare an arena and full consumable reserves before activation. Collect the Eternity Banner after passing, then check both advancements: finishing Aftermath does not replace the trial.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.aftermath.title: Aftermath
codex.quest.et_ultimate.arkemer_tech.tex: These four devices are made in the Aetherium Forge opened by the later story. Their base pattern uses an SSD, Aetherium and a source item: Hammer of Eternity for the Quarry, Tiger Rune for the Gravicycle, Rocket’s Gun for Aleph and an Atomic Bomb for Heavenbreaker.

Gather the inputs in advance: the hammer from the neighbouring card is needed before this collection closes. Take each result into your inventory. The Quarry starts with a right-click and digs a 3×3×3 area, so try it on a separate site.

Advancements check acquisition, not weapon use. There is no need to launch Heavenbreaker near your base for credit. Configure transport and tools first, and investigate destructive functions only with prepared distance and protection.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.blackhole.text.0: The Stabilized Miniature Black Hole is a summoning weapon. The Aetherium Forge makes it from an Infinity State Drive, Arkemer Cube Harness and Strangelet. Its tooltip requires Slaying level twenty-five for use; owning the item does not remove that threshold.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.blackhole.text.1: The summoned hole fights for you for two minutes. Do not confuse it with dangerous world black holes, which require an Arkemer Quarry for handling. Prepare a complete Ergosphere set and check its protection functions before experiments.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.blackhole.text.2: The second objective requires obtaining all four Ergosphere Forged Armor pieces. Their tooltips describe Event Horizon Limitation and Life Support; configure the set before approaching hazards. The card does not automatically verify a successful safe experiment.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.blackhole.title: A Black Hole in Your Hands
codex.quest.et_ultimate.crystal_ult.text: The Ultimate World crystal combines the Unahzaal, Rayana, Karvat and Purgatorium crystals with The Ultimate Bricks. These bricks occur in the Ultimate Portal structure and also among Crabzilla’s drops; they are not ordinary bricks or interdimensional stairs.

Let the brick block register first, then use it in the recipe: the guide remembers previously detected items, so no spare block is needed for completion. Arrange the five components in the Interdimensional Creator and collect the crystal.

Both items are required for completion. Avoid dismantling your only usable transition without a prepared replacement; the finished crystal helps establish your own route, while the next card separately checks visiting the world.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.emblems.text.0: The Grand Emblem combines an Orange Emblem, Grand Marvel and Grand DC Emblems, a Starly Emblem and a Crystal of Eternity. Obtain it first: it is the next upgrade’s base, and its own advancement should register before consumption.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.emblems.text.1: Make the Arkemer Emblem in the Aetherium Forge from an SSD, Grand Emblem and Aetherium. Then an Infinity State Drive, Arkemer Emblem and Strangelet make the Singularity Emblem. The actual upgrade order matters more than the objective list’s order.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.emblems.text.2: Check all three advancements and skill requirements before use. Grand Emblem requires Slaying level ten, and its flight unlocks after defeating Unahzaal. Owning the final emblem does not automatically explain earlier controls.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.emblems.title: Emblems
codex.quest.et_ultimate.enter_ult.text.0: Enter the Ultimate World with repaired equipment, healing and an independent return method because it contains late materials and hazards. Prepare the appropriate transition and leave unique future recipe trophies in storage.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.enter_ult.text.1: Record your coordinates on arrival and identify a safe area for initial reconnaissance. Collect samples gradually; unusual technologies and black holes require suitable equipment rather than merely the strongest ordinary pickaxe.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.enter_ult.text.2: The card checks changing dimension to Ultimate World and being there. Then pursue Aetherium and Arkemer recipes while continuing Aftermath for the Aetherium Forge; a visit does not automatically grant every technology.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.enter_ult.title: The Ultimate World
codex.quest.et_ultimate.guide_smartphone: Configure worn Arkemer or Ergosphere Armor, test flight and disable ground ignition near the base

The Smartphone is more than a collection item: it controls Arkemer and Ergosphere Armor settings. Wear the prepared set, open configuration and find movement and additional-effect options. Check assigned keys in the game’s controls.
Test enabling and disabling flight on safe ground, not over the void. Disable ground ignition around your home base and verify that ordinary movement leaves no fire behind.

Tick it after checking the settings and safe movement. A Smartphone in your pocket does not guarantee the right configuration; deliberately saved settings beat an ability that switched itself on halfway home.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.hammer.text.0: The Hammer of Eternity combines a Chainsaw, Pickaxe of Eternity, Khartthone, Shovel of Eternity and Axe of Eternity in a shapeless recipe. Prepare those five tools and a spare working set first: assembly consumes the originals.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.hammer.text.1: The Hammer later becomes an Arkemer Quarry ingredient, so obtain it in your inventory and wait for its mark before upgrading. This card’s position after technologies does not prevent crafting the necessary Hammer beforehand.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.hammer.text.2: The Divine Pickaxe and Divine Hoe are separate goals; they do not come out of the hammer by themselves. Check the three advancements and try the tool on a small patch before digging wide next to your buildings.
codex.quest.et_ultimate.hammer.title: Hammer of Eternity
codex.quest.et_ultimate.ultimate_items.r: The absolute ceiling of Eternal Tales
codex.quest.et_ultimate.ultimate_items.t: Apply the Order of the Universe page to a Notice Board

This long-term collection includes The Ultimate One, The Ultimate Two, Gauntlet of the Destinies, Heart of the Elements, The First Prism and learning Order of the Universe. Begin with one chosen item and preserve its inputs: expensive assemblies can consume useful artifacts.

The Gauntlet uses a seven-slot Aetherium Forge recipe combining a Dwemer Gauntlet with six stones: Great Destruction, Interdimensional, Warped, Victim, Lost Memories and Thinking. Check the other outputs’ own recipes by name.

Order of the Universe calls for a separate action: apply its page to a Notice Board, as the tooltip says. Five items plus the studied page — six independent advancements, and the book needs all of them.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.armor_un.text.0: This card combines three separate sets: Chthonic Armor, its Orichalcum version and Grand Unahzaal Armor. Begin with a full base set and inspect upgrade recipes so you do not consume needed original pieces before their checks register.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.armor_un.text.1: After crafting, wear the corresponding complete set and wait for its advancement. Mixing the strongest pieces from different series may be useful in combat but need not satisfy a specific armor-set check.
