codex.quest.et_unahzaal.armor_un.text.2: Keep spare equipment before expensive upgrades. The three marks confirm several protection options; choose the final-battle set whose effects you understand and whose condition you can support with repairs and consumables.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.armor_un.title: Unahzaal Armor
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.astral.text.0: The Damaged Astral uses a shapeless recipe containing nine items: Divine Edge, Royal Greatsword, Toxic Sword, Royal Slayer, Cursed Page, Bloody Talwar, Blue Cutlass, Raitoningu and a Truadamantite Sword. This is a composite recipe rather than smelting one metal.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.astral.text.1: Check every component and prepare replacements for weapons you still use. The recipe consumes the original items; avoid sacrificing your only serviceable sword immediately before an expedition just for another mark.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.astral.text.2: Obtain the Damaged Astral and preserve it for Unahzaal’s crystal. Restored Astral is a different item at another stage, so the two should not be substituted in recipes.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.astral.title: Damaged Astral
The Unahzaal Multiverse crystal requires Sorcery level sixteen. The creator takes the Amber, Comets, Eden and Volcanech dimension crystals, with Damaged Astral in the center. These are four completed travel items, not similarly named ores or decorative crystals.
Make fresh crystals for the recipe and make sure your home portals will keep working after the components go into the creator. Then lay out the five items and take the result.

The book mark confirms the crystal, not combat readiness. Stock healing and repair supplies, establish a return method and read the difference between a normal victory and Eternal Darkness conditions before crossing.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.crystal_un.title: Unahzaal Crystal
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.enter_un.text.0: Unahzaal’s Multiverse is a late expedition best attempted after repairing your main equipment. Bring healing, a Return Ticket and building blocks, then activate the corresponding portal. Leave rare ingredients for your next recipe in storage.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.enter_un.text.1: First establish a safe route and mark the entry point. Avoid experimenting on unusual dangerous objects with an ordinary pickaxe before understanding their purpose: later technologies provide specialized tools.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.enter_un.text.2: This objective requires the entry advancement and presence in the correct dimension. After reconnaissance, decide where to gather armor materials and seek enemies; arriving in the multiverse does not mean the final encounter has started.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.enter_un.title: The Multiverse
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.eye.task.0: Kill Eye Of Unahzaal; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.eye.text.0: The Eye of Unahzaal is an independent opponent, not an item used to fill a portal. Watch creature names while exploring the multiverse and carry a ranged weapon with ammunition; ordinary loot with a similar icon does not complete the goal.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.eye.text.1: Choose stable ground with a view of the enemy and room to retreat before fighting. Avoid gathering materials during the encounter; finish it and restore health first.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.eye.text.2: Collect the Eye of Unahzaal Banner after victory. The advancement tracks this trophy, so leaving it on the ground can keep the card open. Secure the result and proceed to preparing late armor sets.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.eye.title: Eye of Unahzaal
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.gifts.task.0: Choose and receive one of five gifts at the Altar of Eternal Knowledge
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.gifts.text.0: Unahzaal’s Gifts are selected through the Altar of Eternal Knowledge dialogue. This is a choice of one of five items, not a requirement to collect all five. Read the offers before confirming: a sword, shield, Archer Glove, sorcery artifact and summoning staff support different styles.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.gifts.text.1: The gifts grow stronger with the number of boss species you have defeated. Take what you actually use rather than the grandest name; repeated victories over the same boss do not count as new species.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.gifts.text.2: After selecting, obtain the item and check the one-gift advancement. The card’s placement after the main victory is useful for collection review but does not mean a gift randomly drops from the final boss.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.gifts.title: Gifts of Unahzaal
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.tetra.text.0: Tetragrammaton belongs to the later Arkemer story. Continue Aftermath through the allegiance choice and final confrontation; the character appears through a story sequence rather than randomly using a rune in the multiverse. Prepare repairs and healing before the scene.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.tetra.text.1: A’Hisi’s route describes servers behind the throne that sustain the opponent’s recovery. Destroy them to stop endless regeneration, then finish the fight. Dealing heavy damage while that support remains active does not resolve the encounter.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.tetra.text.2: Seraphim is obtained separately: the Aetherium Forge makes it from a Solid State Drive, Restored Astral and Aetherium. The book needs both the victory and this item — battle trophies will not close the second goal.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.tetra.title: Tetragrammaton
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.unahzaal.task.0: Defeat all Unahzaal phases and receive the final victory advancement
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.unahzaal.text.0: Approach Unahzaal after Amber’s story and your return to Miguel. In Unahzaal’s dimension, find the ritual chamber in his dungeon: the central summoning block has four helper blocks immediately adjacent in the cardinal directions.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.unahzaal.text.1: Supply a redstone signal to each helper so all four become active. The central block checks that complete group and starts the boss spawn; one active helper is insufficient. Clear the area and prepare healing and serviceable weapons before completing the circuit.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.unahzaal.text.2: The fight has several phases, and the first lull is not yet a victory. Wait for the final advancement. A normal victory opens the later events and Aftermath; the Darkness rewards have conditions of their own.
codex.quest.et_unahzaal.unahzaal.title: Unahzaal
codex.quest.et_volcanech.arahulum.task.0: Kill Arahulum; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_volcanech.arahulum.text.0: Arahulum is summoned in the End even though this card sits beside Volcanech. Miguel explicitly directs you to find Arahulum’s Altar in the End and activate it with an Ender Artifact. Prepare that item, ranged weapons, healing and fall protection.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.arahulum.text.1: Find the correct altar, mark the return route and make sure the surrounding area provides room to move. Apply the artifact only after preparing; another altar or dimension does not replace this route.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.arahulum.text.2: Defeat the boss and collect the Eye of Arahulum. Completion requires both separate marks: the kill and obtaining the Eye. Preserve the trophy until you inspect its recipes instead of leaving it among ordinary post-battle clutter.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.arahulum.title: Arahulum
Kill Brimstone Agaric; collect the boss banner in your inventory
The Brimstone Agaric comes out when a Strange Brimstone Fungi is destroyed. Look for that block among Volcanech’s fungal thickets and read its name: ordinary mushroom wood is not it.
Prepare the surroundings, healing and an exit before breaking the unusual fungus. The block triggers a boss spawn, so finish reconnaissance and remove interfering enemies first, then destroy it.

Defeat Brimstone Agaric after it appears and check the advancement. Keep useful fungal materials separately; they participate in later recipes, including Truadamantite. Breaking the fungus without completing the fight does not finish this card.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.brimstone.title: Brimstone Agaric
codex.quest.et_volcanech.crystal_vol.tex: The Volcanech crystal needs Sorcery level ten. Its five ingredients are Ichor, Tayemiyadoht Tapinella, an Aragotium Ingot, Armored Beetle Chitin and Dark Ichor. The light and dark substances occupy different positions and cannot replace one another.

Gather the plant and chitin before assembly, reserve the ingot from Eden and check your personal skill on the board. Arrange the ingredients in the Interdimensional Creator according to the recipe and take the crystal.

The finished item is enough for detection. Prepare fire protection and an independent return route before using the portal: crafting a crystal does not make your character resistant to the hot world’s dangers.
Before entering Volcanech, prepare Fire Resistance, healing, building blocks and a Return Ticket. Use a portal with the matching bricks and crystal, leaving rare materials at home until reconnaissance is complete. Ordinary water in another dimension should not be your only rescue plan.
Find stable ground, mark the exit and observe local enemies. Miguel warns about floating shields and blades as well as sulfur clouds; avoiding fire does not protect against every attack.
The entry advancement and presence in Volcanech complete the card. Then search for the wounded Sunfurry scout and the golem’s location while preserving a route between them and the portal.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.enter_vol.title: The Molten World
codex.quest.et_volcanech.golem.task.0: Kill Volcanic Golem; collect the boss banner in your inventory
codex.quest.et_volcanech.golem.text.0: The Volcanic Golem wakes from Pyro Volcanite, which is obtained through a local monster spawner. Craft a Flame Sphere from Volcanech materials and apply it to a spawner in that dimension — Miguel says it will start releasing Flame Sphere creatures.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.golem.text.1: Defeat them, gather Pyro Volcanite Shards and combine them into the complete item. Prepare the area around the golem statue, healing and Fire Resistance, then use the finished Pyro Volcanite on the statue. An ordinary Flame Sphere does not directly replace this final step.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.golem.text.2: Fight on solid ground and check the advancement after the victory. Keep the spawner materials for another attempt: break it too early and you lose a handy source of shards.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.golem.title: Volcanic Golem
codex.quest.et_volcanech.sulfur.text.0: Sulfur explosives are needed here for one verified blast. Choose an empty patch far from your base, portal, settlements and valuable monster spawners, and think through the exit and cover. Testing the radius next to a storeroom is a bad idea.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.sulfur.text.1: Craft Sulfur TNT specifically, place one charge and ignite it using a normal TNT activation method. Move behind reliable cover immediately, avoid standing nearby to watch and do not combine the first test with a chain of additional charges.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.sulfur.text.2: Wait for the explosion and check the advancement: the book needs the blast itself, not a block in your pocket. Looking over the crater will show you where such a tool is useful in later work.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.sulfur.title: Sulfur Explosives
Extract five blueprints using a Spawner Cracker and complete the Sunfurry scout’s assignment
The wounded Sunfurry scout in Volcanech asks for five blueprints hidden in monster spawners. Find him and accept the assignment before breaking any devices. Only a Spawner Cracker can extract a blueprint — an ordinary pickaxe is useless here.

With the cracker in hand and your gear repaired, go round the local spawners one by one. Collect five blueprints, glancing at the Journal counter, and keep them safe until you return. If one of the spawners is feeding you golem shards, gather the reserve you need first.
Return to the scout and finish the dialogue. The advancement concerns the completed assignment; the acquired blueprints can then support crafting improved equipment.
codex.quest.et_volcanech.vol_quest.title: Defection
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.board.text.0: The cutting board is the workstation for cutting and other manual processing in Farmer’s Delight. The result depends on the item placed and the tool in your hand: some recipes need a knife, others a different suitable tool.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.board.text.1: Craft the board, show it to the book and place it on a convenient surface. In JEI, open the cutting section for your chosen ingredient, lay it on the board and strike it with the listed tool. Collect the output and compare the amount with the recipe.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.board.text.2: For the first try, use one cheap ingredient and leave space around the board, since results drop onto the floor. If nothing happens, the tool or the recipe is wrong, not the number of items on the board. Once cutting is familiar, it prepares meal ingredients and becomes the basis for automation later.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.board.title: Cutting Board
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.crops.text.0: New meals require their own range of crops. Farmer’s Delight adds tomatoes, cabbages, onions and rice. Treat a discovered wild plant as the beginning of a future garden rather than just another snack.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.crops.text.1: Look for unusual plants while exploring and identify them through tooltips. Preserve planting material, using seed recipes where provided. Rice grows from planting in shallow water; establish the other listed crops on prepared farmland with sufficient light.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.crops.text.2: Carry one tomato, cabbage, onion and rice item for the objective. Keep planting reserves separately and wait for a repeat harvest of your own. Complex recipes will then stop depending on luck during expeditions, and the kitchen gains a regular vegetable supply.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.crops.title: New Crops
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.feast.text.0: Farmer’s Delight feast dishes can be placed on a table and divided into portions. This objective needs a whole roast-chicken platter and a serving of honey-glazed ham. Whole dishes and servings are different items, so inspect recipe outputs carefully.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.feast.text.1: Assemble the chicken platter from cooked chicken and its listed sides. For the ham, first prepare the large Honey Glazed Ham dish with smoked ham, honey, berries and rice, then place it and take a portion with suitable tableware. Compare recipe outputs and names in JEI.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.feast.text.2: Carry the whole chicken dish and the ham serving for completion. Afterwards, arrange a safe serving area and prepare dishes. A feast table is useful when guests have space and the kitchen keeps enough ingredients to repeat the meal.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.feast.title: Feast
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.food_service_batc: A trial batch checks the kitchen better than owning cookware. Prepare eight beef-stew servings and collect them in your inventory. The cooking process should now end with real travel supplies.

The Farmer’s Delight recipe needs raw beef, carrot and potato for each serving, plus a bowl for dispensing it. Prepare eight operations’ ingredients, load the heated pot and watch cooking progress. Collect meals so a full output does not stop production.

The counter checks finished beef stew rather than bread or raw ingredients. After completion, put the meals into expedition storage. Note which ingredient is running low: the next check concerns repeatable kitchen operation, not crafting another pot.
Cook a repeat batch and replenish kitchen supplies

A kitchen is ready for regular service when it can repeat production without searching for forgotten essentials. Use some of the meals during an ordinary journey, then restore the supply before the next outing.

Inspect meat and vegetable deliveries, bowls, heat and free pot output. Prepare the missing portions and return them to the same labelled storage. If automated transport is connected, check that it sends the intended ingredients into the appropriate slots.

Confirm the manual goal after a successful second batch and replenishing supplies. The Codex does not automatically observe the entire kitchen; your tick records a verified cycle. Food supply can now support farming and expeditions while new recipes are added without losing the basic reserve.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.food_service_setu: An expedition kitchen should produce supplies you can repeat before the next outing. Start with one cooking pot and eight bowls. This is enough for a small batch without complex automation and lets you inspect the complete cooking sequence.

Gather the equipment in your inventory, then place the pot over an active heat source. Reserve nearby storage for raw beef, carrots and potatoes, with a separate destination for finished servings. Keep ingredient slots and meal output accessible.

Check heat and available containers before loading a large batch. The next quest needs eight beef-stew servings. Prepare ingredient supply first: adding more bowls cannot fix an empty ingredient slot.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.guide_cabbage_bat: A modest batch of prep work shows what the cutting board can do. Cabbage suits a first check: one head cut with a knife by the Farmer’s Delight recipe yields two leaves, and the leaves go into later dishes.

Take eight cabbages, an intact knife and free space for the output. Cut the cabbage on the board and collect sixteen leaves in your inventory. If the count is off, look at the dropped items and at how many heads you actually placed.

Once the goal is met, put the leaves into kitchen storage and pick a dish that uses them. Do not cut the whole harvest at once: some recipes need a whole head. You now have a tested example for planning small ingredient batches.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.guide_kitchen_acc: Test a cooking route and fix an awkward section

Kitchen layout becomes apparent during actual cooking. Walking around the stove for a bowl or having nowhere to place a meal makes even a small batch awkward. Test the route from storage to serving with a familiar recipe.

Follow the complete sequence: collect ingredients, prepare what needs the board, load the pot, collect a serving and restore tableware or supplies. Notice where you must climb over blocks or open unrelated containers, then rearrange the obstacles.

Repeat cooking after the change and confirm the manual objective. Everything need not be within one step; clear access and recognisable purposes matter more. This layout will cope better with larger batches and automated input later.
A kitchen with clear working access
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.guide_menu_reserv: Prepare two dishes and verify ingredient replenishment

A varied menu is good as long as the kitchen can keep up with it. Choose a main travel dish and one more from the crops you have, then compare their needs: a shared ingredient can run out for both lines at once.

Write down the ingredients and containers for a small repeatable batch of each dish. Check where meat, vegetables and rice come from, and keep planting stock apart from kitchen stock. Cook a trial batch of both recipes and store the result somewhere obvious.

The goal can be ticked after cooking and restocking. If one recipe keeps demanding long expeditions, save it for feasts and build the everyday reserve on what grows nearby. A good menu matches the farm and never forces you to rebuild the kitchen before each trip.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.guide_rice_plot.t: A rice plot differs from dry farmland. Farmer’s Delight rice grains are planted in shallow water, so prepare a small level area with convenient access. Your first trial does not need a deep flooded pit.

Reserve some rice for planting, establish it in suitable conditions and wait for maturity. Process harvested panicles through their recipe; a cutting board and knife provide rice and straw. Preserve the growing base and planting reserves so harvesting can repeat.

Collect sixteen rice items for the inventory goal. Afterwards, cook a small portion and divide the remainder between planting and kitchen storage. The plot will support rice dishes while also supplying useful farming materials.
Straw connects harvesting with practical recipes for rope and organic compost. Keep a small separate reserve that can be replenished during ordinary crop work instead of accumulating it without a purpose.

Use a knife for suitable grass, wheat or rice harvesting. Another clear route is processing a rice panicle on the cutting board, which produces rice and straw. Choose an available method and collect sixteen straw items in your inventory.

After completion, label their storage and reserve some for your next recipe. Avoid processing all planting supplies merely to obtain a by-product. This modest batch lets you test rope or compost while keeping the main farm running.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.guide_straw.title: Straw with a useful purpose
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.guide_tomato_supp: Grow a tomato along rope and harvest it
Farmer’s Delight tomatoes climb a rope hung above the bush. The bed grows upward, but it needs room for harvesting and for watching the stem. Start with one plant at an accessible edge of the plot.

Plant the tomato in farmland and hang rope directly above it. Provide light and ordinary growing conditions, then wait for the plant to change. If the stem does not climb, check where the support hangs and how the bush is doing instead of adding rope higher and higher at random.

Confirm the manual goal once you have seen growth along the support and gathered a harvest. Repeat the successful arrangement along the row, leaving enough space between plants and the walkway for maintenance.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.knife.text.0: A Farmer’s Delight knife is more than a weapon. It cuts food on the cutting board and gathers straw when you harvest suitable grass or grain. The flint knife introduces the tool; the iron one lasts longer and needs replacing less often.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.knife.text.1: Craft both knives from their JEI recipes and let the book see each one in your inventory, one after the other. Take some wheat or find tall grass and try cutting it with the knife. If a single plant yields nothing, the tool is fine: straw does not drop from every stalk.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.knife.text.2: A kitchen knife lives next to the board, not in the crate of factory parts. The next step is the board itself, where both the right tool and the specific recipe matter, because not every ingredient can be cut any way you like.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.knife.title: Knife
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.pot.text.0: The cooking pot prepares composite dishes from several ingredients. It needs live heat underneath and bowls for the portions if the dish is served that way. It works best beside the food cabinet, so you are not carrying every carrot across the base.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.pot.text.1: Craft the pot and place it over suitable heat. For beef stew, add raw beef, carrot and potato as the JEI recipe shows, prepare a bowl and wait for it to finish. When you take the portion, check that the output slot is not blocked by other food.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.pot.text.2: The pot and the beef stew are two separate objectives. Show the book the pot before placing it, then cook and pick up a portion; recorded equipment never needs to come down again. Remember the main condition: a cold pot with the right ingredients simply stays cold.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.pot.title: Cooking Pot
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.rope.text.0: Farmer’s Delight rope is useful beyond kitchen decoration. It supports farm interactions, including tomatoes growing upwards along a suspended support. Start with a short section that is easy to inspect and remove.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.rope.text.1: Gather straw through suitable knife harvesting and craft rope using its recipe. Carry it for the goal, then attach it where your small project needs it. For tomatoes, place rope above the crop with space for growth and convenient harvesting.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.rope.text.2: Inspect its placement and nearby access. Rope does not replace every ladder or structural wall; use the interactions the mod supports. After the first trial, extend a modest support above part of the plot and observe how the farm uses the extra height.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.rope.title: Rope and Hanging
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.skillet.text.0: A Farmer’s Delight skillet handles simple cooking and can be used while travelling. It connects a portable tool to a heat source; merely holding it beside a cold stove is insufficient.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.skillet.text.1: Craft the skillet and complete the item goal. For portable cooking, stand near suitable heat, hold food in the other hand and use the skillet. Sneaking also lets you place it as a block. Check supported ingredients and outputs through the available recipes.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.skillet.text.2: Test one piece of food before processing your entire travel supply. Watch the fire’s placement and collect the result. A skillet suits small batches, while the cooking pot handles multi-ingredient meals; these workstations serve different kitchen needs.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.skillet.title: Skillet
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.soil.text.0: Farmer’s Delight organic compost gradually becomes rich soil. It is a separate processing block, not the ordinary Minecraft composter. Sunlight, water and mushrooms help composting, and the resulting soil supports your farm.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.soil.text.1: Craft organic compost using an available recipe with straw and other organic supplies. Place part of the batch in a suitable location and wait for the block to change. Ordinary furnace smelting does not produce rich soil; the transformation happens in the world.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.soil.text.2: Let the Codex record the compost before placement, then collect the finished rich soil. The objectives remember each item separately, so one transformed block is enough. Afterwards, use the soil around crops and inspect the appropriate planting method. Start with a small plot and compare plant behaviour before rebuilding the entire farm.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.soil.title: Rich Soil
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.storage_fd.text.0: A kitchen cabinet keeps ingredients within reach. The Farmer’s Delight oak cabinet fits into a working wall and serves as storage, and its value depends on where it stands rather than how much decoration surrounds it.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.storage_fd.text.1: Craft the oak cabinet and show it to the book. Place it beside the board or pot, check that the door opens freely and arrange the food. Keep raw ingredients, finished meals and tableware apart — in separate cabinets or at least in clear groups of slots.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.storage_fd.text.2: Cook a familiar dish taking everything from this spot. If a bowl requires a walk through half the house, rearrange storage now, while the kitchen is small. The book cannot see the order inside the cabinet; the trial cooking shows what is missing near the workstation.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.storage_fd.title: Food Storage
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.stove.text.0: The Farmer’s Delight stove is a permanent place for heating and frying. A pot or skillet sits above it, and suitable foods cook directly on its surface. Before building, leave clear access to the working side.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.stove.text.1: Craft the stove, show it to the book and set it in the chosen spot. Light it with a suitable fire source and make sure the cookware above receives heat. An extinguished stove looks like part of a finished kitchen, but it does not cook.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.stove.text.2: Cook a sample and collect the result instead of leaving random supplies on the surface. Decide in advance where finished dishes go and where ingredients live. A good kitchen reads at a glance: what is heating, where the food is and where meals go, all without hopping over work blocks.
codex.quest.fd_kitchen.stove.title: Stove
codex.quest.final_bridges.adventure_brid: Tech gear pulls its weight on an expedition if it was tested back in the workshop. Obtain the Meka-Tool and the MekaSuit chestplate. One chestplate is not a suit, and with an empty charge or without the right module even that will not do what you expect.

Charge the equipment, inspect installed modules and test ordinary movement, mining and mode switching somewhere safe. Prepare food, lighting and a return method separately. Damage protection does not replace oxygen, radiation protection or a dimension's special conditions when your route requires them.

The two items count once obtained, and they promise no boss victory. Before a distant expedition, open its chapter and weigh the threats there against what the kit can do. Keep charging and a stock of consumables at the base, so on return you restore readiness rather than gather everything anew.
codex.quest.final_bridges.autocraft_brid: Refined Storage autocrafting can send materials into external processing when you describe its inputs and expected result. Prepare an autocrafter and sixteen patterns. Owning them provides configuration tools but does not automatically create every mod's recipes.

Pick a simple first operation: one furnace or one processing machine. In the pattern grid switch to processing mode, enter the exact input and output amounts, and hand the pattern to the autocrafter. The result needs its own way back into the network; delivering ingredients to the machine is only half the job.

After registration, use those same patterns and install the autocrafter. Run a small request and watch it finish in the monitor. For complex Create sequenced assembly, configure the line and output sorting first, then describe the external order; an unknown or incorrect result leaves the network waiting.
The Mechanic's workshop and the MineColonies warehouse tie the citizens' labour to your base's needs. Obtain the blocks of both buildings and construct them the usual colony way. A placed hut block is not yet a building: the worker, the level and the recipes come later.

Choose one recipe the mechanic's interface actually lets you teach. Supply the worker with materials and follow the delivery through the courier and the warehouse. Not every tech-mod recipe is open to any craftsman: profession, building level and research each draw their own limits.

Install the blocks after registration; no separate book copies are needed. Set aside a small transfer reserve for the factory connection and test a specific citizen order. First make sure the colony receives its own tools and food, then direct surplus production into external storage.
codex.quest.final_bridges.defense_bridge: Base defence combines systems with different operating rules. Obtain an Immersive Engineering gun turret, a MineColonies barracks block and a Create Radar fire controller. They do not all use one energy supply: a turret needs electricity and ammunition, while guards need training, equipment and colony support.

Test each system within its own chapter first. Configure turret targets and supplies; finish barracks construction and staff the garrison; check artillery control compatibility, aiming and a safe firing direction. A controller alone does not become a complete gun.

The items count once obtained; after that you can put them into the build. Spread the positions so the line of fire does not cross the routes of citizens, trains and maintenance. Three components in a chest will not stop an enemy: test the defence against specific threats and give each system its own supply.
codex.quest.final_bridges.energy_bridge2: Electrical devices from different mods often exchange FE, but connections still depend on their sides and terminals. Prepare a starter Powah energy cell, Create: New Age basic motor, Ad Astra coal generator and two IE low-voltage connectors.

The first pair is the generator and the storage: set the energy output, run a compatible cable and watch whether the reserve grows. Connect the New Age motor the way its own mod intends, once you know it. IE wires need connectors and their own voltage; one mod's wire will not stand in for another's cable.

The card records the four equipment types sequentially without consuming them. Test transitions individually by watching stored energy and a small working load. If a section transfers no power, fix its side, connection or throughput limit before extending it across the base.
codex.quest.final_bridges.fuel_chain.tex: Plant material can feed different fuel lines, but their fluids and recipes do not become interchangeable. Obtain an Immersive Engineering garden cloche, a bucket of IE biodiesel and a bucket of Create Crafts & Additions bioethanol. The cloche really has a normal crafting recipe and places from an item, unlike large multiblock factories.

For biodiesel, prepare plant oil and ethanol, then use the IE refinery with saltpeter as its catalyst. Make the other mod's bioethanol through its own chain. Choose crops by the consuming machine's recipe rather than visual similarity.

Show the device and both buckets sequentially; this card does not consume them. When integrating farms, compare water, power and crop demand first. A full cloche output or an empty ingredient tank can stop production before room for another generator becomes relevant.
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_colony_d: Produce the exact batch requested by a citizen and fulfil that request

Take the first shared order from a real shortage in a citizen's or the builder's interface. A simple batch of planks, stone or another material your factory already makes will do. Write down the exact type and amount: planks of a similar colour will not always pass for the ones requested.

Produce the batch on existing equipment and deliver it through a normal colony-supply route you understand. Manual transfer is acceptable initially: the task checks production against a real need rather than promising automatic integration of every warehouse.

Wait until that request is fulfilled and the citizen's work can continue, then confirm. Resources appearing in a random chest are insufficient. After a successful order, automate the repeated section while retaining workshop reserves and avoiding materials the citizens' current recipes do not use.
The Factory Fulfils a Citizen Request
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_external: Extract 8 of 32 cobblestone from external storage through RS and return them to that same store

Test External Storage with a small easily counted stock. Put 32 cobblestone into a separate bin or Create vault and connect it to RS through External Storage. Keep other cobblestone stores out of the test so you observe this container specifically.

Find the items in the RS grid and extract eight. The external store should now hold 24. Return eight through the grid and verify the original amount. Write settings and priorities should send them back to the tested store.

Confirm by hand once both observations agree. If the items landed on a disk rather than in the external storage, reading works but the way back is not yet set. Fix it before connecting large stocks, and set up filters for materials you do not want cluttering this warehouse.
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_ore_comp: Compare finished-ingot output from two equal batches of identical raw iron through two different lines

Compare processing recipes with identical inputs or the numbers become misleading. Prepare two equal small batches of the same raw-iron item. Choose two existing lines with valid recipes for that input and keep their outputs separate.

Run one batch through each line. Bring both through to finished ingots, accounting for intermediate smelting and leftovers when recipes work in groups. Record ingots and secondary products without including old stock from shared storage.

Confirm manually after comparing complete outputs from both equal batches. One method need not win for the entire pack: different ores have different recipes. Choose an iron route using actual yield and available supplies, retaining the notes for your next production expansion.
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_ore_rout: Process filtered iron, keep cobblestone separate and prevent the batch from circulating

After comparing iron, configure an input that keeps incompatible materials separate. Take a small supply of raw iron and ordinary cobblestone. Iron should reach the chosen processing line, while cobblestone enters separate storage without attempting the same recipe.

Use available funnel, sorter or network-interface filters. Begin with one direction for each item type and disable unnecessary opposing imports. Visually follow several items: the filter must act on the actual transfer path rather than sit in a nearby chest.

Confirm when iron has been processed, cobblestone remains in its own store and the input batch no longer circulates. This checks route separation rather than sorter count. Add further ores individually afterward, verifying each recipe and output.
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_power_tr: Charge another mod’s store from a Create Addition alternator and complete a machine operation through it

The first shared energy experiment gets by with one machine and one storage block from another mod. Take a harmless consumer such as an electric furnace and a little raw material. Disconnect its old power, or the result could be put down to the previous cable.

Power the Create Crafts & Additions alternator with rotation, transfer FE into the chosen store and connect its output to the consumer. Check charging first, then one completed operation. Inspect side settings and energy direction rather than merely a wire drawn nearby.

Confirm manually when the other mod's store charges from the alternator and the machine finishes processing through that chain. Restore the workshop's convenient supply afterward. This small experiment establishes real device compatibility before investing in a long shared power line.
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_processi: Complete a network processing order through an external machine without moving items by hand

Test network processing with one operation your machine already performs. Choose a recipe with a clear input and one expected result, such as smelting feedstock. Prepare ingredients and temporarily separate existing finished product from accessible network stock.

Write a processing pattern with exact quantities, put it in an autocrafter and configure delivery to the machine. Return finished output through an importer or another working route. Request a small batch from the grid and avoid moving items manually during processing.

Confirm after the monitor marks the order complete and the result appears in accessible storage. If the machine finished but the order still waits, check the return path and declared output quantity. One fully working recipe matters more than pattern count and becomes a model for later integrations.
An Order for an External Machine
codex.quest.final_bridges.guide_stock_bo: Complete a network production order while preserving 16 ingots in a separate reserve chest

Shared storage is convenient until automation takes the last materials needed for manual work. Create a separate reserve chest beside the network without connecting it for reading or extraction. Put sixteen iron ingots inside and label its purpose.

Leave another small iron batch in connected storage and run an ordinary production order. After completion, inspect the reserve: all sixteen ingots should remain. Do not choose a test recipe demanding more material than the working store contains.

Order done and reserve intact — you can confirm. To begin with, a chest standing apart from the network is enough; clever access restrictions can wait. Such a stock helps with tool repair, hand-made cable or supplying citizens while the factory is busy with its next big batch.
A Reserve the Factory Cannot Take
codex.quest.final_bridges.logistics_brid: A Refined Storage grid searches connected storage, while Create packages arrange physical deliveries between prepared endpoints. Obtain a grid and Stock Ticker to compare both approaches. Owning the ordering device does not join them into one automatic system.

In Create, configure the packager, stock connection, delivery address and unpacking first. In RS, verify power, accessible storage and the grid. Choose one boundary between the systems, such as an ordinary buffer chest at a loading area, and check how each side interacts with it.

The two devices count once obtained, while moving cargo is a separate trial. Make sure the same material is not shuttled back and forth by opposing exports: such a loop keeps the transport busy and supplies no one. Separate the incoming and outgoing batches and give each a clear purpose.
codex.quest.final_bridges.magic_tech_bri: Magical systems can serve one workshop while keeping their own rules. Obtain a Botania Mana Spreader, an Ars Nouveau Source Jar and four Apotheosis Gem Dust. These do not turn mana, source and electricity into one interchangeable fluid or energy.

A Botania spreader directs mana toward a suitable receiver; an Ars jar fills from that system's working generators; gem dust comes through Apotheosis salvaging and related recipes. Learn each small section separately before placing it beside automation.

The book records components, which you can then install or use. Begin integration with ordinary item exchange, such as supplying iron for manasteel. Check whether a particular tool accepts a gem or upgrade in the mod's interface rather than inferring compatibility from the general word magic.
codex.quest.final_bridges.ore_chain.text: Compare processing methods using exactly the same feedstock. Prepare a pair of Create crushing wheels, obtain four Immersive Engineering iron dust and craft a Mekanism chemical dissolution chamber. No unobtainable standalone IE multiblock-crusher item is required.

For each chosen ore, inspect its specific recipes and compare outputs from ore blocks, raw ore and raw-ore blocks separately. There is no universal multiplier for every material. The dissolution chamber belongs to a larger chemical chain and does not produce finished ingots on its own.

Show each result to the book, then install equipment on the chosen lines. Do not pass the same dust through several crushers expecting it to double repeatedly: further processing needs an actual recipe. Begin integration with one material, a dedicated output and a measurable number of finished ingots.
codex.quest.final_bridges.resource_bridg: Resource crops, laser drilling and digital mining reduce manual work in different ways. Prepare four Mystical Agriculture supremium essence, an Industrial Foregoing laser drill and a Mekanism digital miner. These represent three paths rather than interchangeable sources of every ore.

Growing a resource needs an existing seed recipe and suitable farmland conditions. A laser drill works with the correct base machine, with results governed by available recipes and settings. The digital miner extracts actual blocks within its selected area according to filters.

Use the same items in installations after registration. Choose one needed metal and compare cost, speed and maintenance among methods that genuinely support it. Check power and output space; high-tier essence alone does not turn every material in the pack into an available crop.
codex.quest.final_bridges.rot_to_fe.text: The Create Crafts & Additions alternator converts rotation into FE electricity, while the electric motor performs the reverse job. Prepare both devices, an Immersive Engineering low-voltage capacitor and a Mekanism basic energy cube. This introduces conversion between systems rather than promising perpetual motion.

First power the alternator mechanically and direct its electrical output into one store. Configure the receiving side and use a compatible connection. Test the motor separately from a charged source: its shaft should drive the chosen Create machine.

The devices count one after another, so once ticked they can be installed. Looping the generator into the motor will not yield free energy: conversion has losses and limits. A stable base needs a real source of power and a clear direction for passing it on.
codex.quest.final_bridges.storage_bridge: Refined Storage's External Storage connects any compatible inventory to the network, and nothing has to be moved onto disks. Obtain External Storage, a Create vault and a basic Mekanism bin. The latter two are fine for a first look at bulk storage; a multiblock warehouse has its own rules and its own working faces.

One storage block and a handful of a chosen item are enough for the experiment. Attach the External Storage to its working face, check the network's power and find the contents in the grid. Then withdraw part of the stock and put it back.

Item objectives only record obtaining equipment; you verify the combined store's operation. Do not connect an entire colony blindly: rack access and courier behaviour need separate checks, and network export can remove supplies citizens need. One understandable external inventory is enough for the first project.
codex.quest.final_bridges.transport_brid: Cargo transport and rapid player movement solve different problems. Prepare a Create station, Portable Storage Interface and Mekanism teleporter. The station defines a train stop, interfaces transfer moving storage contents, and the teleporter needs a configured frequency, power and suitable frame.

For cargo transfer, place the receiving interface opposite the moving construction's interface and test docking while stopped. Start with a small batch aboard a train or another compatible construction. Test teleportation separately between two correctly configured endpoints while retaining an ordinary return route.

It is the devices that count, not the delivered cargo or the journey made. Install them after the tick and test both tasks in turn. A transport hub is easier to build around clear places for loading, waiting and exiting, so an arriving player does not end up in the path of a moving train.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_adventure.t: Three items connect Aether and Twilight Forest exploration: Hammer of Kingbdogz, Lamp of Cinders and Trophy Pedestal. The hammer belongs to Aether bronze-dungeon treasure, so begin with defeating the Slider and accessing its reward rather than searching a golden temple.

In Twilight Forest, the pedestal supports progression toward the knight stronghold, while the Lamp of Cinders arrives much later through the highlands chain. Follow local boss order and remove the world's protections through normal advancements. Finding a structure does not always mean its interior is accessible yet.

The three items count once obtained and stay with you. The book does not track visits to every dungeon or the unfinished Final Castle. Look after useful tools and the crossings between worlds; for a missed trophy it is better to return to the right chapter than to repeat every expedition in a row.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_all.text.0: The final card combines this map's ten summits: Create, Immersive Engineering, Mekanism, storage, colony, adventures, Eternal Tales, space, magic and hunting. Complete every preceding milestone rather than merely collecting similar items in one chest.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_all.text.1: Once the ten summits are taken, show the book a single Nether Star. It is not consumed here; if the book has seen one before, no second Wither fight is needed. The reward remains a keepsake of the chain you have completed.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_all.text.2: Check overall Codex progress afterward: skipped chapters and side branches are not automatically completed. Choose a project using several learned systems together, such as supplying a remote settlement. This gives rare items and large factories a shared purpose in your world beyond their marks in the book.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_all.title: All at Once
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_colony.text: A large colony needs reliable housing and supplies, not just an attractive Town Hall. This summit checks the fifty-citizen population advancement and obtaining university and barracks hut blocks. It does not automatically require every building at level five, all research or victory against every raid.

Expand housing and the allowed population through available buildings and research. Watch food, health, tools and couriers: more citizens increase pressure on storage and crafters. Build the university and barracks through normal builder requests and supply their actual functions.

Register hut items before placing them. The population advancement must trigger in your colony; collecting fifty decorative figures cannot replace it. If growth stops, inspect free housing, population limits and current citizen requests before issuing more construction orders.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_create.text: This summit gathers equipment from three late Create branches: four factory gauges, four steam engines and the Aeronautics physics assembler. Each item belongs to its own system, and a chest full of them is not yet a factory filling orders, a boiler at full power or a ship ready for take-off.

Complete steam-power and package-logistics lessons first. Use factory gauges with properly connected stock and production, and engines with a boiler supplied with enough water and heat. The assembler prepares physical constructions under Aeronautics rules.

Obtain the required stock of each type together, wait for registration and then install it. Different types can be shown sequentially. After this equipment milestone, choose a working combined project such as supplying a shipyard or workshop by orders, so expensive devices perform useful work instead of remaining a chest collection.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_eternal.tas: Complete all Eternal Tales story assignments
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_eternal.tex: The Eternal Tales summit combines defeating Unahzaal, visiting Ultimate World, obtaining The Ultimate Two and completing the mod's story assignments. These four advancements are checked independently. A collection of dimension crystals does not replace conversations and quest hand-ins.

Follow the Journal through the worlds, then return for the late Aftermath story. For The Ultimate Two, study its rare-component chain and Aetherium Forge requirements. Preserve artifacts you use and inspect which later recipes consume them before processing the last copies.

Check all four marks on this card and complete the missing one specifically. Unahzaal's victory here is ordinary; the special Eternal Darkness challenge belongs elsewhere. All Eternal Tales quests means that mod's assignments, not automatic completion of the entire Codex and its industrial projects.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_hunt.task.0: Personally defeat all eight bosses required by the Cataclysm advancement
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_hunt.text.0: In this version, the Cataclysm advancement requires personal victories over eight bosses: Ignis, the Leviathan, the Harbinger, the Ender Guardian, Maledictus, the Ancient Remnant, the Netherite Monstrosity and Scylla. The old promise of ten bosses does not match its actual criteria.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_hunt.text.1: Follow the individual hunting cards for structures, offerings and arena preparation. A trophy received from another player does not replace a personal kill criterion. Check the advancement after each expedition to see which opponent remains.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_hunt.text.2: The second objective needs an Ignitium Elytra Chestplate. Fuse an Ignitium Chestplate with ordinary elytra using Cataclysm's Weapon Fusion system. Let the finished item register, then use it; the book neither consumes the equipment nor presents one chest piece as a full armour set.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_hunt.title: Peak of the Hunt
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_ie.task.0: Verify excavator output, a completed arc-furnace recipe and a load powered by the diesel generator
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_ie.text.0: The IE industrial summit checks three large operating installations and ownership of a railgun. The excavator, arc furnace and diesel generator are assembled in the world; unobtainable standalone items representing their completed structures are no longer required.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_ie.text.1: Run an excavator with bucket wheel on a surveyed vein and collect ore in storage. Complete a suitable arc-furnace recipe with power, usable electrodes and free output space. Then feed compatible fuel to a formed diesel generator and verify it powers a connected load.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_ie.text.2: Tick the shared operational point by hand only after all three checks. The railgun counts separately as an item; before firing it needs charge and suitable ammunition. The summit confirms the processes you have mastered, and after that it is life as usual: fuel runs out, electrodes wear, the vein depletes.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_ie.title: Peak of Immersive Engineering
Personally defeat the hard-mode Guardian of Gaia
This summit concerns Botania's stronger Guardian of Gaia. Defeat its hard-mode version personally and obtain a Dice of Fate. A relic produced after using the dice does not replace the dice item in the objective, so let the book register it first.

The arena must be in order: a working beacon and four pylons. The empowered guardian is summoned with a Gaia Spirit Ingot — terrasteel fused with four spirits of the ordinary guardian. Holding Shift, use the offering on the beacon; it is consumed, while plain terrasteel summons the other, weaker version of the fight.

Check armour, mana and healing beforehand. After victory, collect rewards and verify the hard-mode advancement rather than only the first Guardian's. The book does not consume the dice or require a particular random relic; using it further continues your own magical collection.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_magic.title: Peak of Magic
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_mek.text.0: Late Mekanism combines major power production, antimatter and modular equipment. This summit needs an antimatter pellet, MekaSuit bodyarmor, a Meka-Tool and a fusion reactor controller. The controller is only part of a reactor, and bodyarmor is only part of a suit.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_mek.text.1: Complete fission and waste processing through the SPS separately from fusion fuel and reactor construction. Do not transfer one installation's rules to another: inputs, startup conditions and maintenance differ. Charge equipment and configure modules for actual tasks.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_mek.text.2: Each item counts once obtained: a ticked controller can be placed, the tool put to work. A running turbine or a full suit is not what this goal checks. With the collection complete, look at the energy reserve, the product output and the maintenance access of the installations you will live with from here on.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_mek.title: Peak of Mekanism
This map's final space milestone requires a tier-four rocket, jet-suit chest piece and a visit to Glacio. Interstellar triggers upon entering the Glacio dimension; owning the rocket alone does not grant it.

Prepare through the Ad Astra chain: build and fuel the rocket, inspect equipment and reserve room for return cargo. A jet chest piece does not replace the rest of a required suit. Glacio's surface has oxygen in the installed version, so continuous oxygen consumption there should not be presented as mandatory.

The book records items and the actual visit separately. Bring return supplies, remember the landing site and inspect the surroundings before building a remote base. This card does not verify a finished colony or oxygen system; fully settling the planet remains a separate project.
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_space.title: Peak of Space
codex.quest.final_goals.goal_storage.tex: This summit brings together late storage from two systems. Obtain a 64k Refined Storage disk, the RS wireless grid and Mekanism's supermassive QIO drive. All three items are required at once; there is no choosing between RS and QIO.

Configure the wireless grid's connection and coverage, then check charge and access. A QIO drive installs in its own array linked to the intended frequency. It neither replaces an RS disk nor fits an RS drive merely because both store items.

The book records items sequentially without consuming them. Show drives before installation, then leave them in operating systems. Compare capacity and type limits in each device's tooltip; RS 64k refers to item count, not distinct types. Give both networks clear responsibilities within a shared base.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.affixes.task: Open the World Tier screen (Ctrl+T); this advancement is granted automatically
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.affixes.text: Affix items show additional properties and rarity in their tooltips. Find them in structure loot or on empowered enemies, starting with accessible chests and isolated targets. Compare the actual bonuses with your current equipment.

Gem Dust comes from Apotheosis gems. Crush an unwanted gem beneath a falling anvil in the world, standing clear of the impact. Once available, the Salvaging Table provides a more convenient interface. Collect four dust together.

The root advancement opens automatically when you enter the game; it does not demonstrate a strong equipment set. Save dust for stations, slate, and gem upgrades. Keep genuinely useful gems and crush weaker duplicates from later expeditions instead.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.augment.text: The Augmenting Table changes individual affixes while preserving the others. Craft it with an Enchanting Table, Nether Star, and two Godforged Pearls. Obtain pearls by salvaging unwanted Mythic items rather than destroying your only strong armour.

Show the pearl for its mark before spending it on the table. Put the affix item in the upper slot and Sigils of Enhancement in the lower one, then pick the property you want from the list. Two sigils raise its internal value by 25%; how much that adds to the stat depends on the affix itself.

Alternatively, one sigil rerolls the selected affix into another of the same type, with options shown in the interface. Compare the result carefully. This station refines a promising item without risking its other useful bonuses through a complete reforge.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.deepshelf.te: Craft a Dormant Deepshelf from Cracked Deepslate Tiles and books. Infuse it at Eterna 60, 40% Quanta, and 40% Arcana, repeating for two Deepshelves. Further increases also require a World Tier that permits the value.

The next stage uses Deep Dark materials. Search Ancient City chests for Echo Shards, mine Sculk with Silk Touch, and defeat a Warden for its Tendril. Prepare a retreat route and serious combat equipment; quietly exploring with wool does not produce that trophy.

Register the Tendril before using it for a Sculkshelf and then an Echoing Sculkshelf. Stages can be shown sequentially. Check the new shelf’s actual contribution and readjust Quanta: higher Eterna alone does not satisfy every infusion recipe.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.enchanting.t: Place an Apothic Enchanting Table with functioning shelves and the usual clear gap. Eight Basic Bookshelves are this card’s starter stock, not a guarantee of maximum stats. Check actual Eterna, Quanta, and Arcana after each change.

The Geode-Encased Bookshelf of Stability removes negative Quanta variation. Its components involve Budding Amethyst, obtainable by infusion. A Sightshelf adds enchantment preview information rather than weapon damage. Both utility shelves require developing the initial setup further.

If Eterna is capped by World Tier, activate an unlocked higher tier in its selection screen. More identical shelves beyond their limit will not fix that cap. Test a book before spending experience on your main equipment.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.gems.text.0: Gem-Fused Slate is made from eight deepslate blocks around one Gem Dust and yields eight slates. Four are enough for the mark; the rest go into the Gem Cutting Table and Gem Case. A gem in a chest does nothing on its own: its bonus works only once it is socketed into gear.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.gems.text.1: At the cutting table, prepare dust, rarity material, and the required second gem for your chosen purity upgrade. Costs increase with quality; inspect the input slots before committing. Compare the new bonus for the equipment type you intend to use.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.gems.text.2: The Gem Case sorts by name, compatibility, and purity, and can upgrade gems directly when supplied with materials. Organise the collection and select a compatible gem. Socketing uses a Smithing Table; the cutting station alone does not improve worn armour.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.gems.title: Gems
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.guide_gem_cu: Raise the purity of one gem at the Gem Cutting Table

The Gem Cutting Table raises a gem’s purity: from cracked to chipped, flawed, normal, flawless and perfect. Each step needs gem dust and one of the rarity materials; a chipped gem, for example, rises for three dust and nine Mysterious Scrap Metal, or three Timeworn Fabric, or one Luminous Crystal Shard. JEI lists the sets for the other steps.

Your first dust comes from dropping an anvil onto a discarded gem; afterwards the Salvaging Table produces it from unwanted gems. Rarity materials come from the same table by salvaging affix items: common gear yields scrap, uncommon gear fabric, rare gear crystals. Gather three dust and nine scrap in one stock so the book marks the preparation.

Then place the gem in the table, add dust and material and confirm; mark the manual objective only after the purity really increased. Higher purity means a stronger bonus in a socket, so cutting pays off for gems already set in your armour or weapon rather than for random finds.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.guide_potion: A potion charm stores an effect and applies it while it sits in your inventory and is switched on. Craft it with three identical potions in the middle row and six blaze powder in the top and bottom rows. The finished charm takes the effect’s name, such as “Charm of Fire Resistance”, and its state and source appear in the tooltip.

Brew three potions of one kind: fire resistance for the Nether, night vision for sunken cities or regeneration for arenas. The charm has durability and wears down while the effect is active; the right button toggles it, so save the charge for genuinely dangerous stretches.

In this pack the charm works straight from the inventory, without a Curios slot. One charm of any effect is enough for the mark; choose the one that covers your next hunt. Do not make charms from potions with short or harmful effects: the resource is wasted, and you may not manage to switch it off mid-fight.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.guide_salvag: Reforge an unwanted affix item and compare its properties before and after

Reforging rerolls an item’s affixes while keeping the item itself: the Reforging Table needs a Sigil of Rebirth and rarity materials matching the item’s tier. The Salvaging Table supplies them: common affix gear breaks into Mysterious Scrap Metal, uncommon into Timeworn Fabric, rare into Luminous Crystal Shards, epic into Arcane Sands, mythic into Godforged Pearls.

Collect three Timeworn Fabric by salvaging surplus uncommon finds and show them to the book. Then pick an item you would hate to discard but not to change: a spare weapon or armour piece with one good and one useless affix. Note its properties, reforge it once and compare, which shows what reforging preserves and what it rerolls.

Confirm the manual objective after the comparison. Reforging is a gamble and consumes materials every time, so stockpile them from loot rather than from your working kit; the Simple Reforging Table is also capped by rarity. For tuning a single affix without losing the rest, the Augmenting Table waits further along the branch.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.hundred.text: Collect Dragon’s Breath in a bottle and infuse it at Eterna at least 80, Quanta 15–30%, and Arcana at least 60%. This needs Pinnacle because earlier World Tiers cap Eterna. One bottle produces three infused components for Endshelves.

Develop the setup to level 90 and obtain a Dragon Head from an outer-End ship. A Draconic Endshelf raises the ceiling to 100 but does not supply the required Quanta or Arcana by itself. Keep supporting shelves for precise tuning.

Infuse an Enchantment Library into the Library of Alexandria at exactly Eterna 100, Quanta 45–50%, and exactly Arcana 100%. Excess randomness blocks this narrow recipe. Its upgrade preserves stored data; verify enchantment records and extraction afterwards.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.infusion.tex: Infusion uses the enchanting table’s third option when the input and stats match. A Hellshelf requires Eterna 45 and at least 30% Quanta; a Seashelf needs Eterna 45, 15% Quanta, and 10% Arcana. Infuse two of each.

Place the new shelves and raise the setup to Eterna 60. Accumulated experience alone will not get you there — you also need a suitable active world tier. Choose additional shelves by what each contributes, watching the numbers rather than piling up one kind indiscriminately.

Infuse an Improved Scrap Tome at Eterna 60, Quanta 25–75%, and at least 45% Arcana to obtain four Extraction Tomes. These remove every enchantment without destroying equipment. Ordinary Scrap Tomes destroy the item, so inspect the exact consumable before recovering valuable enchantments.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.invaders.tex: An Apothic Invader is an empowered named enemy wearing enchanted equipment and carrying an affix item. Assess its rarity and clear a retreat route before engaging. Ordinary crowds do not guarantee equivalent loot.

After victory, collect the invader’s named equipment. Additional drops may include a gem or Sigil of Malice, but the sigil is not guaranteed every fight. Continue hunting at a suitable World Tier and save the requested drops.

The Sigil of Malice does not summon an invader. It overcharges one affix while resetting another, making it a risky modification to existing equipment. Compare the selected item’s properties and protect your working set before experimenting. Obtaining the sigil and gem completes this card without requiring that experiment.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.leads.text.0: Craft a Flimsy Ender Lead from a lead, Ender Pearl, and Gold Ingot. Right-click a suitable animal to capture it, then a clear surface to release it. Test an ordinary cow between two enclosures first.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.leads.text.1: Once the item is recorded, infuse the lead at Eterna 45, Quanta 25% and Arcana 40%. The finished Ender Lead takes most creatures, but there are exceptions. If a particular creature refuses, that is not a sign the whole system is broken; in any case, never release a dangerous captive near villagers.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.leads.text.2: Check the stored creature’s name and release space. The lead moves one existing creature rather than duplicating it. Register both stages sequentially, using the same flimsy lead for the upgrade.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.leads.title: Ender Lead
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.reforge.text: The Salvaging Table destroys unwanted affix equipment to recover materials matching its rarity. Separate spare gear from your working set and test a cheap piece first. Ordinary iron cannot replace these rarity materials.

A Simple Reforging Table supports up to Rare; Epic and Mythic require the full Reforging Table requested here. Supply equipment, the desired rarity material, and Sigils of Rebirth, then compare the experience and material costs of its three choices.

Reforging creates a new affix set and can also enhance valid unaffixed equipment. The most expensive choice does not guarantee the best effects for your build. Read every resulting property, equip useful pieces, and evaluate unwanted results as potential salvage.
The three sigils serve different equipment operations. A Sigil of Socketing adds a socket within the item’s allowed limit. Combine it with your chosen equipment at a Smithing Table and inspect the preview before using a valued piece.

A Sigil of Withdrawal removes socketed gems at a Smithing Table, returning both equipment and gems. This transfers useful gems into new armour. Salvaging instead destroys the original equipment, so it is a different operation.

A Sigil of Rebirth fuels reforging rather than extraction. Register one of each, then use the proper station. Record the item’s original properties so you can distinguish what socketing preserves from what a complete reforge replaces.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.sigils.title: Sigils
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.spawners.tas: Lighting, creature funnelling and a safe waiting point have been checked
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.spawners.tex: Find an ordinary monster spawner in a dungeon and secure the approach first: place light, clear the enemies already there and mark a retreat. Leave the block itself in place. This pack does not include Apothic Spawners, so the runes and chains from that separate module have no use here.

Look around the cage and work out exactly where the creatures appear. An ordinary spawner works only while a player is nearby, and a crowd of the same monsters next to it stops further spawns. Arrange a way to funnel creatures out of the cage area and a separate safe spot for attacking by hand and collecting drops.

Test it from your chosen waiting point: once the room is empty, new creatures appear, and restored lighting once again stops the dangerous spawns of an ordinary dark dungeon. Tick the verified cycle by hand. Do not blow the spawner up — you would lose a useful structure; nor can it be moved with Silk Touch without the right module.
Equip a full Uncommon affix set with a weapon and personally slay an Apothic Invader

Ascent requires affix armour in all four slots and an item in hand of Uncommon rarity or better, plus a personal victory over an Apothic Invader. An ordinary armoured monster does not count as an invader: look for its special empowerment and wait for the advancement to register after the fight.

Fill weak equipment slots through loot or reforging, then choose an accessible invader with retreat space and extra healing. Equipment and victory are separate criteria, making missing progress visible.

Activate Ascent once unlocked. Its Eterna allowance supports early deep-shelf infusions, but Quanta and Arcana still depend on the table’s surroundings. Save useful Rare pieces for Summit instead of immediately salvaging every blue drop.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tier_frontie: Equip an affix helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots and hold an affix weapon (Common or better)

Frontier requires affix equipment in head, chest, legs, feet, and hand slots. Common is sufficient, and higher rarities also count. Equip the armour and hold an affix weapon; storing items in a chest does not register equipped-slot criteria.

Open the advancement and check its five separate criteria. If one is unmet, reread the properties of the item in question: a coloured name or vanilla enchantments do not count as Apotheosis rarity. Reforging a suitable base item helps when loot for one slot refuses to turn up.

Once unlocked, press Activate in the tier menu. Frontier raises the Eterna allowance and changes loot without automatically improving your protection. Test its difficulty on a routine expedition and prepare Uncommon replacements for the next step.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tier_haven.t: Haven is Apotheosis’s default personal World Tier, but its advancement requires picking up an affix item. Inspect the extra properties of found loot; ordinary enchanted iron armour without affixes does not satisfy it.

Open World Tier Select, normally Ctrl+T, and inspect Haven’s detailed information. Tiers affect rarity and gem-purity distributions along with other modifiers. Multiplayer characters can use different personal tiers.

Check the advancement after obtaining the item. Haven limits available Eterna, so stronger enchanting progresses alongside equipment upgrades. The next goal needs affix armour equipped in all four slots and an affix item held in a hand. Start saving missing pieces now.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tier_pinnacl: Equip a full Epic affix set with a weapon and personally slay the Ender Dragon

Pinnacle requires Epic or Mythic affix equipment in all four armour slots and a hand, plus a personal Ender Dragon victory. Inspect rarity before entering the portal, and bring blocks, fall protection, healing, and weapons for crystals and dragon landings.

Destroy healing crystals first, then attack during suitable openings. After victory, verify the kill criterion and any missing equipped slots separately. Visiting the End or obtaining a Dragon Egg does not replace personally killing the dragon.

Activate Pinnacle to access full Eterna and its loot distribution, then return to breath and library infusions. Strong shelves alone were insufficient without the active tier. You can later choose a lower difficulty when appropriate to your preparation.
Equip a full Rare affix set with a weapon and personally slay the Wither

Summit requires Rare-or-better affix gear equipped in all four armour slots and a hand, plus a personal Wither kill. Gather skulls and Soul Sand separately from armour hunting, and keep the destructive encounter away from storage and machinery.

Prepare protection, healing, and both ranged and melee attacks. Wait out the opening explosion and adjust distance for the boss’s phases. Collect the Nether Star after victory and check the kill criterion; a transferred star cannot replace it.

Activate Summit once all criteria are met. Its Eterna limit is still below Infused Dragon’s Breath requirements, so the final table needs Pinnacle. Use this stage to gather Epic equipment and prepare the End expedition.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tomes.text.0: Bow and Chestplate Tomes restrict possible enchantments to their corresponding equipment types. Register both, then enchant one at your prepared table; it becomes an enchanted book. This focuses the search without guaranteeing a specific rare result.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tomes.text.1: Combine a Prismatic Cobweb with equipment in an anvil to remove all curses. Inspect the preview and experience cost first. The affix Salvaging Table is unsuitable because it destroys the equipment.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tomes.text.2: The Enchantment Library stores enchantments from deposited books as points and remembers the highest level ever deposited for each one. Build a small collection and try extracting one book. The library will not hand out a level you never deposited, and anything beyond its capacity is lost — check the limit before a large deposit.
codex.quest.hunt_apotheosis.tomes.title: Tomes
These three items involve different animals. Tarantula Hawk Elytra combine ordinary Elytra with two Tarantula Hawk Wings, each made from nine Tattered Wings. Search deserts and store fragments until the set is complete.

Deep in the caves live venomous centipedes. Seven of their dropped legs make the Centipede Leggings, which let you climb walls. Bring milk and light, and do not let the long creature cut off the only exit from a narrow tunnel.

A Vine Lasso needs vines, a lead, and two Shed Snake Skins. Anacondas shed after swallowing several meals, making chicken feeding more useful than random killing. Test the thrown lasso safely: it can restrain hostile creatures but cannot tether them to a fence. Register each finished piece before using it.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.beast_gear.title: Gear from the Hunt
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.chemx.task.0: Obtain a Potion of Chemical X
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.chemx.task.1: Set a downed Mutant Zombie on fire with flint and steel or a fire charge
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.chemx.text.0: In this version, brew Chemical X from a Thick Potion and one mutant trophy: a Hulk Hammer, Creeper Shard, Endersoul Hand, or Mutant Skeleton Skull. Water plus Glowstone Dust makes the Thick Potion. Start with a naturally encountered mutant instead of looking for an early Obsidian recipe.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.chemx.text.1: Bring Flint and Steel or a Fire Charge for the Mutant Zombie. Knock it down in combat, then use the fire item directly on the fallen body to prevent revival. Waiting nearby or placing a campfire beneath an ordinary zombie does not explain the required interaction.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.chemx.text.2: Collect and register the Hulk Hammer before spending trophy loot on Chemical X. Its advancement checks the potion in inventory. Conduct transformation experiments in a separate arena with an escape route.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.chemx.title: Chemical X
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.combat.task.0: Read: every weapon has its own arc and its own reach
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.combat.text.0: Practise your weapon’s movements against ordinary enemies before hunting. Better Combat changes animations and attack sequences by weapon type; a polearm, quick blade, and heavy axe need different spacing. Start in an open area without pets or villagers.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.combat.text.1: Make one attack, observe its delay and reach, then try a short sequence. Watch target positioning and safe retreat timing. Broad swings help against groups but need careful aim near allies. The damage number alone does not describe how the whole movement handles.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.combat.text.2: After practising, tick by hand that you have read the note on weapon arc and reach. The mark completes your control training; it does not promise a boss victory. Take already-tested weapons to a difficult arena, and try new trophies at home so you are not learning their rhythm under a deadly attack.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.combat.title: The New Combat
Craft the Animal Dictionary before searching for rare Alex’s Mobs creatures. Combine a book, green dye, and a suitable animal material, such as a Roadrunner Feather, Bear Fur, or shed Moose Antler. An arbitrary vanilla bone is not sufficient.

Open the entry for a nearby animal and identify its habitat, food, and useful interactions. Many resources come from shedding, feeding, or rescue; killing the first specimen may be less useful than observing it.

Take the book into your inventory for the mark, then use it as a field journal. Start with a familiar biome and note the coordinates of a stable population. The taming branch will need a variety of foods, so a food farm near home saves more time than chasing after yet another animal.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.dictionary.title: Animal Dictionary
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.frostmaw.text.0: Frostmaws sleep in snowy regions. Scout the approach and choose clear retreat space without deep drops. Bring dependable armour, healing, and a weapon suited to short attacks after dodging.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.frostmaw.text.1: Once it awakens, watch its freezing breath and broad strikes. Avoid standing in front of its face: freezing makes the next hit especially dangerous. Move around the creature and heal during safe openings rather than treating a pause as victory.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.frostmaw.text.2: This card requires killing Frostmaw and separately obtaining an Ice Crystal. Acquiring the crystal through stealth alone does not complete the combat advancement.
