Collect the trophy and test its freezing breath on ordinary enemies while watching durability, then repair before visiting the savanna.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.frostmaw.title: Frostmaw
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.guide_blowgun.te: Nagas from Mowzie’s Mobs live on rocky shores: where beaches meet mountains or hills, and on stony coasts. They attack from the air, spit and dive, so prepare a bow or crossbow, a shield and a roofed spot to retreat to. The kill counts personally, and a naga drops fangs.

Craft a blowgun from bamboo and two strings; darts come from a naga fang, a stick and a feather, eight per recipe. A dart poisons its target, so the weapon suits hunting and weakening dangerous creatures at range, not finishing sturdy bosses quickly.

For the mark, show the book the blowgun and eight darts at the same time, then use them as intended. Check the dart’s range and drop on a stationary target before trusting it in combat. Leftover fangs go into the naga fang dagger, a fast blade from the same hunting branch.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.guide_creeper_mi: Hatch a Creeper Minion from its egg

When a Mutant Creeper dies, a minion egg remains at the battle site. It does not fit in the inventory: walk up, sneak and right-click, and the egg settles on your head to be carried home. Until it hatches, keep it away from explosions and falls and stay out of new fights.

After a while the egg hatches, and the Creeper Minion is already tamed to whoever defeated its parent. The pet follows you, can ride on your shoulder, and its explosion, blast radius and block destruction are configurable. The advancement is granted at hatching, not when the egg is picked up.

The Creeper Minion Tracker is crafted from a creeper shard and four iron ingots. Use it on the pet to open a panel with its name, health, blast radius and explosion mode. Disable block destruction near buildings. The shard drops from the same Mutant Creeper, so both items of this branch come from a single hunt.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.guide_grottol.ta: Kill a Grottol with a Silk Touch pickaxe
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.guide_grottol.te: The Grottol is a small armoured creature of deep caves that flees and burrows into stone the moment it notices a player. A plain kill only earns the kill advancement; the value lies elsewhere: a Silk Touch pickaxe leaves a captured grottol, and a Fortune pickaxe rolls the diamond drop double-or-nothing. Prepare the right pickaxe in advance.

Look for grottols in deep caves of any biome except mushroom fields; they favour dark stone hollows and are easy to spot by their glittering shell. Block the escape routes and strike quickly: the creature vanishes into rock within seconds. Do not use explosives, which destroy the prize as well.

A captured grottol smelts into one diamond in a furnace or blast furnace; showing it to the book is enough for the mark, and you can smelt it afterwards. This is not a diamond farm but a rare find, and it teaches matching the tool to the creature: almost every Mowzie’s Mobs beast wants its own approach.
Steal the ice crystal from a sleeping Frostmaw while invisible

The ice crystal need not be won in battle: it can be stolen from a sleeping Frostmaw. The beast dozes beside its crystal in snowy plains and wakes when it notices a player. The mod hands the crystal to whoever comes right up to it while invisible, so brew a potion of invisibility and budget its duration for the approach and the retreat.

The crystal rests by the front paws, and you must be closer than two blocks. Sneak in from the crystal’s side, wait for it to jump into your inventory, then withdraw at once. A woken Frostmaw remains dangerous, although by the mod’s description it loses its ice breath without the crystal.

The advancement is granted at the moment of theft; the book requires no separate item, but the crystal stays with you and counts for the Frostmaw card. Stealing is enabled in this pack’s settings. It is the safest route to a crystal for a player without heavy armour, yet it does not replace the personal kill the neighbouring card demands.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.locators.text.0: Ambergris rewards rescuing a Cachalot Whale stranded during a thunderstorm. Search suitable ocean coasts and gently push the animal into water without hurting it. Killing a whale does not replace this rescue reward; clear its route to the sea.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.locators.text.1: Craft an Echolocator from Ambergris to reveal nearby caves. It has limited uses, so use it where you already intend to explore underground and plan a safe descent. It is not a universal structure finder.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.locators.text.2: After detection, upgrade it with four Ender Pearls into an Endolocator. This reveals a nearby End Portal around a stronghold rather than locating distant strongholds across the world. Reach the area with ordinary Eyes of Ender first. Register the two locator stages sequentially.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.locators.title: Echolocation
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.mutant_gear.text: Build the Mutant Skeleton Chestplate from separate bones. Two Shoulder Pads and four Limbs make Arms; six Ribs make a Rib Cage. Combine the Arms above the cage, collecting scattered pieces after battle.

Mutant Endermen leave Endersoul Fragments when defeated. Right-click fragments to claim them, then toss an Eye of Ender while nearby: owned fragments within eight blocks transform it into an Endersoul Hand. More fragments provide more initial durability. Attacking them is dangerous.

Obtain a Creeper Shard after defeating a Mutant Creeper. Retreat from its final explosion and return only after the dangerous animation ends. Register the three items sequentially, and practise telekinesis and explosive abilities away from your base.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.sculptor.text.0: The Sculptor’s challenge begins with a Bluff Rod, obtained from stone Bluff creatures. Find the Sculptor and bring food plus a safe approach route. Register the rod before offering it; the configured entry price is one rod.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.sculptor.text.1: Climb the generated platforms to the top. Placing or breaking blocks, flying, and teleporting are forbidden: this challenge checks the route, so ordinary shortcuts cause failure. Judge jump distances and choose each platform carefully.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.sculptor.text.2: At the top, right-click the Sculptor — that is how the trial ends. Height alone is not enough: without that interaction there is no finish. Wait for the advancement and receive the Earthrend Gauntlet, then test its powers away from your buildings. Killing the Sculptor is no substitute for a completed route.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.sculptor.title: The Sculptor's Trial
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.tame.task.0: Tame a grizzly bear with honey and salmon
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.tame.text.0: Prepare honey and salmon for a Grizzly Bear. Let it become honey-sated through a beehive, then offer salmon to tame it. A hungry predator is dangerous, especially near cubs.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.tame.text.1: Find Gorilla groups in jungles. Bananas drop from Jungle Leaves; gather several and feed your chosen gorilla until tamed. Check both advancements separately because friendship with one species does not complete the other.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.tame.text.2: The Falconry Glove belongs to a different bird — the bald eagle of wooded mountains. It is tamed with fish oil, and with the glove you can then perch the eagle on your arm and send it at a target. The glove alone does not mean a tamed bird. Lead new companions to a protected place and test their commands before a long expedition.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.tame.title: Taming
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.transmute.text.0: The Transmutation Table requires two Farseer Arms, a Nether Star, and Obsidian. Farseers appear near the world border, so defeating the Void Worm only begins transport preparation. Transform a Dimensional Carver into its Shattered version inside a Capsid and prepare your return route.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.transmute.text.1: The shattered carver carries you enormous distances in a chosen direction; several jumps in a row bring you close to the world border. The Farseer has a dangerous beam that bypasses ordinary protection, so keep to cover and do not expect to survive it standing still. Take the two hands and return with the loot.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.transmute.text.2: Place the table permanently. It exchanges the entire input stack for one of three offers at an experience cost and learns from supplied items. Test a small cheap stack first. Breaking it erases its knowledge and causes a powerful explosion, returning only the Nether Star.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.transmute.title: Transmutation Table
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.umvuthi.text.0: Obtain Sun’s Blessing peacefully before attacking Umvuthi. Find a savanna settlement, obtain an Umvuthana Mask, and wear it in the helmet slot. Approach the calm leader: the mask enables trading while he is not fighting.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.umvuthi.text.1: This pack’s first trade costs seven Gold Blocks. Open the trade, pay, and wait for the Sun’s Blessing effect and advancement. Register this peaceful stage before planning combat; a dead leader cannot bless you at that settlement.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.umvuthi.text.2: For the fight, bring full protection, healing, and room to avoid solar beams and summoned warriors. Collect Sol Visage after a personal victory. Blessing, victory, and the mask are separate checks, so the trophy cannot prove a skipped peaceful interaction.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.umvuthi.title: Umvuthi
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.voidworm.text.0: Summon the Void Worm in the End by throwing a Mysterious Worm directly into the void. Craft a Mosquito Larva from a Maggot and Mosquito Proboscis, then transform it inside an Enderiophage’s Capsid. Let the resulting worm register before consuming it.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.voidworm.text.1: Choose a large island with clear sightlines, fall protection, healing, and ranged equipment. Attack the head: damaging body segments splits the worm and complicates the encounter. Avoid chasing every segment beyond the island.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.voidworm.text.2: A personal victory completes the advancement. Collect the eye and mandibles for a Dimensional Carver with its Netherite component. The carver opens a route to spawn with a return portal lasting about a minute. Test this limited-use evacuation tool near home before relying on it.
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.voidworm.title: Void Worm
codex.quest.hunt_beasts.wroughtnaut.text: Find the Ferrous Wroughtnaut in its underground stone chamber. Bring a strong melee weapon, food, and enough room to circle its wide axe swings. Blocking the entire arena with obstacles removes your manoeuvring space.

Ordinary hits against its protected body accomplish little. Bait the heavy attack that leaves the axe stuck and exposes its back, circle behind, and strike the vulnerable area. Retreat after the short opening and repeat while watching attack preparation.

Register a personal victory and collect both Wrought Axe and Wrought Helmet. These item checks are separate from the advancement. Practise the axe’s broad attacks away from pets and villagers, then replenish healing before the Frostmaw expedition.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.acropolis.tas: Find the Acropolis above a warm ocean
Personally defeat Scylla, the Storm Empress
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.acropolis.tex: Cataclysm’s Acropolis generates in warm oceans, and the Storm Eye locates it. Prepare transport, fall protection, armour, and healing. Mark a safe arrival point before exploring exposed platforms and connecting passages.

Defeat Clawdian, then find Scylla and replenish supplies before another encounter. Interacting with inactive Scylla starts her fight, so avoid accidental clicks during scouting. Dodge lightning, thrown weapons, and hazardous areas while retaining movement space.

Collect four Lacrima and two Essence of the Storm, accumulating each type together. The card also requires both personal victories and Acropolis discovery. Once detected, allocate materials to weapons and later recipes; spending loot does not remove the guide’s saved marks.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.all_bosses.ta: Personally defeat all eight Cataclysm bosses
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.all_bosses.te: Cataclysm’s final advancement requires eight personal victories: Netherite Monstrosity, Ender Guardian, Harbinger, Ancient Remnant, Leviathan, Scylla, Maledictus, and Ignis. Additional foes such as the Ender Golem and Clawdian have their own cards but are outside this particular list.

Open the advancement and compare its criteria with your expedition log. For each missing boss, prepare the correct dimension, locator eye, awakening item, and fresh healing. Transferred weapons or trophies do not satisfy player-killed-entity conditions; check registered battle results.

Finish remaining arenas one at a time and bring loot home between attempts. Wait for the combined advancement after the last victory and retain your route notes. Further repeats then serve materials, new weapon builds, or personal challenges.
Find the Burning Arena in the Nether
The Burning Arena generates in Nether Wastes and is located with a Flame Eye. Prepare Fire Resistance, strong armour, healing, and a familiar weapon. Defeat the Ignited Revenant first and collect Burning Ashes without spending them on random experiments.

Place the ashes on the arena’s Altar of Fire to summon Ignis. The offering is consumed. Inspect the arena and refill supplies beforehand: Ignis uses long dangerous sequences, and some attacks require sidestepping instead of merely holding a shield.

Collect Ignitium and materials for The Incinerator after personal victory. Let three ingots register before allocating them to weapons and armour. Revenant and Ignis victories are separate advancements; expensive gear from someone else’s chest cannot replace them.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.burning.title: Burning Arena
Find the Ruined Citadel in the End
Locate a Ruined Citadel on the outer End islands with a Void Eye. Prepare fall protection, strong armour, healing, and a reliable route back to the gateway. A large stone structure does not eliminate void hazards around the island.

Explore the citadel, defeat the Ender Golem, and then reach the Ender Guardian. Watch area attacks and emerging rune hazards, repositioning instead of standing still through dangerous sequences. Recover health and durability between encounters.

The card counts both personal victories and the visit to the citadel itself. Collect the Gauntlet of Guard and the Void Core from the loot after the fights — they are two separate objectives, and one find does not close the other. Set the core aside for fusion with the Infernal Forge, and test the gauntlet on open ground first, well away from your buildings.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.citadel.title: Ruined Citadel
Wake and personally defeat the Harbinger
The Ancient Factory lies underground in the Overworld, and a Mech Eye locates it. Descend safely and leave supplies outside. Prepare a Nether Star before meeting the Harbinger; it is a consumed awakening item, not arena decoration.

Use the star on the inactive Harbinger when ready. Avoid rockets, laser lines, and charges, attacking between sequences. Do not assume a narrow entrance enables unlimited damage from any distance; fight within the intended area.

Collect Witherite after victory and accumulate four ingots for detection. Craft the Mechanical Fusion Anvil for weapon combination. Discovery, boss victory, material, and workstation are separate objectives, so verify each before spending all the loot elsewhere.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.factory.title: Ancient Factory
Find the Frosted Prison in snowy plains
The Frosted Prison stands in snowy Overworld plains, located with a Cursed Eye. Bring substantial protection, healing, and durability reserves. Explore gradually, marking exits and safe intermediate rooms; this is a large combat expedition rather than sightseeing.

The Strange Key drops from Aptrgangr and opens the Door of Seal. Let it register before use. Continue toward Maledictus beyond the opened passage and recover before entering the main chamber; winning the earlier encounter does not guarantee readiness.

Avoid grabs, strikes, and ranged sequences, retaliating during pauses. After personally defeating the boss, collect three Cursium Ingots together. Check the boss advancement separately from the key and structure discovery, then bring the metal back to your prepared cache.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.frosted.title: Frosted Prison
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.fusion.text.0: The Void Forge combines trophies from different dimensions. Prepare an Infernal Forge from the Netherite Monstrosity and a Void Core from the Ruined Citadel. The operation requires the Mechanical Fusion Anvil from Ancient Factory progression.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.fusion.text.1: Use the Infernal Forge as the base and Void Core as the addition, then collect the fusion result. Inspect the output before confirming; a vanilla anvil and arbitrary void material cannot substitute. Both inputs become part of the new weapon.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.fusion.text.2: Test the Void Forge away from animals and buildings. Using it on a block summons a fan of Void Runes, so keep allies out of the area ahead. The quest detects the item; a short practical test establishes its reach before your next difficult hunt.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.fusion.title: Fusion
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.guide_black_s: Black steel is the first Cataclysm metal that turns into tools at an ordinary crafting table. The sword takes two ingots and a stick, the pickaxe three ingots and two sticks, in the familiar iron-tool shapes. The targe, a small shield, is built differently: an ingot in the centre, four planks on the sides and four nuggets in the corners; nuggets come from an ingot at the same table.

Gather your stock from abandoned snowy structures and draugr drops, then craft the items one by one. Tracking is historical: after the mark you may use the tools rather than keep them untouched. Unwanted black steel gear smelts back into a nugget in a furnace or blast furnace, so part of the material returns.

The targe is held in the off hand and raised with the right mouse button, like an ordinary shield. Test its block on simple enemies before trusting it in a boss fight. This branch does not replace netherite gear, but it gives a sensible interim kit for trips into the mod’s first structures, where black steel is most common.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.guide_cursium: Cursium drops only from Maledictus: three or four ingots per victory. The Frosted Prison card merely checks that you have them, so the same ingots can be put to use. The cursium upgrade template is crafted with a netherite upgrade template in the centre, two black steel ingots at the sides and six gold ingots above and below.

At a smithing table combine the template, a netherite helmet and one cursium ingot. The other netherite armour pieces upgrade the same way; a full set costs four ingots, which may mean more than one fight with Maledictus. Cursium and black steel also make weapons: the Soul Render with its rush attack and the Cursed Bow that fires three phantom arrows.

Let the helmet be your first piece: it will show whether the rest of the metal is better spent on armour or on weapons. Do not melt down netherite parts for the sake of an experiment, and do not turn the ingots in to other cards that consume them until you have decided what matters more. A finished set is a real step up before the Burning Arena and Ignis.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.guide_eyes.te: The eight Cataclysm eyes are the only reliable way to find a specific structure. Each is crafted around an Eye of Ender from materials hinting at its purpose: the Eye of Monstrous needs two lava buckets, two netherite scrap and blackstone, while the Eye of Desert uses gold, an emerald, chiseled sandstone, cactus, a dead bush, bone and rotten flesh. JEI shows the exact layouts.

Use an eye in the dimension where its structure generates: the Eye of Monstrous works in the Nether, the Eye of Desert in Overworld deserts. Once thrown, the eye flies toward the target like an Eye of Ender heading for a stronghold and then vanishes; the item itself stays in your hand, so throw again every few hundred blocks until the direction is obvious.

Having both items once is enough for the mark; the book does not consume them. Craft them before hunting the Netherite Monstrosity and the Ancient Remnant so you never wander at random. Record coordinates as soon as you find a structure: the “find” advancement triggers on entering its bounds, and the fight itself can wait until you are fully prepared.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.guide_wither_: Test both firing modes at an open range away from any buildings

The Wither Assault Shoulder Weapon is a ranged weapon made of witherite from the Ancient Factory. The recipe places two witherite ingots in opposite corners, four gunpowder and a block of redstone in the centre. Witherite is also needed for the factory card and the Mechanical Fusion Anvil, so decide in advance how many ingots the weapon may take.

The right button fires Wither Missiles; sneaking while firing launches heavy howitzer shells. Both modes hit an area, so run the first test on open ground far from your base, animals and colony. Check the range, the spread and whether the shells break blocks, so you know where the weapon helps and where it endangers the shooter.

Confirm the manual objective only after trying both modes. The cannon works well against dense groups on Cataclysm arenas but does not replace melee in tight corridors where the blast catches you too. Keep it in a separate slot for open spaces and never fire near loot chests.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.ignitium.text: Ignitium armour upgrades Netherite equipment with a smithing template. Craft the template from a Netherite Upgrade Template, Nether Bricks, and Blaze Powder. Let it register, then prepare Netherite helmet and chestplate plus Ignitium Ingots.

Upgrade the pieces at a Smithing Table and inspect retained properties. The Elytra Chestplate additionally needs ordinary Elytra and a Mechanical Fusion Anvil: combine the completed Ignitium Chestplate with the wings. This follows smithing rather than attaching wings to an empty template.

Take the helmet and the combined chestplate, then test flight and protection somewhere safe. Two pieces do not make a full set — the leggings and boots are upgraded with the same template once you have more ignitium. Keep spare repair materials and rockets so that the rare armour serves on future expeditions instead of sitting in a chest as a collector’s piece.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.pets.text.0: These two objectives concern smaller Cataclysm creatures and interaction items. Craft a Netherite Effigy from a Netherite Ingot, Totem of Undying, redstone, gold, and Nether Bricks. Prepare it at home and let it register before use.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.pets.text.1: Remnant Skulls occur in Ancient Remnant and Modern Remnant loot. After item detection, use the effigy or skull on a clear surface: the item is consumed and creates a Netherite Ministrosity or Modern Remnant respectively. Leave enough room or creature placement fails.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.pets.text.2: The Ministrosity is tamed with a Lava Power Cell, while the Modern Remnant is fed a sniffer egg. Both items are expensive, so stock them in advance, and once tamed, watch how the pet behaves and obeys commands. House it somewhere protected near your base. The card checks only the starting items; spawning the creature and taming it are the next steps.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.pets.title: Pets
Find the Cursed Pyramid in the desert
Wake the Ancient Remnant by brushing the suspicious sand, then personally defeat it
The Cursed Pyramid stands in an Overworld desert, and the Desert Eye points the way. Bring a brush, a dependable weapon, armour and food. Treat the suspicious sand inside with care: broken with a pickaxe, it will not yield the archaeological find without which the boss cannot be woken.

Brush the sand until you obtain the Necklace of the Desert. Let it register, then use it on the inactive Ancient Remnant. It is a consumed awakening key; merely finding the large statue does not complete victory.

In the fight, keep away from charges, kicks and dangerous patches of sand, and strike once a sequence has ended. After a personal victory, gather the loot, including the material for the Sandstorm in a Bottle, and finish its recipe. You need not hunt for the necklace again for a mark you already hold, but a new summoning will need a new offering.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.pyramid.title: Cursed Pyramid
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.root.text.0: For early Cataclysm materials, explore the Overworld rather than searching everywhere for matching ores. Black Steel comes from abandoned snowy structures and Draugr, while Ancient Metal appears in desert structures and Koboleton loot. Prepare a shield, weapon, and room for separate batches.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.root.text.1: Collect four ingots of each metal together by type. Both types need not remain present simultaneously after detection. Craft the Belt of the Beginner separately from leather and an iron ingot for accessible starter equipment.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.root.text.2: Scout a small structure first and bring the loot home before you set your sights on a major boss. The first card has a modest name, but Cataclysm’s enemies are not built for early iron: the next expedition, to the Soul Forge, will demand far better protection, healing and fire resistance.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.root.title: First Find
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.soulforge.tas: Find the Soul Forge in the Nether
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.soulforge.tex: The Soul Blacksmith generates in the Nether. Craft a Monstrous Eye to locate it, record coordinates, and secure the approach. Bring Fire Resistance, enchanted armour, healing, and a weapon suited to a prolonged close fight.

Find the Netherite Monstrosity and clear smaller enemies from your route before the main battle. Avoid area strikes, lava attacks, and straight charges. Attack during openings and move away after your own sequence.

Collect the Infernal Forge after personally defeating the boss, checking structure discovery and victory separately. Despite its name, the forge item is a weapon rather than an industrial machine. Save it for later fusion with the Ruined Citadel’s Void Core at the Mechanical Fusion Anvil.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.sunken.task.0: Find the Sunken City in a deep ocean
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.sunken.task.2: Summon and personally defeat the Leviathan
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.sunken.text.0: Locate the Sunken City in deep Overworld oceans with an Abyss Eye. Prepare sustained Water Breathing, underwater mobility, lighting, and protected air reserves. Scout the entrance and local enemies while preserving a separate route to the surface.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.sunken.text.1: Craft an Abyssal Sacrifice for Leviathan using a Heart of the Sea, Nautilus Shell, Athame, coral component, and valuable material blocks. Let it register, then place it on the Altar of Abyss when ready; summoning consumes the offering.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.sunken.text.2: Track Leviathan’s movement and major attacks without neglecting air. Collect victory loot and craft Tidal Claws. Visiting the city, obtaining the sacrifice, personally winning, and crafting claws are distinct results; complete and check them in sequence.
codex.quest.hunt_cataclysm.sunken.title: Sunken City
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.bottling.task.1: Manual: form and power the bottling machine, supply water and an empty bucket and collect the filled bucket at the belt output.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.bottling.text.0: The bottling machine fills containers and runs fluid recipes, duroplast forming included. It is a multiblock where conveyor direction matters. Form it with the hammer on the central belt; connect fluid to the metal tank's ports and energy to the opposite top side.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.bottling.text.1: Make the first run with water and an empty bucket. Wait for the full bucket at the output and pick it up rather than leaving it on the floor. This test checks the belts, the power and the fluid input without spending expensive resin.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.bottling.text.2: Once a container has genuinely been filled, tick the manual goal. The machine may hold large containers while they fill under continuous supply; that is not a jammed conveyor but the switchable waiting mode described in the manual. For fuel and resin later, set up a separate line or fully account for the remaining water before changing fluids.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.bottling.title: Bottling Machine
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.cloche.text.0: The garden cloche grows suitable plants in a single compact block, consuming water and electricity. Match seeds and soil: not every plant accepts any ground. For the first run, take a familiar crop from the cloche recipes.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.cloche.text.1: Place the device, connect power through its connectors and water through the fluid input. Put soil and seed in the central slots. The harvest appears in the output slots on the right; place a receiver at the front hatch of the glass section.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.cloche.text.2: Fertiliser speeds growth, but check ordinary operation without it first. If production stops, check soil compatibility, water, energy and a free output. A separate cloche with oil seeds helps the fuel line, but compare its energy use and harvest rate with the squeezer's appetite; it will be no endless free farm.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.cloche.title: Garden Cloche
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.diesel.task.1: Manual: form the generator, supply accepted fuel and verify increasing receiving-storage energy while fuel is consumed.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.diesel.text.0: The diesel generator turns permitted liquid fuel into a strong flow of energy. First stock up on biodiesel and give the squeezer, fermenter and refinery independent power for start-up. The generator must not be the only source in a completely drained fuel system.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.diesel.text.1: Assemble the radiators, pipes, engineering blocks and scaffolding by the manual and form the mechanism with the hammer at the indicated point. Fuel enters through the lower corner ports; energy leaves through the connectors on top. The total output is shared among connected outputs, not multiplied by their number.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.diesel.text.2: Connect a load or a partly empty store and check that fuel falls while energy rises. Without a receiving output the generator need not run at all. Tick the manual goal after this check; then watch whether the farm keeps up with consumption. A fuel reserve that keeps shrinking means the supply is short, even while the generator still hums evenly.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.diesel.title: Diesel Generator
Duroplast is made from phenolic resin and serves as an insulator in electrical components. The chain begins with ethanol: the refinery turns it into acetaldehyde with a silver plate in the catalyst slot. The plate is not consumed, but without it the stage does not run.

Then another refinery recipe joins twelve units of acetaldehyde and eight of creosote into eight of resin. Split the stages between installations or clear the unsuitable inputs first. Feed the finished resin into the bottling machine and send the plate mould through as the item ingredient.

Every two hundred and fifty units of resin give one duroplast plate and return the mould; four plates take a thousand units. Collect both outputs: a lost mould stops the repetition. The metal press without resin is no substitute for this operation.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.duroplast.title: Duroplast
Manual: form and power the fermenter, process a supported crop and output ethanol into separate storage.
The fermenter turns suitable farm produce into ethanol. Build the multiblock to the diagram and strike the central cauldron with the hammer on the control port's side. Connect power, prepare a crop input and a separate tank unconnected to the squeezer's oil.

Potatoes or sugar cane will do for the first run: each gives eighty units of ethanol in the installed recipe. Different plants yield differently, so farms cannot be compared by item count alone. The input hatches at the back are marked blue; the fluid leaves below the orange item output.

Make ethanol and confirm it flows into storage before ticking the manual goal. If the process stops, inspect the power, the fluid level, leftover items and the redstone signal on the panel. With honey bottles, provide a return for the glass: a by-product item can halt production too.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.fermenter.title: Fermenter
The current biodiesel recipe has a third mandatory participant: saltpeter dust. It goes into the refinery's catalyst slot; without it the oil and ethanol just sit in their tanks. Get the dust by an available recipe or by processing raw material, checking the options in JEI.

Open the biodiesel recipe and check the exact catalyst before installing it. The silver plate belongs to acetaldehyde and does not replace saltpeter. The catalyst is not consumed, and the manual specifically describes manual installation: no stream of dust to the refinery is needed.

Make sure the item stays in its slot after the reaction. This small stock removes the usual cause of a motionless refinery with full fluid inputs. If it still does not run, check the power, fluid compatibility, the output and the control signal instead of piling in catalysts by the stack.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.guide_fuel_rest: Manual: keep a separate biodiesel reserve, restore generation from it on an isolated load and replenish the reserve.

The fuel line can stall in a circle: a generator without biodiesel does not power the machines that make the biodiesel. A jerrycan with a separate reserve and a charged capacitor break the deadlock. Prepare the reserve before the experiment, not after the whole base has stopped.

Fill the jerrycan with biodiesel from supported storage and keep it away from automatic consumption. On a small isolated load, stop the generator's ordinary supply, then bring it back with part of the reserve. Do not drain the whole shared grid for the test.

Once the restart has succeeded and the set-aside reserve is replenished, tick the manual goal. An empty jerrycan is no reserve: check what is in it and how much. If production loses fuel again after the restart, fix the long-term balance of oil, ethanol and electricity; an emergency refill solves the start, not a chronic shortage.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.guide_oil_seeds: A separate seed stock makes the oil line independent of a chance harvest. For this experiment take industrial hemp: its seeds suit the squeezer and give a hundred and twenty units of oil apiece in the installed recipe. Prepare plantings or a compatible cloche.

Build up sixty-four seeds while keeping a planting reserve apart. In a cloche, check soil, water, power and a free output for the plant's other products. Send only seeds into the oil line, and store the fibre separately for cloth and engineering goods.

The stock counts without being handed in, and it says nothing about the farm's speed. Once counted, compare how seeds replenish and how they are spent with the diesel section running. If oil goes faster than it comes, expand the planting or reduce the load: extra empty tanks only postpone the stop.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.mixer.task.1: Manual: form and power the mixer, combine water and redstone dust and extract redstone acid separately from input water.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.mixer.text.0: The industrial mixer combines a fluid with item ingredients. It makes redstone acid, certain chemicals and potions in bulk. Build and form the multiblock to the manual's layers, leaving access to the fluid ports and the item input.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.mixer.text.1: For a clear first test, make redstone acid: one redstone dust and two hundred and fifty units of water give the same amount of acid. Supply water, dust and power and send the result to a separate tank. Do not merge the finished acid with the incoming water line.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.mixer.text.2: Once the result is made and drawn off, tick the manual goal. If the machine holds several fluids, sort out the output mode and do not expect any connected tank to receive only the product you want. Before changing recipe, account for leftover fluid and ingredients, or the new process will wait on incompatible inputs.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.mixer.title: Industrial Mixer
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.refinery_ie.tas: Manual: form and power the refinery, install saltpeter, supply oil and ethanol, obtain biodiesel and check continued operation after extraction.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.refinery_ie.tex: The IE refinery mixes fluids and works with catalysts. Biodiesel needs plant oil from the squeezer, ethanol from the fermenter and saltpeter dust in the catalyst slot. In the installed version that dust is mandatory but is not consumed by the reaction.

Build the structure and form it with the hammer on the heavy engineering block of the middle layer. Fluids enter through the two side ports; the result leaves through the orange one at the front. The recipe joins eight units of oil and eight of ethanol into sixteen of biodiesel; both lines and electricity are required.

Get a bucket of biodiesel and make sure work continues after removing it, then tick the manual goal. If both tanks are full and there is no result, check the catalyst and the redstone control first. Old diagrams without saltpeter are incomplete for this version and will not start the reaction.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.squeezer.task.1: Manual: form and power the squeezer, process seeds and output plant oil into separate storage.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.squeezer.text.0: The squeezer extracts plant oil from suitable seeds and runs a few solid-material recipes. Build the multiblock by the manual and activate it with the hammer on the central wooden barrel on the control connector's side. Prepare electricity and separate storage for the oil.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.squeezer.text.1: Seeds go in through the blue-marked inputs at the back. An industrial hemp seed, for instance, gives a hundred and twenty units of oil by the installed recipe. The item output is marked orange, and the fluid leaves below it; an oil pipe is never attached to the item hatch.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.squeezer.text.2: Run a small batch and confirm the manual goal once oil has appeared and gone into a container. Keep seeds back for replanting. The same machine makes graphite dust by a separate recipe, so not every input yields fluid; check the process you chose.
codex.quest.ie_chemistry.squeezer.title: Squeezer
codex.quest.ie_gear.buzzsaw.text.0: The IE buzzsaw runs on a replaceable blade and suitable liquid fuel. The tool in the quest is only the base: make an ordinary blade separately and fit it through the engineer's workbench. Fuel the saw with biodiesel or another fuel permitted for it.
codex.quest.ie_gear.buzzsaw.text.1: Choose a small first tree well away from a wooden base. See which connected blocks the felling mode grabs and make room for the fallen wood. Do not try mass felling on a tree pressed right against a building.
codex.quest.ie_gear.buzzsaw.text.2: The blade wears, and the lubrication and capacity upgrades lift different limits. The stone-cutting blade turns the saw into a neat tool for stone, but it no longer fells trees. Before changing tasks, look at the attachment: a fuelled saw performs differently on different materials.
codex.quest.ie_gear.buzzsaw.title: Buzzsaw
codex.quest.ie_gear.chemthrower.text.0: The chemthrower sprays the loaded fluid and can ignite flammable mixtures. For a first acquaintance load water, not fuel: that way you learn the range and modes without a fire in the workshop. Fill the tool from compatible fluid storage or the bottling machine.
codex.quest.ie_gear.chemthrower.text.1: Open the settings and check the state of the pilot flame. Make a short spray on a clear pad and watch consumption. Different substances have different in-game effects, so the colour of a bucket will not tell you whether a mixture is safe for plants, animals and buildings.
codex.quest.ie_gear.chemthrower.text.2: Before changing fluid, remember what is left of the old one in the tank. Herbicide ruins vegetation and soil, and fuel with the igniter on is dangerous to the base. Such modes belong only on a prepared site with a clear purpose and a way to stop spraying; crafting the chemthrower requires no dangerous test fire.
codex.quest.ie_gear.chemthrower.title: Chemthrower
codex.quest.ie_gear.drill_ie.text.0: The IE hand drill runs on biodiesel and needs a drill head fitted. Make the tool body and the steel head, then put the drill into the engineer's workbench to install it. A drained battery has nothing to do with it: the engine needs liquid fuel.
codex.quest.ie_gear.drill_ie.text.1: Fuel the drill from a supported container or the bottling machine. Test mining on a small patch of stone and see what area the chosen head takes. There is a restricted mode for a single block; it helps next to utilities and valuable walls.
codex.quest.ie_gear.drill_ie.text.2: The head wears independently of the fuel and is repaired at the anvil. Underwater the ordinary drill does not work without the compressed-air upgrade. Take spare fuel into the mine and watch the head: a full tank of biodiesel will not save a broken working part.
codex.quest.ie_gear.drill_ie.title: Drill
Manual: use the maintenance kit to replace a drill head, retain the old head and verify mining one stone block.

The maintenance kit is only good together with a suitable spare part. For the test, take an assembled drill, a spare iron head and the kit itself. Choose a safe place away from fights, and do not wear out to breaking the only tool that can get you out of the mine.

Open the kit's portable interface and replace the drill head. Keep the old one for repair at the anvil. Make sure the new head is fitted rather than merely moved to a neighbouring slot, then mine one ordinary stone block.

Head swapped, stone mined; the manual goal can be ticked. The kit fills no empty fuel tank and makes no spare parts, so the jerrycan stays part of the travel set. Before returning to mass mining, look at the new head's area: a different material changes how the tool behaves.
codex.quest.ie_gear.misc_ie.text.0: The floodlight, the electric lantern and the maintenance kit cover different everyday needs. The lantern draws power straight from an LV wire and lights the work area; the floodlight throws a directed beam and needs its own power and the right control mode.
codex.quest.ie_gear.misc_ie.text.1: Put the lantern by the walkway and aim the floodlight at the far end of the site. The hammer changes the floodlight's direction, the screwdriver its redstone logic. If the light does not come on, check electricity and signal together instead of replacing a working lamp.
codex.quest.ie_gear.misc_ie.text.2: The maintenance kit lets you swap supported parts and service a tool away from the workbench, replacing a drill head for instance. It is no free repair for any item. Take a spare part with you and try the interface before the trip: without the right part the kit cannot undo wear.
codex.quest.ie_gear.misc_ie.title: Odds and Ends
codex.quest.ie_gear.powerpack.text.0: The powerpack carries a reserve of electricity for tools and armour. In the installed version the crafted frame needs a battery fitted through the engineer's workbench. So start with a suitable storage unit and look inside the pack before treating it as a ready battery.
codex.quest.ie_gear.powerpack.text.1: Fit the battery, charge the pack at the station and put it on the intended way. For the first try, hold a partly drained tool and watch the energy flow. The charging station itself needs power through the correct input.
codex.quest.ie_gear.powerpack.text.2: The pack can be combined with a compatible chestplate, but the manual warns that such a combined item charges at the station with restrictions. Try the plain separate pack first. By default it serves items in your hands and worn armour; charging the whole inventory takes a separate upgrade.
codex.quest.ie_gear.powerpack.title: Powerpack
codex.quest.ie_gear.railgun.text.0: The railgun accelerates a chosen projectile item with electricity. Prepare a charging station or a working powerpack and a stock of compatible projectiles, iron rods for example. A crafted weapon fills itself with neither energy nor ammunition.
codex.quest.ie_gear.railgun.text.1: Charge the railgun, choose a projectile type and fire at a safe target. Hold the button until the charge is ready, then release; look up the exact controls and ammunition switching in the pack's settings. Do not waste expensive electrodes as a first projectile.
codex.quest.ie_gear.railgun.text.2: The weapon spends both energy and the fired item. Some projectiles have special effects, so you need a clear line of fire and a backstop behind the target. The small internal reserve makes the powerpack a useful companion, but first make sure a charged battery is fitted inside it.
codex.quest.ie_gear.railgun.title: Railgun
codex.quest.ie_gear.revolver.text.0: The revolver is a weapon with separate cartridges, assembled from engineering parts. The quest wants the revolver itself and the hammer part; set that component aside until it is counted, even if others like it have already gone into recipes. Ammunition is made separately from a suitable blueprint.
codex.quest.ie_gear.revolver.text.1: Open the cylinder by interacting while crouching and load compatible cartridges. Fire the first shot with the ordinary type at a safe target with a backstop behind it. Different cartridges have different effects, so do not mix random ammunition before testing.
codex.quest.ie_gear.revolver.text.2: Shots attract hostile creatures and spend cartridges; an empty cylinder will not refill at the charging station. The speedloader hastens reloading, and other upgrades are fitted at the workbench. After the trial, take the weapon out of your active hand in the workshop and keep dangerous ammunition apart from everyday consumables.
codex.quest.ie_gear.revolver.title: Revolver
codex.quest.ie_gear.shaders.text.0: Shaders change the look of compatible engineering gear, not its properties. An ordinary bag holds a random shader. By the manual, bags are found in chests, traded from villagers and received as rewards for certain bosses; pick whichever path is already open to you.
codex.quest.ie_gear.shaders.text.1: Get a bag of common rarity first and let the goal count it in your inventory, only then open it. Look at the list of compatible items and fit the chosen shader through the engineer's workbench's special slot. Some decorative objects accept a shader right in the world.
codex.quest.ie_gear.shaders.text.2: A new pattern adds no damage, fuel or speed. Rarer bags can be exchanged by an available recipe for bags of a lower tier, but that changes the odds of a rare design. The branch is optional for industry and works well as a small collection once the workshop is equipped.
codex.quest.ie_gear.shaders.title: Shaders
codex.quest.ie_gear.skyhook.text.0: The skyhook carries the player along suitable wires and cables. For a safe first route take the structural steel cable from the quest: it carries no current. String it between two low platforms with an easy step-off.
codex.quest.ie_gear.skyhook.text.1: Hook on while standing next to the cable. Ride a short span, checking the turn at junctions and a controlled dismount. Grabbing a cable hard after a long fall hurts, so do not begin the lesson with a jump from a tower.
codex.quest.ie_gear.skyhook.text.2: Live electrical wires are dangerous without the insulated-grip upgrade. Even with protection you need a safe landing spot: releasing the hook or crouching drops you off the cable. Master a low route without electricity first, then extend the line to distant platforms without blocking conveyors and access to machines.
codex.quest.ie_gear.skyhook.title: Skyhook
codex.quest.ie_gear.steel_armor.text.0: Steel armour is the engineer's ordinary material protection before complex electric gear. Take steel from the blast furnace and make the chestplate by the recipe. Do not spend the last steel set aside for a tool if the armour is only a spare set for now.
codex.quest.ie_gear.steel_armor.text.1: Put on the chestplate and compare protection and durability with your current gear. It asks for no fuel or charge, but it wears in combat. For a proper ordinary set, fill the other slots with matching pieces and leave room for tools.
codex.quest.ie_gear.steel_armor.text.2: Steel gives no Mekanism radiation shielding and does not replace Faraday electrical protection. Choose equipment for the specific danger, not just by material. Such a chestplate serves well as a reserve in a clean corner of the base while the main set is repaired or charged before the next expedition.
codex.quest.ie_gear.steel_armor.title: Steel Armor
codex.quest.ie_gear.turret.text.0: The gun turret and the chemical turret guard a chosen area on their own. Before supplying power and the enabling signal, set the owner, the target list and the exceptions for allies. Tell the blacklist and the whitelist apart carefully: the same names in the other mode change the meaning of the setting.
codex.quest.ie_gear.turret.text.1: The gun turret needs compatible cartridges and room for casings; the chemical one a permitted fluid and the right pilot-flame mode. Resources go to the lower and rear ports as the manual shows. Start with the installation off and check where it could fire.
codex.quest.ie_gear.turret.text.2: Switch on at a separate site with no villagers, pets or passers-by. Keep an emergency cut-off within reach and a solid backstop behind the target. Two turrets in a chest do not yet pick targets correctly: before guarding the base, check each turret's settings and allow no fire on your own buildings.
codex.quest.ie_gear.turret.title: Turrets
codex.quest.ie_machines.arc.task.1: Manual: form and power the arc furnace with three electrodes, run a recipe, collect its product and check the slag output.
codex.quest.ie_machines.arc.text.0: The arc furnace melts metals and runs alloy recipes in parallel. Build it to the manual's layers and form it with the hammer on the cauldron. Bring strong power to the rear connectors, prepare three graphite electrodes and separate spots for product and slag.
codex.quest.ie_machines.arc.text.1: In the interface, main materials go on the left, additives into the special slots on the right and electrodes on top. For the first melt, take a simple proven recipe and a small batch. Metal comes out at the front, slag at the back; when those spots are full, the furnace stops.
codex.quest.ie_machines.arc.text.2: Electrodes wear out and are replaced by hand: automatic ore feeding does not make the furnace maintenance-free. Watch their remaining life and keep spares nearby. Tick the manual goal after a successful melt, collection of the product and a check of the slag output; an electrode without a formed furnace says nothing about a start.
codex.quest.ie_machines.arc.title: Arc Furnace
codex.quest.ie_machines.assembler.task.1: Manual: form both machines; run an ordinary assembler recipe and a blueprint recipe in the automated workbench, collecting both outputs.
codex.quest.ie_machines.assembler.text.0: The assembler repeats ordinary crafting recipes, while the auto engineer's workbench works from IE blueprints. They are two different multiblock machines, both built by the manual. Do not look for them as finished items: prepare the structural parts and form each with the hammer at its own point.
codex.quest.ie_machines.assembler.text.1: The assembler can hold up to three recipes in sequence and use the result of one in the next. Start with a simple wooden item, supply materials and power. Insert a suitable blueprint into the auto workbench, choose a result and load its ingredients; finished items roll off the end of the belt.
codex.quest.ie_machines.assembler.text.2: Check that each machine produces at least one item and that the output is reachable, then tick the manual goal. A blueprint and an ordinary assembler recipe are different things. If something stops, compare the chosen template, the actual materials, the power and the redstone control before complicating the routes from the warehouse.
codex.quest.ie_machines.assembler.title: Assembler
codex.quest.ie_machines.conveyor.text.0: Conveyors carry items through the shop in plain sight. An ordinary belt moves whatever lands on it but will not pull a chest's contents without a proper extractor. Make eight belts and test the direction on a short line before any large build.
codex.quest.ie_machines.conveyor.text.1: The item router distributes cargo by filters, and the batcher releases pre-assembled sets. Start with two different cheap materials and separate outputs. Belt directions and filters must agree, or items will ride to the wrong machine or stall on the line.
codex.quest.ie_machines.conveyor.text.2: Check a full receiver and any dropped items; do not leave them lying until they vanish. Near the player, covered belts and clear walkways are appropriate. Batch feeding matters most for recipes with several ingredients: it keeps one resource from hogging the whole input.
codex.quest.ie_machines.conveyor.title: Conveyors
Manual: form and power the crusher, process cobblestone and collect gravel through its intended output.
The IE crusher processes ore, metals and some building blocks. Stack the parts to the manual's layers and form the structure with the hammer on the central fence of the long side, where the control input sits. Electricity goes to the connector on top of the side section; items drop into the drums.

Fence off the top intake: a living creature in the crusher takes heavy damage. For the first run, drop one cobblestone block and collect the result through the lower front output without stepping inside. Tick the manual goal after real processing and extraction of the product.

An iron ore block gives two dust and a possible by-product; raw iron gives one dust with a chance of a second. No doubling of every material is promised here. If the crusher stands idle, check power, the input recipe, the output and the redstone signal on the panel; the screwdriver may have changed the control logic.
codex.quest.ie_machines.crusher_ie.title: Crusher
codex.quest.ie_machines.excavator.task.1: Manual: form the engine and bucket wheel at a surveyed vein, supply power and collect mined output at the rear.
codex.quest.ie_machines.excavator.text.0: The excavator draws minerals from a surveyed IE vein and slowly depletes it. Choose the site by core samples, then prepare two structures: the engine and the bucket wheel. Their relative position is shown in the manual; the working point is at the bottom of the wheel.
codex.quest.ie_machines.excavator.text.1: Build the engine and form it with the hammer on the rear central heavy engineering block; a correctly placed wheel joins the assembly. The wheel itself is formed separately on its central steel block. Bring power to the side connectors and prepare the rear product output.
codex.quest.ie_machines.excavator.text.2: Fence off the moving part, run a trial dig and get the result into storage before ticking the manual goal. Barren rock is no fault: its share depends on the location and richness. Watch the energy, the output filling up and the vein depleting; the excavator makes no endless ore from any patch of ground.
codex.quest.ie_machines.excavator.title: Excavator
codex.quest.ie_machines.guide_electrode_: The arc furnace needs its worn electrodes replaced by hand. So that a stop does not catch you out, make a separate stock of three and keep it by a safe approach to the interface. Electrodes also suit certain weapon recipes, so do not mix the maintenance stock with ammunition.

In the installed version eight coke dust are pressed by the squeezer into one HOP-graphite dust. The bottling machine forms an electrode from four such dust, the rod mould and a thousand units of creosote; the mould is returned. Set this process up in advance rather than hunting for the old recipe through a rare blueprint.

Stop the furnace before servicing, inspect the life of all three working electrodes and replace the worn ones by hand. The check itself does not spend the quest's spare items. After replacing, run an ordinary melt and remove the slag: a fresh electrode will not fix a blocked output or weak power.
codex.quest.ie_machines.press.task.4: Manual: form the press, install the plate mould and produce an iron plate from an ingot while supplying FE.
codex.quest.ie_machines.press.text.0: The metal press shapes metal with interchangeable moulds. Build the multiblock by the manual and activate it with the hammer on the piston. Energy comes in on top of the piston, items travel by conveyor; the belts' direction determines which end is input and which output.
codex.quest.ie_machines.press.text.1: Make the plate, rod and wire moulds from the right blueprint at the engineer's workbench. A mould is installed by applying it to the press; then feed in a suitable metal. For the test, stamp an iron plate: the recipe takes one iron ingot, and the mould goes back to work and is not spent like metal.
codex.quest.ie_machines.press.text.2: After a successful operation, find the result in the output inventory and tick the manual goal. Change the mould deliberately, before a new batch. Iron rods and copper wire have recipes and outputs of their own; with three moulds in the chest the press still produces one kind at a time.
codex.quest.ie_machines.press.title: Metal Press
codex.quest.ie_machines.sample.text.0: IE mineral veins are separate deposits for the excavator, not the ore blocks you see in a cave. Survey tools find their traces in natural soil and stone. Take samples at well-spaced points: neighbouring readings do little to pin down the centre of a deposit.
codex.quest.ie_machines.sample.text.1: Once you find a promising spot, place the sample drill on solid ground, connect power and start it. When it finishes, pull the core sample out by hand. Water, air or an artificial structure under the drill will not stand in for a proper mineral survey site.
codex.quest.ie_machines.sample.text.2: Study the core's composition and richness, write down the coordinates and compare neighbouring points before building the excavator. A good spot raises the share of useful material over barren rock. The item goal wants the tools, the drill and a core, but one random core does not yet mean the deposit is worth working.
codex.quest.ie_machines.sample.title: Ore Survey
codex.quest.ie_machines.storage.task.1: Manual: form the silo and fluid tank; test insertion and extraction of items and fluid through their intended ports.
codex.quest.ie_machines.storage.text.0: The silo holds a large amount of one item type, the big tank a single fluid. They are separate multiblocks of sheet metal and supports built to the manual's diagrams. Decide first what goes where: seeds in the silo, creosote in the tank, so the working flows do not mix.
codex.quest.ie_machines.storage.text.1: Build both structures and form them with the hammer. Items enter the silo from the top or bottom and leave at the bottom. Fluid enters the tank through the top or bottom port and is drawn through the lower central block; a redstone signal can enable automatic output.
codex.quest.ie_machines.storage.text.2: The installed version's manual gives the capacities: 41,472 items for the silo and 512 buckets for the tank. Test a small input and retrieval of each resource, then tick the manual goal. A comparator will show the fill level, but it stops the upstream production only when wired into its control.
codex.quest.ie_machines.storage.title: Storages
codex.quest.ie_power.capacitor.text.0: The LV capacitor stores energy between the generator and the machines. It helps ride out a short lull in the wind or build a reserve for the drill rig. It produces no energy and makes a weak transmission line no stronger.
codex.quest.ie_power.capacitor.text.1: Place the block, set its sides with the hammer and connect the source to the input and the consumer to the output. Compare the face markings with the manual, especially after rotating it. With the consumer disconnected the reserve should grow; then connect a small load and make sure it falls.
codex.quest.ie_power.capacitor.text.2: If the battery is full and the machine idle, check the output face, the connector and the machine's energy port. If the reserve melts away under any work, compare average generation with consumption. The next grid tiers need compatible capacitors or transformers: joining different wires at random makes no voltage step.
codex.quest.ie_power.capacitor.title: Capacitors
codex.quest.ie_power.dynamo.text.0: The kinetic dynamo turns the rotation of an IE water wheel into electricity. The wheel itself has no FE output, so the generator next to it is mandatory. Place the dynamo first, then attach the wheel to its mechanical side as the manual shows.
codex.quest.ie_power.dynamo.text.1: Run the water around the wheel so the flow actually turns it rather than surrounding it with still source blocks. As you reshape the channel, watch the speed and how much energy reaches the capacitor. IE allows up to three wheels in a row on one shaft.
codex.quest.ie_power.dynamo.text.2: Connect the wire to the dynamo's energy output while keeping the channel accessible. A Create shaft is no substitute for the wheel: the dynamo accepts only IE's own rotational sources. If the wheel turns yet storage stays empty, check the dynamo's orientation and the electrical connection separately from the water.
codex.quest.ie_power.dynamo.title: Dynamo and Water Wheel
codex.quest.ie_power.guide_grid_diagnosi: Manual: verify unloaded capacitor charging, supply to one operating machine and transfer interruption with the breaker.

To diagnose the grid, pick one generator, one capacitor and one ordinary machine. Disconnect the other branches while keeping safe access to the readings. The task is to tell no generation from a wrong route and from a shortage of power under load, without building a new power station.

First charge the capacitor with the machine disconnected. Then run it on a short, known batch and watch the reserve and the transfer with the voltmeter. A full battery beside a starving machine points to the output, the connector or the wire; a melting reserve with sound transfer means consumption has outrun generation.

Open the breaker and confirm the supply has stopped, then restore the original layout. Tick the manual goal after all three observations: charging without load, running under load and a controlled cut-off. Do not overload a wire until it burns on purpose; its limit is compared with the readings and the values in the manual.
codex.quest.ie_power.guide_insulated_rou: Insulated low-voltage wire belongs where a power line runs close to the workplace. Make insulated copper coils by the recipe and mark out a short segment to replace. Never swap live wire: cut off the source and account for batteries on both sides.

Remove the old connection with the cutters and string insulated wire between compatible LV connectors. Keep a clear span and safe connector placement. Insulation protects against touch, but it does not raise the wire's carrying capacity.

Switch the power on and check the same load that ran before the swap. If the wire vanishes under load, look for an overload, not a lack of insulation. Safety is not tested by touching on purpose: confirming the wire type and a correct connection is enough. The next experiment will separate a transmission problem from insufficient generation.
codex.quest.ie_power.lightning.task.1: Manual: form the lightning rod from the manual, install its steel mast and connect its energy output to storage.
codex.quest.ie_power.lightning.text.0: The IE lightning rod is a multiblock power station, not the copper lightning rod of the vanilla game. Build the base to the manual's layers and form it with the hammer at the indicated point. No finished multiblock item is needed: the installation grows from building parts in the world.
codex.quest.ie_power.lightning.text.1: Above the top connector, stack steel fences into a tall mast; a lattice of fences at the top raises the chance of catching a strike. Connect the side energy outputs to storage that can absorb the pulse and keep a safe distance for watching.
codex.quest.ie_power.lightning.text.2: Output depends on the weather and on lightning strikes, so this is a supplementary source, not power for a continuous factory. Tick the manual goal after forming the base, mounting the mast and checking the output connection. Waiting for a storm is interesting, but there is no need to summon lightning by command or put the player at risk.
codex.quest.ie_power.lightning.title: Lightning Rod
codex.quest.ie_power.safety.text.0: Working with wires begins with switching off and a safe route, not with hoping to survive a shock. The breaker switch opens a controlled connection, the voltmeter shows electrical readings, and the Faraday suit has a limited protective mechanic. One chestplate from the quest does not yet count as a suit.
codex.quest.ie_power.safety.text.1: Fit the breaker into a test line and make sure the transfer stops. Take voltmeter readings before and after switching off. Remember the storage beyond the switch: a disconnected generator does not mean the whole segment is dead.
codex.quest.ie_power.safety.text.2: The full Faraday suit is meant chiefly for its own voltage range and gives no universal safety on HV; a heavy discharge is especially dangerous. Do not test that on yourself. Use insulated wire wherever possible, keep the rest out of walkways and make sure nothing is flowing before touching with a tool.
codex.quest.ie_power.safety.title: Safety
codex.quest.ie_power.thermo.text.0: The thermoelectric generator draws energy from the temperature difference on opposite sides. It needs no dynamo. Prepare one hot and one cold source from supported fluids or blocks, checking their properties in the manual.
codex.quest.ie_power.thermo.text.1: Place the sources facing each other on opposite sides of the generator. Two adjacent faces make no pair: a hot block in front and a cold one at the side may not give the expected result. Connect the output to storage and look at the real output.
codex.quest.ie_power.thermo.text.2: Protect the surroundings from lava and keep the cold block from changing. If the cold source melted or was replaced, recheck the temperature difference. The generator suits a small steady load, but its output is set by the pair you chose; it will not replace a diesel source no matter how many wires you attach.
codex.quest.ie_power.thermo.title: Thermoelectric Generator
codex.quest.ie_power.transformer.text.0: Transformers link the different tiers of the wire grid. The ordinary one joins LV and MV, the high-voltage one MV and HV. They produce no energy and replace no battery, so first prepare a source and a proven consumer on opposite sides of the step.
codex.quest.ie_power.transformer.text.1: Place the transformer with access to both connections and attach the permitted wire types. The manual shows the sides and placement options. Two identical tiers are no pair for a transformer: to simply continue a line you need a connector or a relay.
codex.quest.ie_power.transformer.text.2: Test the transfer with a small load, then connect the rest of the shop. The lower tier of a segment still sets the allowed power: a high-voltage main line does not protect a thin low-voltage tail from overload. Place the steps so the wires stay out of walkways and remain reachable with the power off.
codex.quest.ie_power.transformer.title: Transformers
codex.quest.ie_power.windmill_ie.text.0: The IE windmill turns the kinetic dynamo, and it is the dynamo that produces electricity. Prepare the dynamo in addition to the quest items. Place it first, then attach the windmill to the right side and leave open space in front of the blades.
codex.quest.ie_power.windmill_ie.text.1: Eight cloth sails make the blades more efficient. Apply them to the installed windmill as the manual describes and watch the speed change. Obstacles in front of the structure reduce output, while rain and storms can strengthen the wind; height alone does not describe the mechanics.
codex.quest.ie_power.windmill_ie.text.2: Bring the dynamo's energy to a capacitor and check the output in ordinary weather. After a successful test, do not build right up against the site: a decorative wall can spoil the airflow. A windmill and eight sails in your inventory speak of a kit, not of a link to the generator.
codex.quest.ie_power.windmill_ie.title: Windmill
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_hv.text.0: High voltage serves big consumers and long-distance lines. The steel coil and HV connectors are rated for their own tier. Plan the route before installing so the wires cannot be touched by accident and can be serviced safely.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_hv.text.1: Connect a compatible source and receiver; use the HV transformer for the step down to MV. HV wire is never attached straight to an LV connector. Check the allowed span, the wire's capacity and each connector's limit in the manual.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_hv.text.2: The insulated LV and MV variants do not carry over to HV. Protect the line with distance and by switching it off during work; a Faraday suit is no reason to touch high voltage. With several generators the combined flow on the main line can exceed its limit even though each source works fine on its own.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_hv.title: High Voltage
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_lv.text.0: The low-voltage grid suits the first machines and modest generation. Make a copper coil and two LV connectors. Put one on the source's energy output and the other on the consumer's input; a decorative relay will not stand in for a connector here.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_lv.text.1: Apply the coil to the first connector, then to the second. The line between them must be clear of blocks. Before adding branches, check that energy accumulates at the consumer and look at the source's state.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_lv.text.2: Bare wire shocks on contact. Route it away from walkways or take the insulated LV variant. The wire limit and the connector limit are different constraints; the manual shows their current values. Several sources on one segment can overload it even when every individual connection is sound.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_lv.title: Low Voltage
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_mv.text.0: Medium voltage travels through electrum wire and MV connectors. It suits an expanding workshop once the low-voltage route limits transmission. First make sure the source really has the output: new wire will not raise a water wheel's generation.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_mv.text.1: Make an electrum coil and two MV connectors and prepare compatible connection points. Join them with a separate line and measure the consumer's supply. The link to the old LV segment needs a transformer, not a relay of another colour.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_mv.text.2: Route bare wire where it cannot be touched; MV has an insulated variant. Check the load on the whole shared line: branches add up. If the problem remains, look for a connector or machine-port limit before replacing every cable with the next tier; there may be only one bottleneck.
codex.quest.ie_power.wire_mv.title: Medium Voltage
codex.quest.ie_start.blast.text.0: The simple blast furnace turns iron into steel on high-carbon fuel. Prepare twenty-seven blast bricks, iron and coke or suitable charcoal. The structure is a solid three-by-three-by-three cube; the hammer strikes the centre of a side face.
codex.quest.ie_start.blast.text.1: Load the raw material and fuel through the interface. Slag comes out along with the steel; remove both products regularly. This furnace needs no cable, and ordinary coal is no substitute for permitted blast fuel.
codex.quest.ie_start.blast.text.2: Collect sixteen steel ingots. The simple furnace has no automatic inputs or outputs: a hopper outside will not spare you the hand work. Later it can be upgraded; for now keep coke nearby and do not forget the slag, which stops the work even with a full stock of iron.
codex.quest.ie_start.blast.title: Blast Furnace
codex.quest.ie_start.coke_oven.text.0: The coke oven makes coke and creosote without electricity. Stack twenty-seven coke bricks into a solid three-by-three-by-three cube and strike the centre block of a side face with the hammer. Once it forms, open the interface rather than trying to light a single brick.
codex.quest.ie_start.coke_oven.text.1: Load coal for coke or logs for charcoal. In the installed version the oven takes batches of up to sixteen coal or eight logs at a time; it runs slowly, so fill it up. For the goal, collect sixteen coke.
codex.quest.ie_start.coke_oven.text.2: Creosote builds up separately, and when it has nowhere to go, production stops. The oven does not push the fluid out by itself: scoop it with a container or set up a pump. Save the creosote for treated wood and the coke for the blast furnace: one site, two useful products.
codex.quest.ie_start.coke_oven.title: Coke Oven
codex.quest.ie_start.components.text.0: Iron, steel and electronic components keep turning up in engineering machine recipes. Besides ingots, prepare plates, wire and a suitable blueprint. Hand tools are enough for the first small batches; the industrial press comes later.
codex.quest.ie_start.components.text.1: Make eight iron, eight steel and four electronic components. Check the recipe of each kind: similar parts are not interchangeable, and an electronic component does not come from simply adding redstone to a steel one. Some of the operations run on the engineer's workbench from a blueprint.
codex.quest.ie_start.components.text.2: Keep the three stocks apart and look at the material list of the next multiblock in advance; that way you return to the workbench less often mid-build. Once components are needed constantly, the auto workbench can repeat the blueprints, but walking the chain by hand once is worthwhile.
codex.quest.ie_start.components.title: Components
codex.quest.ie_start.guide_creosote_drai: The coke oven stops when the creosote has nowhere to go. A pump and a separate barrel turn hand scooping into a proper drainage section. Prepare pipes and put the barrel where its level is easy to check without going near wires or open lava.

Set the pump's lower sides with the hammer: input toward the oven, output toward the barrel, unneeded connections off. The pump works on an enabling redstone signal, and electricity switches on boosted pumping. Look at the fluid actually moving, not just at a connected pipe.

Drain the accumulated creosote and wait for the coke batch to continue. The barrel is finite too: spend the fluid on wood or expand storage when the surplus is steady. This branch removes one specific stoppage of steel production and builds a creosote reserve for graphite and chemistry.
codex.quest.ie_start.guide_hot_blast.tex: Preheaters speed up the improved blast furnace with hot blast air. They do not replace coke, and they cannot be bolted onto the simple furnace as accelerators. Prepare two devices and a grid that can carry them alongside the workshop.

Fit one preheater at each of the improved furnace's designated side ports. Bring power to the right connectors and compare the same recipe with heating off and on. For a fair experiment, use the same amount of iron and free outputs.

If no speed-up shows, check placement and power first, then fuel and slag. A faster furnace eats coke faster, so make sure the coke oven and the creosote drain do not become the next bottleneck. A pair of preheaters speaks of equipment; the real acceleration shows on the working pair.
codex.quest.ie_start.guide_improved_blas: Manual: form an improved blast furnace, feed iron and coke from above and receive steel at the front and slag at the back.

The improved blast furnace removes the simple furnace's limit of manual inputs. Make twenty-seven reinforced blast bricks and prepare a hopper for the top. Before rebuilding, stop the old furnace and take out the iron, fuel, steel and slag so nothing is lost.

Build the new structure by the manual and form it with the hammer. Iron and coke go in at the top, steel comes out at the front and slag at the back. Set separate receivers and load only a small trial batch at first, without accelerators or big warehouse lines.

Wait for both products to be ejected automatically and tick the manual goal. If the metal came out but the slag found no room, the installation is not yet ready for long runs. Preheaters are added later and need FE; the furnace upgrade itself chiefly brings supported automation of maintenance.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.text.0: The engineer's hammer, wire cutters and screwdriver do different jobs. The hammer forms multiblock machines and changes block settings, the cutters work with wire and certain recipes, and the screwdriver switches supported control modes. Keep all three within reach on the hotbar.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.text.1: Try the hammer on a safe block and watch how the direction changes. A multiblock comes to life not from a blow on any casing but from a strike at the point the manual names. On a complex structure compare the layers first and only then hunt for the mistake with the tool.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.text.2: The cutters must not snip a live supply line by accident while equipment is running. Cut off the source before servicing wires and watch tool wear. The screwdriver often inverts the redstone response, so after changing a mode check what the signal now means: start or stop.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.title: Engineer's Hammer
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.text.0: The Engineer's Manual is the main reference for building Immersive Engineering machines. Craft it at the crafting table and keep it next to the hammer. The multiblock pages are the most valuable: a single picture of a finished machine will not tell you where the hidden parts go.
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.text.1: Open the coke oven section and page through the layers of the diagram. Look at the material list and the spot to strike with the hammer. Then find the electrical connections: the manual distinguishes connectors, relays and transformers, though they look alike and often stand side by side.
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.text.2: Numbers on some pages are filled in from the world settings, so take current outputs from your own copy of the book. JEI shows component recipes; the manual shows assembly and machine ports. The two sources complement each other, and both are worth a look before buying a large batch of steel.
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.title: Engineer's Manual
codex.quest.ie_start.scaffold.text.0: Steel scaffolding serves both as machine framework and as a handy industrial platform. For the quest, make sixteen blocks of the standard variant.
