Before a journey, choose a useful effect: healing, fire resistance or regeneration. Check the remaining doses and do not mistake identical-looking vials for endless ones. Partly used vials of the same brew can be combined on a crafting table, making the travel stock more compact.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.elements: Make the four basic runes separately. Each uses Manasteel and Mana Powder, produced by treating a suitable ordinary powder in the pool. Water also needs bone meal, sugar cane, and a fishing rod; Air uses a carpet, feather, and string.

Earth needs Stone, a Coal Block, and a mushroom. Fire needs a Nether Brick item, gunpowder, and nether wart; check that you have the item rather than a brick block. Finish each recipe with mana, Livingrock, and a wand click.

Store completed runes separately. Rune catalysts return from later Runic Altar recipes, but that rule does not extend to the apothecary or crafting table. These four elements unlock seasonal runes and the Terrasteel plate.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.flowers2: Obtain a functional flower such as a Hopperhock

The Hopperhock collects dropped items and places them in nearby storage. Craft it in the apothecary and plant it beside the collection area with an accessible chest. As a functional flower, it binds to a pool when using mana, rather than to a spreader.
Drop one unneeded item into the working area and make sure it ended up in the right chest. Frames on the storage set filters; test a simple layout without them first, then add restrictions.

Keep it from stealing apothecary ingredients, altar components, or Endoflame fuel. Obtaining the flower completes the item objective; a test transfer proves useful operation. Filtering supports crop collection and safer servicing of other magical equipment.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.guide_re: A seasonal rune demonstrates the difference between consumed ingredients and catalysts. For Spring, prepare Water and Fire runes, three saplings, and wheat. Put everything on the Runic Altar and supply eight thousand mana.

Once ready, add Livingrock and finish with the wand. Collect the Rune of Spring alongside the returned input runes. Count your materials before another operation so a catalyst is not left outside storage.

This return applies to the Runic Altar operation; a petal recipe may consume its runes. Save Spring for the Terrasteel Helmet. Understanding these roles reduces unnecessary basic-rune production and pressure on your mana supply.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.halo.tex: The Assembly Halo is a portable crafting table with recipe memory. Craft and hold it to display its slots. Clicking the crafting-table image opens a grid for making items from your inventory.

Complete a simple recipe, then click an empty halo slot to save the last-used pattern. Selecting that saved recipe attempts to craft it from available materials. Torches or planks make clear first experiments.

The halo cannot create ingredients or retrieve them from arbitrary world chests. If repeating a craft fails, inspect your supplies and selected recipe. Sneak-punch a saved pattern to delete it. This is a useful travelling tool before expeditions for elven and runic resources.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.mana_run: The Rune of Mana complements the four elements and is used by more complex devices. Place five Manasteel Ingots and one Mana Pearl on the Runic Altar, with Livingrock ready for the finishing step.

The altar needs eight thousand mana in addition to the energy already spent making its ingredients. Aim a charged spreader at it, wait for readiness, add Livingrock, and use the wand. Putting the pearl back into a pool does not make a rune.

Make sure you picked up the rune and not components lifted too early. Keep it for the terra plate or another planned recipe. There is no need to stockpile runes: first see which ones your next device consumes and which come back as catalysts.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.terra_ge: The Terra Blade and Terrasteel Helmet are your first expensive uses for the alloy. The helmet needs an existing Manasteel Helmet, Livingwood components, and a Rune of Spring; it upgrades armour rather than following the ordinary five-ingot helmet pattern.

Craft both items and charge portable mana storage. The Terra Blade uses mana for its abilities, while Botania equipment can use mana to restore durability. Test the weapon against a safe target away from animals and decorative builds.

Check the result and the available charge before a serious fight. One helmet is not protection yet, so cover the remaining slots with suitable armour. This gear will help you prepare for Gaia, but enchantments, healing and a clear arena will still be needed.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.terra_pl: The Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate transforms mana materials into Terrasteel. Its crafting ingredients include Lapis Blocks, a Manasteel Block, and five runes: the four elements plus Mana. It also needs a separate foundation in the world.

Build a three-by-three base with Livingrock in the centre and corners and Lapis Blocks at the four side centres. Put the plate above the central Livingrock. Check the Lexicon projection, then add sparks above the plate and a nearby pool.

Before starting, fill the pool at least halfway and remove any item collectors nearby. A plate without its base will not run the recipe. A fully built platform lets you carry out the next expensive experiment without a break, without dismantling anything in the middle of the mana transfer.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.terraste: Collect a Terrasteel Ingot from the plate

One Terrasteel Ingot costs half a million mana, half a normal pool. Accumulate this reserve first and verify the plate foundation and spark connection. Prepare one Manasteel Ingot, one Mana Pearl, and one Mana Diamond.

Drop all three onto the plate and step back to avoid picking them up. Watch the transformation while maintaining supply. Retrieving an ingredient midway loses the mana already transferred to the plate, making a restarted attempt expensive.

Collect only the completed ingot and wait for the Terrasteel advancement. Decide how to spend it before crafting: portals, tools, and armour need further batches. This recipe tests home generation much more seriously than a few Manasteel Ingots.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.text.0: Arcane Essence supplies clothing and ingot recipes. Collect it in magical structures and from spellcasting enemies. Surround an iron, copper, or gold ingot with eight essence to make one Arcane Ingot; the four requested ingots need thirty-two essence.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.text.1: The Arcane Anvil has a separate recipe using a normal anvil, Amethyst Blocks, a diamond, and Polished Deepslate. Place it beside the Inscription Table. It upgrades scrolls, equipment, and books, while inscription remains the table’s job.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.text.2: To raise a scroll’s level, use ink of the rarity of the spell’s next level and look at the result in the interface. Stacking two identical scrolls in the hope of vanilla book-combining does nothing here. Save rare ink for a spell you truly need and mind the cost shown.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.title: Arcane Metal
codex.quest.magic_irons.guide_ink_ladder: In the alchemist’s cauldron ink rises in rarity while shrinking in volume. The cauldron itself needs Cinder Essence, so prepare for the ancient knights of the Nether first. Place the finished device by your bottle storage and label the input tier.

Four bottles of Common Ink plus a copper ingot produce one Uncommon Ink. Later upgrades use iron, gold, and amethyst. Each recipe takes one thousand millibuckets of the previous tier and yields two hundred fifty of the next. Load one selected type and bottle the result.

Check the new ink’s name before repeating. The chain eats the starting volume quickly, so leave a reserve for simple scrolls. This route leads to legendary ink, but it does not make it free and does not lift your book’s rarity limit.
codex.quest.magic_irons.guide_scroll_for: The Scroll Forge creates spells from paper, ink, and a school focus. Craft it from Crying Obsidian and Polished Deepslate. Prepare ink of an available rarity and a school item, such as a Blaze Rod for Fire or Ender Pearl for Ender.

Open the forge and inspect available options before confirming. Ink limits rarity and level, while the focus selects the school. Choose a useful spell that fits your current book rather than merely the most expensive result.

Collect the scroll and inscribe it at the Inscription Table. Test mana cost, cooldown, and effect safely. The forge neither replaces inscription nor automatically teaches the character; it provides controlled spell acquisition instead of waiting for random loot.
A scroll from your chosen school
codex.quest.magic_irons.inscription.text: The Inscription Table uses a book, wooden slabs, and fences, making it available before dangerous magic expeditions. Prepare a Copper Spell Book and a suitable found scroll. The Ruined Book from the adjacent quest is unnecessary.

Open the table, insert the book and scroll, and choose an empty slot. Books have capacity and rarity limits; if the interface refuses inscription, check those rather than consuming the scroll directly.

Select the inscribed spell and test it with your book or a compatible casting implement. Repeated casts now use personal mana and respect cooldowns. You can retrieve the scroll, but doing so removes that spell from the book. This turns a disposable find into a permanent spell option.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.task.0: Obtain a bottle of Legendary Ink
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.text.0: Legendary ink makes the strongest scrolls. It can be found in rare magical loot, but there is also a repeatable route — the alchemist’s cauldron. Prepare the cauldron, epic ink, amethyst and an empty bottle, and keep a reserve for the spells you already use.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.text.1: The installed recipe converts one thousand millibuckets of Epic Ink plus amethyst into two hundred fifty millibuckets of Legendary Ink. Four bottles of the previous tier become one of the next. Bottle the result to earn the Legendary Ink advancement.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.text.2: Rarity does not guarantee every spell’s maximum level. Some highest levels require further Arcane Anvil upgrades. Choose the desired school and spell in the Scroll Forge before spending expensive ink; a powerful random scroll may exceed your current book’s limits.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.title: Legendary Ink
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.task.0: Assemble a complete four-piece magical armour set
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.text.0: This manual objective requires a complete magical outfit: headpiece, chestpiece, leggings, and boots from one chosen set. Wandering Magician armour, made from leather armour and Arcane Essence, is an accessible start; your first set need not wait for mithril.
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.text.1: Craft all four pieces and equip them in normal armour slots. Check their names and remove any accidentally retained vanilla piece. Specialised school clothing needs Arcane Cloth and the relevant school runes, with materials budgeted for every part.
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.text.2: Confirm after completing the full set, rather than one attractive robe. Assess protection, mana, and bonuses before combat. If using cosmetic slots, ensure the functional armour is equipped correctly; appearance alone proves neither an active set nor readiness for the catacombs.
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.title: Mage Robes
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.text.0: Runestones specialise magical clothing and upgrades. Look for a blank stone in magical loot: it appears in mage-tower chests and drops from the Dead King. Completed runes hardly ever drop from mages — only the Archevoker drops an Evocation Rune — so the Fire Rune has to be crafted yourself. Enemies in their towers are dangerous, so prepare protection and an escape route.
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.text.1: Surround a Blank Runestone with eight Blaze Rods to make a Fire Rune. Let the blank register first, then use it in the recipe: the guide remembers previously detected items, so the two objectives do not require a spare stone. The fire focus is a rod, not Blaze Powder.
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.text.2: Save runes for your chosen school and inspect clothing or orb recipes. Owning a Fire Rune neither teaches a spell nor generates mana. Fire spells still require suitable scrolls and a book, while the rune is an equipment-upgrade component.
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.title: School Runes
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.text.0: Early scrolls appear in loot and magical Overworld structures. Read the spell name, level, and rarity before use. Casting directly consumes a scroll, so save a useful copy for inscription into a spell book.
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.text.1: The second objective, Ruined Book, is found in deep Ancient Cities and belongs to later exploration. Prepare wool, food, and an escape route, and carefully avoid triggering sculk shriekers. Do not confuse it with an ordinary book or a completed spell book.
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.text.2: The Ruined Book is unnecessary for starting magic: make the table and Copper Spell Book while this card remains unfinished. Collect both requested items for full completion. Your saved scroll becomes a repeatable spell, while the rare book supports later recipes.
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.title: First Scroll
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.text.0: The Blood Staff is rare Dead King loot from Iron’s Spells catacombs. Prepare enchanted armour, healing, food, strong inscribed spells, and personal mana. Clear dangerous passages and remember the exit route before entering the boss chamber.
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.text.1: Interacting with the resting king awakens him, so do not click during an unprepared inspection. Keep moving, avoid spell areas, and remove summoned enemies promptly to preserve room. Collect all loot after victory.
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.text.2: The staff is not guaranteed: the loot table chooses between it and the Necronomicon after a chance check. Another reward means another attempt may be needed. The staff casts your selected spell and improves summoning; it has no general rule replacing mana costs with health.
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.title: Staff
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.text.0: An Empty Upgrade Orb needs Arcane Ingots, Cinder Essence, and mithril material. Search below Y −38 in the Overworld; mithril ore does not generate exposed to air and requires a netherite pickaxe. This is late progression beyond the Copper Spell Book.
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.text.1: Cinder Essence drops from Ancient Knights awakened by breaking armour piles in the Nether. Prepare for combat before disturbing them. Craft the empty orb and let it register, then convert it into the configured form; its saved mark does not require a second spare base.
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.text.2: Surround a base with eight Recovery Runes for the Cooldown Upgrade Orb. Apply it to compatible equipment through the Arcane Anvil and inspect the preview and limits. It reduces cooldown rather than eliminating mana costs. Compare repeated casts of the same spell after installation.
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.title: Upgrade Orbs
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.reward.0: A huge palette of building materials
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.text.0: The architect's cutter makes Domum Ornamentum decorative goods from chosen materials. Place it near your building materials and start with available wood or stone. It needs no electricity; the main decisions here are the type of item and its components.
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.text.1: In the window choose a group and shape, then fill the material slots. Look at the result before a large batch: some shapes combine several materials, and swapping them changes the look. Make one sample and compare it with the builder's request through the tooltip or the goggles.
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.text.2: If the request stays open, check the composition, not just the block's general name: one identifier can hide many finishes with different data. After a successful sample, note the palette and produce the batch; that is more reliable than sorting through similar panels in the middle of construction.
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.title: Architect's Cutter
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.task.1: Construct one blueprint decoration and inspect its available management
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.text.0: The decoration controller links a decorative blueprint to its construction and upkeep in the colony. Choose a small decoration with the build tool and place the plan within the colony. The controller appears as part of working with the blueprint; there is no item recipe to look for.
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.text.1: Open the plan's window, give the order and provide materials. Take a decoration with a clear purpose, say a small square, without blocking the citizens' way. It will not become a residence hut and adds no population.
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.text.2: When construction is finished, open the decoration's management and make sure it refers to the right object. Tick the manual point after the real build, not the ghost preview. Make further changes through this management and the exact blueprint, or the builder will restore the details you removed.
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.title: Decoration Controller
codex.quest.mc_build.guide_palette_sampl: A Domum Ornamentum sample was crafted for a real request; the builder accepted its exact material and shape

A complex decorative request is easier to work out on one sample. Open the builder's requirements and choose a Domum Ornamentum item for which you have materials. Note the shape, the infill and the frame if the type has one.

Reproduce these parameters in the architect's cutter and make a few pieces. Compare the tooltip with the request and hand the sample over through supply. A similar façade colour does not replace an exact match: variants of one family can be named almost alike.

The objective is closed when the builder accepts the sample and the remaining request shrinks. Note the accepted palette and produce the batch. That way you will not make a heap of almost-right blocks that look fine in your own wall while the blueprint's construction stays stalled.
codex.quest.mc_build.guide_upgrade_clear: The next building level’s preview was inspected; its bounds marked, neighbours’ entrances and the road kept clear

Upgrading a building can change its footprint and approaches. Before a new order, pick one working hut and inspect the preview of the next level in the chosen style. The first level's walls are no guide: a staircase or roof may reach past the old edge.

Measure the disputed gap to the neighbour with the caliper and mark the future boundary with temporary blocks. Check the road, entrances, light and access to the warehouse. If the plan conflicts with infrastructure, move a simple path first or choose another placement.

Inspection done, passages preserved: tick it without launching an expensive upgrade unsupplied. Repeat the check before every major rebuild of a quarter: an approach fixed in advance saves you from a handsome façade that blocked the courier's only route.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.text.0: The multipiston moves blocks between configurable directions and suits compact moving devices. Make it and find a free plot with ordinary cheap blocks. Starting next to a working warehouse or someone else's machine is awkward: a wrong direction will hit them.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.text.1: Open the settings for input, output and a short range. Input and output cannot coincide; the window will say so. Apply a signal and watch the movement, leaving room for the result and a safe way past the mechanism.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.text.2: After the first cycle remove the signal and check the return or the next movement. One stone block says nothing about compatibility with containers. For a real structure repeat the trial with its own materials, and only then connect gates or other colony infrastructure.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.title: Multi-Piston
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.text.0: The scan tool saves an area as a blueprint, the caliper measures distances, the shape tool prepares geometric volumes. All three exist in the pack; the shape tool's recipe comes from MineColonies, an emerald and two sticks. The scan tool and the placement tool are different things.
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.text.1: Measure a small mock-up with the caliper, then set two corners of the area and make sure the anchor point lies inside. Save the blueprint under a clear name. Start the shape tool with a small cube, checking materials and mode before confirming.
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.text.2: Open the saved project through the build window and check the dimensions. In survival, scanning copies no blocks: the future build needs resources and a way to place them. A large warehouse is a poor first exercise; an empty mock-up is easier to check, rotate and reproduce.
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.title: Structurize Tools
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.text.0: Substitution blocks record special rules for the surroundings into a blueprint instead of a plain wall. Placeholder and Solid Placeholder behave differently, so they cannot be scattered at random as building material. Make both by recipe and prepare a small mock-up away from housing.
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.text.1: Put the substitutes into chosen spots of the model, scan it and compare the preview on different terrain. The meaning of such blocks shows when the blueprint is placed: they help fit the project into the existing environment. They do not promise to fill any void with one arbitrary stone.
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.text.2: Build a small project and inspect the result at ground level and in cavities. For an ordinary room real blocks usually suffice; substitutes serve an author of blueprints that must adapt to terrain. Keep an original copy of the mock-up so a wrong rule can be fixed without damaging a finished building.
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.title: Substitution Blocks
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.text.0: The timber frame block combines a visible frame and wall infill in one item. Make it in the architect's cutter, in the Timberframes section. The name dynamic_timberframe denotes a whole family, not one fixed pair of wood and plaster.
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.text.1: Take materials for the frame and centre, choose the beam pattern and make one sample. Place several side by side in different orientations to see the joints and the direction of the diagonals. A stray mirrored panel spoils a façade even with identical ingredients.
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.text.2: For a colony order, compare the tooltip with the materials and type of the panel actually requested. The Codex objective is an introduction to the block family; the palette of a whole façade is yours to choose. Keep the chosen sample in the workshop, make the required quantity and leave access to the wall for repairs and later levels.
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.title: Timber Frame
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.text.0: The builder turns plans into real buildings and begins with their own hut. Place it with the tool, assign a free citizen, open Build Options and choose Build Building. Without an order there is nothing to raise, even with a chest of stone standing nearby.
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.text.1: The Required Resources tab lists the project's materials; Open Requests on the worker shows which tool is missing and what else stopped the work. Deliver items into a supported inventory or fulfil the request directly. Bind the resource scroll to the builder to see their needs on the way to the warehouse.
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.text.2: Wait for the hut to be finished and see which orders became available. The builder's level limits the work, so developing the workshop cannot be postponed forever. If the citizen stands idle, check food, time of day, route, tools and the open request before cancelling the construction or moving the colony.
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.title: Builder
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.text.0: The Structurize build tool selects a blueprint, rotates it and places it precisely. Its golden look is deceptive: by the installed recipe it is made of stone and sticks. The builder's goggles help decode the requirements of decorative blocks when you supply a construction site.
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.text.1: Take the hut you need, open the blueprint selection and inspect the preview from all sides. Check future entrances, floor level and room for the building's next level. Confirming places the plan; it gives no materials and finishes no order.
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.text.2: The goggles are useful with complex Domum Ornamentum materials: they show the shape and what it is made of. A similar texture does not always mean the right item. Fix an awkward position before mass deliveries; an early inspection is cheaper than moving an almost finished building.
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.title: Build Tool
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.text.0: Housing decides how many citizens you take in and where they wait out the night. Prepare two residence huts and one tavern and order their construction. In the installed tutorial the tavern gives four places, a separate house one place per building level.
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.text.1: A finished tavern attracts visitors who can be hired for the items they name, if the settlement is ready for it. Read a candidate's traits beforehand and count the free places. A second tavern will not help: the colony allows only one.
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.text.2: The two house blocks can be shown to the book as one batch and then placed; check occupancy in the management. The player's bed next to a hut does not count as a colony place. After hiring, provide food and work, or new people bring not production but a pile of unmet requests.
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.title: Citizen Housing
codex.quest.mc_found.food.text.0: The farm grows crops, and the dining hall with the blockhutcook block feeds the hungry. These are two different links: a field without a menu produces no finished meal. Build both, assign workers and put the field block on a convenient irrigated plot near the farm.
codex.quest.mc_found.food.text.1: In the field window choose the crop, provide seeds and a hoe, and check that the plot is assigned to the farmer. In the dining hall set up the menu and add permitted food with fuel for supported cooking. A raw dish, or one below the required level, will not satisfy citizens, even if you would eat it yourself without a second thought.
codex.quest.mc_found.food.text.2: Watch the harvest reach the warehouse and food reach one citizen. Upgraded houses demand better nutrition; later you will need the chef's kitchen and varied products. If people go hungry, look first at the menu, warehouse stock and delivery rather than blindly expanding a plot that already works.
codex.quest.mc_found.food.title: Food
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_housing_audit: The town hall shows free housing and filled jobs; a home and a job are chosen for the next citizen

Before the next hire, find out where the newcomer will live and what they will do. Open the town hall and compare the head count, free housing and population limits. Two placed huts are not yet two places until construction is finished.

Pick a specific vacant profession and make sure its building is actually built. If automation assigns citizens, look into the hiring and housing settings so the newcomer does not wander off to a random post. Check the food reserve as well: new housing adds work for the dining hall.

Tick it when a home and a job for the next citizen are chosen; hiring at once is not required. This census tells a housing shortage from a research population cap. If a tavern guest is not accepted, check these conditions and the hiring price rather than building a second, forbidden tavern.
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_menu_trial.ta: An available menu was chosen in the dining hall, suitable food delivered and a citizen observed being served
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_menu_trial.te: A warehouse full of produce does not yet mean the dining hall will serve it. Open the menu and pick a dish that suits the current citizens and that your farm can manage. Prepare a small batch, keeping a separate reserve for yourself and for workers away on trips.

Hand the finished food into supply and watch a hungry citizen being served. If they refuse, compare the quality requirements, the menu and the item's variant, raw or cooked. Player and colonist judge food differently: edible in your hand does not necessarily mean fit for the menu.

The objective closes with an actual serving. Then estimate whether the current harvest can sustain the chosen dish. If not, change the menu or set up the ingredient chain before upgrading houses en masse, or handsome new houses will raise citizens' demands before the kitchen has learned to meet them.
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_request_tools: A working citizen’s tool request was fulfilled through the colony system and the worker resumed work

Even a site heaped with timber stops when the worker lacks a suitable tool. Find an open request from the builder or a gatherer and read the allowed properties. An expensive pickaxe is not always available to a worker of the current level; go by their conditions.

Prepare a suitable item and put it into the registered warehouse or close the request through the window. Follow the status change and the handover of the tool. A purchase left on the ground by the door does not count: the colony system must see the stock meant for it.

When work resumes, tick it. There is no need to break a good tool on purpose; wait for a natural request or serve one already open. Remember the supply route and keep a reserve of simple tools: it breaks the circle where the only toolmaker is waiting for a tool and the whole site seems stuck.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.text.0: The hospital treats the sick; the graveyard relates to losses and to the research that concerns them. Prepare both blocks, but do not count them as automatic protection for the population. Help comes when the buildings are built, staff assigned and the requested supplies delivered.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.text.1: Lay a safe path from the residential quarter to the hospital. In case of illness open the healer's requests and bring exactly the listed remedies; similar food may not do. After a citizen's death study the graveyard window and the current conditions before counting on the return of everyone who died.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.text.2: Count stocks and free places before a crisis, not during one. Two huts in inventory history close the item part; healing and resurrection show only in the world. Light, defence and food take the load off these buildings; a hospital will not save a colony where monsters walk straight to the houses.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.title: Hospital and Graveyard
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.text.0: The mystical site is a colony structure for citizens' happiness and a handsome public space. In the installed mod its effect on happiness grows with the building's level. It is not a portal, not a magical resource generator and not a substitute for a working hospital.
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.text.1: Check the required research and choose a blueprint, mindful of the large footprint and the cost of materials. Place the plan with the tool and give the order once the settlement's basic needs are covered. A handsome project must not stall urgent housing, food or defence for long.
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.text.2: After construction look at the happiness figure in the town hall and keep access to the structure. The hut block closes the objective before the build, while the real effect comes only from the finished building. Upgrade it along with the colony, weighing the next level against other open needs; it will not answer every complaint at once.
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.title: Mystical Site
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.text.0: Through the post box you address the colony's request system without rummaging through racks by hand. Make it once the warehouse and courier exist and put it by your permanent workplace, where deliveries are convenient to bring.
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.text.1: Open the window and request a little of an ordinary material already in the warehouse. Check the item and a sensible quantity. The courier needs a road, the system needs stock or trained production; the box does not create a resource out of nothing.
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.text.2: Wait for completion and collect the delivery without leaving old orders in the receiver. If the parcel is late, look at the request's state and the courier's workload. For a first try, stone or planks beat a rare part with no profession yet: that way you test the link to the warehouse itself.
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.title: Postbox
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.text.0: The supply chest deploys a starting camp with provisions for the future colony. Make the deployer and find open ground where the whole preview fits. It is a large structure: a cramped room in your own house will not do.
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.text.1: Inspect the orientation and height of the ghost model and confirm placement only after checking the edges. Take the starting tools and the town hall from the camp and leave the rest for the builder. The game limits redeployment, so there will be no endless supplies from new chests.
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.text.2: The deployer in hand closes the item objective, but there is no colony yet. The next step is a permanent site for the town hall with land to spare for houses and production. The camp helps you begin; it will not replace citizens, orders and materials for the chosen style.
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.title: Supply Chest
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.text.0: The town hall is the colony's centre: population, happiness, permissions and general settings are all here. Take it from the starting camp or craft it by recipe. Choose a site with easy approaches and room for future buildings, not just a fine view.
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.text.1: Place the block with the build tool and a chosen blueprint, check the edges and create the colony. A placed block is not a building yet: the builder raises the shell later. Before that you can already use the management and hand out the first jobs.
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.text.2: Open the colony's details and make sure you are managing your own settlement. In shared play think through participants' permissions so helpers can build and service warehouses. The town hall in inventory history closes the item objective; the citizens and the first construction you will see in the world.
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.title: Town Hall
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.text.0: The warehouse and the courier tie professions into one supply system. Build both, assign a courier and prepare eight colony racks. Put the warehouse close to the main consumers: a short road helps more than an extra chest on the outskirts.
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.text.1: Fill the registered storage with simple tools and materials for the current construction. The courier delivers on request rather than guessing your plans. Check the approach to the entrances, access to the racks and room for the gatherers' output.
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.text.2: Follow at least one delivery from the warehouse to a citizen in need; items in the history will not show it, nor will the worker's assignment or route. A chest outside does not become part of the warehouse: use its window and registered storage, or the courier will not see the stock you laid out so neatly.
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.title: Warehouse and Courier
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.text.0: The rally banner temporarily gathers chosen guards and later returns them to duty. Make the item, check the required military research and management permissions. The banner hires no fighters and does not equip empty towers.
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.text.1: Sneak and apply it to the towers you want, adding them to the list. Ordinary use opens a window showing the bound posts. Test a rally in a safe part of the colony and make sure the chosen defenders are the ones who respond.
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.text.2: After the trial, dismiss the squad and watch the guards return. They are bound to the protected area and will not follow you to the ends of the earth. During a real raid do not pull the entire gate guard at once: pick a reserve and a rally point, leaving citizens a protected path.
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.title: Rally Banner
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.text.0: The barracks together with barracks towers house a larger military force. Prepare the main block and the tower block after studying the blueprint and research. The tower belongs to this system; it is no standalone substitute for an ordinary post.
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.text.1: Inspect the overall plan with the tool, leave room for the component structures and order construction in the intended sequence. Assign defenders when places appear and equip each one. Do not pull every worker out of supply: an army without food and repairs is unreliable.
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.text.2: Check the number of occupied places and the available defence commands. The book counts the two different blocks in turn, so a built hut need not be dismantled. Barracks pay off as territory grows, provided stocks of weapons and armour grow with them and the approaches to dangerous areas are thought through.
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.title: Barracks
A guard tower gives a defender a post and extends the protected territory. Make two huts as one batch for the objective, then decide which approaches to cover. A tower by the town hall does not always see the entrance to a distant mining quarter.

Build the towers, assign guards and issue gear by their role and level: a melee fighter and an archer need different things. Set a patrol or a guarded point and check that the route does not run into a locked door or a pit.

Make sure the defenders reach their posts, eat and are not waiting for a tool. Two blocks in the book's history say nothing about the service itself. Towers should help a living colony, not just push the border out: a lit passage and the ability to gather help quickly matter more than symmetry on the map.
codex.quest.mc_military.guardtower.title: Guard Tower
codex.quest.mc_military.guide_patrol_rou: The assigned guard walked the whole route, gates remain passable and dangerous drops are fenced

A route on the map is only as good as the defender's ability to walk it. Take one guard and a short patrol around the residential area. Check stairs, gates, bridges and pit edges in advance, with mechanisms in their usual position.

Watch the fighter pass every marked point. If they get stuck at a fancy façade, look for a real passage instead of reassigning the profession. Light dark spots and fence dangerous drops without cutting off citizens and couriers.

A full pass with no detour through a dangerous area, and the objective is closed. No need to summon an enemy: what is tested is geometry and access to duty. After rebuilding, revisit the route near changed entrances: a new building level can take over an old path or change the approach height.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.text.0: The chief's sword is a rare trophy from the barbarian leader. The quest is named after a repelled raid, but the item objective checks this sword specifically, not the fact of victory. The loot table holds many other outcomes, empty hands included.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.text.1: Before the fight prepare the defence, the guards' supplies and shelter for citizens. During the attack watch the approaches and do not lead defenders far beyond the settlement's edge. Collect loot once no enemies remain nearby.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.text.2: If the sword did not drop, the defence still succeeded, and the node will wait for the trophy. Do not confuse swords of ordinary materials with the Chief Sword. Keep the one you find for the record and display, and plan the next fight by the colony's condition, not for a promised reward.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.title: Raid Repelled
codex.quest.mc_military.training.text.0: The combat academy trains melee fighters, the archery range trains archers. Prepare both buildings after the required research and place them so students can walk safely. Training is not patrol: a student will not go out to guard the gate.
codex.quest.mc_military.training.text.1: Assign suitable citizens and issue the requested training gear. Wait for lessons to begin and compare stats after a while. Do not remove elements of the training blueprint: a missing target halts exercises even with a chest full of weapons.
codex.quest.mc_military.training.text.2: Move a trained student to a military post and check their combat gear separately. Two blocks in hand do not make the army more experienced. While training goes on, keep the active guard at its posts so developing future ranks does not open a gap in the defence of a populated quarter.
codex.quest.mc_military.training.title: Training
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.text.0: Walls steer the enemy; gates leave citizens a controlled passage. Prepare a wooden gate and a gatehouse, and choose the entrance with roads and sightlines in mind. A handsome closed wall without a working entrance hinders your own couriers as much as attackers.
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.text.1: Inspect the gatehouse blueprint and the defence positions in it. Build the section, open and close the gate with the available control, then lead a citizen through it along their usual route. Do not lock the main supply path until there is a bypass or a clear opening procedure.
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.text.2: After attacks watch the gate's condition and access for repairs. Blocks in history confirm materials, not an impassable border: a change in height, water or a neighbouring building can offer a way round. Walk the defence from outside on foot and keep a safe way home before the first raid.
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.title: Walls and Gates
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.text.0: The shepherd, cowhand and beekeeper provide different renewable products: wool, milk with offspring, bee materials. Prepare the huts and safe pens. Bring the animals and hives yourself: a worker will not conjure a herd from an empty pen.
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.text.1: Check the breeding settings, feed, tools and head-count limits. The shepherd also keeps the flock in check, so set aside breeding stock in advance. Hives are bound with the beekeeper's tool; how many are allowed depends on the apiary's level, and a neighbour's hive is not necessarily serviced.
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.text.2: Wait for one collection of each product and its delivery. Do not move the animals to a pretty common pasture if the worker has stopped reaching them. Store feed, containers and results separately, so a shortage of consumables can be told from a routing or assignment error.
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.title: Livestock
codex.quest.mc_production.blacksmith.tex: The blacksmith forges tools and metal gear, the mechanic services complex devices and redstone, the glassblower works with glass. Three workshops take three kinds of manual work off your hands. Prepare the blocks, check research and set up material deliveries.

One needed recipe per profession is enough to begin: an available tool, a simple mechanical part, a glass item. Check the exact output and whether the current level can make it. A recipe for a complex machine from another mod does not transfer to the workshop merely because it contains iron.

Create a small request and follow it. If the craftsman is waiting for a tool himself, close that request first, or tool production runs into itself. After the trial, expand teaching around the builders' real needs, leaving recipe room for the chosen style's materials.
The concrete mixer produces setting building materials; the alchemist deals with potions, nether wart and mistletoe. These are two independent late-supply professions. Place them after the required research and where ingredients are convenient to carry, not by the adjacency of names in the book.

Set the concrete mixer's colour and shape and provide sand, gravel and dye by recipe. Choose a supported job and reagents for the alchemist. A brewing stand at the far end of the base is invisible to the colony: the citizen takes only from colony storage.

Test one order each, following raw material use and output separately. The concrete colour and potion kind matter for an exact request, so do not substitute similar ingredients without checking the recipe. Such workshops shine once basic logistics runs; otherwise expensive specialists wait for the same simple consumables as the first builder.
codex.quest.mc_production.concrete.title: Other Production
codex.quest.mc_production.fisherman.text: The fisher catches at an accessible body of water and now and then brings up finds from the bottom. Choose a hut blueprint with a safe descent to the water, build it and assign a worker. A drop of water behind a blank wall does not count as a workplace.

Provide a fishing rod and check the messages about the fishing spot. Watch the citizen walk to the water and begin, without blocking the way with boats, fences or your own storage. Possible treasures depend on the current fishing rules and research; a rare catch owes you nothing first.

Arrange delivery of fish to the dining hall or the right kitchen and leave room for by-products. Raw fish still needs a menu and cooking. If fishing stops, inspect the rod, the spot and the inventory fill first, and leave widening the pond for last.
codex.quest.mc_production.guide_chef_kit: The chef’s kitchen is built, a cook assigned and one available recipe completed

The chef's kitchen cooks special MineColonies dishes for more demanding citizens and differs from the dining hall, which simply feeds the hungry. Prepare a separate kitchen hut, check the conditions and finish building it before expecting refined dishes.

Assign a cook and choose a recipe whose ingredients your farm actually yields. New colony plants are obtained with a hoe and grown by the farmer with the biome in mind; a random player plot is not obliged to accept such a crop. Fulfil the kitchen's specific requests.

The first dish is ready: tick it. Then set up its delivery and allow it in the dining hall's menu. The kitchen does not cancel the other links: ingredients, cooking, delivery and serving must work together. Start with one repeatable dish and leave a long menu of rare seasonal stock for later.
codex.quest.mc_production.guide_compost_: The composter’s allowed inputs are set, seed stock kept separately and the first output collected

A composter earns its place when organic leftovers pile up on their own. Before enabling processing, set aside the seeds and produce without which the next sowing would stop. A labelled crate helps you, but for the worker availability is decided by real storage and permission settings.

Open the list of items allowed for composting and choose one genuinely surplus resource. Provide a small batch, follow the processing and check the product against the current recipe. Do not send all your plant produce to waste just because the warehouse filled up for the first time.

After the first result and a second check of the seed reserve, tick it. Then compare consumption with what the farm yields, so composting stays a way to use up surplus. If kitchen ingredients go missing, revisit the allowed list and the delivery route: the issue is spending policy, not a slow farmer.
codex.quest.mc_production.guide_sawmill_: The sawmill produced oak stairs from the taught recipe for a request

Oak stairs are a simple way to test the sawmill's training without rare materials. Prepare oak planks and a free recipe slot, and open training at the built hut. The result must be oak specifically: a similar shape from another species will not close the request.

Save the recipe and create a need, through a colony request or a construction. Follow the ingredients arriving, the crafting and the delivery. The numeric objective wants sixteen stairs as one batch in your hands and does not ask which workshop made them.

Close the manual part once you have seen the sawmill work. The saved recipe will serve future orders, so do not erase it for a tidy window. If production waits, check the plank stock, the courier and the active request: a missing request and an unknown recipe are cured differently.
codex.quest.mc_production.lumberjack.tex: The lumberjack plants and fells trees according to the hut's settings. Place it not far from the warehouse, but separate the forest plot from ornamental trees and wooden buildings. Provide an axe and saplings of the chosen species, then check the list of allowed plants.

With the forestry tool set the working area by two opposite corners, with spare height for the crowns. Too low an area misses the tops; too wide a one catches the park. Watch the first felling and replanting before expanding the plot.

Logs must leave the worker's storage to make room for the next cycle. If work stops, check the axe, saplings, access to the tree and the citizen's messages. The hut block merely introduces the profession to the book; real supply for the builder begins with felling, delivery and restored plantings.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.text.0: The mine yields stone and ore, the stonemason makes goods, the crusher grinds loose material, the sifter picks useful bits out of sand and gravel. Place the four huts in turn, but launch the professions as research and needs allow: their roles are not interchangeable.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.text.1: The miner needs pickaxes and shoring materials: first the shaft goes down, then the galleries spread. Teach the stonemason a specific recipe. For the crusher check the cobblestone, gravel, sand, clay transitions and the current conditions; give the sifter suitable feed and a mesh.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.text.2: Four blocks side by side do not form an ore-doubling line. Watch each profession's output separately and clear it by delivery. The mine may break into a dangerous cavity, so keep access to the worker and heed their requests rather than driving them deeper at any cost.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.title: Miner
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.text.0: The Nether worker obtains dangerous resources through a special colony building. It is a separate profession with its own gear and its own risk, not a miner nudged toward your portal. Check the research and build the blueprint in full.
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.text.1: Assign the worker and, before the first sortie, fulfil their requests for equipment and consumables. Provide food and delivery. Do not send your last experienced citizen for the sake of one rare material: the profession's description in the mod warns of the danger outright.
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.text.2: After each sortie see what state the worker came back in and what they brought. The hut opens the branch but promises neither a successful trip nor a quantity of loot. Establish a short cycle, then expand supply; learn about a missing product from requests and the worker's state, not from faith in endless production.
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.title: Nether Worker
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.text.0: The plantation grows sugar cane, cactus and bamboo, the florist supplies flowers, the composter processes organic leftovers. Prepare a plantation field as well: the farmer's ordinary field does not replace the specialised plot.
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.text.1: Check the open research for the chosen field type and assign it to the plantation. Provide the plant and growing conditions. Choose a supported crop for the florist and set what the composter may process. Do not send seeds, food and rare plants to waste without a separate reserve.
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.text.2: Follow at least one cycle from consumable to product. If the plantation refuses the field, read the reason in the research limits instead of moving the block again and again. The branch is useful for paper, dyes and building consumables once the grain farm already feeds the citizens.
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.title: Horticulture
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.text.0: The medium quarry marks out a large open excavation. In this version it needs a built mine, a hired quarrier and assignment to a specific quarry. One block will not strip a column of earth down to bedrock by itself.
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.text.1: Choose a site away from foundations, roads and underground lines. Check the blueprint's size with the tool and give the worker access, tools and supplies. An open pit mostly yields common building resources; a large volume promises no rare ore.
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.text.2: Wait for the first digging and delivery, then fence the edge off from citizens and animals. When the quarry is finished the worker needs a new assignment; they will tell you themselves. A quarry suits mass construction, but decide in advance what to do with the pit left behind: use it or close it safely.
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.title: Quarry
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.text.0: The sawmill makes wooden goods for the settlement's requests and complements the lumberjack: a delivered log will not turn into stairs, fences and doors of the chosen style by itself. Check the research, build the hut and assign a free worker.
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.text.1: In the recipe window teach the sawmill one simple item from available wood, the species the builder needs. Then create a small request. The recipe set grows with the building's level; the whole JEI page will not open right after assignment.
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.text.2: Follow the raw material arriving and the courier bringing the finished order. If the builder needs a different species, repainting the planks in your mind will not change the worker's recipe. Check the exact ingredients and output, then widen the list while keeping logs for your own buildings and new lessons.
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.title: Sawmill
The ordinary smeltery handles ores and metals; the stone smeltery handles fired building materials and charcoal. Prepare both huts and split the raw materials by direction in advance: the names are alike, but a request for smooth stone is not addressed to the metallurgist.

Build the huts, assign workers, provide fuel, feedstock and an available recipe. The smelter can break ore blocks down to raw material and melt it; how much comes out is decided by the current processing. Mekanism ratios do not carry over until a separate recipe is verified.

Order a little metal and a little building product and follow both to the warehouse. If work stalls, compare the assignment, recipe and fuel. A coal shortage can halt several services at once, so agree to keep a reserve for the kitchen and metallurgy before a big batch of decorative firing.
codex.quest.mc_production.smeltery.title: Smelteries
codex.quest.mc_production.timber_service: Gather thirty-two oak logs as one batch so the book records the stock. Single logs obtained separately do not add up to that figure if you never held such a batch. The timber is not consumed, and the book does not care where it came from.

For a real test take logs your colony's forestry felled and return them to accessible storage. Make sure saplings are restored after felling and the next cycle has not stopped for want of an axe. The batch must suit the builder's coming request exactly.

Do not saw the whole stock into planks before checking log delivery: that is a different item and a different request. If the blueprint needs processed wood, teach the sawmill the recipe in advance. The next quest follows the material's route and finds the causes of stops that a plain counter cannot see.
Create a timber construction request; follow worker → warehouse → builder and inspect tool supply and route

Create a construction request for timber and follow the material from the worker through the warehouse to the builder. Pick a small, clear order so you can see the batch sent and received. The logs recorded in the book from the previous step do not confirm this delivery.

Check tool shortage separately: open the lumberjack's or builder's requests and make sure you know where the needed item will come from. Then walk the courier's route and inspect doors, stairs, fences and the warehouse entrance. No need to break working tools; seeing the request system operate is enough.

Chain, tool and route all checked; that is when to tick the manual objective: the Codex does not watch the citizens for you. If timber sits in the warehouse while construction waits, check the exact material variant and the order's state; the error may hide in a request for a processed item rather than in felling speed.

This branch checks whether timber reaches the builder through the colony's services. You need a lumberjack hut and a warehouse, already counted or new. Once shown to the book, working buildings stay put: dismantling them for the objective is unnecessary.

Make sure the lumberjack is assigned and has an axe, oak saplings and a suitable working area. The warehouse must be served by a courier with a passage to both buildings. Pick the builder a project that genuinely needs oak, so the coming order has a clear address.

Equipment does not yet prove delivery. Before the trial batch, check for free racks and for the absence of an unfinished request holding the lumberjack. The point of this preparation is to tie production to a specific worker's need, not to set two blocks side by side and expect adjacency to replace the request system.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.text.0: The enchanter's tower produces enchanted books and magic scrolls with the colony's own means. Build the hut, assign a specialist and set which workers they may observe to gather mana. Without observation targets the mod names the cause of idleness outright.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.text.1: A teleport scroll needs three paper, a compass and the build tool: the enchanter's installed recipe yields three scrolls. Deliver the materials through supply and wait for the crafting. This is a citizen's recipe; the player's enchanting table does not replace the tower.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.text.2: Obtain one scroll for the objective, then work out its binding and purpose before taking it on a long journey. Do not spend your last way home on a casual experiment. For enchanted books count tomes and the tower's level separately: a scroll in hand does not mean the tower already issues any enchantment you like.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.title: Enchanter
codex.quest.mc_research.guide_first_rese: An available research was chosen, paid for and completed; its effect checked in the relevant building

Choose the first research by the needs of a living colony: let it unlock a waiting profession or improve a service you understand. Read the price and all conditions, gather the materials without taking the workers' last food and tool.

Start the research and make sure it appears among those in progress. Wait for the end with an assigned researcher and a serviced building. A paid button gives no effect; research time is part of the process.

Open the related building or setting and find the promised change; only then tick it. If the expected result is absent, check the finished research against its effect, not against a similar name in a neighbouring branch. This experience makes the next investments deliberate.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.text.0: The library is a place of study for adult citizens, where their intelligence grows. It does not start university research, and a placed block makes no one smarter by itself. Check whether the building is unlocked, choose a blueprint and wait for construction to finish.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.text.1: Assign an adult student who will benefit from the training and provide the requested study materials. Compare their stats before and after. Intelligence helps master other skills, so choose the student for a future profession rather than the first one to hand.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.text.2: See that study does not leave the colony without its only builder or courier. If lessons have not begun, check the assignment, the building's state and the requests. The hut in history closes the item objective; stat growth takes time and real work by the citizen, which a stack of books in your chest cannot replace.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.title: Library
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.task.1: Complete an available citizen request and find it in the log’s finished quests
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.text.0: The quest log keeps citizens' errands, current stages and finished stories. Make it and open it near the colony. Some errands appear only after a certain building, profession or conversation, so a blank page is not a fault.
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.text.1: Choose an available errand, talk to the named citizen and read what is required. When delivering, hand items to the character rather than leaving them nearby: the dialogue must move to the next stage. See the story through and receive the reply or reward.
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.text.2: Once the errand shows among the finished ones, the manual objective is closed. The internal Monster Encounter token is not needed: it describes a fight inside the expedition simulation and is no reward. What counts here is a real conversation with a citizen; it explains colony requests and the chains that follow.
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.title: Colony Quests
codex.quest.mc_research.school.text.0: The school takes care of the colony's children and prepares future workers. Place the block after the required research, build the blueprint and find a teacher. An empty building creates no new citizens: population growth still depends on housing and colony conditions.
codex.quest.mc_research.school.text.1: Assign children to lessons and look at the requests for study materials. Leave the seating the blueprint provides alone: the mod complains separately when there is nowhere to sit. The school's interior is not decoration until you have checked its role.
codex.quest.mc_research.school.text.2: Judge attendance and progress by the school's window, not by the building on the map. The school also cheers the assigned children. Have a job and housing ready for when they grow up, so a trained citizen goes straight to work instead of waiting for a new hut and a materials queue.
codex.quest.mc_research.school.title: School
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.text.0: The ancient tome turns up among the loot of MineColonies raiders and serves as material for colony enchanting. In the barbarian chief's loot table it is only one random option, so victory does not guarantee a book. Do not count on an exact number of tomes per raid.
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.text.1: Pick up the tome when the fight is over and the area is safe, and show it to the book before processing. Store it separately, with the rare trophies. An ordinary Minecraft book or a similar grimoire from another mod is not the same thing.
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.text.2: The enchanter spends the tome by recipes that depend on the tower's level and obtains enchanted books from their own tables. Check research against its own requirements: the tome is no universal payment for science. For the first copy, securing defence and loot matters more than inviting another dangerous raid.
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.title: Ancient Tome
The university unlocks research: new professions, better supply, new colony capabilities. Build the hut and assign a researcher; one hut item does not start any study. Choose the first discovery by the settlement's most pressing current problem.

Open the tree and read the prerequisite research, building requirements, level and price. Materials can be allocated from the university's inventory. Starting locks in the choice, and completion takes time; several visible branches do not mean all can run at once.

Wait for the completion message and check the new capability in the relevant profession. Upgrading the university widens the choice and the number of researchers. An inactive button is not a bug: most often it honestly points to a condition still to be met by construction, supply or an earlier discovery.
codex.quest.mc_research.university.title: University
codex.quest.mek_gear.atomic_disassembler: The atomic disassembler gathers several mining functions in one electric tool. Prepare the expensive alloys by the recipe and a place to charge it: uncharged, it shows nothing. Keeping the old pickaxe as a spare for the first outings is only sensible.

Charge the tool, look through the available modes and start at normal speed on a safe patch of stone. Changing mode changes both how it works and how much energy it draws. Check the controls in the settings, not by keys from someone else's pack.

Try the mass-mining modes away from the base floor, cables and decorations. Before the mine, estimate the energy reserve and the room for dropped blocks. The disassembler is a fine all-purpose tool, but it does not replace the Meka-Tool's module abilities and guarantees no particular mining enchantment.
codex.quest.mek_gear.guide_charge_stop.t: The chargepad is a convenient permanent spot where electric gear is readied for the road. Place it by the base exit and connect it to the battery through an allowed side. A spot in the path of a dangerous conveyor line or next to an exposed laser will not do.

Put on a partly drained set and stand on the pad. Watch the energy rise in your gear and fall in the feeding cube. If an item does not charge, check its compatibility, the source's reserve and the connection before rebuilding the whole grid.

The Robit's home pad must stay free as well; with the helper at work it is easier to give the player a separate spot. Crafting the pad closes the item goal, and the trial will show the real servicing speed. Before a long expedition check every piece of the set: a full body armour says nothing about the tool or the boots.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.text.0: The Mekanism laser emits a dangerous directed beam powered by electricity. The amplifier stores energy for a controlled pulse, and the tractor beam helps collect what the destruction leaves behind. The quest needs all three devices, but run the first experiment with a single short, fenced-off beam.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.text.1: Position the source so the beam crosses no walkways, chests or other people's buildings. Connect power only after checking the direction. Study the amplifier's thresholds and signal control: stored energy may be released later, when a player is already standing nearby.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.text.2: Before servicing, cut the power and remember the energy left in the amplifier. To ignite the fusion reactor the beam is aimed at the focus matrix, not at a random wall. Even in ordinary experiments the laser section must have a controlled switch and a safe terminal block.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.title: Lasers
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.text.0: The MekaSuit is electric armour in four parts. Its recipes reach into late Mekanism materials, polonium components included. Set up steady production and charging before spending your stock on one random piece.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.text.1: Make the helmet, body armour, pants and boots; the book counts the different parts one after another. Then charge them and put on the whole set. Look at the internal reserves: the armour spends energy on protection by itself, and modules add separate abilities. A piece worn after being counted need not come back.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.text.2: An empty set neither flies nor shields you from radiation: that takes installed modules and tested conditions. Try the armour in safe surroundings and keep an ordinary set; the modification station will later let you grow the suit to match real tasks.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.title: MekaSuit Set
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.text.0: The Meka-Tool is a configurable electric tool whose abilities are extended by modules. Make the tool itself, the excavation escalation module and the vein mining module. They are three separate quest items; once counted, install the upgrades through the modification station.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.text.1: Charge the tool and choose a moderate speed for the first trial. Test vein mining on a small natural deposit well away from important structures. Silk touch, fortune and other modes need their own modules and settings; they do not switch on together with vein mining.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.text.2: Energy draw and the stream of dropped items deserve attention: a fast tool easily overflows the inventory. Keep a calm, safe mode for workshop use. If the tool eats too large an area, stop and adjust the parameters; rebuilding a dismantled structure takes longer.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.title: Meka-Tool
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.text.0: The modification station installs modules into compatible gear and removes them. The module base is an ingredient of functional modules, so the four blanks in the quest add neither charge nor speed by themselves. Prepare power for the station and the item you want to improve.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.text.1: Make one functional module you need, open the station and put in a compatible suit piece or tool. Look at the list of allowed modules and the count limit: some upgrades can be installed several times, others need only one.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.text.2: After installing, open the gear's own settings and make sure the function is enabled the way you want. Keep removed modules: extraction lets you repurpose equipment without new armour. Do not grab the whole range of upgrades at once; first learn which pieces accept them and how much energy the chosen mode consumes.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.title: Modification Station
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.text.0: The energy module raises the energy reserve of compatible gear, but it does not create charge from nothing. Electrolytic breathing and inhalation purification are separate helmet functions. Set up a charging system first so there is something to test the new abilities with.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.text.1: Install the modules through the station into the right suit pieces. For breathing, check the helmet settings and the energy reserve, then step into shallow water next to the exit. Air purification has its own list of supported effects; it does not save you from every danger in the world.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.text.2: Watch consumption with the functions on and switch off what you do not need before a long trip. Extra capacity helps you survive an outing, but charging afterwards takes longer too. These modules do not shield you from radiation: a nuclear site needs every piece protected, not just improved breathing.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.title: Core Modules
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.text.0: Movement modules change how the suit handles and noticeably affect energy use. The gravitational modulator gives controlled flight and needs late resources, the hydraulic propulsion unit changes the jump, the locomotive booster the running speed. The three do not substitute for one another.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.text.1: Install each into the supported suit piece through the station and open the gear settings. Start with moderate values: a high jump and fast running only get in the way in a cramped workshop. Test flight over flat ground after a full charge.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.text.2: Before an expedition, rehearse switching functions on and off, landing, and moving on a low charge without the risk of falling. If flight drains the suit quickly, extra energy modules help. A module in your pocket has no effect: it must be installed, enabled and the relevant piece powered.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.title: Movement
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.text.0: Three utility modules solve three tasks: enhanced vision, item attraction and radiation shielding. Start by checking each suit piece's compatibility in the modification station. One crafted shielding module does not mean the whole set is protected.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.text.1: Install vision and the magnet into supported pieces, switch them on and try them on a dark, safe pad with a few ordinary items. Tune the magnet mode so it does not drag rubbish toward you while you build or sort the warehouse.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.text.2: For nuclear work, shield every required piece and check the set before entering the site. A radiation counter is no substitute for shielding, and good vision does not save you from monsters. Keep the extra functions' controls within reach: switching off an unneeded effect is often more convenient than running every module at once.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.title: Utility
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.text.0: The Robit is a portable helper with an inventory and useful work interfaces. To deploy it and send it home you need a chargepad, which has to be made separately. Bring power to it and leave room around it for the helper to appear.
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.text.1: Put the Robit on the pad, open its interface and work out the follow and item-collection modes. Drop one cobblestone and see where the cargo ends up. Check the charge and settings before taking it on a long mining trip.
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.text.2: The Robit will not become an autonomous factory: its smelting, storage and other functions are bounded by its interface. Before a dangerous crossing, make sure you know the recall command and remember where the home pad is. The helper shines at carrying finds once the way home is already safe.
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.title: Robit
codex.quest.mek_gear.scuba.text.0: The scuba mask works together with an oxygen tank that is not on the goal list: make and fill it separately. The jetpack burns hydrogen, the free runners spend energy. Each of the three devices needs its own resource, so a set of items alone is not enough.
codex.quest.mek_gear.scuba.text.1: Oxygen and hydrogen are easiest to get by electrolysing water; fill the gear through the appropriate slots. Charge the runners and check which modes are on. The pack integrates the jetpack with accessories, but verify the actual slot and controls in the equipment interface.
codex.quest.mek_gear.scuba.text.2: Test breathing near the shore and flight low over flat ground. Watch the gas reserve and keep an ordinary way out of the water at hand. The runners soften falls and help you move, but still check the charge before a jump from height.
codex.quest.mek_gear.scuba.title: Breathing and Flight
codex.quest.mek_gear.security.text.0: The security desk manages access to supported Mekanism devices. It belongs on a shared base, where some machines are one player's and some the team's. Start with a test device so you do not accidentally lock yourself out of servicing an important line.
codex.quest.mek_gear.security.text.1: Craft the desk, open the owner settings and choose an access mode. Add trusted players deliberately and check how a device behaves under the chosen setting. Wireless device frequencies have access parameters of their own; align those separately.
codex.quest.mek_gear.security.text.2: Machine security does not replace the server's territory protection and does not prevent every way of damaging the world. Leave the owner a clear route to regain access, especially to power and teleporters. The quest counts the desk itself; a working access policy appears only after configuring and testing it on specific devices.
codex.quest.mek_gear.security.title: Security
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fuel.text.0: The fuel assembly is an internal reactor part, while the fissile fuel itself enters as a chemical. Build the chain without starting the reactor: the enrichment chamber makes yellow cake, the chemical oxidizer turns it into uranium oxide. Separately dissolve fluorite in sulfuric acid to get hydrofluoric acid.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fuel.text.1: The chemical infuser combines uranium oxide with hydrofluoric acid into uranium hexafluoride, and the isotopic centrifuge turns that into fissile fuel. Check chemical names in the tanks: a liquid of the same name will not pass through a chemical input without the proper conversion.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fuel.text.2: Lay separate lines and power every stage. Five assembled devices are not yet a working chain. Until fuel goes into the reactor, keep production stopped or send the result to permitted storage; cooling and waste intake are prepared before the first reaction.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fuel.title: Fuel Assemblies
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fusion.text.0: The fusion reactor runs on deuterium and tritium, not uranium fuel. Heavy water comes from an electric pump with a filter upgrade; electrolysis splits it into deuterium and oxygen. Brine is evaporated into lithium, converted to chemical form and processed in the solar neutron activator to yield tritium.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fusion.text.1: Both continuous lines and a tritium reserve for the night must be ready before assembly. Build the reactor to the layout with its ports and laser focus matrix. Fill the hohlraum with D-T fuel, insert it into the controller and prepare a laser pulse of the energy the installation reports.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fusion.text.2: Before the pulse, fence off the beam and check either the energy output or the water cooling with steam removal, depending on the mode you chose. Keep fuel injection within confirmed supply. The first flash is not yet steady operation: watch the temperature and both fuels after the starting hohlraum is spent.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.fusion.title: Fusion Reactor
Manual: without fuel, verify that the emergency control withdraws operating permission and leaves the reactor stopped.

Test the reactor controls before the first fuelling. Leave the fuel input disconnected and make sure there is no fissile fuel inside. You will need a control adapter, a separate emergency button or lever and a clear display of the reactor's state.

Grant the run permission and remove it with the emergency control. The reactor must go to a stopped state and must not restart from a stray constant signal of a neighbouring machine. For temperature automation, separately trace the signal path from the sensor to the control input.

Tick the goal after a real shutdown on a cold, empty installation and a return to a controlled state: only your own observation counts here. The test does not prove the cooling will cope under load; water, steam removal and spare waste capacity are checked separately before fuel goes in.
