codex.quest.mek_nuclear.guide_complete_h: The previous node introduced the gown and the instruments; now gather all four Hazmat pieces. The full kit is needed before any work near a possible release. Check the recipe of each piece and do not stand in for missing boots with ordinary metal armour.

Make the mask, gown, pants and boots, let the book count them in turn, then put the set on in the matching slots. Check that no slot still holds your usual gear. Only a suit worn all at once protects you, not an accumulated list of items.

Record clean instrument readings and set aside a safe cabinet for the spare kit. Do not enter a contaminated area to test the protection: the test is checking the set and what is worn. Contamination is removed by stopping the leak and by time; the suit merely protects the operator within its mechanics.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.guide_heavy_wate: The deuterium line begins with heavy water, produced by an electric pump with a filter upgrade. It does not come out of the brine evaporation tower. Prepare the pump, the filter, power and a reachable water source next to the future fuel workshop.

Put the upgrade into the pump and check the name of the fluid at the output. Feed heavy water through a mechanical pipe into the electrolytic separator: in the installed recipe two units of heavy water give two deuterium and one oxygen. Both chemical outputs need free space.

If deuterium stops arriving, inspect not only the pump but also the separator's oxygen tank. A small buffer reveals an interruption before the reactor goes out. This side branch secures the deuterium supply; tritium still needs lithium, solar activation and a reserve for the night pause.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.hazmat.text.0: Only the full kit protects against radiation. The gown in the quest is just one part of the suit: make the Hazmat mask, pants and boots as well and put everything on before entering the site. Ordinary armour offers no protection from radiation.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.hazmat.text.1: The Geiger counter shows the ambient radiation, the dosimeter the dose your character has accumulated. Take baseline readings in a clean place and learn to tell the two measurements apart. The suit neither cleans a contaminated world nor undoes a dose already received.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.hazmat.text.2: Keep a spare kit outside the reactor room. In a release, do not approach unprotected and stop the source by a safe means. The gown and instruments complete the item part of the quest, but only a fully worn suit protects you; check every part before work.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.hazmat.title: Hazmat Suit
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.reactor.text.0: The fission reactor heats coolant and produces radioactive waste. Build the shell to the layout, place fuel assemblies with control rods on top and configure the ports for fuel, coolant, heated output and waste. The casing count in the quest is no substitute for a full structure calculation.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.reactor.text.1: Before loading fuel, fill the cooling loop, prepare steam intake and a safe waste container. Set the logic adapter to control mode and test the emergency circuit on a cold reactor: removing permission must stop it. Monitoring and control may need different adapters.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.reactor.text.2: Start at a low burn rate and watch temperature, damage, coolant and waste. The moment any flow stops keeping up, halt the reaction at once. Overheating leads to destruction and contamination; a hot reactor, or one full of radioactive chemicals, is never dismantled over a single pipe.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.reactor.title: Fission Reactor
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.sps.reward.0: The top of Mekanism's tech tree
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.sps.text.0: The supercritical phase shifter turns polonium into antimatter at an enormous energy cost. Take it on once polonium flows steadily and a powerful supply exists: this load must not hang on the emergency reserve of reactor cooling.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.sps.text.1: Assemble the SPS shell to the layout, with its ports and supercharged coils. The casings from the quest are only part of the structure. Feed polonium through a dedicated chemical line and energy through the prepared coils, watching the internal progress and a free output.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.sps.text.2: Antimatter can be crystallised: in the installed recipe a thousand units give one pellet. The antiprotonic nucleosynthesizer spends antimatter in specific conversion recipes and does not create an arbitrary item. Do not dismantle an input with leftover polonium, and a finished pellet does not mean the SPS is safely stopped.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.sps.title: Supercritical Phase Shifter
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.uranium.text.0: Uranium ore gives the raw material for fissile fuel, but a uranium ingot is not yet reactor fuel. Mine the ore, smelt some of it and prepare the enrichment chamber. The danger of radioactive waste has nothing to do with ordinary uranium ingots in your pocket.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.uranium.text.1: Turn uranium ingots into yellow cake in the enrichment chamber. Show the book eight ingots in one batch first, then process them and collect four units of cake: item goals are remembered one after another, and the ingots need not come back once counted. The cake will go to the chemical oxidizer.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.uranium.text.2: Before expanding, stock up on fluorite and set up sulfuric acid: the fuel chain will need them at a separate stage. No reactor is needed yet. This way you debug the chemistry and the transport before genuinely radioactive waste enters the system.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.uranium.title: Uranium
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.waste.text.0: Reactor waste needs a separate chemical line and spare volume. The radioactive waste barrel accepts permitted waste and slowly reduces it, but it is never bottomless. Overflow blocks the outlet first of all, so keep the whole chain back to the reactor under control.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.waste.text.1: Nuclear waste becomes polonium in the solar neutron activator or plutonium in the isotopic centrifuge. The reaction chamber makes a pellet from the right chemical, water and fluorite dust and leaves spent nuclear waste behind; that output must not be forgotten either.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.waste.text.2: The activator depends on sunlight, so a reserve for production pauses is mandatory. Never break filled radioactive pipes and tanks; that is a release. The full suit protects whoever services the site, but it does not make a release acceptable. Pellets in your inventory speak of the product, not of safe storage.
codex.quest.mek_nuclear.waste.title: Waste
codex.quest.mek_ore.crusher_mek.text.0: The Mekanism crusher turns suitable items into dust and processes clumps from the purification chamber. The combiner does a different job: it joins a main material with a secondary one and restores certain blocks. Both machines need power and a free output.
codex.quest.mek_ore.crusher_mek.text.1: For a clear demonstration, crush an iron ingot into iron dust. Test the combiner separately: its iron ore recipe takes eight raw iron and a cobblestone, and the main and secondary ingredients use different inputs.
codex.quest.mek_ore.crusher_mek.text.2: There is no free loop here: eight raw pieces give a single ore block. Do not pour all your mining into the combiner for the sake of a pretty ×5. The crusher belongs in the purification chain; keep the combiner for a specific recipe or for restoring a block you need.
codex.quest.mek_ore.crusher_mek.title: Crusher and Combiner
codex.quest.mek_ore.dissolution.text.0: Dissolution adds a chemical slurry ahead of the ore line. You will need sulfuric acid, water for washing and separate pressurized tubes for dirty and clean slurry. The sulfur chain runs through sulfur dioxide, sulfur trioxide and water vapour; brine is no substitute.
codex.quest.mek_ore.dissolution.text.1: The dissolution chamber gets a thousand units of dirty slurry from an iron ore block and two thousand from three raw iron. The washer consumes water and yields clean slurry; the crystallizer turns every two hundred units into one crystal.
codex.quest.mek_ore.dissolution.text.2: The crystals still face injection with hydrogen chloride, purification with oxygen, crushing, enrichment and smelting. The result is five ingots per ore block or ten per three raw iron. Do not mix metals in an unfinished batch: leftover slurry of one kind can block the next.
codex.quest.mek_ore.dissolution.title: Dissolution and Crystallization (×5)
codex.quest.mek_ore.enrichment.text.0: The enrichment chamber makes clean metal dust for smelting. Build the machine, connect power and put a furnace next to it: the chamber does not produce ingots. Use iron for the first run; input and output are easy to compare.
codex.quest.mek_ore.enrichment.text.1: In the installed recipe one iron ore block gives two dust, three raw iron give four and a block of raw iron gives twelve. Each dust smelts into one ingot. A single piece of raw iron will not start the recipe; it needs three.
codex.quest.mek_ore.enrichment.text.2: Set up the dust output and the furnace input, then compare the result with the recipe you chose. The ×2 multiplier applies to ore blocks, not to raw material from a pickaxe. The chamber also concentrates materials for the infuser, so it stays useful after you move to a more complex ore line.
codex.quest.mek_ore.enrichment.title: Enrichment Chamber (×2)
codex.quest.mek_ore.evaporation.text.0: The thermal evaporation plant turns water into brine, and a second identical tower turns brine into liquid lithium. In the installed version both recipes take ten units of input fluid per unit of output. Liquid lithium will later serve a different fuel chain.
codex.quest.mek_ore.evaporation.text.1: Build the hollow tower to the Mekanism layout with a controller and valves. The sixteen blocks in the quest are a stock of parts, not a complete kit for any height. Feed water into the configured input valve and draw brine from the output valve with a mechanical pipe.
codex.quest.mek_ore.evaporation.text.2: Operation depends on temperature: provide heating and watch the readings before adding height. If the input is full and there is no brine, check the structure, the heat and a free output. The evaporator does not make heavy water or sulfuric acid; those have processes of their own.
codex.quest.mek_ore.evaporation.title: Thermal Evaporation Plant
codex.quest.mek_ore.factory.text.0: A factory runs several identical operations at once. The basic one has three lanes, the advanced five, the elite seven and the ultimate nine. It is the number of simultaneous operations that grows, not the speed of each.
codex.quest.mek_ore.factory.text.1: Take the basic smelting factory and the basic tier installer. The installer is applied to a compatible machine already placed in the world: check the required tier first, stop the input and note the settings. A different operation needs a factory of the matching type.
codex.quest.mek_ore.factory.text.2: After the upgrade, feed enough dust and enable lane distribution if your mode needs it. One busy lane beside empty ones points either to a sorting setting or to a shortage of material. Measure the power supply as well: extra lanes are useless on a network that is always drained.
codex.quest.mek_ore.factory.title: Factories
codex.quest.mek_ore.guide_carbon.text.0: The enrichment chamber helps supply the steel infusers with carbon more economically. In the installed version ordinary coal gives ten units of infusion carbon, charcoal twenty and enriched carbon eighty. One coal or charcoal enriches into one unit of concentrate.
codex.quest.mek_ore.guide_carbon.text.1: Make eight concentrates in the chamber and route them into the infuser's consumable input. The main input still takes iron or enriched iron. Do not try to smelt the concentrate: it is a reserve of substance, not a steel blank.
codex.quest.mek_ore.guide_carbon.text.2: Compare how many cycles the line runs between refills. Saving raw material costs an extra electric operation, so keep the ordinary feed available in case the chamber stops. A small stock of concentrate is especially useful to the two infusers, where carbon is spent on both passes.
codex.quest.mek_ore.guide_carbon.title: Concentrated carbon
codex.quest.mek_ore.injection.text.0: Chemical injection goes in front of the purification chamber and turns ore into shards with hydrogen chloride. Keep the oxygen line: the shards still face purification, crushing, enrichment and smelting. One new machine does not make finished metal.
codex.quest.mek_ore.injection.text.1: Make brine in the evaporation plant, split it by electrolysis and combine chlorine with hydrogen in the chemical infuser. It takes two chemicals and has nothing in common with the metallurgic infuser and its item input. Lay the chemical lines before assembling the main line.
codex.quest.mek_ore.injection.text.2: An iron ore block yields four shards, three raw iron yield eight. If output stops, check chlorine, hydrogen and the room for the separator's by-products. Raise speed only once both gases and the oxygen at the next stage flow steadily.
codex.quest.mek_ore.injection.title: Chemical Injection (×4)
codex.quest.mek_ore.miner.text.0: The digital miner mines blocks by filter inside a set area. Prepare steady power, a chest for the result and a clear filter for the ore you want. Set the radius and height range before starting: a small patch is easier to check than the whole neighbourhood of your base.
codex.quest.mek_ore.miner.text.1: Run the search and see how many blocks were found before mining starts. The inverse filter reverses the meaning of the list, so do not switch it on blindly. Silk touch keeps ore blocks intact and changes energy use; handy for comparing processing recipes.
codex.quest.mek_ore.miner.text.2: The stone generator upgrade replaces mined blocks when configured to, but it will not write a safe filter for you. Check the first finds and the stop on a full output. Do not lay the working area over other people's buildings or hidden utilities on the strength of a filter name alone.
codex.quest.mek_ore.miner.title: Digital Miner
For the trial batch prepare twelve raw iron: enrichment gives sixteen dust and smelting sixteen ingots. Eight iron ore blocks mined with silk touch will do as well. Just do not mix the two methods in one count.

Clear old leftovers out of the chamber, the smelter and the output chest. Run the batch and follow the dust to the smelter. If one or two raw pieces remain in the chamber, they lacked the full set of three for the next recipe.

Gather sixteen iron ingots into your ordinary inventory. The book looks at possession and does not take the metal, and it has no idea where the ingots came from. Note the input you chose for the next manual test, or old ingots in the chest will distort the measured output.
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_batch.title: Enrichment workshop: test batch
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_run.task.0: Manual: compare batch inputs and outputs; fill the destination chest and verify that intermediate dust is retained.
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_run.text.0: This trial checks material accounting and how the line behaves when full. Clear the test section of leftovers from earlier batches, count the input material and count the ingots you get. Compare against the recipe for raw iron or ore blocks specifically, not against the chapter title.
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_run.text.1: Then fill the final chest with cheap items so the ingots have nowhere to go. Feed a small new batch and make sure the dust stays in the machines or the transport while processing halts without losing intermediate material.
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_run.text.2: Empty the chest and wait for work to resume. Tick the manual goal after counting the output and confirming the dust survived a full receiver; this is an observation in the world, not a measurement by the book. If the result does not add up, find the wrong side or the stray route and repeat.
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_run.title: Enrichment workshop: operation test
A small enrichment section consists of a chamber and an energized smelter. Prepare an input chest, a receiver for ingots and power for both machines; a short line without factories or upgrades is enough for now. Keep every interface reachable so you can see the intermediate dust.

Give the chamber an item input on the chest side and an output toward the smelter. On the smelter, allow input from that side and output of finished ingots. Enable auto-eject where the machine must push items itself; a passive chest will need extraction.

Before pouring in a whole stack, pick the recipe: an ore block gives two dust, three raw iron give four. Two machines are only the equipment in place. The next batch will test the output, and the manual trial will show whether materials survive a full final chest.
codex.quest.mek_ore.ore_line_setup.title: Enrichment workshop: equipment
codex.quest.mek_ore.purification.text.0: The purification chamber opens the oxygen chain and produces metal clumps. Have the crusher, enrichment chamber and furnace ready before starting, or the clumps will stay half-finished. The electrolytic separator gets water through a mechanical pipe and power through a cable.
codex.quest.mek_ore.purification.text.1: The separator splits water into hydrogen and oxygen. Send the oxygen through a pressurized tube to the purification chamber and give the hydrogen its own storage or a deliberate overflow; a full hydrogen output stops the oxygen too.
codex.quest.mek_ore.purification.text.2: An iron ore block gives three clumps, a piece of raw iron two. Each clump is then crushed into dirty dust, enriched into clean dust and smelted. Track every intermediate form and never put clean and dirty dust into the same unfiltered input.
codex.quest.mek_ore.purification.title: Purification Chamber (×3)
codex.quest.mek_ore.sawmill.text.0: The precision sawmill, the energized smelter and the formulaic assemblicator solve different everyday workshop tasks. The sawmill processes wood and gives sawdust along the way, the smelter melts on electricity, and the assemblicator repeats a recipe recorded in advance.
codex.quest.mek_ore.sawmill.text.1: Connect the devices to the network and try each with one clear input: a log for the sawmill, metal dust for the smelter. Check the sawmill has room for both its main and secondary output; backed-up sawdust can halt the planks.
codex.quest.mek_ore.sawmill.text.2: For the assemblicator, write the formula first, set the recipe you need and supply the full set of ingredients. A random pile of resources without a formula will not turn it into an automatic crafting table. These machines shine on repeated casings and building parts once circuits and metals arrive steadily.
codex.quest.mek_ore.sawmill.title: Sawmill and More
codex.quest.mek_ore.upgrades.text.0: Upgrades change how compatible machines behave, but first work out what is actually holding them back. If the infuser is waiting for iron or oxygen, speed will not conjure the missing resource. Prepare one speed, one energy and one anchor upgrade.
codex.quest.mek_ore.upgrades.text.1: Put the speed upgrade into a busy machine and watch the energy draw. Add the energy upgrade and compare behaviour on the same recipe. Internal buffer, cable throughput and average generation are three different limits, and each shows itself differently.
codex.quest.mek_ore.upgrades.text.2: The anchor keeps a supported device running while the area is unloaded and depends on server permissions; it does not improve every machine and does not check the loading of the whole chain for you. When the grid sags, start with energy savings; speed up only the stage where material genuinely piles up.
codex.quest.mek_ore.upgrades.title: Machine Upgrades
codex.quest.mek_power.bio.text.0: The bio generator turns Mekanism biofuel into electricity. Biofuel comes from crushing plants and farm produce; different crops yield differently, so for the experiment take whatever you already grow regularly.
codex.quest.mek_power.bio.text.1: Craft the generator, set up a crusher and process a small batch. Feed the biofuel into the generator's item input and send the energy to a cube. The crusher needs power too; keep a reserve for start-up, or the closed loop will simply stay drained.
codex.quest.mek_power.bio.text.2: Watch whether the harvest keeps up with continuous operation and whether the crusher's output stays clear. Do not send in the last seeds you need to replant the farm. A mastered biofuel line will later feed the reaction chamber with ethylene, so keep it separate from the food store.
codex.quest.mek_power.bio.title: Bio Generator
codex.quest.mek_power.boiler.text.0: The thermal boiler passes heat into water and releases steam; the turbine is what turns that steam into electricity. Prepare the shell, valves, heating elements and pressure dispersers to the structure layout. Two valves and sixteen casings from the quest are far from the whole boiler.
codex.quest.mek_power.boiler.text.1: Assemble the water section with superheating elements, separate the steam area with a layer of dispersers and make sure the structure is recognised. Bring in water and a suitable heat source. With sodium reactor cooling, heated and cooled coolant travel through their own connections.
codex.quest.mek_power.boiler.text.2: Make the first run on a small, safe flow of heat with an unobstructed steam outlet. Losing water or stopping the consumer changes the heat balance of the entire linked installation. Judge the boiler together with its pumps, turbine and water return, not by the count of casing blocks.
codex.quest.mek_power.boiler.title: Thermal Boiler
codex.quest.mek_power.gas_gen.text.0: The gas-burning generator can burn ethylene from the pressurized reaction chamber. Prepare biofuel from the crusher, water, and hydrogen from the electrolytic separator. The chamber needs an item input, a fluid, a chemical and its own electricity all at once.
codex.quest.mek_power.gas_gen.text.1: The installed recipe takes two biofuel, ten units of water and a hundred hydrogen, yielding one substrate and a hundred ethylene. Substrate is a by-product here, not a starting ingredient. Send it to a separate chest and route the ethylene through a pressurized tube to the generator.
codex.quest.mek_power.gas_gen.text.2: Before switching to self-supplied power, build up an energy reserve for the crusher, the separator and the chamber. If things stop, check all three inputs and both outputs, including the separator's unwanted oxygen. Raising generation is pointless while a full substrate chest or a hydrogen shortage holds the chamber.
codex.quest.mek_power.gas_gen.title: Gas-Burning Generator
codex.quest.mek_power.guide_ethene_phase: Ethylene for the gas generator and liquid ethylene for plastic are two forms of one material. The rotary condensentrator moves supported substances between chemical and liquid form. Make it and keep an energy reserve: the conversion consumes electricity too.

Select condensation, feed ethylene from the reaction chamber through a pressurized tube and draw the liquid off with a mechanical pipe. Different tanks should fill in the interface, not one shared pipe's contents sloshing back and forth. The device has another mode for the reverse conversion.

Do not take all the ethylene from your only working generator: the plastic line can starve its own source of raw material. Start with a small separate reserve and check the stop on a full output. You will need to tell the forms apart for lithium too, when preparing fusion fuel.
codex.quest.mek_power.guide_hdpe.text.0: High-density polyethylene is made in the reaction chamber from substrate, liquid ethylene and oxygen. All three resources are already tied to the biofuel line, but the recipe differs from making ethylene itself. Set up a separate chamber or fully clear the old inputs before switching.
codex.quest.mek_power.guide_hdpe.text.1: One substrate, fifty units of liquid ethylene and ten oxygen give one HDPE pellet. Feed the liquid through a mechanical pipe, the oxygen through a pressurized tube and the substrate by item transport. Connect power and collect six pellets.
codex.quest.mek_power.guide_hdpe.text.2: If the chamber accepts substrate but does not run, first check the form of the ethylene and that no other chemical is left inside. Pellets open the way to sheets and the other plastic parts. Set some substrate aside so plastic production does not depend on whatever happens to be in the generator line's output chest.
codex.quest.mek_power.guide_hdpe.title: First plastic pellets
codex.quest.mek_power.guide_hdpe_sheet.t: HDPE sheets are the next practical product of the chemical workshop. In the enrichment chamber three pellets become one sheet, so the six pellets from the last batch will give two. Oxygen and liquid ethylene are no longer needed at this stage; only energy.

Clear ore dust out of the chamber and load the pellets in full threes. Collect two sheets and look at what is left in the input: one or two pellets are no machine fault, they simply lacked a full set for the recipe. A separate input keeps them from mixing with ordinary ore processing.

Before launching a big run, look at where the sheets are used: plastic goes into specific late components and gear variants. While ethylene also feeds the generator, a small stock beats an overflowing warehouse of pellets. This batch closes the chain from plants to a finished industrial material.
codex.quest.mek_power.heat_gen.text.0: The heat generator is an early source of electricity for the infuser. It burns fuel and also gathers heat from the blocks around it. For the first start, craft the generator, set it beside the future workshop and prepare fuel.
codex.quest.mek_power.heat_gen.text.1: Connect the generator's output to a machine or an energy cube with a universal cable. Make sure the reserve grows without load first, then run one recipe. If you draw heat from lava, plan its placement and fence off the walkway: an exposed hot block is dangerous to the player and to dropped items alike.
codex.quest.mek_power.heat_gen.text.2: This source will not carry a large factory, however neatly the cable is connected. When the infuser works in fits and starts, compare consumption with current generation and let the buffer charge. Later the heat generator remains a small independent source for start-ups.
codex.quest.mek_power.heat_gen.title: Heat Generator
codex.quest.mek_power.induction.text.0: The induction matrix is a multiblock battery for a large power grid. Cells set the capacity, providers the transfer rate. Many cells with a single weak provider give a huge reserve that discharges too slowly for your load.
codex.quest.mek_power.induction.text.1: Assemble the shell with induction ports and put at least one cell and one provider inside. The sixteen casings in the quest are only a starter batch; build the volume and bounds to the matrix rules. Once it forms, set an input port and a separate output.
codex.quest.mek_power.induction.text.2: Charge the matrix and connect a known load, comparing readings in a single energy unit. If the reserve is large yet the machines starve, look at providers, ports and cables. The matrix generates no electricity and will not save a reactor when every consumer stops; it only buys time.
codex.quest.mek_power.induction.title: Induction Matrix
codex.quest.mek_power.solar.text.0: Solar generators produce energy as long as the sky above them is open. Make the ordinary and the advanced version, but do not spend all your parts before you have a battery: at night the production line will be left without the sun.
codex.quest.mek_power.solar.text.1: Place the panels in the open and connect an energy cube. Leave the advanced design room for its unfolded panel and build nothing above it. Open the interface by day and see how much energy your biome yields in your weather.
codex.quest.mek_power.solar.text.2: Compare daytime accumulation with the workshop's night-time draw. If the reserve runs short, lower the night load, add storage when the daytime surplus allows, or set up an independent source. The advanced panel promises no round-the-clock power, and the cable sides still need checking.
codex.quest.mek_power.solar.title: Solar Panels
codex.quest.mek_power.turbine.text.0: The industrial turbine takes steam and turns its flow into energy. A real installation needs more parts than the quest lists: prepare valves, vents, pressure dispersers, the rotational complex and electromagnetic coils to the Mekanism Generators layout.
codex.quest.mek_power.turbine.text.1: Inside the shell, assemble the central rotor with blades; the upper section links the rotation to the coils, and condensers return the water. Place parts layer by layer as in the layout and wait for the structure to be recognised before admitting steam. Four rotors alone do not set the output.
codex.quest.mek_power.turbine.text.2: Connect the steam, the energy output and the water return. Watch the actual flow, the energy reserve and the steam build-up: full storage or weak removal will limit operation. Paired with a reactor, rehearse a consumer shutdown on a cold system and keep an emergency heat cut-off ready.
codex.quest.mek_power.turbine.title: Steam Turbine
codex.quest.mek_power.wind.text.0: The wind generator provides passive energy and suits a remote workshop. Its output grows with installation height within the world's settings, so choose the spot wisely: a tower with a safe climb is often handier than a distant peak with no road.
codex.quest.mek_power.wind.text.1: Choose the site in advance, place the generator with room for its structure and run a cable to the battery. Before connecting machines, make sure energy actually reaches storage. A tall mast with no connected output is merely an expensive landmark.
codex.quest.mek_power.wind.text.2: Compare the readings at your chosen height with the base's load and do not expect figures from someone else's guide. When expanding, check the throughput of the shared line and the margin for peak recipes. Wind is a fine steady foundation, but accelerated chemical machines may ask for far more.
codex.quest.mek_power.wind.title: Wind Generator
The quantum entangloporter carries supported resources between devices on the same frequency. A real link needs at least two blocks, though the quest asks for one. Test moving ordinary items or energy over a short distance where both ends are in view.

Set the same frequency and configure sides for each resource separately. Allow input at the source and output at the receiver, with auto-eject if needed. The frequency buffer is shared, so production lines with incompatible fluids deserve frequencies of their own.

Check access rights and loading at both sites. The entangloporter does not carry radioactive chemicals around the restrictions: do not plan to haul reactor waste this way without confirmed support. If energy flows but items do not, the network is fine; usually the item sides need fixing.
codex.quest.mek_qio.entangloporter.title: Quantum Entangloporter
Manual: transfer eight items, retain the next batch with a full output and complete delivery after clearing it.

Test quantum delivery of ordinary items before spreading the devices across dimensions. Place two entangloporters side by side, choose a separate test frequency and prepare an input chest with eight cobblestone. At the receiver, leave an empty chest for this batch alone.

Configure the source's item input and the receiver's item output, enabling the extraction you need. Wait for eight items at the output and compare the count. Then fill the receiver, send another small batch and make sure the resource stayed in reachable buffers.

Free the output and confirm the delivery completed without losses. Only then tick the manual goal and move the proven pair to distant sites. There you will also need both ends loaded and matching frequency rights: the side-by-side test checks routing, not the conditions of the world.
codex.quest.mek_qio.guide_stock_signal.t: Manual: add and remove one material to verify the QIO signal switches both ways across the configured threshold.

The QIO adapter can produce a consumable up to a target stock without flooding the whole drive. For the experiment take ordinary cobblestone in a quantity that is easy to count. Connect the adapter to the frequency holding the test material and prepare a visible signal indicator.
Set the filter to cobblestone and a threshold. Add material to cross it, then take some back out. Watch the output; if the logic turns out reversed, fix the mode before connecting real production.

After two verified crossings of the threshold the manual goal can be ticked. For real use, tie the signal to a machine's supported control and leave a margin for operations already begun. Until the signal is connected to something it stops nothing, and an adapter in your inventory says nothing about restocking yet.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_array.text.0: The QIO drive array holds the media of the wireless item storage. An array without a drive gives no capacity, and a drive without a chosen frequency creates no reachable network. Prepare a basic drive and the array, then place them in a serviced part of the base.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_array.text.1: Insert the drive, create a storage frequency and set access. Working with items will need the QIO dashboard from the next node. Run the first test on a handful of cobblestone and leave valuables in the old chest until retrieval has been checked.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_array.text.2: Drives are limited both in total item count and in number of types. A pile of different damaged tools fills storage differently from big stacks of stone. Check both figures in the interface before expanding; choose the next drive tier by the actual shortage, not by its name.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_array.title: QIO Drive Array
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_dash.text.0: The QIO dashboard opens the contents of the chosen storage frequency. The stationary one suits the workbench, the portable one the road. Both need an existing array with a drive and the right frequency; crafting a dashboard alone conjures no network.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_dash.text.1: Select the same frequency as the array and put a few ordinary items in through the interface. Find them by search and take them back out. Charge the portable dashboard in advance and check access before you stash backup tools in remote storage.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_dash.text.2: If the list is empty, compare frequency, owner and access rights, then the state of the array. Moving the whole warehouse is premature until retrieval has been checked. After that the dashboard becomes a comfortable workstation, and importers and exporters will link QIO to your machines.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_dash.title: QIO Dashboard
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_io.text.0: The QIO importer pulls items from a neighbouring inventory into the network; the exporter hands matching ones back out. The redstone adapter turns the presence of a set stock into a control signal. That makes a handy basis for restocking consumables without searching the dashboard by hand.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_io.text.1: Connect all three devices to the right frequency. Import a small test chest first, then give the exporter a single filter and point it at a separate receiver. Do not enable broad extraction next to the chest with your personal tools.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_io.text.2: Set the adapter's threshold and check how the signal changes as material is added and removed. That way automatic output can stop once the stock is built up. Avoid an importer–exporter pair endlessly cycling one item through the same chest: every inventory should have a single direction.
codex.quest.mek_qio.qio_io.title: Import and Export
codex.quest.mek_qio.stabilizer.text.0: The dimensional stabilizer keeps chosen chunks loaded while it has power and the feature is allowed. Remote production that must run without the player needs it. Before placing one, make sure it really is chunk unloading that stops the line, not an empty battery or a blocked output.
codex.quest.mek_qio.stabilizer.text.1: Place the device, supply power and select the areas you need in the interface. Think of the whole chain: the generator, the pump, the input storage and the receiver may sit in neighbouring chunks. A loaded machine with an unloaded water source will not run steadily.
codex.quest.mek_qio.stabilizer.text.2: Run the experiment on safe, ordinary production: walk away and compare what accumulated when you return. A radioactive reactor is no place for a first test. Mark only the area you need; extra loading eats server resources and is no substitute for placing linked devices compactly.
codex.quest.mek_qio.stabilizer.title: Dimensional Stabilizer
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleport_core.text.0: The teleportation core goes into recipes for devices that work across distance. It is a part, not a pocket teleporter: on its own it moves no one anywhere. Gather the circuits, alloys and remaining ingredients by the recipe before spending rare stock.
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleport_core.text.1: Make four cores and let the goal count them in your inventory. Then choose the first use: a stationary teleporter for the place you visit most, or wireless infrastructure devices. A complete route usually takes several finished blocks and its own power.
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleport_core.text.2: Think the destination through in advance: a safe pad, access to power and a clear frequency name matter more than a spare core in a chest. A remote teleporter must not stay your only way home until a two-way test has passed. Cores open the quantum branch, but the link itself is still to be built.
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleport_core.title: Teleportation Core
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleporter.text.0: The stationary teleporter creates a travel point once the frame is built and the frequency set. The portable teleporter picks a suitable stationary point but does not replace it. Prepare frame blocks beyond the quest items and charge the portable device.
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleporter.text.1: Build the portal in the teleporter's shape, bring in power and set a frequency with the right access. For two pads, match the frequency and check each is ready. In the interface, make sure the device sees a real destination before you leave for another dimension.
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleporter.text.2: Make the first jump with a backup way to return and a clear pad at the exit. An exit in lava, a cramped mine or inside a running machine is a bad idea. If the point is unavailable, check power, structure, frequency rights and area loading: a matching name without those conditions moves no one.
codex.quest.mek_qio.teleporter.title: Teleporter
codex.quest.mek_start.alloys.text.0: Infused alloy is iron processed with redstone in the infuser. The configurator and most early machines already need it. Set aside a separate batch of iron ingots for it: osmium in this recipe would give a basic circuit instead.
codex.quest.mek_start.alloys.text.1: Make four alloys while keeping an eye on the redstone reserve and the power. Further on, infused alloy is processed with diamond substance to become reinforced; the next step with refined obsidian gives atomic alloy.
codex.quest.mek_start.alloys.text.2: Diamond on top of unfinished redstone in the tank will spoil the batch. Either dedicate an infuser to each substance or finish one batch before clearing. The enrichment chamber can concentrate infusion consumables; while resources arrive by hand, that is more useful than chasing speed.
codex.quest.mek_start.alloys.title: Alloys
codex.quest.mek_start.box.text.0: The cardboard box carries supported blocks together with their contents and settings. It needs sawdust, easiest to get from the precision sawmill. Until you have one, look up other sawdust recipes in JEI; your first steel does not need a box.
codex.quest.mek_start.box.text.1: Try it first on an ordinary chest holding one expendable item. Pack the block, carry the box, place it and unpack it with the intended interaction. Make sure the contents are intact before you move the workshop.
codex.quest.mek_start.box.text.2: Packing has limits: it will not take apart a multiblock. Radioactive tanks and a running reactor are no place for experiments. Stop an ordinary machine first, cut off materials and power, note its orientation, and check the connections again after the move.
codex.quest.mek_start.box.title: Cardboard Box
codex.quest.mek_start.cables.text.0: Mekanism networks carry different things. The universal cable carries energy, the mechanical pipe fluids, the pressurized tube chemicals and the logistical transporter items. Water reaches the separator through a mechanical pipe, and the oxygen leaves through a pressurized tube.
codex.quest.mek_start.cables.text.1: Craft the starter kit and connect a pair of devices of each type you need. On a machine, set input and output separately for energy, items and chemicals. A pipe touching a block carries nothing until the chosen side allows it.
codex.quest.mek_start.cables.text.2: To pull contents out of passive storage, enable Pull mode on the connection or use an active output. Never share one line between incompatible fluids or chemicals. Transport tiers are basic, advanced, elite and ultimate; heat travels through its own conductor.
codex.quest.mek_start.cables.title: Transmission
codex.quest.mek_start.casing.text.0: The steel casing is the part most machines grow from, so eight casings will go quickly. Prepare steel, osmium and glass, and set some osmium aside for circuits in advance; otherwise the casings will stall everything else.
codex.quest.mek_start.casing.text.1: Craft the casings at the crafting table. A casing has no interface of its own: placed in the world, it becomes neither a furnace nor an enrichment chamber. A machine comes from a separate recipe with the right circuits and materials.
codex.quest.mek_start.casing.text.2: Before spending the batch, decide which line comes first: the enrichment chamber and the energized smelter pay off immediately. The quest wants eight casings in your inventory, so do not turn the last one into a machine before the goal registers. Steel will later go into transport networks too.
codex.quest.mek_start.casing.title: Steel Casing
codex.quest.mek_start.circuit.text.0: Control circuits go into recipes for machines, cables and upgrades. The basic one is simple: an osmium ingot processed with redstone in the metallurgic infuser. Iron in the same slot would give alloy instead, so keep the two batches apart.
codex.quest.mek_start.circuit.text.1: Fill the infuser with redstone, feed in four osmium ingots and wait for four circuits. Leftover carbon from steelmaking will block the recipe: give redstone an infuser of its own, or clear the tank first.
codex.quest.mek_start.circuit.text.2: Advanced, elite and ultimate circuits are made from the previous tier with the matching alloy. It is a chain of recipes, not an infuser setting. A small stock of basic circuits spares you the temptation to dismantle working machines for parts.
codex.quest.mek_start.circuit.title: Control Circuits
The configurator changes transport network connections and helps set up equipment. It is an electric tool, so charge it first in any suitable device. The configuration card carries settings between machines and saves time when installing identical units.

Check which mode is selected before you press anything. Items, fluids, chemicals and energy each have their own actions; verify the key combinations in the controls, since the pack allows rebinding. Practise switching a connection on a short stretch next to a chest.

Record the settings of a proven machine on the card and apply them to a compatible second one. After copying, compare orientation and sides: the same configuration on a differently rotated block moves the inputs. A mastered configurator saves more time than dismantling the main line at every stop.
codex.quest.mek_start.configurator.title: Configurator
codex.quest.mek_start.energy.text.0: The energy cube smooths out generation pauses and short load peaks. It stores energy already produced, so it cannot fix a permanent power shortage. Craft the basic cube and keep its interface reachable.
codex.quest.mek_start.energy.text.1: Connect the generator to the input side and the consumers to the output side. Look at the cube's own side configuration: an accidentally rotated block often leaves the cable on a disabled face. With the machines stopped, the reserve should grow.
codex.quest.mek_start.energy.text.2: Start the enrichment chamber and watch the reserve. A slow decline means the average load exceeds generation; a full cube beside starving machines points to the output or the throughput. Compare readings in one energy unit, FE for example, across all interfaces.
codex.quest.mek_start.energy.title: Energy Storage
codex.quest.mek_start.infuser.text.0: The metallurgic infuser combines the item in its main slot with a substance stored inside the machine. Craft it from iron, furnaces, redstone and osmium, then connect it to the heat generator with a universal cable.
codex.quest.mek_start.infuser.text.1: The interface has two inputs: the main slot and the infusion material slot. Redstone tops up the internal reserve of its substance, while iron in the main slot becomes infused alloy. Carbon goes toward steel; that is a separate batch of work.
codex.quest.mek_start.infuser.text.2: If the machine sits idle, check the charge, both inputs and a free output. Leftover redstone inside will block the switch to carbon: unload the consumables and clear the tank deliberately, or place a second infuser. Clearing destroys whatever was still inside.
codex.quest.mek_start.infuser.title: Metallurgic Infuser
codex.quest.mek_start.osmium.text.0: Osmium is the metal of the first Mekanism machines, and tin will serve bronze and many later recipes. Both ores turn up during ordinary mine exploration. Gather whatever you find along the way, but set aside a separate stock of iron: tools and the first generator will need it.
codex.quest.mek_start.osmium.text.1: Smelt what you found in an ordinary furnace. Electric processing can wait; right now the point is sixteen osmium ingots and eight tin ingots. An ore block and the raw material that drops from it are different inputs for future machines, so do not pile them together.
codex.quest.mek_start.osmium.text.2: Keep technical metals apart from building materials. The book expects ingots: ore in a chest will not close the goal. Osmium opens the infuser, and with steady power you can move straight on to circuits.
codex.quest.mek_start.osmium.title: Osmium
codex.quest.mek_start.sorter.text.0: The logistical sorter takes matching items out of a neighbouring inventory and sends them into the transport network. It belongs between the shared chest and the steel line: iron should go to the first infuser and coal to the carbon feed.
codex.quest.mek_start.sorter.text.1: Place the sorter right against the chest, connect its output to a transporter and set one simple item filter. Test a small batch; add colours and extra destinations later, once a single line truly stops being enough.
codex.quest.mek_start.sorter.text.2: The diversion transporter switches connections by redstone signal and is no substitute for the sorter's filter. If cargo comes back or stays in the chest, check the destination inventory, the colours and the signal state; that keeps foreign material out of machine inputs.
codex.quest.mek_start.sorter.title: Logistical Sorting
codex.quest.mek_start.steel.text.0: Steel is born from iron in two passes through the infuser and one smelting. Prepare iron ingots, coal or charcoal for carbon, and fuel for the furnace. Infusion consumes electricity as well.
codex.quest.mek_start.steel.text.1: The first pass turns iron and carbon into enriched iron. The second pass, again with carbon, yields steel dust; smelt it into an ingot. In the installed version each pass takes ten units of infusion carbon.
codex.quest.mek_start.steel.text.2: Enriched iron sent straight to the furnace will not become steel; the second pass is mandatory. For sixteen ingots you walk the chain sixteen times, and carbon is needed at both stages. Later, two dedicated infusers will take over the shuffling.
codex.quest.mek_start.steel.title: Steel
codex.quest.mek_start.steel_line_batch.t: A trial batch shows where the line loses pace or waits for a consumable. Separate sixteen iron ingots from the rest of your stock, supply both infusers with carbon and empty the output chest. Do not add speed until the experiment is over.

Send the iron into the first infuser. Watch the enriched iron, the steel dust and the finished ingots in turn; a delay at one stage tells you at once which interface to open. Sixteen steel ingots should gather at the output.

Take the ingots into your ordinary inventory so the goal registers; the book neither consumes them nor tells hand-made from machine-made. If everything came out by hand, the stock is still useful, and the next test will confirm whether the setup holds up.
codex.quest.mek_start.steel_line_run.tas: Manual: verify separate carbon and material feeds; interrupt and restore an input without mixing intermediate materials.
codex.quest.mek_start.steel_line_run.tex: Now find out whether the steel line survives an ordinary supply interruption. Remove valuables from the test input and prepare a few iron ingots. You will need to watch both infusers and the smelter, not just the final chest.

Cut the raw material feed, then restore it. Separately interrupt the carbon feed, wait for the right infuser to stop and top it up again. Enriched iron must stay an intermediate product, and steel dust must reach the smelter without rerouting by hand.

Tick the manual goal once separate inputs, the stop and the restart have passed without mixing materials; the book does not watch this work itself. If a stray item lands in the slot instead of a stop, fix the filter or the sides and repeat the experiment.
codex.quest.mek_start.steel_line_setup.t: This side branch turns hand-made steel into a small section with clear stages. You will need two infusers and an energized smelter; add cables, transporters and chests to suit the spot. Leave a walkway in front of the interfaces for maintenance.

The first infuser takes iron and carbon, the second enriched iron and carbon. Route its steel-dust output into the energized smelter. On every device, item sides are configured separately from the power side.

Leave elaborate sorting for later: fill the carbon reserves by hand and walk a single iron ingot through every stage. The machines you have are only the equipment for now. The trial batch and the shutdown test come in the next quests, and a stack of machines is not yet a working line.
codex.quest.missiles.computer.text.0: The computer links the target to the missile’s fins. The guidance interface picks the target and can talk to the radar network. You need both items, configured fins and an available network controller; leave the warhead off for now.
codex.quest.missiles.computer.text.1: Use the computer item to select the Actuator Fins, then place the computer in the allowed area. The guidance interface is placed by interacting with a Create seat and bound to the Network Controller with the intended action. Read the messages about the chosen actuator and the completed binding.
codex.quest.missiles.computer.text.2: A target on the radar, a seat and a computer do not connect by themselves. Make sure the right object is selected and the command reaches the right fins. After moving any node, check the bindings again. The launch mount and a flight without explosives come only after that.
codex.quest.missiles.computer.title: Guidance Computer
codex.quest.missiles.fins.text.0: Actuator fins give the computer a way to change the missile’s course. The four items in the goal are a stock of parts, not a finished aerodynamic layout. Take a light airframe without a warhead and mark its long axis.
codex.quest.missiles.fins.text.1: Place the fins in line with the direction of flight and make sure they joined the right construct. When setting up the computer, the actuator is chosen by using it on the fins before the computer is placed. Keep every node reachable to fix a binding.
codex.quest.missiles.fins.text.2: Make sure control surfaces do not face opposite ways. Check the fins’ response without a fuelled motor first, then make a short separate flight. If the craft spins, compare orientation, centre of mass and the chosen actuator: extra fins without understanding the fault only amplify the wrong control.
codex.quest.missiles.fins.title: Fins
codex.quest.missiles.fuze_prox.text.0: The proximity fuze triggers on approach after launch, and its sensitivity is set separately. It is part of a dangerous device, so make the item and study its state on an unloaded training construct. Detonation is not tested next to the base.
codex.quest.missiles.fuze_prox.text.1: Install the fuze facing the intended way and set the detection distance on its panel. It works together with the state of the launched craft and does not become a safe sensor for any surroundings. Configure everything before the warhead goes on.
codex.quest.missiles.fuze_prox.text.2: For a real trial choose a distant target and a clear flight area. The word “aerial” does not mean the fuze ignores walls or friendly constructs. Watch one launch and keep the settings; for a guidance-only test, leave the fuze and the warhead off.
codex.quest.missiles.fuze_prox.title: Proximity Fuze
codex.quest.missiles.motor_rocket.text.0: The rocket motor gives a physical construct thrust and holds its own stock of charges. Make the motor and a training airframe once the physics assembler is familiar. A block on the floor is not yet a flying craft.
codex.quest.missiles.motor_rocket.text.1: Open the motor’s interface and look at the propellant slots. Install it without fuel, checking the nozzle direction and the attachment to the future missile. Mass, the thrust point and the airframe’s makeup change how the whole construct moves.
codex.quest.missiles.motor_rocket.text.2: A second motor does not double the burn time by a simple formula; it all depends on loading and configuration. Before fuelling, prepare a clear corridor and a way to hold the missile on its launch mount. Fly the first trial without a warhead: judge orientation and burn before assembling the full guided craft.
codex.quest.missiles.motor_rocket.title: Rocket Motor
The launch mount holds the missile and ties it to launch control. You need the mount, a training physics construct and a network link. The node is two-sided: missiles can attach on the corresponding faces, but check the position in the world.

Align the craft with the mount’s working face and check the hold without fuel or warhead. For the weapon network, place a red Weapon Link at the mount as the tooltip says. Make sure the chosen guidance interface belongs to this very rig.

Before a real launch, check the missile’s clear exit and the fin bindings. The release command must not also drop a neighbouring parked craft. Start with one training airframe and watch the separation.
codex.quest.missiles.mount_missile.title: Launcher
codex.quest.more_et_side.arky.task.0: Use white dye on a raccoon to summon Arky
codex.quest.more_et_side.arky.task.1: Equip fursuit items in all four armour slots
codex.quest.more_et_side.arky.text.0: Arky appears through a special interaction with a raccoon: white dye changes the creature’s form. Take a suitable raccoon and a safe place where the transformation touches no ordinary pets. A white costume summons no character.
codex.quest.more_et_side.arky.text.1: Use white dye on the raccoon and wait for Arky together with the advancement. The second goal is a full worn fursuit set of a supported family: helmet, chest piece, leggings and boots. The check is on equipment; one piece will not close it.
codex.quest.more_et_side.arky.text.2: Assemble the set through its branch, wear all four parts and wait for the mark. Change outside a dangerous environment: a decorative costume is no protective armour. Afterwards put your working gear back on and make sure the pets are safe.
codex.quest.more_et_side.arky.title: Arky
Remain in the participating world until the Blue Moon event ends and its advancement is awarded
The Blue Moon is an Eternal Tales event, not an odd sky colour and not a visit to Terralith’s moonlight grove. Prepare a fortified spot, food and healing before going out at night. Wait for the start message and stay in the world where the event runs.

The night brings event-related threats and materials. Explore them as your gear allows, keeping a path to shelter. Summoning a boss is optional: the advancement comes from the Blue Moon ending, not from any blue item.

Wait for the end message and check the mark in the book. Do not leave for another dimension at the last moment if you want to be there when the current event ends. In the morning restock consumables, inspect the approaches to base and decide whether the next night is worth its loot.
codex.quest.more_et_side.blue_moon.title: Blue Moon
codex.quest.more_et_side.bomb.task.0: Ignite an atomic bomb with flint and steel or a fire charge at an isolated range, then retreat
codex.quest.more_et_side.bomb.text.0: The Eternal Tales atomic bomb is a destructive block. The recipe surrounds sulphur TNT with eight jester bombs. Make it only for a separate range far from buildings, villagers, vehicles and everything you value.
codex.quest.more_et_side.bomb.text.1: Arrange a quick retreat and an observation spot in advance. Place the bomb and ignite it with flint and steel or a fire charge. The advancement is granted when the block becomes an armed bomb; there is no need to stand by until the blast.
codex.quest.more_et_side.bomb.text.2: Leave at once and wait for the effect to end at a distance. The advancement restores no world and spares no territory. Return to the debris only after looking it over. This goal is a prepared experiment, not an item test inside your own workshop.
codex.quest.more_et_side.bomb.title: Royal Boom
codex.quest.more_et_side.chests.text.0: The four chests belong to the Eternal Tales skills of digging, fishing, growing and sorcery. Each entry checks that the right chest entered your inventory. A wooden chest renamed on an anvil does not count.
codex.quest.more_et_side.chests.text.1: Develop the occupations and keep the reward containers that drop until the mark. Digging works with eligible blocks, fishing with its own system, growing with plants, sorcery with magic. Four stations side by side create no rewards.
codex.quest.more_et_side.chests.text.2: Get the containers one at a time and check the advancement before opening if you want the contents. Holding all four at once is unnecessary; the advancements are independent. Missing one type? Go back to its skill instead of opening more chests of another profession.
codex.quest.more_et_side.chests.title: Four Chests
codex.quest.more_et_side.clown.task.0: Remain in the participating world until Clown Moon ends and its advancement is awarded
codex.quest.more_et_side.clown.text.0: The Clown Moon is a separate Eternal Tales event with its own start and end. Prepare a range or a fortified area away from villagers. Clown gear in a chest does not mean the event has even begun.
codex.quest.more_et_side.clown.text.1: Follow the unlocked branch for summoning the event and wait for the announcement. Keep the enemies under control, healing at hand and the fight away from the colony’s narrow streets. Do not spend random trophies as an “activator”: check the launch item’s purpose beforehand.
codex.quest.more_et_side.clown.text.2: Wait for the Clown Moon to end and for the mark while in the corresponding world. This checks the event, not a clown costume worn or a look-alike creature killed. Afterwards gather the remaining loot and tidy the area.
codex.quest.more_et_side.clown.title: Circus
codex.quest.more_et_side.crabs.text.0: The Crabsapocalypse is marked by an advancement for its special banner. The name speaks of completing the event, but the criterion checks crabsapocalypse_banner in your inventory; neither a crab trophy nor a renamed banner fits.
codex.quest.more_et_side.crabs.text.1: Follow the Eternal Tales combat branch with spare healing, room for loot and a safe retreat zone. Read how the event is summoned and what the encounter requires in the guide beforehand. Killing any crab grants no final banner.
codex.quest.more_et_side.crabs.text.2: Having got the banner, pick it up, wait for the mark and keep it for display. Hanging it on a wall before registration is awkward: the item must be obtained by the player. The book counts no stages of the fight; the advancement means the trophy in hand, and repeat encounters are your own choice.
codex.quest.more_et_side.crabs.title: Crabsapocalypse
codex.quest.more_et_side.darwin.task.0: Use the Emblem of Mite at Slaying 2+, die from nettle damage and eat Unahzaal pancakes
codex.quest.more_et_side.darwin.text.0: The advancement’s name combines three odd flags, but it demands no three identical deaths. In the code it is using the Emblem of Mite, dying from nettle damage and eating Unahzaal pancakes. Run the trial without valuable luggage.
codex.quest.more_et_side.darwin.text.1: The emblem needs combat skill level two and no cooldown; using it sets its flag. The pancakes set their flag when eaten and apply a dangerous effect. Only the nettle entry checks a death, and specifically nettle_damage, not any death near the plant.
codex.quest.more_et_side.darwin.text.2: Secure your belongings, respawn point and access to the trial site in advance, mindful of your world’s item-loss rules. With all three conditions met, wait for the joint mark. Random deaths speed no check; they only cost experience and time spent re-equipping.
codex.quest.more_et_side.darwin.title: Darwin Award
codex.quest.more_et_side.gravicycle.task: Put 64 acceleration modifiers in gravicycle slot 0 and mount it
codex.quest.more_et_side.gravicycle.text: The Arkemer gravicycle is Eternal Tales’ own way of getting around. The first advancement checks obtaining the item, while “maximum acceleration” in this version has a precise equipment condition. Take the vehicle, acceleration modifiers and a roomy site.

Put sixty-four Gravicycle Acceleration Modifiers into slot zero of its inventory and mount it. The check needs a full stack, the vehicle with a rider and the player nearby; it measures no speed, so a long dangerous ride without modifiers gives nothing.

Wait for the mark and only then learn the controls with short trips. Watch stopping and terrain before riding with valuable luggage. Acceleration is not tested between colony houses: first make sure you can return to the pad without hitting anything.
Eternal Tales adds small things that make trips more comfortable. The portable chest is carried storage opened straight from your hands: a chest in the centre, two chains at the sides and four pieces of leather in the crafting grid’s corners. It is a separate item with its own contents; an ordinary chest does not count instead.

The glow berry cookie is crafted from two cookies and glow berries, two at once. The berries grow on vines in lush caves, and at home you can grow them by planting on the underside of a block. Both advancements are granted the moment the items appear in the inventory, with no further action.

Assemble the kit before a long expedition: food, torches and blocks in the portable chest, the cookie as a light snack that takes almost no space. Do not hide the portable chest inside a backpack: nested containers are convenient, but after a death they take longer to find.
codex.quest.more_et_side.guide_skills.ta: Reach the first level of the Digging skill
Raise any skill with a skill point on the Notice Board
codex.quest.more_et_side.guide_skills.te: The Notice Board is Eternal Tales’ built-in reference: it is crafted from any planks and a sheet of paper, and inside it shows quests, dimension crystals, boss statistics and skills. Place it at home and open it: the skill and ammunition overlays on screen are toggled there too.

The Digging skill grows by mining ores; the higher the level, the more often an extra ore chunk drops. The first level arrives by itself after ordinary pickaxe work, and the book credits the “Young Miner” advancement. The other skills grow from their own activities: catching, growing, archery, sorcery, archaeology.

Every skill increase grants player level points, and a new player level grants a skill point that can be invested in any skill right on the board. Do this at least once: that is how the second advancement is credited. Do not spend points at random; read the skill description on its board tab first.
codex.quest.more_et_side.lamps.task.0: Obtain all 9 lamp variants: lava, water, snow, blood, black water, acid, liquid aetherium, soul lava and ender
codex.quest.more_et_side.lamps.text.0: The collection is nine lamps: lava, water, snow, blood, black water, acid, aetherium, soul lava and ender. Each has its own criterion, so “all lava lamps” describes no full set. Keep a list of what is missing.
codex.quest.more_et_side.lamps.text.1: The first lava lamp is made from cobalt, a honey bottle, glass, a lava bucket, iron and redstone. Further lamps are converted with the matching contents; check the result before spending a rare liquid. One form can be shown to the book before it becomes another.
codex.quest.more_et_side.lamps.text.2: Mark each variant and keep your favourites to light a room. There is no need to line up all nine or pour dangerous liquids on the floor. If the collection is incomplete, check the nine criteria rather than the number of similar blocks on the shelf: two lamps of one colour are still one form.
codex.quest.more_et_side.lamps.title: Light of the Night
codex.quest.more_et_side.music.task.0: Obtain all 31 specific discs listed by the Eternal Tales music collection advancement
codex.quest.more_et_side.music.text.0: This version’s music collection is thirty-one Eternal Tales records: world recordings and separate biome compositions. A few vanilla discs replace no set. Keep a labelled store and check against the advancement’s own criteria.
codex.quest.more_et_side.music.text.1: Gather recordings from the sources of their branches, keep the discs among your trophies and study the uses of musical materials. Take each new disc into your inventory before putting it in a jukebox: the game marks obtaining, not listening.
codex.quest.more_et_side.music.text.2: There is no need to hold the whole set at once; the criteria are saved one by one. For an exhibition keep one of each and separate duplicates from rarities. If one gap remains, look for the exact composition name, including second recordings of the same world: one Rayana disc closes none of its biome variants.
codex.quest.more_et_side.music.title: Collector
codex.quest.more_et_side.raccoons.task.0: Tame the required raccoon variants and obtain Alien Martian Raccoon and Peacoon transformations
codex.quest.more_et_side.raccoons.task.1: Interact with a raccoon to pet it
codex.quest.more_et_side.raccoons.text.0: A raccoon is tamed with a cookie, and petting counts as interacting with it. Stock up on treats and a safe place for pets. “All variants” is not one colour: the game remembers tamed variants and separately checks two special transformations.
codex.quest.more_et_side.raccoons.text.1: Tame the variants you find and note them by name or look. The check counts variants two through seven and the regular or white base one. The Alien Martian Raccoon and Peacoon advancements come through comet cabbage and the Dreadful Pea.
codex.quest.more_et_side.raccoons.text.2: Look at the final mark after each new kind; herding every animal into one pen is pointless, since this is a history of actions, not a stack of items. Try dyes and special plants on a favourite pet deliberately: a transformation may change its form.
codex.quest.more_et_side.raccoons.title: Raccoons
codex.quest.more_et_side.tarkos.task.0: Tame green, crimson, cyan and albino tarkos using fermented tarantula eyes
codex.quest.more_et_side.tarkos.text.0: Tarkos are large reptiles of Rayana tamed with a fermented tarantula eye. Take a stock of bait, a safe way into Rayana and a place for pets. The advancement needs four variants, green, crimson, cyan and albino, not four identical beasts.
codex.quest.more_et_side.tarkos.text.1: Greens are the most common, crimsons live in deserts, cyans in the snow, and the albino is rare. Feed the treat and watch for success: one attempt promises no result. Note the colours already counted so you do not waste bait.
codex.quest.more_et_side.tarkos.text.2: Check the final advancement after the last variant. There is no need to turn the animals into items or keep them all nearby; the taming history is kept. When moving one, give its large body room and do not lead a pet along a narrow dangerous path you walk with ease.
codex.quest.more_et_side.tarkos.title: Tarkos
codex.quest.more_explore.amberian.text.0: The amberian city stands in Eternal Tales’ Amber Kingdom and is checked as the amberian_city biome. First open the way into the dimension through its story branch, bringing protection and a way back. A colony of yellow stone is a different place entirely.
codex.quest.more_explore.amberian.text.1: Once inside, write down the coordinates of the first portal: important turns of the amber story depend on it. Look for the city biome within the Kingdom itself and check the name on the spot. The geographic goal needs no maze cleared and no king beaten.
codex.quest.more_explore.amberian.text.2: Look over the passages, the characters and a safe stopping point without starting fights in the narrow streets. After the mark, continue the needed conversations separately. Amber items brought by another player prove no visit of yours.
codex.quest.more_explore.amberian.title: Amberian City
codex.quest.more_explore.amethyst.text.0: The Terralith amethyst canyon is dramatic relief and warm greenery: bamboo, vines, local trees. Take blocks for the descent and think about how to get back up; jumping into a pretty crevice is optional.
codex.quest.more_explore.amethyst.text.1: Find amethyst_canyon with Nature’s Compass and approach along the rim, judging the heights. Descend in steps and check the biome name on your chosen ledge. An underground amethyst geode replaces no canyon, even if the material in the name is the same.
codex.quest.more_explore.amethyst.text.2: Remember the entrance, take in the view from several levels and keep the way back. The goal counts the visit, not crystals. When gathering a palette, remember: the canyon’s name makes no found block a renewable shard source; amethyst grows by the usual rules.
codex.quest.more_explore.amethyst.title: Amethyst Canyon
codex.quest.more_explore.atlas_done.text: A filled map is the tangible result of the atlas walk, but it holds none of the biomes you found. Make an empty map and use it in the right area of the Overworld. Choose the scale for a specific district; the whole world will not fit on one sheet.

Walk around the activation point, gradually revealing the picture, and keep the route home. The cartography table helps with scale, copies and locking the map. Label the district clearly so near-identical sheets do not get mixed up in shared storage.

The goal checks one filled map; the visits were confirmed by separate nodes. Hang the map on a wall or keep it in the travel kit. For several areas, keep separate sheets and coordinate notes: a map becomes no navigator between worlds just because it closes a chapter about different worlds.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.text.0: The mirage isles are a Terralith biome in the Overworld. The node’s technical name is left over from another theme, but the goal is mirage_isles and no trip to the End is needed. Take a boat or another familiar way across water and a stock of food.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.text.1: Search for the biome with the compass from the Overworld and approach the islands. Large and small mushrooms stand among the trees, but a similar mushroom island of another type replaces no required identifier. Land on a safe shore and check the biome.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.text.2: Remember the shore for the return and look for a mooring spot. The mushrooms here grant no vanilla mushroom-field rules; this is a different biome with its own data. One visit is enough for the mark, so do not abandon the boat at sea to circle the whole island.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.title: Mirage Isles
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.text.0: Geobstractsite is a special Eternal Tales area and a useful material of the same name. The goal checks geobstractsite_biome, so an ordinary amethyst geode will not do. Take light, a pickaxe, blocks for a safe passage and mark the exit.
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.text.1: Search for the biome with the available tools in the right world, mindful of height: if the pointer leads above or below you, check the vertical instead of walking the surface endlessly. On finding an unusual formation, read the area’s name first, then decide what to take.
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.text.2: Wait for the mark and keep the way back. The material has its uses in Eternal Tales, including comet-creature mechanics, but mining it replaces no visit. Do not demolish the whole formation before learning its use: a preserved section and coordinates are worth more than a heap of unknown items.
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.title: Geobstractsite
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.text.0: The glacial chasm is a cold area with steep drops and slippery ice. Take food, building blocks and a safe way down. The goal needs glacial_chasm; a snowy plain or a frozen ocean will not do.
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.text.1: Approach the chasm and check your footing before going down. Ice slides you past the edge easily, and snow hides an awkward drop. Choose a ledge you can return from the same way, and check the biome once there.
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.text.2: Write down the coordinates of a reachable entrance, not a point on an unreachable cliff, and work out where a ladder or bridge could go without blocking the existing road. There is no need to stand in a dangerous cold block: the quest teaches terrain and navigation, not endurance to damage.
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.title: Glacial Chasm
codex.quest.more_explore.guide_cartograp: A named banner is marked on the map and shown with its label

A cartography table expands maps, copies them and locks them against changes. Craft it from two sheets of paper and four planks, make an empty map from eight sheets of paper and a compass and open it outdoors to get a filled map. Two different filled maps in the inventory satisfy the item objective; the second may be a copy or a neighbouring area.

To mark a place, name a banner on the anvil before placing it, set it down and click it with the map in hand. An icon in the banner’s colour with that label appears on the map. If the banner is removed, the marker disappears the next time you visit the area: the map remembers only what it has seen.

Expand the map on the table by adding paper until the scale covers your route; make a copy with an empty map in the lower slot. A map locked with a glass pane can no longer be drawn on, which is handy for an expedition archive. Tick the manual objective when the banner label is visible on the map itself, not only in the world.
codex.quest.more_explore.guide_desert.te: Terralith redraws deserts: among the familiar dunes you find oases with water and greenery and desert spires, tall stone pillars. Both biomes are visible from afar, yet finding them at random takes long. Take a Nature’s Compass from the conveniences map or food and water for a long day’s march and leave while it is light.

Search hot, dry regions: neighbouring Terralith biomes of the same temperature hint at the direction. Descending into an oasis, check the area name on the debug screen or in the compass: the objective counts precisely desert_oasis and desert_spires, not any picturesque corner of desert. At night the desert fills with husks, so keep a shelter or return before sunset.

The marks arrive on first entering the biome. Write down the coordinates: the oasis gives water, sugar cane and shade for a farm, and the spires make a good spot for a lookout and a waystone. Block samples are useful for building, but for the visit the book counts only your own steps.
codex.quest.more_explore.hotsprings.text: The Terralith moonlight grove lies in the Overworld; no Ad Astra rocket needed. Recognise it by blue flowers, unusual soil and amethyst details. Look for moonlight_grove; the old technical node name about hot springs is no hint.

Find the biome with Nature’s Compass and step inside. Study the details in daylight: the night tint is pretty, but threats stay. Save the entrance so you can return to the palette without another long search.

Wait for the mark and pick a few combinations for your own garden. The water here does not heal, and the grove’s name has nothing to do with the Eternal Tales moon event. The quest teaches you to tell mods’ styles apart without mixing their mechanics.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.text.0: The lavender card asks for two different biomes: the valley and the forest. Their flowers and trees look alike, but the identifiers differ, so one meadow will not close both entries. Take Nature’s Compass and note where you have been.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.text.1: Find lavender_valley first, step inside its borders and wait for the mark. Then switch the search to lavender_forest and visit the forest separately. Go by names: there is no “lavender” item, Terralith paints its landscapes from existing blocks.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.text.2: Save two points with different labels; they help when choosing a spot for a house or a flower bed. If the second entry did not trigger near the first, look for the forest variant itself: walking the valley again changes no identifier.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.title: Lavender Valley
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.text.0: The Mucunfectio abyss is a specific biome of Eternal Tales’ infection theme. The goal names mucunfectio_abyss, so the blue Mucunfectio beach or any other infected patch will not close it. Take healing, protection and a safe way down.
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.text.1: Search for the biome with dimension and height in mind and advance in small inspected sections. Meeting mutated creatures, keep room to retreat and do not mix scouting with optional combat. You need a confirmed point, not an infection trophy.
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.text.2: After the mark, note a safe entrance. Carry infection materials home only once you understand how they behave: some forms spread. No infected garden by the colony is needed; with samples and a separate site the branch can be studied without losing a convenient road to base.
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.title: Mucunfectio
