codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.text.0: The Terralith emerald peaks are cold high mountains with sparse vegetation. The goal needs emerald_peaks; the name implies no mountain of emerald ore. Take supplies and a tool, but above all plan a safe route.
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.text.1: Find the bearing with Nature’s Compass and climb the ledges, checking each slope before crossing so you do not descend by jumping off the summit. The mountains hold infested stone inclusions: idly cutting into walls adds an enemy to the dangers of height.
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.text.2: Wait for the mark and save the ledge’s coordinates. Look at the palette and the view over the valleys for future building. Mined emeralds replace no biome entry, and standing on the highest, most awkward point is not required.
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.title: Emerald Peaks
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.text.0: The Terralith volcanic crater has its own identifier, volcanic_crater, and differs from the caldera. Take blocks for little bridges, food and fire protection if you want to inspect the hot parts up close. There is no need to walk into lava.
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.text.1: Move along the outer rim, choosing firm footing and watching the inner terrain. Dark rock proves nothing; check the biome name. An accessible part of the area is enough for the mark; leave the descent to the centre for a separate, prepared expedition.
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.text.2: Note a safe approach and bypasses for a future road. A volcano provides neither electricity nor endless fuel. When taking stone for building, first make sure mining is safe, and do not spoil the one path you will carry a full inventory home along.
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.title: Volcanic Crater
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.text.0: The cloud forest on this map is Terralith’s cloud_forest, not a grove of giant redwoods. It has its own trees and bright flower clearings. Take Nature’s Compass and room in your bags for palette samples if you collect materials.
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.text.1: Approach the forest and check the biome underfoot. Dense foliage hides the view, so mark the entrance and do not circle after similar trees. On slopes, keep lit footholds and safe crossings.
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.text.2: After the mark, weigh the mix of foliage, flowers and stone without felling the landmark for a couple of blocks. No item named Redwood exists for this goal. The old name lives only in the technical identifier; the real route is set by the Russian title and the Cloud Forest biome.
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.title: Cloud Forest
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.text.0: The Terralith sakura grove is blossoming trees mixed with birches and bamboo. The goal needs the sakura_grove biome, not any vanilla cherry grove. Take Nature’s Compass, food and a tool for cutting a narrow passage.
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.text.1: Choose the exact name in the search and follow the pointer around ravines and water. On arrival, step into the grove itself and read the biome name: pink leaves next door may belong to another area.
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.text.2: A safe spot is worth remembering, and so is a look at how the local wood sits beside stone; it will serve in building. No need to fell the grove or collect a wood type. If you take saplings, keep planting stock and replant by the trail so the place stays a landmark.
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.title: Sakura Grove
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.text.0: The Terralith spring skylands are high terrain with waterfalls, pools and flowers. It is an Overworld biome; no portal needed. Prepare a controlled ascent and supplies for the way down.
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.text.1: Find skylands_spring and judge its height against your road. With elytra, leave room to land and check durability before flying. On foot, build a ladder with supports: a visible waterfall promises no convenient descent.
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.text.2: Enter the area and wait for the mark. Save the coordinates of a ledge where you can stop with luggage, not just a pretty point in the air. A sky base will need its own supply and railing solutions: a visit builds no bridges, lift or fall protection.
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.title: Skylands
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.text.0: The Terralith caldera is its own kind of mountain landscape; do not confuse it with the neighbouring quest for the Volcanic Crater. A caldera has vegetation and ordinary surface features; the name promises no lava lake. Gear up as for a mountain walk.
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.text.1: Choose caldera in Nature’s Compass and enter from an accessible slope, judging the inner terrain before descending. Check the biome name inside. A crater-like shape with a silent goal means another landscape with a similar outline.
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.text.2: Keep the approach, a viewpoint and the way home in your notes. A visit is enough; no need to break the rim or mine a special volcanic item. If you later choose this place for a base, weigh the height differences and the lighting of the inner slopes so the natural amphitheatre does not complicate every delivery.
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.title: Caldera
The Terralith painted mountains show coloured layers and steep slopes, a good place to study a building palette. The goal names painted_mountains, not a wasteland or a vanilla plateau. Take blocks for climbing, food and a free slot for a sample.

Find the biome with the compass and walk the ledges with room to spare: goats graze on the open heights, and a narrow edge is no place to stop. When mining stone, remember infested inclusions; not every block of the mountain is safe.

Wait for the mark and note a good viewpoint. Compare the colours in daylight before carrying the palette home: shadows and distance deceive. A big cut in the slope is unnecessary and only complicates the way back with loot.
codex.quest.more_explore.wasteland.title: Painted Mountains
codex.quest.more_home.bed.text.0: A bedroom and bathroom begin with the pack’s items: a red bed, two blue Handcrafted cushions and a white Refurbished Furniture bathtub. Make them by their recipes and show the book each in turn. No unloaded furniture pack is needed for this room.
codex.quest.more_home.bed.text.1: Place the bed with a path to the wake-up spot and the door. Lay the cushions in the rest area and put the tub where it blocks nobody. A tub next to pipes becomes no plumbing node of another mod.
codex.quest.more_home.bed.text.2: A bed does not work everywhere: in the Nether and the End it will not save you, so furnish the bedroom at home. The book judges no interior beauty; the result is a clear room where you can recover and pack.
codex.quest.more_home.bed.title: Bedroom and bathroom
codex.quest.more_home.garden.text.0: The garden combines three independent ways of growing: Farmer’s Delight rich soil, the Eternal Tales gardener’s pot and the Immersive Engineering cloche. You need sixteen blocks of soil and one of each device. Being neighbours gives them no shared water, fertiliser or electricity.
codex.quest.more_home.garden.text.1: Rich soil appears when organic compost matures under suitable conditions; freshly made compost is not rich_soil yet. The Eternal Tales pot lives on its own water, fertiliser and plants. The cloche needs FE, water, permitted soil and seeds by its recipe.
codex.quest.more_home.garden.text.2: Check growth or output on each plot separately, leaving an outlet for the harvest. Do not waste rare seedlings on an incompatible machine: one sample first, and planting stock to restore the garden.
codex.quest.more_home.garden.title: Garden
The dining room continues the kitchen: a table, chairs, tableware and light above them. Handcrafted makes furniture from ordinary planks: a table is three planks above two sticks, a chair is a slab, two planks and two sticks; each recipe yields two items. A wooden plate is three wooden slabs in a row, giving three.

The copper chandelier from Macaw’s Lights is crafted by the recipe in JEI and hung under the ceiling. Arrange the chairs so that each can be reached and keep the table close to the kitchen. Plates go on the table as decoration, and food can be placed on them so the table looks set.

The item goals count the quantities shown: two tables, four chairs, four plates and one chandelier. They need not be held together, and placed furniture need not be taken down. Check the lighting: the chandelier is lovely, but dark corners of the dining room still breed monsters.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_dining.title: Dining Room
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.task.3: The yard and the path to the door are lit so that no mob spawned near the house overnight
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.text.0: The yard is the first thing a guest sees and the first place monsters appear at night. The classic street lamp and the garden light from Macaw’s Lights are made from iron and glowing materials: the garden light from iron nuggets, an ingot and glowstone dust, low and good along paths; the street lamp is tall and lights a whole corner of the yard.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.text.1: The Refurbished Furniture mail box is made on that mod’s workbench from eight oak planks; through it other players can leave you items. Put the box by the gate, street lamps at the yard’s corners and by the door, garden lights along the path to the entrance and towards the workshop or colony.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.text.2: Walk the yard at night: monsters spawn where there is no light at all, so there should be no dark patches between the lamps. Make sure the lights block no path and hinder no doors. Tick the manual goal after a quiet night with not a single monster inside the lit yard.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.title: The Yard
codex.quest.more_home.hall.text.0: The trophy hall gathers the Twilight Forest trophy pedestal, the Handcrafted bear trophy and the Naga trophy. Their origins differ: a decorative head replaces no boss reward. Clear a lit passage and do not block working chests with exhibits.
codex.quest.more_home.hall.text.1: Win the Naga trophy in battle in the Twilight Forest, pick it up and show the book before placing. Get the pedestal from that mod’s available source, mindful of its role in twilight progression. Make or obtain the bear decoration through Handcrafted, checking the name.
codex.quest.more_home.hall.text.2: Place the exhibits after the marks and look at them from an ordinary walking height. No need to beat the boss again if the trophy is already registered. Label the source of each piece: that way decorative items are not confused with key trophies other adventures may need.
codex.quest.more_home.hall.title: Hall
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.task.0: Assemble an accessible Refurbished Furniture kitchen and test its furniture
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.text.0: The kitchen is built from Refurbished Furniture items, from that installed mod in particular. Choose worktops, storage and the appliance you need, leaving room in front of the doors. The manual goal checks a furnished kitchen, not a pile of similar furniture.
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.text.1: A small area next to the ingredients is enough to start. Give an appliance that needs power the Refurbished Furniture electrical system and its connections, then look at its screen. An FE cable from the industrial workshop replaces no generator of this furniture’s own.
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.text.2: Open the containers, walk through the kitchen, perform the appliance’s available action and tick the goal. Decorative cupboards need not cook. Keep dry ingredients apart from finished dishes and do not place furniture so that lunch means moving the warehouse.
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.title: Kitchen
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.text.0: The architect’s cutter and the Create schematic table serve different building preparation: the first cuts decorative blocks from chosen materials, the second works with Create schematics. Make both and place them by the store of samples, paper and building materials.
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.text.1: Cut one small element in the cutter and compare its makeup with the palette you want. At the schematic table, work with a saved Create schematic without confusing it with a Structurize file: they are different systems, and adjacent tables make them no kin.
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.text.2: Label the samples and keep the interfaces reachable. Two blocks are equipment, not a house built to a plan. A real build needs a tool or a building machine, materials and a site; the workshop orders those stages rather than removing them.
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.title: Workshop
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.text.0: Sandwiches are assembled at the crafting table from bread, cooked meat and vegetables. You need eight bacon and eight chicken ones; both batches are turned in and vanish, so you will not travel on this food afterwards.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.text.1: Bacon: bread, cooked bacon, leafy greens and tomato. Chicken: bread, cooked chicken, greens and carrot. Raw slices still need frying, and carrot in place of tomato changes the recipe; the vegetable slot is not universal.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.text.2: Make one of each, bring each batch to eight and turn in the whole set. Steady output needs its own sources of bread, greens and meat; a chest of wheat replaces no missing filling. This step pairs well with a farm and a cutting board.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.title: Sandwiches
codex.quest.more_kitchen.colony_food.tex: The colony lunch is two cheese pizzas and four MineColonies borscht; the dishes are turned in and leave your inventory. Set aside a stock for the dining hall in advance and do not take the citizens’ last food for a tick.

Make the pizza by its recipe and order borscht from the chef’s kitchen: the entry lives in crafterrecipes/chef. A Farmer’s Delight pot replaces no citizen, even if the dish is called a soup. Check the ingredients and whether the recipe is available at the colony’s current stage.

Wait for the finished items, gather the set and turn it in. If the kitchen is waiting, look at the cook’s assignment, their requests and the delivery of plants. Raw vegetables in storage are not borscht yet; this batch ties colony growth to the output of special dishes.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.text.0: Three Eternal Tales advancements check different things, though all are about food. Blueberries and the crabsburger only need to be obtained, while mutatongue chowder must be eaten. Showing the book three dishes is not enough.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.text.1: Look for blueberries on their plants in the Overworld. The crabsburger comes from the Mucunfectio crab branch; gather the ingredients by the unlocked recipe and keep trophies apart. For the chowder, make the dish first, and if fullness stops you eating, wait for hunger.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.text.2: Check the mark after each step. Food is consumed, so a rare dish is best shown to the book first and eaten after. No need to sample the mod’s random dangerous foods: this is about three named advancements that teach the difference between getting food and its effect.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.title: Food of Other Worlds
codex.quest.more_kitchen.feast_hall.text: The feast turn-in is two honey-glazed hams, two whole roast chickens and one stuffed pumpkin; all are consumed. It takes full dishes, not portions taken off a laid table.

Cook the ham by the glaze recipe and assemble the chicken from cooked meat and a side. Stuffed pumpkin is cooked in the pot from rice, onion, brown mushroom, potato, berries and a suitable vegetable, with a pumpkin as the container. Set up heat and containers before starting.

Keep everything as items and recount before the turn-in. Dishes given to the book will not appear in the hall; if you want a real feast, cook a second batch and lay it out separately, leaving the paths to the tables open.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.guide_three_cou: A dinner of salad, fried rice and pasta with meatballs demonstrates three ways of cooking in Farmer’s Delight. Mixed salad is assembled directly in the crafting grid: a bowl, any leafy green, a tomato and a beetroot. Fried rice and pasta need a cooking pot above a heat source, a furnace, campfire or stove, with bowls in its lower slot.

For fried rice put rice, an egg, a carrot and an onion into the pot. For pasta first prepare minced beef by cutting raw beef with a knife on the cutting board, cook tomato sauce from tomatoes and make raw pasta, then combine everything in the pot. JEI shows exact ingredients and portion counts for each dish.

Each dish must be held at least once as two portions at a time; gathering all three together is not required, and eating them after they were counted subtracts nothing. Hearty meals give long saturation and extra effects: read the item tooltip and take such a dinner on a long trip instead of a pile of bread.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.text.0: The pies must be whole: two apple and two chocolate. The turn-in takes all four, so do not slice them into portions beforehand. Prepare crusts and fillings, and a sample for your own table if you like.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.text.1: Apple: three wheat, three apples, two sugar and a crust. Plain chocolate: cocoa, milk, sugar and a crust; the Create integration fills a crust with five hundred millibuckets of chocolate. Pick one way and check the result.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.text.2: Keep the pies whole until the turn-in: the cutting board slices each into four, and slices replace no whole pie. If the recipe will not assemble, tell the crust from finished baking, and on the fluid route check the chocolate type and the volume in the system.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.title: Pies
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.text.0: You must turn in four each of Farmer’s Delight beef stew, chicken soup and fish stew; all three goals take the portions. You need a cooking pot with a heat source, bowls to take the dishes out and separate food for yourself.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.text.1: Beef stew is raw beef, carrot and potato. Chicken soup is raw chicken, carrot, leafy greens and a suitable vegetable. Fish stew is safe raw fish, tomato sauce and onion. Cook each recipe separately and wait for it to finish.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.text.2: Collect the portions in bowls and hold all three batches until the turn-in. A similar vanilla soup replaces no named dish. If the pot stops, check heat and containers: without a free outlet the finished food stays in the pot instead of becoming items.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.title: Three Soups
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.text.0: An autocannon needs assembled cartridges and a feed container, not the big gun’s powder bags. Make one hundred and twenty-eight autocannon_cartridge and two containers. The cartridges are turned in; the containers are counted without consumption and stay in your kit.
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.text.1: Follow the chain of the finished cartridge with its projectile and casing and check the assembled result: an intermediate part is not a cartridge yet. Start with a small run and make sure the autocannon accepts the chosen type before producing a large stock.
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.text.2: Turn in a separate hundred and twenty-eight cartridges and keep a loaded working container if you need it for trials. A container in hand means neither filled nor connected. On the range check feed orientation and the stop of fire: a long burst eats the stock fast and needs an empty zone ahead of the barrel.
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.title: Belt
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.text.0: Fuzes decide when a shell goes off: on impact, after a time, or near a block. You need eight each of impact, timed and proximity fuzes for the turn-in. Each of the three recipes yields four, so there are fewer operations than items.
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.text.1: The timed fuze is set in its own interface before use. The proximity fuze reacts to a block within the set radius; it hunts no enemy. The impact fuze fires with a probability and may stay silent on a glancing hit or ricochet.
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.text.2: The turned-in batch needs no training blast. For your own test, remember the mounting face: impact and proximity fuzes go in front and never at the base. Label the settings of working fuzes so you do not confuse delay with distance and get a surprise over your own battery.
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.title: Fuzes
codex.quest.more_munitions.guide_range.t: A test shot at a target was fired from the carriage away from buildings; nobody was behind the target or on the firing line

The range keeps cannon trials away from housing. The carriage is built from planks, a shaft and a pair of cannon wheels and can carry a small gun; a target of four hay bales and redstone dust signals a hit and shows where the shot landed. Set four targets at different distances.

Choose a firing direction towards empty land: no buildings, colony citizens or animals behind the targets and no people on the firing line. Make the first shots with few powder charges and solid shot: high-explosive and shrapnel shells on a close range tear up the ground and damage everything nearby.

Fire a test shot and find the impact by the target and the crater. Tick the manual objective once the firing line is verified and nobody was hit. Repeat shots while changing angle and charge to learn the range of a specific barrel, and write the results down: before combat firing a table beats guesswork.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.text.0: The CBC machine gun round is cheap autocannon ammunition against creatures. The quest takes sixty-four finished rounds. There is no need to build a separate weapon from another mod with a similar name.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.text.1: Recipe: a copper nugget, accepted gunpowder and an empty machine gun cartridge. Assemble and check that you got machine_gun_round itself: the empty casing is a different item and closes no counted goal.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.text.2: Set operational rounds aside if you intend to try the autocannon. No shooting at colonists or livestock is required; the check is an item check. On the range use a safe target, a suitable feed and a switch within reach.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.title: Machine Gun
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.text.0: CBC powder charges are the propellant for big guns. Turn in sixty-four; the batch vanishes and moves itself into no artillery store. Keep working charges for firing separately.
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.text.1: By the recipe a charge is assembled from packed powder and an empty casing. Make the components, then the powder_charge items themselves, without confusing them with plain gunpowder or empty bags. Before mass production, check the stock of each component.
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.text.2: Recount the charges before the turn-in. Their number in the quest is no allowed load for one barrel: the limit is set by the gun and its material. On the range use only a proven pair of shell and charge, and treat a large stock as supply for many shots, not an invitation to load it all at once.
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.title: Powder Magazine
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.text.0: The arsenal accepts eight shrapnel, eight smoke and four fluid shells; all three batches are consumed. The casings are made differently: shrapnel and fluid on the Create mechanical crafter, smoke by an ordinary shaped recipe.
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.text.1: Make one sample of each type and check the result’s name before the batch. Shrapnel hits with fragments, smoke lays a screen, the fluid casing delivers its contents. The empty fluid shell is the goal item; it is no filled round yet.
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.text.2: For a working round, pour the fluid in through the fuze face first and fit the fuze after: an installed fuze blocks filling. Water, lava and liquid potions work; an unknown fluid may do nothing. Such a filling is not tested beside your own machinery.
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.title: Shell Rack
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.text.0: Battery supply ties Create orders to the delivery of ammunition. You need a redstone requester, two cannon loaders and two Frogports. Each has its role: the request forms the batch, the port moves the package, the loader serves the cannon mechanics.
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.text.1: Set up a small order of safe material and a correct package address to test the logistics. Link the ports to the working package network and test the loader separately with a clear stroke and direction. A Frogport connects to no breech directly.
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.text.2: With the path proven, move to a controlled ammunition stock and a clear reorder condition. Do not order endlessly with the receiver busy; overflow complicates servicing. Fire cut-off and supply stop must work separately so a delay can be investigated without an unplanned shot.
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.title: Battery Supply
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.text.0: Nature’s Compass finds biomes; the Explorer’s Compass finds structures. Make both and choose a target that exists in the current dimension. The search moves no character and promises no safe road over mountains, ocean or caves.
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.text.1: Open the interface, enter the exact name and start the search. Read the distance, bearing and coordinates. Nothing? Check the dimension and the search limit: no find nearby does not yet mean the structure is absent from the pack.
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.text.2: Travel with ordinary supplies and mark the return. For biomes mind the height; for structures the real entrance, which may not match the central coordinate. Scouting succeeds when you personally reach the place and check its name or contents.
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.title: Compasses
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.task.0: Hover an enchanted item and read its enchantment description while holding Shift
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.text.0: Enchantment descriptions explain the enchantments before an expensive upgrade. Take an enchanted item or book, open your inventory and hover the enchantment name. Hold Shift to read the explanation.
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.text.1: Compare the description with the item you mean to upgrade. Weapon, mining and protection enchantments do different things, and compatibility is still governed by the game’s and the mod’s rules. The tooltip text lets you put no enchantment on any tool.
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.text.2: The manual goal is to read a description with Shift. No book on an anvil and no levels paid are needed for the tick. Then choose the upgrade deliberately and check its price separately: the hint helps decide, but the experience cost and combination limits remain.
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.title: Enchantment Descriptions
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.text.0: Building Gadgets 2 provides devices for building, exchanging and copy-paste; the template manager keeps projects. Make the kit, charge it the supported way and stock materials: copying geometry grants no free blocks.
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.text.1: With the building gadget pick a simple block and a small mode. With the exchanging gadget test one wall, inspecting the selection first. For copying, set a small area without valuable containers, save the template and check the preview before pasting.
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.text.2: Learn undo on the same example and keep the chunks loaded: the mod refuses to undo too far from the operation. Before a big project, check materials, charge and mode so an accidental exchange does not touch the neighbouring shop.
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.title: Building Gadgets 2
The destruction gadget’s area is configured and verified by removing a test wall on an empty plot

The Destruction Gadget from Building Gadgets 2 removes a whole volume of blocks in one use, the opposite of the building gadget. Recipe: iron in the corners and centre, redstone dust on top, ender pearls at the sides, lapis at the bottom. Before using it open the settings: they define the size of the removal area from the aimed point.

Set the width, height and depth of the area and aim the gadget at a surface: the preview shows exactly what will disappear. Before clicking, move chests, machines and valuable blocks out of the area: the setup is tested on an empty plot, not on the wall of your own warehouse.

On waste ground, remove a test wall with a small volume and make sure the preview matched the result; tick after that check. In town use the gadget with a reduced area and only after inspecting the preview; one wrong click erases the wall along with the neighbouring house.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.text.0: The Just Hammers iron hammer breaks several neighbouring blocks at once. Make it and pick a plain stone wall for the first try. In a tunnel the wide area saves time, but next to a complex mechanism it removes more than you meant.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.text.1: Look at the selection and strike the centre block, leaving spare durability and room for drops. Surface orientation changes how the cut goes, so test a wall and a floor separately. Hard ore obeys the hammer’s material tier like any tool.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.text.2: Check the collected blocks and the shape of the cut, then head to the mine. Do not dig blindly downwards: the wide area reveals no lava, void or someone’s build in advance. Keep an ordinary pickaxe near the base and use the hammer where the cut has already been inspected.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.title: Just Hammers
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.task.1: Open a Lootr chest, barrel and loot minecart
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.text.0: Lootr makes natural container loot separate for every player. The first advancement is to open a Lootr chest. The second, Social, needs no friend: in JSON it combines opening this mod’s chest, barrel and loot minecart.
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.text.1: Explore structures and check the container’s marking before opening. Take your loot and leave the object itself for others. A chest placed by a player becomes no Lootr container, whatever it looks like.
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.text.2: After the chest, find a barrel and a minecart of the right type and open each yourself. Check the separate marks if the joint goal stays silent. Breaking found containers is pointless: the system exists to keep independent loot available, and the advancement is about opening.
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.title: Lootr
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.text.0: The Macaw’s series adds building details with their own placement rules. You need oak roofing, a roofing hammer and a window base. Start with a small facade model: one roof sample shows the pitch and joints before a big batch of timber is spent.
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.text.1: Lay the roofing on a clear slope and shape it with the hammer. Inspect neighbouring blocks and the roof edge, then make a window section from the chosen base by its recipe. Glass nearby changes no window variant by itself.
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.text.2: Look from outside and walk through inside, keeping light and access for maintenance. Roofing a whole house is not required. Choose the palette and joint type first, then make the full batch: mixed pitches and materials give gaps and an awkward eave above the door.
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.title: The Macaw's Series
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.task.0: Choose an installed additional style while preparing a colony building
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.text.0: Style Colonies extends the MineColonies schematic set. Getting acquainted needs the build tool and access to pack selection, not a machine or electricity. Take a hut and open the preview to compare the new style with the familiar one.
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.text.1: Choose an installed additional style and inspect a suitable building on a clear site: dimensions, entrances, palette on several levels. A pack name guarantees no wood or decoration already lying in your chests.
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.text.2: The tick goes on once the new style is chosen while preparing a colony build. Rebuilding every house at once is unnecessary; one project shows whether supply can cope. Keep the variant for a future district and secure materials first, so beauty stalls no urgent housing, kitchen or defence.
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.title: Style Colonies
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.task.1: Obtain an item, fluid or energy trash can; the item version here qualifies
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.text.0: The item trash can destroys what it receives, freeing space in an automated line. Make it and test it away from the warehouse. The advancement is granted for obtaining the can; no rarity needs destroying for it.
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.text.1: Set the filter to one unwanted material and feed a few ordinary blocks. Make sure only the chosen item goes and the sample you need is refused. Do not connect general storage before this check: what is removed cannot be recovered by opening the interface.
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.text.2: After the trial, put the can only on a clearly surplus stream. The fluid and energy versions do other jobs. If the line starts losing useful items, stop the feed and check the filter rather than raising production to cover accidental deletion.
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.title: Trash Cans
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.text.0: The track coupler joins and separates trains without fully dismantling them at a station. The quest takes four devices, so keep a working one for yourself. You need a level shunting section and room for two aligned parts of a train.
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.text.1: Select a track and place the coupler beside it. The wrench switches coupling and decoupling; scrolling sets the spacing between the working pads. Bogey centres must match the marked points and carriages must face the same way; a station helps stop the train precisely.
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.text.2: Send the signal after aligning and check the result. Turned-in blocks will not return to the track. If the device complains, compare bogey positions and carriage orientation before boosting the signal or dismantling the train: the coupler wants the right geometry, not nearby bodies.
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.title: Couplers
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.task.2: Manually: test train passage and pedestrian access with the section stopped
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.text.0: A crossing reconciles the railway with people walking. You need eight track pieces and two signals, a straight visible section and a waiting spot outside the train’s clearance. Signals save no pedestrian who steps in front of a train.
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.text.1: Divide the section by the signalling rules and check each device’s direction. Run a train through the crossing, watching the track become occupied and free. Then halt traffic and test a person crossing, over the stopped section, not in front of a moving locomotive.
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.text.2: Tick after both checks. Set clear waiting markers and keep the view open. If the line runs to a timetable, remember the next train: one passage makes the crossing free for no length of time.
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.title: Crossing
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.text.0: Three schedules organise different runs, and four blue caps are the depot’s turn-in stock. Only the caps vanish on turn-in; the schedules stay as counted items. Keep the gear of working conductors separate.
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.text.1: In each schedule set existing stations with clear names and waiting conditions; a short route first, then a circular timetable. Steam ’n’ Rails conductors are made with an andesite casing and a cap as the Ponder scene shows; a stack of caps appoints no drivers.
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.text.2: Test one run and the return to service, then extend the timetables. Identical station names send a train the wrong way. The turn-in completes your contribution to the depot but checks no schedules: unloading delays, refuelling and occupied tracks show only on a live railway.
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.title: Depot
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.text.0: Steam ’n’ Rails fuel tanks are part of a train’s fluid supply. You need two tanks and a diesel smokestack for the look. The stack makes the train no FE generator and means no fuel in the tanks.
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.text.1: Include the tanks in the construct and fill them with accepted fuel, checking the fluid is supported: ordinary liquid fuels are chosen by the c:fuel tag, not by the word “diesel” in a name. A fuel interface and a coordinated stop help refuel en route.
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.text.2: Check the stock and consumption on a short run. What a train does without fuel depends on the realism mode, so promise no identical stop for every world. The goal accepts empty tanks; readiness means filled, included in the train and supplied.
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.title: Diesel
codex.quest.more_rails.guide_timetable.t: The scheduled train travelled between two stations and returned to the origin without manual control

A schedule turns a train into an automatic route between stations. Place two stations on straight sections and give them clear names; each is crafted from a railway casing and a compass, and the recipe yields two. The assembled locomotive must stand at a station to accept the schedule and depart.

Open the schedule with a right click and add instructions: “Travel to” with the first station’s name, a wait condition such as a delay, then the trip to the second. Hand the sheet to a conductor: a Blaze Burner on the train or a creature seated on a seat. Without a conductor the train stays put even with a correct schedule.

Watch a full cycle: departure, the stop at the named station and the return. If the train cannot find a station, check the spelling and a track without gaps or opposing signals. Tick the manual objective after an unattended round trip; schedules stay in the inventory and count without being handed in.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.text.0: The coal smokestack, four Locometal boiler blocks and the smokebox dress the locomotive’s body. They form no engine with a water supply; it is a look for a Create train you already understand, with bogeys and controls.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.text.1: Place the parts on one linked construct, keeping access to the cab and the luggage. Smokestack variants are chosen in the block cycle menu; the tooltip names the Open Cycle Menu key. Check the body on a curve so protrusions do not clip platforms.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.text.2: The real train is assembled at a station and tested separately: make sure every part joined the train and make a short run with a stop. A handsome boiler makes up for no missing bogey, broken track or misplaced controls; start with those.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.title: Steam Locomotive
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.text.0: A semaphore shows the signal’s state with a visible mechanical arm. Make four and mount them on poles above Train Signals. The semaphore divides no track into occupied sections and replaces no basic Create signalling.
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.text.1: One pole to begin with: the signal beneath should move the arm as a section is taken and freed. Any pole material works. On a brass signal with several exits, two semaphores say different things: the lower closes when any path is blocked, the upper when all are.
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.text.2: View the indication from the side the driver approaches from and keep it visible near curves. On an ordinary non-brass signal a pair of semaphores closes together, so a second adds no information. A finished system should clearly show the section the train is about to enter.
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.title: Semaphores
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.text.0: A beacon gives the area an effect when it stands on a mineral pyramid and its beam is unobstructed. The nether star comes from defeating the Wither. The nine iron blocks in the quest are only the first three-by-three layer.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.text.1: Put the beacon in the centre of the layer and give the beam a way up. Open the interface, choose an available effect and pay. Pyramid blocks are structure, not fuel; there is no feeding them every tick.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.text.2: Standing nearby, check that the effect appears. The first layer unlocks not all of a full pyramid’s powers and gives no second-tier Haste yet. No beam? Inspect the base and the cover above; no effect? Check the choice, the payment and the distance to the beacon.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.title: Beacon
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.text.0: Sixteen diamonds are a stock for enchanting, tools and later upgrades. Diamond ore lies in the deep layers of the Overworld; you need an iron-tier pickaxe or better. Check the tool before working a vein so it does not break halfway.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.text.1: Look at neighbouring blocks for lava, bring light and an exit. Fortune adds diamonds per block; Silk Touch keeps the ore for later processing. The goal counts the diamonds themselves, so ore brought home is not yet a batch.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.text.2: Gather sixteen at once, let the book see them, then spend to plan. Finds spent one by one never add up to this check. Do not turn everything into armour before you have an enchanting table and material for the tools you need.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.title: Diamonds
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.text.0: Elytra give gliding and rocket boosts but need open space and intact durability. The usual way to them goes through the End city ship. Gear up for the expedition and plan the return from the outer islands in advance.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.text.1: Make sixty-four rockets without firework stars: stars add an explosion that is useless in flight and dangerous. Wear the elytra in their slot, glide and try a short boost over familiar open ground.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.text.2: Check the landing, rocket consumption and durability before a long route. Losing height beside a wall is dangerous even with a full stock of boosters. Keep food and repairs handy: elytra do not mend because another stack of fuel sits in your inventory.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.title: Elytra and Rockets
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.text.0: The enchanting table takes player experience and lapis, and bookshelves raise the offers. You need the table and fifteen ordinary shelves. The table’s recipe is a book, two diamonds and four obsidian; coloured furniture from another mod replaces no working shelves.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.text.1: Arrange the shelves around the table with a one-block gap and nothing in between. Open the table with a suitable item and look at the top offer: it needs level thirty, though the operation itself takes less.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.text.2: Add lapis and choose the enchantment after reading the offer. If the level is low, first check distances and obstacles, including decoration placed in the gap, then your own experience and whether the chosen item can be enchanted at all.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.title: Enchanting Table
codex.quest.more_vanilla.guide_conduit.t: The conduit is activated under water inside a prismarine frame and grants Conduit Power

A conduit is the beacon’s underwater relative: it grants Conduit Power, which lets you breathe, see and mine quickly under water, and with a full frame it also strikes hostile sea creatures. The heart of the sea lies only in buried treasure; treasure maps come from shipwreck and ocean ruin chests. Nautilus shells drop from drowned carrying them and occasionally come from fishing.

Craft the conduit from the heart of the sea and eight shells, then build the frame: at least sixteen blocks of prismarine, prismarine bricks, dark prismarine or sea lanterns arranged in rings one block away from the conduit. Prismarine is mined in ocean monuments guarded by guardians, so stock potions of water breathing and night vision.

A working conduit opens its “eye” and surrounds itself with particles. The effect radius grows with the number of frame blocks up to a full frame of forty-two. If there is no effect, check that the conduit is surrounded by water on all sides and the frame follows the required shape. Tick the manual objective only after you have seen the Conduit Power icon.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.guide_pyramid.t: The beacon stands on a two-layer pyramid (9 + 25 blocks) with Resistance or Jump Boost selected

A beacon’s first layer unlocks only Speed and Haste. The second layer of twenty-five blocks adds Resistance and Jump Boost and extends the range to thirty blocks. The quest counts thirty-four iron blocks seen at once, the mass of both layers together; an already assembled pyramid need not be dismantled, showing the stock once is enough.

Any mineral block works: iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite, and they may be mixed within a layer. Build the pyramid squarely: a five-by-five square, a three-by-three square on top, the beacon centred on the upper one. Nothing opaque may stand above the beacon up to the sky, otherwise the beam will not emerge and no effect activates.

After building, open the beacon interface: available effects light up, and payment is accepted as an iron, gold or netherite ingot, an emerald or a diamond. Choose Resistance or Jump Boost and check the effect icon near the beacon. The third and fourth layers are needed for Strength and boosted effects, but that is the next construction.
Netherite ingots are made from scrap smelted out of the Nether’s ancient debris plus gold: four netherite scrap and four gold ingots per ingot. For a batch of four, prepare the matching stock and do not confuse the raw block with the finished part.

Mine with a suitable pickaxe, mindful of lava pockets and the way back. After smelting, gather four ingots together. Explosive mining suits only a separate site with no infrastructure of yours and a ready shelter, not the inside of your portal base.

Upgrading diamond gear needs the netherite upgrade template and a smithing table; one ingot turns no iron tool into netherite. Save or duplicate the template first, then spread the metal between the most useful items and future mod components.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.netherite.title: Netherite
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.task.1: Apply a smithing trim to any armour item
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.text.0: Armour trim changes the pattern on your gear, not its protection. You need a smithing table, a found trim template, suitable armour and a colour material. The netherite upgrade template is a different operation and gives no pattern.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.text.1: Open the table, place the template, the armour and the material, and look at the preview. Like it? Take it. The template and material are consumed, so a rare specimen is best duplicated by the available recipe first.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.text.2: The manual goal is to trim any armour piece. Wear the result or inspect it in the interface, then tick. For a full set, count templates per piece: a trimmed chestplate decorates no helmet or boots.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.title: Armor Trims
Trading turns renewable resources into emeralds and useful purchases. You need thirty-two emeralds in one batch and the Trader block from Easy Villagers. It serves the villager placed inside; an empty housing offers no deals.

Move a villager the mod’s way, give it a workstation and read the trades before the first purchase. The first trade locks the profession, so choose the specialisation in advance. Watch the stock and the refresh of offers; one batch cannot be sold forever.

The book does not take the emeralds. Split them between purchases and a reserve, and keep raw goods for sale apart. If the Trader does not show the expected profession, look at the villager itself and its past trades: moving the workstation undoes no locked trading.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.villagers.title: Trade
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.text.0: Rock-cutting wheels on a special bearing break blocks around them and put the spoil into an attached container. You need the bearing, the wheel and a container; a cutting item with nowhere to put spoil makes no boring rig.
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.text.1: Assemble the head in front of the bearing as Ponder shows and feed rotation. The wheels have their own joining rules, and the bearing reverses direction and passes a quarter of the input speed. Start with a small patch of plain stone away from the base.
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.text.2: The more blocks worked at once, the slower it goes. A full container stops mining; items are extracted through the bearing, so plan the outlet ahead. Fence the site and leave yourself a retreat from the tunnel.
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.title: Borehead
codex.quest.offroad.tires.text.0: A tyre is fitted by using it on a suitable hub, and its size changes the vehicle’s geometry. You need four regular and four sticky tyres; a sticky one is made from a regular tyre and four honey bottles.
codex.quest.offroad.tires.text.1: Shoe the frame with one set and check the clearances while turning. After a short run, fit the other set, keeping mass, speed and surface the same. That way any change in behaviour can be blamed on the tyres.
codex.quest.offroad.tires.text.2: Sticky wheels are no licence to go down any slope without brakes: grip depends on contact and the whole construct. The goal counts items in your inventory, so show the regular set before converting it to sticky. A stock of both kinds serves repairs and different routes.
codex.quest.offroad.tires.title: Tires
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.text.0: The first wheeled vehicle joins a physical frame, hubs with tyres, a rotation source and clear controls. The directional switch from the goal picks the drive direction but replaces no whole car. Assemble the units on flat, clear ground.
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.text.1: The switch has two command sides: one passes rotation, the other reverses it; with no signal or both at once the output stops. Check that on a shaft before connecting wheels. Set up steering and braking separately, then assemble the body with the physics assembler.
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.text.2: Make a short run, a turn and a stop without cargo. If it will not move, check the engine, the switch commands and the hub brakes in turn. Do not rush to the hills: inertia, wheel clearances and mass distribution are tested on a simple route you can step off easily.
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.title: First Vehicle
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.text.0: The hub attaches a wheel to a ground-based physical machine and accepts brake and steering commands. Four hubs begin a four-wheel frame, but without tyres, a drive and physics assembly it is not yet a car. Prepare a light rectangular platform.
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.text.1: Arrange the hubs along the sides of the body and leave room for wheels. A signal from above brakes; a side signal steers towards the signal. Test both reactions on one unit before wiring all four.
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.text.2: Do not run the same wiring to the top and side inputs: steering and braking are different actions, and a machine that will not move is often just braked all the time. Make sure every hub is reachable, then fit the tyres. On the first rig, low speed and level ground.
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.title: Wheel Mount
codex.quest.radar.controllers.text.0: The yaw and pitch controllers turn the gun towards the selected network target. The fire controller emits a signal when the linked mount is on target; it checks neither the gun’s condition nor its charge. Take the three devices and a fully unloaded gun.
codex.quest.radar.controllers.text.1: The yaw controller goes under the mount and is tied in with data links; set up the pitch controller as Ponder shows. Pick a known safe point on the monitor. Route the fire controller’s output to a lamp first so you can watch the permission without a shot.
codex.quest.radar.controllers.text.2: Check turns in both directions and the return after a target change. If an axis moves the wrong way, fix orientation and settings before ammunition goes in. A ready signal means aimed, not a clear range. Keep a manual fire inhibit that does not depend on the data network.
codex.quest.radar.controllers.title: Targeting Controllers
codex.quest.radar.datalink.text.0: The data link connects radar components to the monitor. It is neither a power cable nor Create’s wireless redstone. You need the link device, a monitor and an assembled radar; keep weapons disconnected for now.
codex.quest.radar.datalink.text.1: Place the monitor somewhere convenient and link it to the radar following the Data Link hints. Open the link settings and check the selected nodes. A wider network uses a separate Network Controller, which holds filters and connects other components.
codex.quest.radar.datalink.text.2: Find a known mark on the monitor and compare it with the object’s position in the world. Check an empty screen in order: assembly, link, filters. Red links belong to the weapon network, blue to the radar network, and the two must not be mixed.
codex.quest.radar.datalink.title: Data Link
codex.quest.radar.guidance.text.0: The guided fuze belongs to a special homing round and must be compatible with your radar system. Make it together with the warning receiver and the transponder; the three items do not assemble a guided shell by themselves.
codex.quest.radar.guidance.text.1: Get a stable target mark and check identification on an unloaded rig. In the recipe and tooltip of the chosen round, find where the fuze mounts and which network link is required. An ordinary shell does not become guided by standing next to a radar.
codex.quest.radar.guidance.text.2: The first trial is a single shot at a distant training target with the flight area surveyed. Watch how the system behaves when the mark is lost, and only then repeat. The receiver merely reports detection and the transponder works through filters; neither protects against a badly configured weapon.
codex.quest.radar.guidance.title: Shell Guidance
codex.quest.radar.guide_fire_inhibit.tas: Manually verify the switch blocks the final firing signal while aiming continues, using a lamp and no ammunition
codex.quest.radar.guide_fire_inhibit.tex: Automatic aiming is easier to service when firing can be inhibited independently of target selection. Prepare a separate switch and a lamp in place of the mount’s firing input. Do not begin with a loaded gun.

Separate aiming from the final firing permission. With permission disabled, change the training target: axes should keep tracking while the firing-input signal remains blocked. Test readiness with permission enabled using only the lamp.

Tick the goal once you can stop fire without dismantling the network or losing observation. Label the switch and keep it reachable outside the gun’s sector. After any rewiring, repeat the short check: a neighbouring signal bypassing the inhibit makes the familiar lever useless while it still looks fine.
Manually exclude your own code from automatic targeting while confirming selection of a permitted training target without ammunition

A transponder does not prevent friendly selection unless its code is excluded. Prepare a friendly physical construct and a separate training object. Keep every linked gun unloaded and temporarily route firing output to a lamp.

Assign a known transponder code and configure its identification filter in the Network Controller. Verify that your own object is excluded from automatic selection while the permitted training target remains available. Do not confuse category exclusion with a specific identification code.

Tick the goal once you have seen both results. Then change the training copy’s code, understand why the behaviour changed and restore the safe configuration. All of this comes before an automatic fire sector: an accidentally invisible object and a correctly identified friendly one look the same at a glance.
codex.quest.radar.iff.text.0: An identification transponder gives a physical construct a name and a code. Automatic targeting excludes it only when the code matches the identification filter in the network controller. Make the transponder and the warning receiver; keep ammunition apart.
codex.quest.radar.iff.text.1: Install the transponder on a Sable physics construct; on an ordinary machine block it does nothing. Set the code and enter it in your radar network’s filter. Then check the object’s mark and make sure auto-targeting no longer selects it. A matching name without the right code replaces no setup.
codex.quest.radar.iff.text.2: The receiver sounds when you are inside radar coverage and when you are locked on, but it does not prevent the lock. Test both sounds with a friendly observer and no fire. Against someone else’s network, where your code is not on the exclusion list, there is no protection.
codex.quest.radar.iff.title: Friend or Foe
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.text.0: The binoculars point guns tied to the network controller at a chosen spot and suit aiming checks without automatic mark selection. You need the binoculars, a working Network Controller and a fully unloaded mount.
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.text.1: Sneak and use the binoculars on the controller to bind them. Then zoom in and hold the left button while pointing at a safe spot. Connected guns follow the bearing according to the network settings.
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.text.2: Walk through several range points and see how the system releases control. Do not point the training setup at a base walkway even with no intention to fire: someone may have left ammunition in a connected gun. If a cannon does not respond, check the bound controller, weapon links and axes rather than the binocular zoom.
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.title: Manual targeting
codex.quest.radar.plate.text.0: Radar plates are part of the antenna and widen coverage. Make eight and find a clear spot above the roof or beside the workshop. Plates in a chest do nothing for the radar: they must become part of the assembled antenna.
codex.quest.radar.plate.text.1: Mount them on a linked frame that will later sit on the radar bearing with the receiver. Dishes and plates are interchangeable in the antenna; check the geometry against Ponder and leave room to rotate.
codex.quest.radar.plate.text.2: The number eight promises no particular range; configuration and network settings decide that. After start-up, compare how a known object shows with and without the extra plates. Keep the mechanism reachable and do not wall the antenna in by accident.
codex.quest.radar.plate.title: Radar Plates
codex.quest.radar.radar.text.0: The radar receiver on its special bearing turns detection into a working unit. You need both devices from the goals, an antenna and a source of rotation. An ordinary windmill bearing will not do here.
codex.quest.radar.radar.text.1: Place the radar bearing, then the receiver and the linked plates or dishes as in the Ponder scene. Feed rotation and check the assembly. The next step connects a monitor that shows what the radar sees.
codex.quest.radar.radar.text.2: Observe without any weapon connected, using a known object. If there is no mark, the cause may be the target type, position, settings or link rather than antenna area alone. Not every moving block is a supported target. Pin down one radar’s working setup before joining several stations into a network.
codex.quest.radar.radar.title: Radar
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.autocrafter.tex: The autocrafter stores patterns and makes them available for orders. An ordinary recipe needs only the network and materials; for processing it hands ingredients out to an external inventory. Make the device and prepare one already recorded simple pattern.

Connect the autocrafter and insert the pattern. Through the grid, order a small batch, review the material calculation and start the task. Make sure the item appeared in the network before adding dozens of recipes.

For a machine pattern the autocrafter's working side matters: it must face the machine's input or an intermediate buffer. Return the machine's output with an importer or another proven feed. If the ingredients left and the order hangs, do not insert a second pattern blindly. First find where the expected product physically lies and check its exact quantity.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.big_project.tex: The advanced processor needs two stages: assembling the blank and smelting it. Eight pieces call for diamonds, silicon, redstone and processor bindings, or working patterns for the intermediate materials. Recording the finished processor as one ordinary recipe will not work.

Record the recipe for the raw blank and a separate processing pattern for the furnace. Route the blanks into the correct input, give the furnace fuel and return the product to the network. Then order eight processors through the grid and watch both stages.

Check the result against the monitor and the network stock. If the book already counted eight processors earlier, there is no need to collect them again for a tick; the new batch tests the chain itself. An old mark and a working return are different things: the furnace must hand the order back by itself, with no carrying by hand.
A nested recipe frees you from preparing bindings by hand: the network makes them from raw material itself when processors are ordered. Prepare string, slime and a blank pattern. First check the ordinary recipe: two string and one slimeball give eight bindings, and that output count in the pattern matters.

Record the craft and put it into an available autocrafter. Order sixteen bindings and compare the calculation with the input stock. A correct pattern takes two runs of the recipe, not sixteen slimeballs.

If the maximum is not yet recorded, obtain sixteen identical bindings together; small outputs do not add up to such a stock. Then spend the bindings on processors without building a needless reserve. A proven nested recipe becomes the base of a long chain where the network calculates intermediate materials itself.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.guide_return_fa: Manually locate the monitor’s expected product while return is stopped, restore import and finish the same task

An order can hang with a perfectly good furnace if the finished product does not return to the network. For the exercise take a cheap process with a known output and an importer that is easy to switch off. Leave alone any recipe serving an important shared order.

Temporarily stop the return, run a small batch and open the monitor. Find the expected result and confirm it really lies in the machine's output. Restore the import and wait for the same task to finish without a new order.

Tick the objective once the cause is found and the task closed on its own. Do not cancel the order as a first move: that way it is easy to miss that the network was waiting for an item already made. If the product returned but the wait remains, check the type, properties and output count in the pattern. This exercise teaches you to tell a logistics error from a calculation error.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.guide_stock_lim: Manually verify export stops at the configured limit and resumes after consumption to restore the same stock

An exporter with autocrafting will keep filling the receiver as long as there is raw material. The regulator limits the amount of a chosen resource in the target inventory. Prepare the upgrade and a small chest with one consumable the network already knows how to make.

Set the regulator to the item and a small limit, then put it into a supported exporter together with the autocrafting upgrade. Wait for the fill and make sure new items stopped arriving. Take some out and check that the stock recovers to the same level.

Tick the manual objective after the stop and the refill. If production does not stop, check that the target chest itself is being regulated and that the filter matches. A big chest does not set a sensible stock by itself. Such a node is good for repair parts; the remaining raw material stays for other orders.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.task.0: Manually request crafting from JEI through the grid and verify the result appears in the network
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.text.0: The JEI integration carries a familiar recipe into a network order and shows what is missing. It does not turn any recipe opened in JEI into a pattern. You need a working grid and a simple resource the network can genuinely make.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.text.1: Open the recipe in JEI from the grid window and use the transfer or order action. Look at the calculation before starting: a missing ingredient may need its own pattern or a restock. Wait for completion and for the result to appear in the network.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.text.2: Tick the manual objective after a real order, not after viewing the recipe. If the button is absent, check the grid type, the integration and whether a pattern is recorded. Do not repeat the request endlessly: first find out whether the first order is stuck waiting for an external machine.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.title: JEI Integration
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.text.0: The autocrafter manager gathers every pattern in one window and helps maintain a workshop that has grown. Place it after the first working order. Recipes get no faster from it, and the blocks holding patterns are still needed.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.text.1: Connect the manager to the network and find a familiar recipe by output, input or autocrafter name. Give devices clear names, especially when several serve identical furnaces. If an autocrafter does not show up, check its visibility setting.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.text.2: For duplicate recipes compare priorities: the network prefers the pattern from the autocrafter with the higher one. Do not delete entries at random during an active order. Finish or deliberately stop the task, fix one entry and repeat a small trial; that way a large recipe list grows without surprises.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.title: Pattern Manager
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.monitor_craft.t: The autocrafting monitor shows the state of orders and helps tell two hitches apart: the network is waiting for ingredients, or it is waiting for a result from a machine. Put it on the same network where a simple pattern already works, and learn on a small order without expensive materials.

Start the recipe and open the monitor while the task runs. See what is required and what is expected, then find the same state in the machine itself. Raw material that vanished from the network may well already lie in an external buffer.

Cancelling a task does not bring items back from other inventories by itself. Before reordering, look into the furnace, the input and the output so you do not double the batch. If the result does not return, fix the physical feed or the pattern's expected output. The monitor helps with diagnosis, but it will not unblock the machine for you.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.pattern_grid.te: The pattern grid records a recipe onto a special item that the autocrafter later reads. Make the device and eight blank patterns, and connect the grid to a powered network. Pick a simple, unambiguous first recipe, say planks from a log.

In crafting mode lay out the ingredients, specify the result and record the pattern. A furnace or another external machine needs processing mode: on the left, what the network will send; on the right, exactly what must come back. The grid does not perform the processing itself.

Do not record a random result as guaranteed without an extra setup. Check the output count and allowed substitutions, especially for items with special data. The finished pattern goes into the autocrafter in the next quest. Assemble a complex recipe by hand first and make sure you recorded the result of your own pack.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.processor_line_: The trial batch pushes several processors through the line at once. Set aside materials for eight advanced ones and look at the preliminary calculation. If something is short, add exactly that material rather than rewriting every pattern at once.

Order through the grid and watch the blanks, the furnace and the return. The importer must take finished processors, not pull raw material out of the input. On completion the output stock grows by exactly the amount ordered.

For the item objective it is enough to show eight identical processors together once; small batches do not add up to such a stock. If that maximum is already recorded, no need to show it again, and the Codex takes no items. What proves this particular line is watching it work, not a tick that processors made long ago could have earned.
Manually request eight processors, check missing materials, replenish supplies and receive all eight outputs back into the network

Acceptance of the line must include a material shortage and a correct finish after restocking. Prepare the network interface, the monitor and free room for finished processors. Keep part of the missing ingredient outside the network so the test stays under control.

Order eight processors from the network interface. Check the list of what is missing; after restocking the order should finish and return all eight. If the interface will not start an order while short, study the calculation first, restock and then confirm the order.

Tick it after checking in the world; the Codex does not watch the furnace for you. Watch the external furnace as well; after the task ends the result must not wait for your hand. If it hangs, check fuel, the import side and the exact output description, and keep the blanks instead of relaunching at random.

The processor line links the autocrafter, the furnace and the return to the network. The objective asks for an autocrafter and an importer; devices already counted will do, there is no need to obtain new ones for the score. Prepare a furnace, cable and a separate fuel feed.

Put the patterns for the raw advanced processor and its smelting into the autocrafter. Route blanks into the furnace input and place the importer against the side where finished goods are taken. Fuel must not land in the same slot as raw material.

Run one processor through from diamond, silicon, redstone and a binding. Blank made but no smelting: look at fuel and the input. Smelting done but the order waiting: look for the product at the output. Parts in place do not yet mean the cycle is closed; the trial batch and a separate check will show that.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.upgrade_craft.t: With the autocrafting upgrade a device orders a missing resource by pattern on its own: an exporter, interface or constructor that needs a steady material. Install it only after that resource has been ordered by hand at least once.

Insert the upgrade into a supported device and set the wanted item in the filter. Start with a small receiving chest and cap the stock with a regulator or a suitably sized container. Remove a little of the resource and watch an order being born.

The upgrade will not invent a missing recipe and does not know a sensible ceiling without the other settings. Endless export into a huge chest eats all of the network's raw material. Make sure production stops at the set amount and resumes after consumption. If an order hangs, look for the usual causes through the monitor: materials, power, access to the machine, return of the result.
The wireless monitor shows and cancels orders without making you walk back to the stationary screen. It uses the network's coverage and its own charge. Charge the item and bind it to the right network.

Start a small order near base, open the pocket monitor and compare it with the ordinary one. Then step away to your usual working distance and check whether the link holds. Coverage depends on transmitters and upgrades, not on how many recipes are recorded.

Cancel an order knowing what happens to external machines: ingredients already sent may stay in the furnace or buffer. A drained device is not a stopped network. Keep the stationary monitor and a charging source in place. The item shines on a long factory where the fault is visible at one end and the autocrafter stands at the other.
codex.quest.rs_network.blocks_storage.te: A storage block combines space and connection in one device: it needs no disk drive. Make the 1k variant and find it a place on the cable run. It suits a small network, where a separate drive would take up needless room for now.

Connect the block to power and insert a small known batch through the grid. Watch how the fill level changes, then take the same items back out. If the network has other storage, remember priority: the items may have gone there.

Before moving the block, learn how it keeps its contents, and preferably empty the training piece. A closed grid window does not mean the block is empty. Block and disk forms solve the same task but expand and are serviced differently. After the trial, pick whichever is easier to place, and leave spare room for incoming production.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.text.0: Cable ties devices into one network, and a relay controls a whole branch. Make sixteen cables and one relay. Lay the first run from the controller to the future grid short and in plain view, without hiding it under the floor.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.text.1: Place the relay at the border of a separate branch and check its direction and mode. In the simple pass-through mode it carries the whole network; finer settings choose what exactly to pass on: storage, energy, security, patterns. Until there is a specific reason, do not complicate the filtering.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.text.2: Switch one branch off and bring it back without losing access to the main part. If the grid is powered but empty, the relay may not be passing storage through. Missing energy and missing permission are different troubles. Cable itself stores nothing; space arrives in the next quest together with disks.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.title: Cables and Relay
The constructor places selected blocks from the network straight into the world; the destructor breaks suitable blocks in front of it and returns the drops. Make both and set aside some dirt or stone. Pick a test site away from important machines.

Connect the constructor, set the material and watch its working side on a free spot. Test the destructor separately, on a single block placed for the purpose. If the drops need limiting, set up a filter and check that storage has room for the result.

Do not point the destructor at an expensive mechanism without knowing what it drops: the loot may differ from the block placed. A constructor and destructor next to each other can shuffle one patch endlessly and burn energy. Add a clear enable signal and look at the result before trusting them with a farm or a self-repairing wall.
codex.quest.rs_network.constructor.title: Constructor and Destructor
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.text.0: The controller is the heart of the network: it distributes energy to every Refined Storage device. A block placed on the floor will not bring the grid or the storage to life on its own; it needs a steady FE source. One controller is enough for a first network, and the old rule of strictly one per network no longer applies in the second version.
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.text.1: Connect power, lay a short run of cable and attach the first devices. Open the controller and compare the energy reserve with consumption. As the network grows, consumption rises, especially after disks and upgrades.
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.text.2: If everything goes dark, look first at energy and at the connection to the source. A chest full of materials nearby will not replace the current. Keep the controller in plain sight and do not move your whole storeroom until you are sure items go in and come out. Then power can be restored without hunting for a part inside a network that is switched off.
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.title: Controller
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.text.0: The disk drive provides slots for disks, and everything stored lives on the disks themselves. First make a housing and show it to the book, then turn that same housing into a 1k disk: a spare one for the sake of a tick is not needed. Prepare the drive as well. An empty housing joins a storage part in the disk recipe but holds nothing by itself.
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.text.1: Connect the drive to a powered network and insert the disk. Once the grid appears, put in a few cheap items and look at the fill level. A drive without disks provides no space.
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.text.2: A removed disk takes access to its contents with it, so label your media and store them carefully. A disk can be taken apart into components only when it is empty: unload everything first and confirm the fill level is zero. The objective checks three items, not writing to the medium. For the first move of your storeroom, take a small batch that is easy to count.
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.title: Disk Drive and Disks
codex.quest.rs_network.external.text.0: External storage opens the contents of a neighbouring chest, tank or other compatible inventory to the network. Items stay where they were rather than being copied onto a disk. Make the adapter and prepare a small chest with known contents.
codex.quest.rs_network.external.text.1: Place the device with its working side against the container, run a cable to it and look in the grid. If your storeroom needs limits, set allowed resources, mode and priority. One container should not be attached to the network by two independent routes without a clear reason.
codex.quest.rs_network.external.text.2: The disk interface from the second objective does a different job: it moves resources between inserted disks and the network in the chosen direction. For the first trial, take a separate medium with cheap contents and make sure there is enough room. Attaching someone's chest and migrating a disk are different operations, and both show in how the real stock changes.
codex.quest.rs_network.external.title: External Storage
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.text.0: The grid shows the shared list of resources, and through it you put items in and take them out. The crafting variant adds an ordinary crafting square right in the window. Make both; show the basic grid to the book before turning it into the upgraded one.
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.text.1: Connect the grid to a powered network that already has a disk or external storage. Put in a stack of stone, find it with the search and take part of it out. In the crafting grid, assemble a simple recipe from what the network holds.
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.text.2: An empty list more often means no storage, a display filter, a switched-off relay or missing permissions rather than lost items.
