codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.text.2: Compare the chest and inventory before confirming the manual objective. A learned gesture should make supplies easier to manage rather than leave you guessing where a stack went. Inspect the result especially carefully in filters, upgrade slots and automated installations.
codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.title: Mouse Tweaks
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.task.0: Identify slowdown conditions and test one setting
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.text.0: Smooth play is made of many things. A large render distance loads the image output, running mechanisms demand computation, and scouting new land adds chunk generation. First understand during which action the lag appears.
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.text.1: Compare standing quietly at the base with moving into the unexplored. Change one parameter at a time — distance, complex effects, far-landscape settings — and check the result under similar conditions, or a chance quiet moment is easily taken for a fix.
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.text.2: Tick the goal after reading and one meaningful check. Do not switch off unfamiliar mods mid-playthrough for the sake of an experiment: some of them are dependencies of game systems. If a particular factory lags, look for piled-up items, unfinished transports and the size of the permanently loaded area.
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.title: Performance
Check that working supplies are stored in containers
Smart Item Deleter monitors dropped items and cleans them up according to the pack’s rules. The floor is therefore not reliable storage: even a neatly gathered pile remains a collection of item entities outside a container.

Move supplies into chests, barrels or other storage after gathering them. Give automated lines an output destination and spare capacity so an overflowing exit does not continually spill items onto the ground. If a pile grows beside a machine, fix transport and storage rather than merely collecting the overflow.

Mark this reference after reading and inspecting your work area. Do not test cleanup by dropping valuables and waiting for deletion. Exact timing and exceptions depend on settings; the useful rule is to place supplies in their intended storage.
codex.quest.start_qol.smartdeleter.title: Smart Item Deleter
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.task.0: Test tree felling and inspect the active TreeChop mode
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.text.0: TreeChop changes how trees are felled: several hits on the trunk gradually prepare the whole tree to fall. The amount of work depends on the tree and the settings, so do not expect any giant to topple from a single swing.
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.text.1: Find an ordinary tree well away from buildings and take an axe. In TreeChop’s settings look at the chopping mode, felling and the behaviour while sneaking. Chop the trunk, watching the indicator and the axe’s durability; when you need a single block, switch to the ordinary mode.
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.text.2: Gather the fallen wood and see what is left standing. Tick the goal after the trial. Next to wooden houses it is especially important to remember the current mode: mass felling is convenient, but it will not choose the block for you. Plant saplings so that the next forest grows close by.
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.title: TreeChop
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.task.0: Inspect voice chat settings and microphone muting
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.text.0: Simple Voice Chat lets you talk to other players by voice if it is set up and enabled on the server. On a shared build that is handy: a partner explains which block to place while you look at the blueprint rather than at the chat line.
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.text.1: Find the voice chat menu in the controls, choose input and output devices and check the volume. Set up the push-to-talk key or the chosen transmission mode. A client-side mod in the list does not yet mean voice works on the server.
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.text.2: For this reference goal it is enough to explore the menu and find how to mute the microphone. A second player and a live transmission are not required. Before playing together, briefly check audibility and the channel with the others so as not to discuss a work task with the wrong group.
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.title: Voice Chat
Modules turn the backpack into a small travelling workshop. Auto-smelting cooks suitable items on its own fuel, the crafting module gives a crafting square, and compacting presses resources into compact blocks. Prepare the three upgrades and a backpack with free module slots.

Install them one at a time and try each on a small stock. For smelting set the input and fuel, then check the product. For compacting look at the available recipe sizes and the filter so you do not compress a material you need piece by piece.

The crafting module does not craft everything by itself; each upgrade has its own rules and compatibility. After setup, close the backpack, open it again and make sure the stock and modes are as intended. On a long expedition take separate fuel and leave room for the processed result, or the portable machine stops when it fills up.
codex.quest.storage_local.backpack_filte: The filter module decides what logistics may put into the backpack and take out of it. The void module destroys selected things, and the deposit module unloads them into a chosen inventory. Make all three, but install only the filter and deposit first.

On a cheap mix, check the allowed inputs and outputs. To unload, sneak and click the chosen chest, then compare what remains on each side. The module must not send your working tools off together with the ore.

Set up the void last and only for strictly chosen junk. Before enabling it, remove everything valuable from the training backpack: deletion is irreversible. The logistics filter does not always override the auto-pickup settings of other modules, so test each route separately, especially if you later connect the backpack to pipes or a machine storeroom.
codex.quest.storage_local.backpack_tiers: A new backpack tier adds room for items and for modules. The objective wants the iron and gold variants, and they can be shown in turn: first the iron one, then the same backpack after upgrading to gold.

Before upgrading, look inside and note the installed modules. The standard recipe keeps the contents, but the first time is best done with a small cheap load and a check of the result. Upgrading the old backpack and crafting a new empty one are different recipes.

After the switch, count the slots and check the settings of active modules: capacity grew, while pickup filters and upgrade limits stayed the same. There is no need to carry two backpacks for two objectives; the iron one is already in the history. From here choose the tier by the size of your usual expedition load and the price of materials.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.text.0: A Mekanism bin holds a mountain of one item: cobblestone, wood or other bulk material that overflows chests. Make a basic bin and prepare a small batch of identical items for setup.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.text.1: Place the block, insert the chosen material and check manual extraction. If an emptied bin must not accept something else, lock its assignment. Its window tells the exact locking method and the capacity.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.text.2: One bin for a mix of every ore is a poor idea: its strength lies in a single kind. For an automated line set a filter and decide in advance what happens when it fills. A tier upgrade changes capacity, not the assignment. After the check, the bin can be handed to the external network, with the resource label visible and extraction still reachable.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.title: Mekanism Bins
codex.quest.storage_local.everlasting.te: The everlasting upgrade protects the backpack itself as an item: it does not burn, despawn or vanish into the void, by the module's rules. Prepare the upgrade and a backpack with a free slot. It does not make the owner invulnerable.

Install the module and check that it is active in the backpack window and that the tooltip describes the expected protection. Do not test it by throwing your only valuable backpack into lava: getting it back is a separate task.

The module does not carry the backpack to a safe chest and does not open a path to the place of death. On an expedition you still need death coordinates, a spare kit and a free slot for the recovered load. The protection belongs to the backpack with the upgrade installed, not to a container standing nearby.
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_bin_assi: Manually verify an emptied configured bin rejects another resource and accepts its assigned material again

An emptied buffer can accept a foreign resource and upset the usual feed. Take a bin with the chosen bulk material and a little of some other item for the test. This storage has a setting that keeps its assignment.
Fill the bin with the first resource, lock the assignment and empty it. Try feeding the second resource, then the first again. The assignment must survive emptying and the correct feed must resume.

Tick the objective after both trials. If the foreign resource got through, fix the lock or add a precise external filter before connecting a shared line. What matters is the result in your version, not the padlock icon. This protection pays off at a cobblestone generator and in the material stock for autocrafting.
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_bulk_net: Manually verify grid insertion fills the chosen external buffer, extraction returns resources, and full-buffer behavior is tested

Bulk raw material is best kept in a separate buffer, leaving disks for the mixed haul. Prepare a configured bin or Create vault, Refined Storage external storage and a small known stock. Do not move the whole storeroom at once.

Connect the buffer and set the priority and a precise filter. Insert the material through the grid and watch where the fill level grew: in the external buffer, not on yet another disk. Then withdraw part of it and compare the remainder.

Tick the objective once the route works both ways. Decide in advance what to do when the buffer fills, redirect elsewhere or stop the input, and test the setting on a cheap batch. Two blocks standing side by side settle nothing; a clear priority does.
Keep Bulk Stock in External Storage
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_deposit_: Manually verify selected loot deposits, the tool stays, and a full chest causes no item loss

Coming back from the mine is nicer when the backpack unloads the haul itself and keeps what the next trip needs. Prepare the deposit module, an empty chest and a training set: some stone, ore and one cheap tool. Disable the void module for the exercise.

Set the deposit filter to what may be unloaded, sneak and click the chest. Compare both sides: the haul should land in the receiver and the tool should stay in the backpack. Repeat with a full receiver and make sure nothing is lost.

Tick the objective after correct sorting and a safe stop. If the tool left, fix the deposit filter itself, not the neighbouring upgrades. This routine separates your personal kit from the shared storeroom and saves you from setting out on the next expedition without a pickaxe.
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_void_fil: Manually delete only the selected cheap material, retain the control and verify deletion stops when disabled

The void module belongs only where the junk is known exactly. Empty the training backpack of anything valuable and put in two different cheap materials: name one as junk and keep the other as a control.

Create a narrow deletion filter for the first material only and enable the module. The selected material should vanish, the control should stay. Then disable the module and make sure a new portion of the junk no longer disappears.

Tick the objective after both states. What was deleted does not return when the module is off, so the trial must contain nothing valuable. Do not set a broad criterion such as a whole mod when a single stone needs removing. Repeat the check after every new module: auto-pickup can bring things under the filter that were never in the backpack before.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.text.0: A MineColonies rack is part of the colony's warehouse system, not just another chest. Make one and first study it as an ordinary container. A network adapter will not replace courier logistics and citizens' requests.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.text.1: Place the rack and check how a small batch goes in and comes out. If it belongs to a working colony warehouse, leave access for the workers and respect the building's rules. For Refined Storage, separately confirm that the installed rack exposes a compatible inventory.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.text.2: Try reading and withdrawing on cheap goods without draining all the citizens' supplies through the network. An item visible in the grid does not mean the colony stopped needing it. Separate personal resources and working stock into clear containers. The objective checks the rack itself, not the friendship of two supply systems.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.title: Colony Racks
codex.quest.storage_local.vault_create.t: The Create vault gives a large buffer for production items even before a digital network. Prepare eight blocks and hoppers or another way in and out. It cannot be opened by hand like a chest, so an output is needed from the start.
Assemble a valid shape, make sure the blocks merged, and load a small known batch through logistics. Then unload it into an ordinary chest. Not every cluster of touching blocks counts as one vault.

Later, Refined Storage external storage can open this inventory to the whole network; the items stay inside the buffer. Watch filters and priority so a stray mix does not take all the room. Before connecting automation, make sure the test batch both survived and came back: eight blocks in hand do not yet make a storeroom.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.task.0: Grow the colony population to 50 citizens
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.text.0: Fifty citizens call for steady supply, not a couple of extra houses. Prepare the mystical site and grow the population while watching housing, research and the colony’s current limits. This building is part of the town project, but by itself adds no citizens and cancels none of the other conditions.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.text.1: Expand housing as food, workplaces and deliveries keep pace. Check for the unemployed, unfilled requests and the distances between districts. If the colony has hit its population cap, look for the growth condition in its interfaces instead of ordering identical houses in the hope of getting around the limit.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.text.2: Wait for the personal advancement for 50 citizens and register the mystical site block before building it; the book does not spend it. After the milestone, estimate the food reserve for the next construction cycle: the final town hall will demand time and materials, and the grown town will keep eating every day.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.title: Fifty
codex.quest.story_colony.found.text.0: A settlement begins with three buildings: the town hall, the builder’s hut and a house. Prepare their MineColonies blocks and the build tool. A hut block is an application for construction; the building itself is raised by the assigned builder from whatever materials they request.
codex.quest.story_colony.found.text.1: Place the town hall and outline the territory, then choose blueprints for the builder and the housing to suit the terrain. Order construction, hand out tools and answer the requests. Do not set projects side by side without viewing their full size: building zones can overlap even when the hut blocks stand far apart.
codex.quest.story_colony.found.text.2: The book remembers every block it has seen before placement, so the settlement you have started will not need demolishing. See the first orders through and check who works where. The card’s name is not a population counter: the goal here is three finished buildings from which a managed colony begins.
codex.quest.story_colony.found.title: Establish a Settlement
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.task.1: Form a colony army of eight soldiers
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.text.0: The garrison turns the first posts into a real military unit. Prepare the barracks and develop military positions until eight soldiers are in the ranks. The advancement counts the size of the army; a raid or a victory over anyone in particular is not required for it.
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.text.1: Place the barracks with the buildings tied to it in the chosen blueprint, order the construction and assign people. For each unit check weapons, armour, food and access to roads. Citizens in other jobs will not become soldiers because a handsome building appeared nearby.
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.text.2: Place the barracks after registering the block. Wait for the eight-soldier advancement in your personal MineColonies tree, then walk the routes to the settlement’s vulnerable entrances. The book judges no tactics and promises no repelled raid: the headcount milestone is a reason to test the defence for real.
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.title: Garrison
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.text.0: The first defenders must cover the real approaches to the colony. Prepare two guard towers and the rally banner for guards. Place the towers so that the guards can walk out to the roads and houses, and not end up behind their own wall with no ladder.
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.text.1: Order the construction, assign guards and issue weapons, armour and food through supply. Walk the guards’ patrol routes on an ordinary day. The banner is for rallying the guards to one spot, but merely having it in the bag creates no army and fills no empty posts.
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.text.2: Show the two towers together before placing them; the banner can be registered later. Nothing is handed in. Both posts should be ready before night or a raid, and expand the defence to match the settlement’s area: two towers will not cover a distant warehouse or farm.
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.title: First Night Under Guard
codex.quest.story_colony.guide_food_chai: The dining hall cooks from colony produce and the warehouse keeps a food reserve

The book took the bread from the previous quest, yet citizens keep eating every day. As long as you carry the food, the colony depends on your trips. Three buildings settle the matter: the farm grows wheat and vegetables, the fisher's hut brings fish, and the bakery bakes bread from the farm's grain. All three huts are made as ordinary colony blocks through the build tool and need no research.

The farm needs fields that you place nearby and assign to the farmer; the fisher needs water close to the hut. The baker takes wheat from the warehouse, so the chain starts working only after the courier begins carrying the harvest. The cook in the dining hall prepares raw produce and hands meals to hungry citizens.

The huts can be placed right after registration. The objective is the moment the cook works with what the colony grew while the warehouse holds a reserve rather than the last loaf. If citizens complain of hunger with a full warehouse, check that the dining hall is built and has a worker assigned.
A guard trained at a training ground has been assigned to a post

Barracks give numbers, not skill. The archery range and the combat academy teach citizens shooting and melee so that posts are taken by more than recruits. Both buildings are locked behind research: in the university's combat branch, after Tactic Training come Improved Bows for the archery and Improved Swords for the academy. Each requires a level-three barracks and six iron blocks.

Order the research early: the university works slowly, and the barracks must reach level three in time. Then place both buildings through the build tool and assign trainees. Training runs during working hours, and a trained citizen is afterwards moved to guard duty on a tower or in the barracks.

The huts can be placed right after the book registers them. The objective is a trained guard standing at a post. If a building does not appear in the list, check that the research is finished, not merely paid for.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.text.0: The industrial district means a smeltery, a blacksmith and a mechanic’s workshop. Prepare their blocks and decide which real requests of the colony they will cover. Three buildings side by side make no chain: every worker needs raw material, tools and the right recipes.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.text.1: Build and start the workshops one at a time. Give the smeltery materials for its processes, hand the blacksmith the recipes for the needed items, and the mechanic the orders allowed for that profession. Look at each building’s interface: a colony worker will not learn any recipe of another mod just because of the profession’s name.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.text.2: Place the huts right after they are counted. For your own check, follow one order from the moment the request appears to the finished item leaving the warehouse. If a worker stands idle, look for the missing resource or recipe: a second identical workshop will not make up for what the first does not know.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.title: Smithy and Mechanic
codex.quest.story_colony.network.text.0: Shared access to the warehouse is convenient as long as it does not get in the couriers’ way. Prepare two Refined Storage external storages and a grid; the controller, power and cables are needed separately. Connecting to an inventory does not yet mean the network sees the entire contents of the multi-block warehouse at once.
codex.quest.story_colony.network.text.1: Connect one warehouse inventory first and find a few familiar items in the grid. Set the external storage’s modes and priorities so that things do not chase each other in circles between import and export. Add the second connection after checking the first, and never connect the same contents twice.
codex.quest.story_colony.network.text.2: Show both external storages together; register the grid separately and place it. Whether the link-up worked is best shown by a courier’s delivery after connecting. Items in the search are only a joy when the colony still receives its building materials and food.
codex.quest.story_colony.network.title: Warehouse on the Network
codex.quest.story_colony.population.task: Grow the colony population to 25 citizens
codex.quest.story_colony.population.text: Twenty-five citizens are a milestone of real growth, not a stockpile of house blocks. Add housing, keep up the food and everything else settlement needs. Prepare a hospital at the same time: a growing population needs a place to be treated, not only new orders.

Order upgrades one at a time and watch the colony’s limits, research and the citizens’ requests. Build the hospital and get it running to the current staffing requirements. A hospital block in the bag closes the item entry, but heals no one and shortens no queue to a doctor who is not there.

The advancement must register a population of at least 25 for your character. Place the hospital block after it is counted; no spare needed. When both entries are closed, weigh the load on the warehouse and the food: growth unlocks schooling and industry, but also eats more every day.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.text.0: The school district divides knowledge between the library, the school and the university. Prepare the three huts. They are not interchangeable decorations: the university unlocks research, while the school and the library raise citizens by their own rules and assignments.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.text.1: Build the buildings, look into their interfaces and provide the requested materials. In the university choose research aimed at whatever is holding the colony back now, and check the required building levels and resources before starting. Tie the school and the library to a real need to train citizens — skills will not appear by themselves once the block is placed.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.text.2: The book counts each item separately, so you can build in stages. How much research is finished, this card does not count. Check the first available research and the assignment of teachers — that is a clear foundation for the town’s growth and for the far more demanding industrial district.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.title: University
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.text.0: The warehouse exists so that the builder and everyone else get materials without your personal deliveries. Prepare the warehouse, courier and restaurant huts, and separately 64 bread for turn-in. The restaurant block feeds nobody until the building is built and the kitchen supplied.
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.text.1: Order the buildings, assign workers and put whatever you have into the warehouse. Watch the courier’s and the cook’s real requests — tools, food, passable roads. Follow one delivery to a construction site and one meal before considering the supply settled.
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.text.2: The huts can be placed after registration. The bread, though, must be in your inventory as a full stack at turn-in, and the book will take it — it does not go to the restaurant. So keep the colony’s rations separate: the reward replaces neither the citizens’ daily food nor the materials for the current build.
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.title: Warehouse and Bread
codex.quest.story_colony.technopolis.tas: Complete construction of a level-five town hall
codex.quest.story_colony.technopolis.tex: Technopolis closes the town line with a level-5 town hall and the turn-in of eight ultimate control circuits from Mekanism. These are two different checks: a finished MineColonies build and a stock of top-tier electronics. A town hall block in the bag and a finished town hall are different things.

Order the town hall upgrades in sequence, keeping the builder stocked with tools and the full list of materials. Make sure the couriers do not carry the kitchen’s last resources off to the site. Assemble the circuits from a calm factory surplus without pulling control components out of running machines.

When construction ends, the personal level-5 town hall advancement appears. All eight circuits must be in your inventory at turn-in and will go. The final mark cancels none of the town’s needs: after a big build, check food, defence and the warehouse so that the technopolis keeps living at its usual pace.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.text.0: Wood and stone give the colony its own building materials. Prepare the lumberjack, sawmill, miner and stonemason huts. These are four different roles: a gatherer brings raw material, and a craftsman processes it by known recipes and current requests — nothing comes out of thin air.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.text.1: Build the workplaces where they are easy to reach and give every citizen a tool of the right level. The lumberjack needs trees nearby, the miner room to deepen the mine, the craftsmen raw material and recipes. Follow a delivery through the warehouse before opening many construction orders at once.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.text.2: Each block is registered and placed separately; no spare huts are needed for the book. Four huts in the bag are not yet a flow of planks and stone. Follow at least one request from the builder through to finished material: that link matters more than the number of handsome workshops.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.title: Forest and Stone
codex.quest.story_current.alternator.tex: The alternator from Create Crafts & Additions hands mechanical power to electrical machines. Prepare two alternators and a rolling mill. This is the second generation branch after steel: the IE dynamo is not required, but a working Create rotation source already is.

Connect the first alternator to the shaft and see how much headroom the source has left before hanging the second one. Send the current through suitable electrical connections into a store or a consumer. The mill is useful for wire and other add-on parts; its input and output also land on the common load.

Show both alternators together, then place them; register the mill separately. The book does not count output — make sure current reaches the receiver. If the shaft stops, look for an overloaded source; if shafts turn but there is no current, check the connections and the side settings.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.text.0: Smoke over the coke oven is the first sign that the electrical story has begun. The book asks for 64 Immersive Engineering coal coke. That is a stock of ready fuel and nothing more: whether the oven runs without pause and whether a proper blast furnace stands nearby, it cannot tell.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.text.1: Load coal into the assembled coke oven and watch both outputs — solid coke and liquid creosote. Empty the internal tank, or full creosote will halt processing. Feed your own steel smelting first, then set aside a stack for the book.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.text.2: At turn-in all 64 coke must be in your inventory and will go. Plain Minecraft coal will not replace coke, though it burns in other furnaces. After handing it in, look at the remaining coal and the free room for creosote: the next step starts two metallurgical chains at once.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.title: Smoke Over the Coke Oven
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.task.7: Form the diesel generator and verify energy transfer into storage
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.text.0: Diesel keeps the grid on liquid fuel that can be stored. The IE generator is built from multiblock construction blocks — it never exists as a ready-made item in survival. Gather the listed parts and, separately, sixteen buckets of biodiesel, without taking fuel out of the base’s only reserve.
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.text.1: Assemble the generator by the Engineer’s Manual and form it with the hammer. Oil from the squeezer and ethanol from the fermenter become biodiesel in the refinery, with saltpeter as the catalyst. Bring in the fuel and lead the current into a store with room to spare; a full tank alone does not start the engine.
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.text.2: Materials can be shown before construction, but the sixteen full buckets are handed in together and go entirely, containers included. Tick the manual goal after you have seen the generator run and the receiver’s charge grow. If it stays silent, check fuel, electrical output and control before tearing down the housing.
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.title: Diesel
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.text.0: Immersive Engineering’s kinetic dynamo turns the rotation of the mod’s own water wheel or windmill into current. You need the dynamo, a low-voltage capacitor and four low-voltage connectors. A Create wheel will not do as a drive, however similar it looks.
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.text.1: Build the IE drive at the working side of the dynamo and get it turning. Lead the current through low-voltage connections into the capacitor, and set its sides for input and output with the engineer’s hammer. One consumer is enough for the first trial — that way the path of the energy is visible.
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.text.2: Place parts as soon as they are registered; show the connectors as a set of four. A rising charge in the capacitor proves generation, not a tick in the book. Keep wires off the walkways and cover the reachable stretches before running the grid across the yard.
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.title: First Current
codex.quest.story_current.fission.text.0: A fission reactor forgives neither unfinished cooling nor waste with nowhere to go. A logic adapter, four turbine rotors and four spare fuel assemblies are only a small part of the project. The reactor’s shape, the turbine’s output and the safety of the chosen burn rate the book cannot judge from these items.
codex.quest.story_current.fission.text.1: First assemble and test the reactor, the coolant loop, the steam path and the coolant return, then arrange the removal of radioactive waste. Set up an emergency shutdown and begin at the lowest safe setting. Watch temperature and damage; radiation work needs a full protective suit, and full pipes and tanks must never be taken apart carelessly.
codex.quest.story_current.fission.text.2: Place the adapter and rotors after registration. The four spare assemblies must be in your inventory for turn-in and will go — do not pull them out of a running reactor. At the slightest instability stop the burn and keep the cooling; forcing the trial with more power is not an option.
codex.quest.story_current.fission.title: Heart of the Base
codex.quest.story_current.grid.text.0: A single grid carries current from generators to consumers, but IE connectors remember the class of their wire. An ordinary transformer joins a low-voltage line to a medium-voltage one, so what is needed here is medium-voltage electrum wire, not high-voltage steel.
codex.quest.story_current.grid.text.1: Prepare a transformer, four coils of electrum wire and a basic Mekanism energy cube. Build the crossover between suitable connectors and set the cube’s sides for input and output. Connect the cube through a supported energy connection — an IE wire nailed to any face of it will not work.
codex.quest.story_current.grid.text.2: Register and place the parts one at a time; show the four coils of one kind together. First make sure the cube charges from your source and one consumer runs. As the grid grows, keep access for disconnecting it and never mix high-voltage wire with an ordinary transformer.
codex.quest.story_current.grid.title: One Grid
codex.quest.story_current.guide_backup_h: With the main source stopped, the storage still receives energy from the backup generator

A dynamo stops with its water wheel, and a diesel generator with its last bucket of fuel. For such moments you need a reserve that depends on neither rotation nor biodiesel. The Mekanism heat generator draws energy from lava and burnable items: lava can be poured into its tank, and lava blocks adjacent to the casing add heat to the output. In the Nether it yields noticeably more.

Place the generator next to the basic energy cube and join them with four universal cables, which carry energy between Mekanism machines and other mods' equipment. Show the four lava buckets together; the book does not consume them, but they go into the tank. One heat generator will not replace diesel, so its job is to keep the storage charged and power what matters most: lighting, pumps and defences.

For the objective, stop the main source and watch the cube's charge grow from the reserve. The generator and cables can be installed right after registration. Decide in advance which consumers stay on the reserve and separate them from the rest of the workshop with a breaker.
The breaker de-energised the section: consumers stopped and the storage behind it stopped charging

One grid is fine until it needs repairs. A breaker switch joins two wires of the same class and passes current only when switched on; it cannot be installed on a high-voltage line. A current transformer sits in any line and counts the energy that passed through it, while the engineer's multimeter shows how much charge is stored in the storage block or machine you click.

Put the breaker between generation and a hungry workshop, and the current transformer on the same line. Clicking the transformer reports average throughput; a comparator at its base gives a signal from zero to fifteen according to wire load. A switched-on breaker also emits a redstone signal, and the engineer's screwdriver inverts that behaviour. High voltage calls for the redstone breaker: an applied signal opens it, and it cannot be toggled by hand.

For the objective, switch the breaker off and confirm that the machines behind it stopped while the multimeter shows their storage no longer charging. The instruments can be placed after the book registers them. Such a cut-off point spares you from tearing down wires every time the workshop is rebuilt.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.text.0: Mekanism’s chemical processing squeezes more out of ore than a furnace, though the word “fivefold” promises no identical yield for every form of iron. Prepare a chemical dissolution chamber and a crystallizer, then trace the whole recipe of your chosen raw material through to iron crystals.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.text.1: The dissolution chamber runs on sulfuric acid and produces dirty slurry; the chemical washer cleans it with water, and only then does the crystallizer yield crystals. Between the stages you need their own reagents, power and free outputs. A straight pipe between the two machines named in the goal will not replace the washer.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.text.2: The book remembers the equipment before installation, but the 64 iron crystals must be handed in at once — they will go. Run a trial on a small batch and check the yield of your own recipe. The remaining crystals become ingots through Mekanism’s usual purification chain.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.title: Fivefold Ore
codex.quest.story_current.steel.text.0: Two steels are two ways to get almost the same thing. You need 32 Immersive Engineering steel ingots and 32 from Mekanism. Many recipes accept them through shared tags, but this turn-in tells the items apart precisely and demands both kinds.
codex.quest.story_current.steel.text.1: In IE, iron with suitable fuel goes through the blast furnace and comes out as steel and slag. In Mekanism, iron takes on carbon in the metallurgic infuser, becomes enriched iron, then steel dust, and only then an ingot. Give each chain its own chest so the origin of the ingots is obvious at a glance.
codex.quest.story_current.steel.text.2: Bring both batches together: the turn-in takes all 64 ingots and does not remember halves shown earlier. Keep some steel for the casings of your own machines. Next comes generation: IE’s kinetic dynamo or an alternator spun by a Create shaft.
codex.quest.story_current.steel.title: Steel of Two Houses
Obtain the Royal Banner after defeating Xaxxas XIX
The Kingdom of Amber leads through local events to Xaxxas XIX. This is no trip for rare ingots: the card needs a visit to the world and the trophy of its ruler. Before crossing, prepare the continuation of the story and restore your supplies after Volcanech.

Go through the dialogues and the required halls of the kingdom, remembering the way through rooms already explored. If progress stalls, return to the current errand rather than looking for a random fight in place of the story condition. For the final encounter free up room for the Royal Banner and check the durability of your gear.

After the victory take the banner into your inventory — it is what triggers the Xaxxas XIX advancement in the installed version. The book does not take the trophy; at home it can go on the wall right after registration. Check your character’s condition and gather the story items before the last crossing to Unahzaal.
codex.quest.story_expedition.amber.title: Amber
codex.quest.story_expedition.comets.task: Obtain the Comet Banner after defeating Terrible Tree
codex.quest.story_expedition.comets.text: The Comets open the long Eternal Tales line after two independent journeys. Prepare access to this dimension through its own chapter and the mod’s advancements: the Aether or Twilight Forest portal does not lead there. Bring durability to spare and leave room for story loot.

Settle the nearest safe area and find the Terrible Tree stage in the local progression. Before the serious encounter, mark the way to the portal and do not stash needed things in random chests. Victory ends with collecting the trophy: look over the ground after the fight instead of running for the book’s reward.

This needs a visit to the Comets and the advancement that the installed version grants for the Comet Banner in your inventory. Pick up the banner yourself before hanging it at home or handing it to a friend. It is not consumed; with it this stretch is closed, and ahead lies preparation for Purgatorium.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.text.0: The Twilight Forest teaches you to take bosses in order. The portal is a small pool framed by flowers and grass by the mod’s rules; a diamond thrown in opens the way. On the other side, memorise the exit and bring food for several encounters in a row, not for a short stroll.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.text.1: First find the Naga’s courtyard and close her stage, then go to the Lich’s tower: the protection of the next area depends on the previous victory. In the Lich’s first phase, reflect his projectiles back at the real boss to strip his shields, and waste no strength on his copies.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.text.2: The book needs a visit to the forest and both trophies — the Naga’s and the Lich’s. Show them one after another, then hang them at home without worry; no second pair is needed. If the tower is still sealed, look at the mod’s own advancements: the ticks in this book do not override the dimension’s rules.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.title: Twilight
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.task.1: Complete the quest to free the Altar of the Sun from Eternal Dawn
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.text.0: Eden is unlike the earlier trophy stops: here you must complete a story errand, not bring a banner. Visit the Gardens of Eden and find D’Kuji’s line about the Altar of the Sun. Read the local dialogue to the end before heading to the appointed meeting — that way you will know who to bring the result to.
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.text.1: The errand is to free the Altar of the Sun from the Eternal Dawn. Prepare gear for that event and go through the quest in full, including the continuation of the conversation after the fight. A single victory without finishing the story dialogue will not yet grant the mark: it is issued by the Eternal Tales quest logic.
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.text.2: When it is done, check the “Drink of the Sun” advancement. The book records the visit to the dimension separately, but does not substitute it for the story condition and does not take the drink itself. From here the road forks into Rayana and Karvat — prepare each as a separate expedition.
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.title: Eden
codex.quest.story_expedition.guide_magic: The filled magic map shows at least three different forest landmarks

The Twilight Forest hides towers, labyrinths and boss courtyards among identical trees, and scouting on foot eats evenings. The magic map solves this: it paints biomes and marks landmark icons within its radius. The focus needs a raven feather, torchberries from the forest caves and glowstone dust; the map itself is made from the focus and eight sheets of paper.

The map works only inside the forest; in another world the magic falters, and the mod says so plainly. Unfold it, walk a little so the area fills in, and compare icons with what you see: the Naga courtyard, the Lich tower, the labyrinth. This way you choose the boss order in advance and do not run into a protected area without the required stage.

An important accounting detail: the objective asks for a blank magic map, and after first use the item turns into a filled map with a different identifier. Show the book the blank map before unfolding it. The focus can be registered separately. The objective is three different landmarks on the filled map.
codex.quest.story_expedition.guide_wayst: Three named waystones stand in different places and travel between them has been tested

A single home waystone brings you back from a trip, but it does not shorten the road to the mine, the portal or the colony. A network of several stones turns the map into a list of stops. A waystone is crafted from three stone bricks, three obsidian and a warp stone in the centre, and the warp stone from four amethyst shards, four ender pearls and an emerald. A warp scroll takes an ink sac, an ender pearl, four gold nuggets and three paper, three scrolls at once.

Place stones where you go most often, activate each with a click and give it a clear name. The stone's menu lists every activated point; a trip may cost experience, and a warp scroll carries you to any known stone and vanishes after use. The return scroll from the expedition kit leads to the nearest stone, so put stones near distant exits too.

Show the three stones together in your inventory, then place them. For the objective, walk a chain of trips between all three and make sure the names in the list are distinguishable. An unactivated stone never appears in the list, however long it has been standing.
codex.quest.story_expedition.karvat.text: Karvat holds three marks at once: Enicrih, Arla and Ikkorh. Prepare for a long expedition with trips home for repairs, not for one set of supplies covering every encounter. Check the order of access and the story conditions against the local Eternal Tales line.

Visit the Lands of Karvat and push through the required events, keeping the loot of every closed stretch. After each victory pick up the matching banner: the three advancements have different items. One trophy will not stand in for the other two, even if the fights look alike and take place in the same world.

Check all three marks in the book and the registered visit to Karvat. The banners are taken one after another and then stay at home: there is no turn-in here. When both Karvat and Rayana are closed, the road leads to Volcanech — gather the story materials of both branches before the new crossing.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.text.0: A travel kit is for coming back, not just for a quick way out of the gate. Prepare a Waystones waystone, two return scrolls and a red Comforts sleeping bag. The colour matters here: a bag of another colour works in the game but does not match this goal.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.text.1: Activate your home waystone and check where the scroll really leads before any dangerous crossing. Leave food and repair materials at the return point. The sleeping bag is fine for a night in a quiet spot, but it makes no foreign dimension safe and does not replace your ordinary respawn point.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.text.2: All items stay with you: show the two scrolls together, the rest as convenient. Before setting out, read the tooltips of your means of travel and mind the limits of the current world. If the way back is still untested, make a short trip nearby first and keep the second scroll for the expedition itself.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.title: Kit
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.task.1: Obtain the Purgatory Banner after defeating Nyetet
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.text.0: Purgatorium continues the Eternal Tales story and calls for separate preparations. Before leaving the Comets, repair your gear and stow story materials somewhere safe. The order of the cards sets the reading route, while the real entrance to Purgatorium is opened by the mod’s own mechanisms.
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.text.1: Inside, find a safe landmark for the return and follow the local line to Nyetet, the Fallen Guardian. Study the approach to the arena before the fight begins: unfamiliar terrain and no line of retreat are more dangerous than a few extra minutes of scouting. On a shared expedition, agree in advance who picks up the trophy.
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.text.2: Completion needs a visit to Purgatorium and its banner, for which the mod grants the Nyetet advancement. The item must pass through your inventory: someone else’s collection on a wall does not count as your victory. The banner stays with you, and the next stop is the story errand of Eden.
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.title: Purgatorium
codex.quest.story_expedition.rayana.task: Obtain the Rayana Banner after defeating Pterion
codex.quest.story_expedition.rayana.text: Rayana is one of the two roads after Eden. Prepare its own crossing and supplies for scouting: an unlocked card does not mean the portal already stands. Do not spend all of Eden’s loot until you have checked the recipes and story requirements of the road ahead.

On arrival, mark the exit and find the Pterion stage in Rayana’s progression. Pick positions with a view and tested footing, especially when you have to chase the enemy. Before the fight, free up room for one specific trophy — the Banner of Rayana, by which the mod counts the victory.

Completion is a visit to Rayana and the advancement for its banner. Pick it up into your personal inventory before it flies off to the base automatically; the book does not spend it. The onward crossing also needs Karvat, so restock and go through the neighbouring branch in full.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.text.0: The first stop in the sky is the Aether and its bronze dungeon. An Aether portal is built from glowstone and lit with water; bring blocks and something against falling. The islands do not form solid ground, and every sideways step here is chosen with care.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.text.1: After crossing, secure a safe platform for the return and find the bronze dungeon. Its master, the Slider, is made of stone and must be hit with what breaks stone; the habit of swinging a sword will not work here. Keep room to dodge and do not leave needed loot in an unreachable part of the structure.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.text.2: The quest checks a visit to the Aether and the bronze dungeon key. Take the key into your inventory before you open the reward chest with it: the book will remember the item and will not ask for a spare. Then compare this straightforward fight with the boss order of the Twilight Forest.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.title: Sky
codex.quest.story_expedition.unahzaal.re: The expedition is over. Another game begins
codex.quest.story_expedition.unahzaal.ta: Defeat Unahzaal and earn the Eternal Tales finale advancement
codex.quest.story_expedition.unahzaal.te: The last crossing leads into the Unahzaal Multiverse and completes the main Eternal Tales line. Finding a decorative block of the world or bringing a similar trophy is not enough here: the card checks a visit to the dimension and the final-victory advancement issued by the mod’s event logic.

Before entering, check your gear, your means of recovery and supplies for a second attempt. Leave everything needed for repeat access in a safe place and understand in advance how you will return after a failure. Starting the final stage with leftover food and a nearly broken weapon is a bad idea.

See the encounter with Unahzaal through, wait for the events to finish and check your personal advancement. The special Eternal Darkness mode is not needed for this card. No loot is consumed, so the reward can be claimed calmly once you are out of danger and back with your expedition collection.
codex.quest.story_expedition.volcanech.t: Volcanech joins the results of Rayana and Karvat and leads to Arahulum. Make sure both branches are closed in the book, and prepare the real crossing by Eternal Tales. Keep the story rewards of earlier worlds apart from raw materials that go into production on their own.

Once in Volcanech, secure the way back first and get to know the nearest piece of the local story. Before the decisive fight restore armour and weapons and check your protection against the local environment. Do not judge the dangers by the dimension’s name — the terrain and the enemies define them.

Completion needs a visit to the world and the Arahulum advancement, which the mod grants for his banner in your inventory. Pick up the trophy yourself after the victory and wait for the mark to update. The banner remains yours, and ahead lies the Kingdom of Amber, which you will reach with the fruits of the whole story so far.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.text.0: A steam boiler gives rotation for a real workshop, but its power rests on several conditions at once. Gather four steam engines, sixteen fluid tanks and four blaze burners. This is a set of parts, not a promise of a particular boiler level.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.text.1: Arrange the tanks into a valid shape, give them a constant supply of water and heat from below. Mount the engines so that rotation reaches a shaft, and watch the boiler’s readout. A shortage of water is not cured by an extra burner, nor a shortage of heat by a bigger tank.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.text.2: Show each batch before installing it; different parts can be registered one after another. Then test the boiler under load, including power for the pump at start-up. If the water comes from the boiler itself, plan the first start: an empty boiler will not pump its own water.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.title: Steam Power Section
codex.quest.story_forge.guide_belt_sorti: Two different items from one belt each end up in their own chest

As soon as ingots and slag travel the belt mixed, you need sorting. A brass funnel is crafted from a brass ingot, an electron tube and dried kelp; a brass tunnel from two ingots, a tube and two kelp. A filter is made from two iron nuggets and wool and stores a list of allowed items.

Place two chests with brass funnels at the end of the belt and give each funnel its own filter: the slot accepts a prepared filter with a list or simply the item itself. A brass tunnel above the belt splits the flow between neighbouring belts and also accepts a filter on each side, so a single junction can send two kinds of cargo in different directions without extra funnels.

The test is simple: send two different items along the belt and make sure each landed in its own chest and nothing jammed at the entrance. Every part can be placed right after the book registers it. If a funnel takes everything, open its filter slot: an empty slot means no restriction at all.
codex.quest.story_forge.guide_signal_blo: A train stopped before an occupied block and proceeded once it cleared

A second train on the line already calls for signals. A signal is crafted from a railway casing and an electron tube, four at a time; the first line rewarded you with exactly such a set. A track observer is made from a casing and a wooden pressure plate and emits a redstone signal while a train passes over it.

Signals are placed in pairs on both sides of the track and divide it into blocks: a train will not enter a block occupied by another train but waits for it to leave. Put two signals before the loading station and check that a carriage left on the block really stops an approaching train. The observer is useful for nearby automation: it can open gates or start a belt while the train rolls past.

The objective calls for observation, not just parts: a train must stop at the signal before an occupied block and move on once it clears. Signals and the observer can be placed as soon as they are registered. If a train ignores the signal, check that both signals stand on the same stretch and face the right way.
codex.quest.story_forge.guide_stress_aud: The stressometer shows spare capacity with every machine of the smelting row connected

The millstone, crushing wheels and fans of the smelting row usually share one shaft, and every new machine takes a share of its capacity. You have owned a stressometer since the start of the road; a speedometer is crafted from a compass and an andesite casing and shows the rotation speed of the chosen section. Together they show the free stress headroom and the speed at the farthest machine.

Place the stressometer on the shaft next to the source and the speedometer at the last consumer. Connect machines one at a time and watch the needle: an overstressed network does not slow down, it stops completely. Stress grows with speed, so speeding up through cogwheels makes every machine hungrier. Two gearboxes made from a casing and four cogwheels carry rotation around a corner without a long chain of cogs.

The objective is complete when, with the last machine connected, the stressometer shows headroom rather than the red zone. Instruments and gearboxes can be placed as soon as the book registers them. If there is no headroom, add a second source to the same shaft or move some machines to a separate shaft with its own drive.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.text.0: It all begins with a hand on the crank. Before you own a windmill or a wheel, the hand crank shows the essential thing: a Create machine needs rotation, and rotation travels along a shaft. For the first trial a crank, a mechanical press and a dozen iron ingots for sheets will do.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.text.1: Run a shaft from the crank to the press, put an ingot on a depot under its head and turn the handle. The press must come all the way down, and the ingot must become an iron sheet. Repeat until you have ten, keeping the finished sheets apart from the raw metal.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.text.2: The crank and the press can be placed as soon as the book has seen them; nothing needs taking apart. Show the ten sheets together: the book remembers the largest count of one item, not the sum of small batches. After this, wind or water will replace your hand — the choice is yours.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.title: Hand on the Crank
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.text.0: The millstone is the simplest way to get something edible out of a working shaft. The book’s order is 32 Create wheat flour. Grown wheat becomes an ingredient for a future kitchen; this batch you hand over to the book.
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.text.1: Place the millstone, connect rotation and load a little wheat. Make sure the flour comes out and is easy to collect before pouring in the whole harvest. Keep seeds for the next sowing and some grain for plain bread until the kitchen is built.
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.text.2: At turn-in all 32 flour must be in your inventory and will be consumed; the millstone itself is not handed over. The millstone is a full replacement for crushing wheels on the way to the fans, so the expensive brass assembly can wait until there is a real need.
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.title: Mill: a batch of flour
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.text.0: The precision mechanism is the first part that cannot be made by hand. The book expects eight finished Create mechanisms. Stock up on gold sheets and consumables generously: sequenced assembly sometimes yields scrap instead of the part you wanted.
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.text.1: One cycle is deployers placing in turn a small cogwheel, a large cogwheel and an iron nugget, and the gold sheet passes through this chain five times. Arrange the return of unfinished mechanisms to the input and the sorting-out of finished ones. Five mechanical crafters have nothing to do with it: what matters is the order of operations and the number of repeats.
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.text.2: Hand in the eight mechanisms at once from your inventory; the batch will go. How automated the line is, the book cannot see, so watch at least one full pass yourself without carrying the workpiece by hand. That skill will come in handy again when trains and controls come up.
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.title: Precision Line
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.text.0: A railway begins with a route, not with painting the locomotive. Prepare 64 Create track pieces and two stations — one for the base, one for the mine. That stock may not cover any distance you like, so walk the terrain first and estimate the real length of the line.
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.text.1: Lay a continuous track between the two sites, leaving level stretches for stations and loading. Make curves with the track-laying tool and check every joint. Give the stations distinct, meaningful names: the schedule will refer to them, and two identical names turn troubleshooting into torment.
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.text.2: Show the full stack of track and both stations before placing them; after that they are yours to use. Whether the line is passable, the kit will not tell you — walk it end to end. Decide in advance how the train will return: around a loop or in reverse with controls.
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.title: First Line
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.task.2: View the encased fan Ponder scene and airflow-processing methods
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.text.0: The encased fan turns a stream of air into a tool: air that has passed through lava smelts whatever rides past. You need two fans, eight belt connectors and the fan’s Ponder scene watched. Lava merely standing next to the machine smelts nothing — what matters is the stream through it.
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.text.1: Choose the direction of the stream, put lava in its path and run a belt with items through the working zone. Start with one material that has a bulk smelting recipe. Shield the lava from accidental contact and make sure the result reaches the output chest.
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.text.2: The book counts parts and the Ponder scene, not smelting speed. Place the fans straight away; show the connectors as one batch of eight. Give a test item time in the stream: a belt that is too fast will carry it away half-smelted.
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.title: Smelting Row
codex.quest.story_forge.source.text.0: The stressometer turns a spinning windmill into an understandable number — spare power. Make the gauge and put it on the same shaft that drives the press. A separate shaft off to the side will show somebody else’s network and say nothing about yours.
codex.quest.story_forge.source.text.1: Take a reading first with processing switched off, then start the press and compare. Engineer’s goggles read Create values right where you stand. If the network stalls, disconnect consumers one at a time and find which machine or extra speed-up overloaded it.
codex.quest.story_forge.source.text.2: The book remembers the stressometer as an ordinary item; a mounted gauge need not come down. Judge the headroom by the needle, not by the tick in the book. Next, choose: millstone or crushing wheels, both roads lead to processing, and the water check remains an alternative entrance.
codex.quest.story_forge.source.title: Source Found
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.text.0: The wheels are turning — now find out how much they can bear. One stressometer on the shared shaft of the water network shows how every new machine moves the needle. If you already own the gauge, use it: the book does not demand a separate one per branch.
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.text.1: Mount the meter where the wheel and the future processing form one network. Switch on the first consumer and watch the load. If everything stops, check the water flow and the drive directions first, and only then speed and the number of machines.
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.text.2: This optional card confirms the water entrance into processing; there is no need to go through the windmill for the sake of a millstone. Keep a little power in reserve for transport: a press that stalled together with the whole network after the first belt is a sorry sight.
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.title: Source Found
codex.quest.story_forge.train.reward.0: The first achievement that moves by itself
codex.quest.story_forge.train.task.4: Manually: the train completed a round trip and transferred cargo through the interfaces
codex.quest.story_forge.train.text.0: The engineer’s road ends not with a train but with a trip. Gather the train controls, a schedule, a blue conductor’s cap and a pair of portable storage interfaces. The cap will not drive the train by itself: the driver is whoever you assign by the rules of Create and the railway add-on.
codex.quest.story_forge.train.text.1: Assemble the train at a station, check that it runs both ways and set a two-stop schedule. At each site align the interfaces so that a stopped train can exchange items with the base. Send a cheap load on the first trip and leave room in the receiving storage.
codex.quest.story_forge.train.text.2: Register the parts one by one and install them. Tick the manual goal only after a full trip with loading and unloading through the interfaces. If the train came back empty, look for the cause in the stop, the interface alignment and the wait conditions — motion alone does not count as haulage.
codex.quest.story_forge.train.title: A Train That Doesn't Wait
codex.quest.story_forge.water.text.0: Water is the second perpetual engine of a first workshop. You need two large Create water wheels and a place where the flow can be directed. A puddle next to the wheel gives nothing: the water must strike the paddles at the right point.
codex.quest.story_forge.water.text.1: Place one wheel first and get it turning steadily, then add the second and join the shafts, checking the directions. Clear spills off the walkways and leave access to the connection point so that later gears need not be mounted blindly through water.
codex.quest.story_forge.water.text.2: Show both wheels to the book together before placing them; a second pair is pointless. Judge the flow by the rotation of the connected mechanism. This branch leads to processing without a windmill, and a second source can be added later, when the load grows.
codex.quest.story_forge.water.title: The Way of Water
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.text.0: Crushing wheels are the road for those who already know brass and Create’s mechanical crafters. You need two wheels and raw material for 128 crushed raw iron. The millstone remains an equal entrance, so there is no reason to build this line before your own level.
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.text.1: Assemble the wheels on mechanical crafters, place them as a pair and set them to turn towards the gap between them. Start with a small portion of iron raw material. Fence off the crushing zone and arrange collection underneath, or the output will get lost among items on the ground.
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.text.2: The book remembers the wheels as ordinary items: show the pair and put it to work. The 128 crushed raw iron, however, must be in your inventory at turn-in and will go in full. That confirms the output; the direction of rotation, the fencing and a steady feed you check yourself.
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.title: Crushing: a batch of iron
codex.quest.story_forge.wind.text.0: A windmill turns by itself, asks for no fuel and moves the drive out of the cramped workshop onto the roof. You will need a windmill bearing and 64 sail frames. Height adds no power of its own — only the assembled structure and the number of sails count.
codex.quest.story_forge.wind.text.1: Fix the future rotor to the bearing, fill it out with frames and leave room around it: the spinning cross must not block walkways. The bearing’s Ponder scene shows how to start the windmill — watch it before assembling. Take rotation from the bearing’s stationary side onto the working shaft.
codex.quest.story_forge.wind.text.2: All 64 frames must sit in your inventory at once at least once; after that, place them, no second set required. Whether the shaft turns, check with your own eyes. The next step with the stressometer will show how much of the power your workshop is already eating.
codex.quest.story_forge.wind.title: The Way of Wind
codex.quest.story_sky.cast.text.0: Four cast iron Big Cannons barrels are an order for finished parts, not for a battery. Before casting, set up a site with rotation and water for the boring machine. A raw casting needs machining, so check the exact item name at every step.
codex.quest.story_sky.cast.text.1: Cast the cast iron blanks by the available blueprint, let the metal set and bore them with the right feed and cooling. Finish the first barrel on its own — that way you see the direction of travel and the result. Do not mix parts of different cannon systems merely because they share a calibre in the inventory.
codex.quest.story_sky.cast.text.2: All four finished barrels are handed in at once from your inventory and go. For your own cannon keep a separate kit with a compatible chamber, breech, shell and charge. Test the assembled gun empty on the ground first, and only then lift it aboard.
codex.quest.story_sky.cast.title: Casting
codex.quest.story_sky.eyes.text.0: Radar exists so you can see the sky before automatic fire appears in it. Prepare a plane radar, a monitor and two Create Radar data links. These items form a network only after you assign the links’ targets and the required controllers through the add-on’s interfaces.
codex.quest.story_sky.eyes.text.1: Set up an observation post and connect the elements one by one, starting with a clear display channel. A data link first selects a valid target — a monitor, a cannon mount or a network controller — and only then takes part in the assignment. A message about no target selected or too great a distance points to a setup error, not to an empty sky.
codex.quest.story_sky.eyes.text.2: Show the two data links together before using them; register the rest separately. Whether there are marks on the screen, the book cannot see. Get a mark for a known target and compare its movement with the world before handing that data to weapons or drawing conclusions about safety.
codex.quest.story_sky.eyes.title: Eyes
codex.quest.story_sky.flak.text.0: An autocannon differs from a big cannon in its build, feed and ammunition. Prepare a steel autocannon barrel and 64 Big Cannons flak rounds for turn-in. One barrel is not yet a weapon: you will need the remaining compatible parts and a working ammunition feed.
codex.quest.story_sky.flak.text.1: Assemble the mount on a ground range, check the empty mechanism and the direction of fire. Load autocannon rounds specifically, not the shells and powder charges of a big cannon. Before loading, assign a safe sector of sky with none of your ships, buildings or player routes in it — the round is explosive.
codex.quest.story_sky.flak.text.2: The barrel can be placed after registration. All 64 rounds sit in your inventory for turn-in and go; keep a stock for test fire separately. Check the feed in short bursts, and fix any lack of lift after mounting the weapon before the next flight, not in combat.
codex.quest.story_sky.flak.title: Anti-Air
codex.quest.story_sky.fleet.text.0: The flagship completes the project: lift, navigation and identification meet on one sound construct. Prepare a navigation table, a transponder and four gyroscopic mechanisms for turn-in. The table gives directional signals towards a navigation item’s destination — it will not become a ready autopilot for any hull.
codex.quest.story_sky.fleet.text.1: On the moored ship check control and lift after fitting the weapons. Give the transponder a name and a code, then enter the same code in the identification filter of the air-defence network controller: an installed transponder alone does not save you from automatic target selection. Pass through the observation zone with firing disabled.
codex.quest.story_sky.fleet.text.2: The table and the transponder can be placed after registration. The four gyroscopes sit in your inventory for turn-in and go — do not strip parts off a flying ship for them. Finish the project with a return and a landing at full working mass and with control to spare.
codex.quest.story_sky.fleet.title: Flagship
The vessel landed on its pad at low speed guided by the instruments

The first balloon climbs by eye, but landing by eye ends with a broken deck. The altitude sensor emits a redstone signal by elevation: by default it grows as you climb, the limits are set in its menu, and the direction can be inverted. The velocity sensor gives a signal by speed along its axis and outputs it away from the motion. The throttle lever is a compact analog signal source: hold and drag to set the level.

Connect the lever to the burner: its output scales with signal strength, so the burner can be throttled rather than switched off. Remember from the Ponder that lift weakens with altitude and the craft settles when lift and weight balance. With engineer's goggles the altitude sensor shows pressure and exact altitude, and a wrench reveals small changes.

Sensors and the lever can be placed right after registration. For the objective, descend while watching the readings, touch the pad at low speed, then make sure the burner holds the vessel in place. Keep in mind that the velocity sensor measures only along the axis it faces.
codex.quest.story_sky.guide_rwr.task.2: The receiver sounded on entering radar range and gave a separate alert on lock-on
codex.quest.story_sky.guide_rwr.text.0: Your radar sees other targets, but the crew of your own vessel will not know a gun has already been trained on them. The radar warning receiver mounts on the hull of a physics contraption and plays one sound when the vessel enters a radar's range and another when it is locked on. The safe zone designator is linked to a monitor and marks, by two points, the area the operator considers safe.
codex.quest.story_sky.guide_rwr.text.1: First link the designator to the monitor from the previous quest, then mark the start and end points above your base: the mod's messages confirm each step. Mount the receiver where the sound can be heard from the control post. Test it on your own radar: fly through its observation area and wait for both signals.
codex.quest.story_sky.guide_rwr.text.2: Both items can be installed right after registration. The objective is two different warnings heard during the pass. The receiver does not cancel a lock-on; it only buys time to leave the zone or hold fire.
codex.quest.story_sky.guide_rwr.title: Radar Warning
codex.quest.story_sky.lift.text.0: The air project begins with understanding lift, not with a heavy deck. Prepare a physics assembler, sixteen white envelopes and sixteen levitite for turn-in. Levitite keeps a construct afloat but gains no altitude: to rise you need another force — a working hot-air balloon, for instance.
codex.quest.story_sky.lift.text.1: For a balloon make an airtight volume and a source of hot air; stray blocks inside eat the useful volume, and gaps let the air out. The sixteen envelopes in the goal promise no adequate size for any ship. Glue the linked blocks together and assemble the construct by the assembler’s Ponder scene on a safe platform.
codex.quest.story_sky.lift.text.2: The envelopes and the assembler can be used after registration. The sixteen levitite, by contrast, sit in your inventory for turn-in and go. Test lift separately, with little mass and an open sky: a reward for materials is no licence to hang guns all over the platform at once.
codex.quest.story_sky.lift.title: Ascent
codex.quest.story_sky.missile.text.0: The missile section is assembled from CBCAeronautics Missiles parts: two rocket motors, four sets of actuator fins, a guidance computer and a missile mount. There is no finished missile with a warhead in this list. First assemble and study the unarmed construct where there is plenty of open space around.
codex.quest.story_sky.missile.text.1: To link the computer, first select the fins with a right-click of the matching item, then place the computer within the allowed distance. Messages about another dimension, missing fins or an exceeded range name the cause of the failure outright. Check further assembly and the assignment of the mount against the add-on’s tooltips.
codex.quest.story_sky.missile.text.2: The parts are not consumed: show the motors and fins in the required batches and place them. The book stages no launch and judges no guidance by the mere presence of a computer. The first launch belongs on a separate range after checking the link, direction, identification and a clear trajectory, with your own craft far from the sector.
codex.quest.story_sky.missile.title: Missile
codex.quest.story_sky.mount.text.0: Automatic aiming joins radar data to the movement of a gun. Prepare a cannon mount, yaw and pitch controllers and a fire controller. The last gives a redstone signal when the linked mount is aimed at the mark; whether that is your own ship or a stranger’s, it cannot tell.
codex.quest.story_sky.mount.text.1: Assemble a compatible gun and assign the controllers to your mount through the add-on’s link system. First trials go without charge or shell: check yaw and pitch separately against a known target. Make sure the limits of travel will not point the barrel at the deck, the base or a neighbouring emplacement.
codex.quest.story_sky.mount.text.2: Register the items one by one and place them straight away; the book does not judge the network setup. Connect the firing permission only after checking identification, the safe sector and the behaviour on losing a target. A barrel that tracks a mark prettily is not yet a weapons system.
codex.quest.story_sky.mount.title: Aiming
codex.quest.tech2_foregoing.animals.text: Animal husbandry here is split into feeding, taking produce and killing creatures. The Animal Feeder breeds animals with suitable food, the Rancher shears sheep and milks cows, and the Mob Crusher kills whatever lives in its working area. Three devices facing one breeding pen is a sure way to lose it.

Place the feeder and the servicing machine in a securely fenced area, supply FE and the right food. Display the working bounds and check one production cycle. Give the crusher a separate closed area with no pets, villagers or passers-by.

Draw off the drops and the essence, and check the crusher's mode before switching it on. Three blocks in a chest make no working farm, and no breeding stock needs sacrificing for the quest. Keep the original pair of animals apart so a filter or facing mistake does not destroy your only means of rebuilding the herd.
codex.quest.tech2_foregoing.farm.text.0: The plant sower and the plant gatherer split the field's work between them. The sower plants material from its coloured slots into the matching parts of the area above it. The gatherer harvests in front of its working side and can grab connected parts of a tree, so set aside a separate small field to begin with.
codex.quest.tech2_foregoing.farm.text.1: Place the machines, display the working areas and prepare soil, water, seeds and FE. Choose one familiar crop and check the full round of planting and harvesting. The ordinary gatherer breaks plants when harvesting; do not assume automatic replanting without a working sower or the special conditions of an improved process.
codex.quest.tech2_foregoing.farm.text.2: Draw off the harvest and the by-product sludge and keep some seeds for the next planting. The fertiliser in the quest has its own use and will not end up in just any slot by itself. If the field empties, check the planting material and the matching areas, not just the harvesting speed.
codex.quest.tech2_foregoing.farm.title: Auto Farm
Industrial Foregoing machine frames come in tiers and go into specific recipes. The simple early frame is made at the crafting table; the next comes from a separate process. Prepare plastic and metals, keeping early frames for the upgrade infrastructure itself.

Make two Pity-tier frames and prepare the dissolution chamber for the Simple one. Its recipe combines items with the required fluid rather than merely surrounding the old frame at a crafting table. Look at the actual recipe before spending rare materials.
